title.rendered: Apple’s First Touchscreen MacBook Pro May Be Near

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Apple plans touchscreen MacBook Pros by 2026: After years of pushback, Apple is preparing to launch OLED MacBook Pros with built-in touch support, starting late 2026.
  • OLED touch displays could improve design and efficiency: Ming-Chi Kuo predicts slimmer MacBook Pros with integrated touch sensors, with large-scale production beginning in late 2026.
  • Mac and iPad features are gradually converging: Mark Gurman highlights Apple’s push to align Macs with iPads through shared technologies like OLED touchscreens and evolving design philosophies.
  • Apple’s shift follows long resistance to touch interfaces: The iPad’s popularity and Microsoft’s touchscreen PCs influenced Apple’s change in stance, opening the door for touch-enabled Macs.
  • Touchscreen rollout may extend beyond MacBook Pro: Apple could bring OLED touch displays to MacBook Air models by 2027, with Samsung expected to supply the necessary display panels.

Apple’s historic opposition to touchscreen Macs appears to be giving way. According to a new report, the company is planning to introduce its first MacBook Pro featuring both an OLED screen and a touchscreen by late 2026.

Reports Suggest OLED MacBook Pro With Touchscreen Is Coming in 2026

Well-regarded analyst Ming-Chi Kuo anticipates that the upcoming MacBook Pro will incorporating OLED displays with an integrated touchscreen, facilitated by on-cell touch technology. This tech embeds touch sensors within the display itself, promising to deliver both a sleeker build and better efficiency. Kuo projects that mass production could start as soon as late 2026, setting the stage for a potential launch in early 2027.

Supporting Kuo’s prediction, Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman—known for breaking Apple news—has also noted Apple’s ambitions towards debuting a touchscreen MacBook Pro as part of a larger redesign. Gurman posits that future Macs and iPads may share increasingly similar features, such as vivid OLED touchscreens and unified applications.

Apple Slowly Warms Up to Touchscreen Macs After iPad’s Rise

Apple’s original stance was firm against touchscreens on laptops, claiming they were unnecessary. However, the evolving role of the iPad, now more akin to a laptop with keyboard and trackpad integrations, has muddied those waters. The iPad, particularly with the update of iPadOS 26 that bears macOS Tahoe’s design elements, exemplifies these intersections. According to Kuo, Apple has learned from observing iPad user interactions, concluding that touch may actually enhance productivity in specific contexts.

Meanwhile, many competitors, notably Microsoft with its Surface lineup, have championed touch interactivity for years. Younger generations, accustomed to the touchscreen interface of iPhones and iPads, tend to expect touch capability across all devices, thus pressuring Apple to adjust its approach.

MacBook Pro Roadmap Shows OLED Touchscreen Coming After M5 Models

The MacBook’s roadmap suggests that the OLED touchscreen iteration will launch following the M5 chip models. Apple is purportedly targeting an early 2026 release for M5-powered laptops, with OLED touchscreen models featuring M6 chips anticipated later that year. These redesigns are likely to include a reduction in body thickness and a smaller display notch.

The OLED panels are reportedly coming from Samsung. Looking forward, Kuo predicts Apple might extend touchscreen technology to more of its lineup, possibly including the MacBook Air by 2027, coinciding with the second generation of the more budget-friendly MacBook models.

What Touchscreen Support Could Mean for Mac Users

Should Apple proceed as envisioned, the MacBook Pro would merge iPad-like interactivity with traditional laptop performance. This blend isn’t merely about making swipes or scrolls easier; it signifies a strategic move towards bridging the functionalities of iPads and Macs. Users could see more versatile device interactions without losing the essence of the Mac’s familiar usage.

How do you feel about a touchscreen on the MacBook Pro? Share your thoughts below.

mainEntity.name: Is there an app to block text messages on iPhones?

acceptedAnswer.text: Several third-party apps, such as Textkiller, Robokiller, etc., can filter and block spam text messages on your iPhone automatically. However, these apps require permission to read all your incoming texts, including OTP, bank alerts, and pretty much everything else, so we wouldn't recommend using them. A better approach is to use the built-in Messages app instead, which lets you block unwanted messages with a few simple taps.

mainEntity.name: How do you know if you're blocked on iMessage?

acceptedAnswer.text: If someone has blocked you on iMessage, you may see green bubbles instead of blue. Likewise, you'll also see the Sent as Text Message label under your messages. For more information, refer to our guide on how to know if someone has blocked you on iMessage.

mainEntity.name: How do I clear the Safari cache without deleting my history on a Mac?

acceptedAnswer.text: Turn on the Develop menu in Safari Settings → Advanced, then choose Develop → Empty Caches or press Option + Command + E on your Mac.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between clearing history and clearing website data in Safari?

acceptedAnswer.text: Clearing history removes your browsing record but leaves you signed in. Clearing website data deletes cookies, cache, and local storage, which signs you out of sites.

mainEntity.name: Why is the "Remove All" button greyed out in Safari?

acceptedAnswer.text: Screen Time is blocking the action. Open System Settings → Screen Time → Content & Privacy, then set Web Content to Unrestricted Access.

mainEntity.name: How do I enable the Develop menu in Safari to clear the cache?

acceptedAnswer.text: Open Safari → Settings... → Advanced, and enable "Show Develop menu in menu bar."

mainEntity.name: Will clearing Safari data delete my saved passwords in iCloud Keychain?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Passwords stored in iCloud Keychain stay intact when you clear Safari data.

mainEntity.name: What happens to my bookmarks when I clear Safari data?

acceptedAnswer.text: Bookmarks are not affected by clearing cache, history, or website data.

mainEntity.name: Why is Safari still slow after I cleared the cache and cookies?

acceptedAnswer.text: Quit and relaunch Safari, check for macOS and Safari updates, and disable or remove extensions that may be hurting performance completely.

mainEntity.name: Why is "Clear History and Website Data" greyed out?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most of the time, Screen Time content restrictions are the cause. Go to Settings → Screen Time → Content & Privacy Restrictions → Content Restrictions, then set Web Content to Unrestricted Access. The button should become available again after returning to Settings → Safari. If Screen Time is off, check for device management or parental profiles that enforce the same block.

mainEntity.name: Does clearing Safari data delete my saved passwords or bookmarks?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. iCloud Keychain passwords, Autofill details, and bookmarks are stored separately. Clearing history, cache, and cookies does not remove them, and saved logins and favorites remain across devices signed in to the same Apple ID.

mainEntity.name: Is there a way to clear only the cache in Safari on an iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: Safari on iPhone does not include a cache only control. The closest option is Settings → Safari → Advanced → Website Data → Remove All Website Data, which clears cache and cookies while preserving browsing history. Individual site entries can also be removed from this screen.

mainEntity.name: How do I clear cookies for just one website in Safari?

acceptedAnswer.text: Go to Settings → Safari → Advanced → Website Data. Search for the site, swipe left on its entry, then tap Delete. Only that site's cookies and cache are removed without affecting others.

mainEntity.name: Will clearing my Safari data fix website loading problems?

acceptedAnswer.text: Often, yes. Clearing data can fix slow pages, login failures, and display glitches. Stale cache and conflicting cookies cause many of these issues, and a reset forces fresh content to load.

mainEntity.name: Is private browsing safer than manually clearing my history?

acceptedAnswer.text: Private Browsing avoids saving history, cookies, and cache during the session, useful for temporary tasks or sensitive research. Manual clearing removes the buildup left from regular browsing and can improve performance.

mainEntity.name: How do Screen Time restrictions affect clearing Safari data?

acceptedAnswer.text: Screen Time Content & Privacy Restrictions can disable the Clear History and Website Data button. This is common with parental controls or personal usage management and requires the Screen Time passcode to change settings.

title.rendered: Apple Watch Gets a Battery Life Boost for Kids

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Adaptive Power expands to Apple Watch for Kids: Apple is extending Adaptive Power mode from iPhone to child-set Apple Watches, reducing performance slightly to maximize battery life.
  • Default setting in watchOS 26: On child Apple Watches, Adaptive Power turns on automatically, but parents can switch it off if they prefer faster performance.
  • Different strategies on iPhone vs Apple Watch: iPhone Adaptive Power dims display and toggles Low Power Mode, while Apple Watch prioritizes performance tweaks for better endurance without an iPhone.
  • Apple’s bigger focus on battery efficiency: Expanding Adaptive Power highlights Apple’s intent to build smarter background optimizations, especially important for kids’ wearables that run independently.
  • Precaution for parents and kids: Adaptive Power may slow animations or responsiveness, so parents should weigh longer battery against slightly reduced speed.

Apple is quietly extending its Adaptive Power mode beyond the iPhone, with the Apple Watch now benefiting from the feature as well. However, this update comes with a caveat: the battery-saving function is currently activated only on children’s watches configured through Apple’s Family Setup—now rebranded as Apple Watch for Your Kids.

How Adaptive Power Works on Apple Watch

In watchOS 26, any compatible Apple Watch set up for a child will have Adaptive Power enabled by default. This setting aims to prolong battery life by making minor compromises in performance. According to Apple, users may notice slightly delayed Siri responses, and animations and scrolling might not be as smooth as before. How frequently these slowdowns will occur isn’t specified, but the goal is to extend battery life in everyday situations.

For parents wanting to prioritize speed over conservation, they can disable this feature by navigating to Settings, selecting Battery, and then Adaptive Power on their child’s watch. It’s crucial to note that this option is available only on Apple Watch models configured through Apple Watch for Your Kids, which necessitates a cellular-capable device.

How It Differs from the iPhone

Adaptive Power debuted on the iPhone with iOS 26 for the iPhone 15 Pro and newer models. On iPhones, the feature operates differently. It slightly dims the display, allows certain tasks to take additional time, and automatically switches to Low Power Mode when the battery dips to 20%. For the latest iPhone 17 series and iPhone Air, it’s enabled by default.

Conversely, the Apple Watch version focuses on nuanced performance adjustments rather than display changes. This could be notably beneficial as kids often use their watches unpaired with an iPhone, making these tweaks helpful for maintaining charge through the day.

Why This Matters

Apple’s decision to integrate Adaptive Power more broadly underscores a shift toward an overarching battery strategy across its products. By incorporating it into the Apple Watch, albeit initially for kids, Apple signals that extending battery life is just as critical for wearables as it is for smartphones. This development also offers a glimpse into Apple’s possible future approach to energy management across its device lineup, leaning towards background optimizations over tasking users with manual settings adjustments.

Does this approach resonate with you? Feel free to share your thoughts below.

mainEntity.name: Is there an app to block text messages on iPhones?

acceptedAnswer.text: Several third-party apps, such as Textkiller, Robokiller, etc., can filter and block spam text messages on your iPhone automatically. However, these apps require permission to read all your incoming texts, including OTP, bank alerts, and pretty much everything else, so we wouldn't recommend using them. A better approach is to use the built-in Messages app instead, which lets you block unwanted messages with a few simple taps.

mainEntity.name: How do you know if you're blocked on iMessage?

acceptedAnswer.text: If someone has blocked you on iMessage, you may see green bubbles instead of blue. Likewise, you'll also see the Sent as Text Message label under your messages. For more information, refer to our guide on how to know if someone has blocked you on iMessage.

mainEntity.name: How do I clear the Safari cache without deleting my history on a Mac?

acceptedAnswer.text: Turn on the Develop menu in Safari Settings → Advanced, then choose Develop → Empty Caches or press Option + Command + E on your Mac.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between clearing history and clearing website data in Safari?

acceptedAnswer.text: Clearing history removes your browsing record but leaves you signed in. Clearing website data deletes cookies, cache, and local storage, which signs you out of sites.

mainEntity.name: Why is the "Remove All" button greyed out in Safari?

acceptedAnswer.text: Screen Time is blocking the action. Open System Settings → Screen Time → Content & Privacy, then set Web Content to Unrestricted Access.

mainEntity.name: How do I enable the Develop menu in Safari to clear the cache?

acceptedAnswer.text: Open Safari → Settings... → Advanced, and enable "Show Develop menu in menu bar."

mainEntity.name: Will clearing Safari data delete my saved passwords in iCloud Keychain?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Passwords stored in iCloud Keychain stay intact when you clear Safari data.

mainEntity.name: What happens to my bookmarks when I clear Safari data?

acceptedAnswer.text: Bookmarks are not affected by clearing cache, history, or website data.

mainEntity.name: Why is Safari still slow after I cleared the cache and cookies?

acceptedAnswer.text: Quit and relaunch Safari, check for macOS and Safari updates, and disable or remove extensions that may be hurting performance completely.

acceptedAnswer.text: Most of the time, Screen Time content restrictions are the cause. mainEntity.name: Does clearing Safari data delete my saved passwords or bookmarks?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. iCloud Keychain passwords, Autofill details, and bookmarks are stored separately. Clearing history, cache, and cookies does not remove them, and saved logins and favorites remain across devices signed in to the same Apple ID.

mainEntity.name: Is there a way to clear only the cache in Safari on an iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: Safari on iPhone does not include a cache only control. The closest option is Settings → Safari → Advanced → Website Data → Remove All Website Data, which clears cache and cookies while preserving browsing history. Individual site entries can also be removed from this screen.

mainEntity.name: How do I clear cookies for just one website in Safari?

acceptedAnswer.text: Go to Settings → Safari → Advanced → Website Data. Search for the site, swipe left on its entry, then tap Delete. Only that site's cookies and cache are removed without affecting others.

mainEntity.name: Will clearing my Safari data fix website loading problems?

acceptedAnswer.text: Often, yes. Clearing data can fix slow pages, login failures, and display glitches. Stale cache and conflicting cookies cause many of these issues, and a reset forces fresh content to load.

mainEntity.name: Is private browsing safer than manually clearing my history?

acceptedAnswer.text: Private Browsing avoids saving history, cookies, and cache during the session, useful for temporary tasks or sensitive research. Manual clearing removes the buildup left from regular browsing and can improve performance.

acceptedAnswer.text: Screen Time Content & Privacy Restrictions can disable the Clear History and Website Data button. This is common with parental controls or personal usage management and requires the Screen Time passcode to change settings.

keyPoints.title: Expansion of Adaptive Power to Apple Watch for Kids
keyPoints.explanation: Apple is extending its Adaptive Power mode beyond iPhone to include Apple Watch, but currently, it is only activated on children's watches set up through Apple Watch for Your Kids, aiming to prolong battery life with minor performance compromises.

keyPoints.title: How Adaptive Power Works on Apple Watch
keyPoints.explanation: On watchOS 26, Adaptive Power is enabled by default for compatible child's Apple Watches, reducing performance slightly to save battery, with options for parents to disable it in settings if they prefer speed over conservation.

keyPoints.title: Differences Between Apple Watch and iPhone Adaptive Power
keyPoints.explanation: Adaptive Power on iPhones dims the display and switches to Low Power Mode, while on Apple Watch it focuses on performance adjustments, which helps in maintaining battery life especially when used without an iPhone, highlighting different strategies for each device.

keyPoints.title: Significance of Expanding Adaptive Power Across Devices
keyPoints.explanation: Apple’s adoption of Adaptive Power across products indicates a strategic focus on enhancing battery efficiency through background optimizations, emphasizing the importance of battery life in wearables as well as smartphones.

title.rendered: Snapchat keeps crashing on iPhone? Here is how to fix it

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Snapchat crashes are usually tied to outdated apps, cache bugs, or iOS issues—network settings and third-party add-ons can also trigger problems.
  • Force quit and restart Snapchat to fix minor glitches by swiping up on the app in App Switcher and reopening it clean.
  • Check Snapchat’s server status on Downdetector to rule out service-wide outages before troubleshooting your iPhone.
  • Update both Snapchat and your iPhone’s iOS to resolve known bugs and ensure app compatibility with system-level changes.
  • Try clearing cache, resetting networks, or reinstalling the app—VPNs or unauthorized plugins can also interfere with stability.

Is Snapchat constantly crashing on your iPhone? Well, you’re not alone. It’s a common problem reported by many iPhone users, wherein the app could either keep crashing when you open it or freeze and not respond at all. But fret not. In this article, we’ll explain why the Snapchat app crashes on your iPhone and what you could do to fix it.

Why does my Snapchat keep crashing on my iPhone?

Here are a few reasons why the Snapchat app might be crashing or freezing on your iPhone:

  • Outdated app: Using an outdated version of Snapchat with bugs.
  • Issues with the Snapchat server: Server issues on Snapchat’s end can cause the app to not function properly.
  • Corrupted app cache: Over time, accumulated cache affects the Snapchat app’s performance and cause it to freeze or crash.
  • Third-party plugins: Unofficial Snapchat plugins or third-party apps can interfere with its functionality.
  • Network problems: Unstable internet connections can prevent you from accessing the app.
  • iOS issues: Your iPhone’s operating system might have glitches. Updating it should fix the issue.

How to fix Snapchat keeps crashing on iPhone

Now that you know what could be causing Snapchat to crash on your iPhone, here’s how you can troubleshoot the issue.

1. Force quit Snapchat and relaunch It

Force closing the Snapchat app can resolve temporary glitches causing app crashes. When you do this, it removes the app from the background and clears it from the RAM.

  1. Open the App Switcher by swiping up from the bottom of the Home Screen.
  2. Swipe up on the Snapchat app to close it.
  3. Reopen Snapchat.

If it still crashes, check the Snapchat server status.

2. Check Snapchat’s server status

Sometimes, issues with Snapchat’s server can cause the app to crash on your iPhone. To know if this is the case, open Safari or any other web browser and go to Downdetector.com. If there’s an outage, Downdetector will show it on the home page. In this case, you’ll have to wait until Snapchat resolves the issue.

3. Update Snapchat app on your iPhone

If the Snapchat app has been crashing on your iPhone for a while, it could be due to a bug. Ensure you’re running the latest version of Snapchat using the steps below if you haven’t updated the app in a while:

  1. Open the App Store on your iPhone.
  2. Tap on your profile icon in the top-right corner.
  3. Scroll down to see if Snapchat has an update available.
  4. If it does, tap Update and wait for it to install.

Once installed, check if Snapchat works fine.

4. Hard Reset Your iPhone

Force restarting your iPhone is another solution you can try if Snapchat keeps freezing or your iPhone.

Press and quickly release the Volume Up button, then the Volume Down button. Hold the Side button until the Apple logo appears. Once your iPhone restarts, launch Snapchat and check if it runs smoothly.

5. Enable Background App Refresh for Snapchat

If you haven’t turned on Background App Refresh for Snapchat, the app won’t be able to update its content in the background. As such, it’ll have to load all of the content at once when you launch the app, which can sometimes cause it to crash or freeze.

  1. Open the Settings app.
  2. Tap General and go to Background App Refresh.

  3. Ensure Background App Refresh is turned on. If not, tap it and select Wi-Fi & Cellular Data.
  4. Finally, toggle on Snapchat.

6. Clear Snapchat cache

Cache from previous versions of the app might weigh it down sometimes. Clearing it may fix the problem, especially if Snapchat crashes mid-operation. When you do this, none of your chats, snaps, or memories will be lost.

  1. Open Snapchat and tap your profile icon in the top-left corner.
  2. Tap the gear icon to access Settings.
  3. Scroll down and select Clear Data.
  4. Tap Clear Cache.

  5. Confirm by tapping Clear.

Now, the app will be closed automatically. Relaunch Snapchat and see if the problem persists.

7. Disable VPN on Your iPhone

Sometimes, VPN services can disrupt specific apps because of IP masking. When the VPN is on, Snapchat is likely to keep on crashing or failing to function at all. Ensuring you deactivate all VPN services while using Snapchat should help in such situations.

  1. If you’ve added a VPN manually, go to Settings and toggle off VPN.
  2. If you use any third-party VPN service, open the VPN app and tap Disconnect.

After disabling VPN, you should also refresh your network connection. Open Control Center and tap Wi-Fi or Cellular data icon to turn them off.

8. Delete and reinstall Snapchat

If none of the fixes so far work, try deleting and reinstalling the Snapchat app on your iPhone.

  1. Long-press Snapchat.
  2. Select Remove App.
  3. Tap Delete App to confirm your action.

  4. Now, go to the App Store.
  5. Search for Snapchat and install it again.

9. Delete third-party Snapchat apps

Do you use third-party Snapchat plugins or apps like Snapchat++? These unauthorized apps can create functionality glitches and cause Snapchat to crash. Delete your account on such apps and remove the app from your iPhone.

10. Update iOS

Lastly, if the problem persists, update your iPhone to the latest version. Sometimes, ff the glitches are courtesy of iOS, Apple ensures to fix them with its software updates.

  1. Launch the Settings app on your iPhone.
  2. Tap General and select Software Update.
  3. If an update is available, tap Download and Install or Install Now.

Signing off…

Snapchat crashes can be incredibly annoying, but by following the steps above, you should be able to resolve the issue and get back to snapping in no time. If you’ve tried everything and the problem persists, contact Snapchat support for further assistance.

FAQs

Why does my camera on Snapchat not work?

If the camera isn’t working inside Snapchat, it could be due to different reasons, such as misconfigured app permissions or a software bug. Our guide on how to fix Snapchat camera problems on iPhone should come in handy in this case.

Should I contact Snapchat Support?

In case none of the troubleshooting steps help, you should ask for help from Snapchat Support. They should be able to give better assistance and help solve the problem.

acceptedAnswer.text: Several third-party apps, such as Textkiller, Robokiller, etc., can filter and block spam text messages on your iPhone automatically. However, these apps require permission to read all your incoming texts, including OTP, bank alerts, and pretty much everything else, so we wouldn't recommend using them. A better approach is to use the built-in Messages app instead, which lets you block unwanted messages with a few simple taps.

mainEntity.name: How do I clear the Safari cache without deleting my history on a Mac?

acceptedAnswer.text: Turn on the Develop menu in Safari Settings → Advanced, then choose Develop → Empty Caches or press Option + Command + E on your Mac.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between clearing history and clearing website data in Safari?

acceptedAnswer.text: Clearing history removes your browsing record but leaves you signed in. Clearing website data deletes cookies, cache, and local storage, which signs you out of sites.

mainEntity.name: Why is the "Remove All" button greyed out in Safari?

acceptedAnswer.text: Screen Time is blocking the action. Open System Settings → Screen Time → Content & Privacy, then set Web Content to Unrestricted Access.

mainEntity.name: How do I enable the Develop menu in Safari to clear the cache?

acceptedAnswer.text: Open Safari → Settings... → Advanced, and enable "Show Develop menu in menu bar."

mainEntity.name: What happens to my bookmarks when I clear Safari data?

mainEntity.name: Is there a way to clear only the cache in Safari on an iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: Safari on iPhone does not include a cache only control. The closest option is Settings → Safari → Advanced → Website Data → Remove All Website Data, which clears cache and cookies while preserving browsing history. Individual site entries can also be removed from this screen.

mainEntity.name: How do I clear cookies for just one website in Safari?

acceptedAnswer.text: Go to Settings → Safari → Advanced → Website Data. Search for the site, swipe left on its entry, then tap Delete. Only that site's cookies and cache are removed without affecting others.

mainEntity.name: Will clearing my Safari data fix website loading problems?

acceptedAnswer.text: Often, yes. Clearing data can fix slow pages, login failures, and display glitches. Stale cache and conflicting cookies cause many of these issues, and a reset forces fresh content to load.

keyPoints.title: Reasons Why Snapchat Crashes on iPhone
keyPoints.explanation: Common causes include outdated app versions, server issues, corrupted cache, third-party plugins, network problems, and iOS glitches.

keyPoints.title: Restart Snapchat to Fix Crashes
keyPoints.explanation: Force quitting and relaunching Snapchat can resolve temporary glitches that cause crashes by clearing apps from RAM.

keyPoints.title: Check Snapchat Server Status
keyPoints.explanation: Visit Downdetector to see if Snapchat is experiencing outages, which can cause app crashes, and wait if needed.

keyPoints.title: Update Snapchat and iOS
keyPoints.explanation: Ensuring both Snapchat and your iPhone’s iOS are up to date can fix bugs and compatibility issues that lead to crashes.

keyPoints.title: Additional Troubleshooting Tips
keyPoints.explanation: Other solutions include resetting your network, clearing cache, disabling VPN, reinstalling Snapchat, and turning off third-party apps or plugins.

title.rendered: Turn Off Your iPhone Without Using the Power Button: Quick Guide

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • iOS 18 adds a Power icon in Control Center letting you shut down your iPhone without using the physical power button—just swipe down and tap.
  • In iOS 17 or older, go to Settings > General > Shut Down to power off if your hardware buttons aren’t working.
  • Plug your iPhone into a charger to turn it on—no power button needed, as it automatically boots when connected to power.
  • AssistiveTouch offers extra control when buttons fail—use it to lock the screen, adjust volume, or trigger shutdown functions.
  • For broken buttons or passcode resets, check Apple’s support for safe guides on troubleshooting without losing your data.

While the chances of this happening are slim, there may come an instance where your iPhone’s Power and Volume buttons get damaged or become unresponsive. This makes it challenging to perform even basic tasks like powering off the iPhone. Fortunately, Apple has already considered this issue and offers multiple ways to turn off your iPhone without the Power and Volume buttons.

Keep reading to learn how to turn off your iPhone without Power or Volume buttons in iOS 18 or previous versions.

How to Turn Off iPhone Without Power Button in iOS 18 or later

With iOS 18, Apple has completely overhauled the Control Center for the first time in years, giving users complete control of customizability. However, other than customizability, one of the standout features of the new Control Center is the addition of the stand-alone Power button. You no longer have to use the traditional Power and Side button to turn off your iPhone if it supports iOS 18.

  1. Swipe down from the top right to pull down the Control Center.
  2. Here, tap the Power icon at the top right corner.
  3. Next, drag the Power Slide to the right to turn off your iPhone.

How to Turn Off iPhone Without Buttons in iOS 17 or Previous Versions

If you have an iPhone running on iOS 17, you can update it to iOS 18 anytime, as all the devices that support iOS 17 also support the new version. Use the new Power button to quickly shut down the device.

However, if you own an iPhone X or a previous model, you’ll have to rely on the age-old method of turning off your iPhone without the Power and Side buttons.

  1. Open the Settings app
  2. Tap on General.
  3. Scroll to the end and tap on Shut Down.
  4. Drag the slider to the right.

How to Turn On iPhone Without Power Button

Now you know how easy it is to turn off your iPhone if the Power or Volume buttons are not working or damaged for any reason. The real problem arises when you need to turn it ON back again, as it requires you to press and hold the Power button. Well, it’s easier than you think it is.

All you need to do is plug your iPhone into a power adaptor via an MFi-certified cable, leave it for a few minutes, and your iPhone will turn on automatically. However, if the battery on your iPhone is dead, the process may take a bit longer.

Signing off…

This is how you can successfully turn off your iPhone running on iOS 18 or previous versions without using any physical button. Next, you may wonder how to lock your iPhone, change volume, and if the side button and volume buttons are not working. The easiest way is to use Assistive Touch to perform all these actions.

Still left with a query or some doubts? Comment them below, and I’ll happily respond.

You may also read here:

  • How to fix if iPhone power button not working
  • How to reset forgotten iPhone passcode without losing data

excerpt.rendered: A broken power button need not stop you shutting down. Here is how to power off an iPhone from Control Center in iOS 18, the Settings method for older versions, and how to switch it back on.

mainEntity.name: Is there an app to block text messages on iPhones?

acceptedAnswer.text: Several third-party apps, such as Textkiller, Robokiller, etc., can filter and block spam text messages on your iPhone automatically. However, these apps require permission to read all your incoming texts, including OTP, bank alerts, and pretty much everything else, so we wouldn't recommend using them. A better approach is to use the built-in Messages app instead, which lets you block unwanted messages with a few simple taps.

mainEntity.name: How do you know if you're blocked on iMessage?

acceptedAnswer.text: If someone has blocked you on iMessage, you may see green bubbles instead of blue. Likewise, you'll also see the Sent as Text Message label under your messages. For more information, refer to our guide on how to know if someone has blocked you on iMessage.

mainEntity.name: How do I clear the Safari cache without deleting my history on a Mac?

acceptedAnswer.text: Turn on the Develop menu in Safari Settings → Advanced, then choose Develop → Empty Caches or press Option + Command + E on your Mac.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between clearing history and clearing website data in Safari?

acceptedAnswer.text: Clearing history removes your browsing record but leaves you signed in. Clearing website data deletes cookies, cache, and local storage, which signs you out of sites.

mainEntity.name: Why is the "Remove All" button greyed out in Safari?

acceptedAnswer.text: Screen Time is blocking the action. Open System Settings → Screen Time → Content & Privacy, then set Web Content to Unrestricted Access.

mainEntity.name: How do I enable the Develop menu in Safari to clear the cache?

acceptedAnswer.text: Open Safari → Settings... → Advanced, and enable "Show Develop menu in menu bar."

mainEntity.name: Will clearing Safari data delete my saved passwords in iCloud Keychain?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Passwords stored in iCloud Keychain stay intact when you clear Safari data.

mainEntity.name: What happens to my bookmarks when I clear Safari data?

acceptedAnswer.text: Bookmarks are not affected by clearing cache, history, or website data.

mainEntity.name: Why is Safari still slow after I cleared the cache and cookies?

acceptedAnswer.text: Quit and relaunch Safari, check for macOS and Safari updates, and disable or remove extensions that may be hurting performance completely.

mainEntity.name: Is there a way to clear only the cache in Safari on an iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: Safari on iPhone does not include a cache only control. The closest option is Settings → Safari → Advanced → Website Data → Remove All Website Data, which clears cache and cookies while preserving browsing history. Individual site entries can also be removed from this screen.

mainEntity.name: How do I clear cookies for just one website in Safari?

acceptedAnswer.text: Go to Settings → Safari → Advanced → Website Data. Search for the site, swipe left on its entry, then tap Delete. Only that site's cookies and cache are removed without affecting others.

mainEntity.name: Will clearing my Safari data fix website loading problems?

acceptedAnswer.text: Often, yes. Clearing data can fix slow pages, login failures, and display glitches. Stale cache and conflicting cookies cause many of these issues, and a reset forces fresh content to load.

mainEntity.name: Is private browsing safer than manually clearing my history?

acceptedAnswer.text: Private Browsing avoids saving history, cookies, and cache during the session, useful for temporary tasks or sensitive research. Manual clearing removes the buildup left from regular browsing and can improve performance.

acceptedAnswer.text: Screen Time Content & Privacy Restrictions can disable the Clear History and Website Data button. This is common with parental controls or personal usage management and requires the Screen Time passcode to change settings.

keyPoints.title: Turning Off iPhone Without Power Button in iOS 18
keyPoints.explanation: You can now turn off your iPhone using the new Power icon in the Control Center, which can be accessed by swiping down from the top right, making it easy to shut down without the physical button.

keyPoints.title: Turning Off Older iPhones in iOS 17 and Earlier
keyPoints.explanation: For iPhones running iOS 17 or earlier, you need to go to Settings > General > Shut Down and drag the slider to turn off your device if the power buttons are unresponsive.

keyPoints.title: Turning On Your iPhone Without the Power Button
keyPoints.explanation: To turn your iPhone back on without the power button, simply connect it to a charging adapter, and it will automatically power on after a few minutes.

keyPoints.title: Alternative Methods to Power Off iPhone
keyPoints.explanation: Besides using the control center or settings, you can utilize Assistive Touch to perform actions like locking the screen or adjusting volume when physical buttons are damaged.

keyPoints.title: Additional Resources for iPhone Troubleshooting
keyPoints.explanation: For more help, visit guides on fixing non-working power buttons or resetting your iPhone passcode without data loss available through linked articles.

aioseo_head_json.author_bio:
"The founder of iGeeksBlog, Dhvanesh, is an Apple aficionado, who cannot stand even a slight innuendo about Apple products. He dons the cap of editor-in-chief to make sure that articles match the quality standard before they are published."

About Dhvanesh

Ever since teenage years, gadgets and technology have held a special place in Dhvanesh's heart. This fascination with gadgets and their inner workings fueled a lifelong passion for exploration and troubleshooting. Disassembled electronic items scattered around the house became a familiar sight during his younger years, a testament to this insatiable curiosity.

From SEO Expert to Apple Evangelist

After completing his IT engineering diploma, Dhvanesh's professional journey began with a 4.5-year stint as an SEO executive, honing valuable digital marketing skills. However, the desire to share tech knowledge and connect with a like-minded community proved stronger. In 2012, Dhvanesh embarked on a new adventure, founding iGeeksBlog. This blog became a haven for Apple enthusiasts and tech aficionados seeking insightful and in-depth information about everything Apple.

A Decade of iGeeksBlog: Leading the Apple Charge

In the past 12 years, Dhvanesh has donned multiple hats at iGeeksBlog. As the founder, he has steered the blog’s vision, ensuring it remains a trusted resource for Apple users worldwide. Additionally, he has been serving as the CEO of iGeeks Media Private Limited for the past 4 years, overseeing the company's growth and development.

Beyond Writing: A Multifaceted Approach

Dhvanesh isn't just a prolific writer, having penned hundreds of articles for iGeeksBlog. He has also served as the blog’s Editor-in-Chief and Content Strategist, ensuring a consistent flow of high-quality content that caters to the diverse needs of the Apple user base. The passion for exploration extends beyond the written word. He has created numerous YouTube videos for iGeeksBlog, providing visual demonstrations and engaging directly with the audience.

Staying Connected with the Apple Ecosystem

Dhvanesh's dedication to the Apple community goes a step further. Currently, he also manages the iGeeksBlog+ weekly newsletter, delivering curated Apple news, gadgets, apps, tips and tricks straight to subscribers' inboxes. This unwavering commitment to Apple technology and a genuine desire to empower fellow users make him a valuable asset to the iGeeksBlog team.

title.rendered: How to Find Hidden Apps on iPhone

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • With iOS 18 Apple adds a secure Hidden folder in the App Library that requires Face ID or passcode to view or unhide apps you’ve intentionally hidden.
  • Use classic tools like Spotlight Search or the App Library to track down apps hidden from the Home Screen or shuffled into folders.
  • Screen Time restrictions can hide apps—check under Allowed Apps and Content Restrictions to see if parental controls are blocking visibility.
  • Search the App Store to confirm status—if the app shows “Open,” it’s still on your device even if it’s not appearing anywhere else.
  • Resetting the Home Screen restores visibility—this puts all apps back in default order if Siri or search can’t locate what’s missing.

Can’t find an app on your iPhone or iPad? Odds are it isn’t deleted just hidden somewhere. With iOS 26, there are now more ways than ever for an app to slip off your Home Screen.

No need to panic. There’s a difference between apps hidden on purpose for privacy (that trick showed up in iOS 18), apps that were yanked off the Home Screen, and apps blocked by settings like Screen Time. Each case has its own fix, and none of them mean the app is gone forever.

This guide lays out a clear path to track down any missing app. Step by step, it covers every hiding spot, from the secure Hidden folder to those random folders where apps sometimes get dragged without you realizing.

Table of Contents
  • How to Find and Unhide Apps from the Secure "Hidden" Folder (iOS 18 and Later)
  • Classic Methods: Finding Apps Hidden on the Home Screen or in the App Library
    • Find Hidden Apps Using the App Library
    • Unhiding Entire Home Screen Pages
    • Using Spotlight Search to Find hidden apps
    • Searching Manually in Folders
  • Checking for System-Level Restrictions
    • How to Check Screen Time Restrictions
    • Verifying if the App is Still Installed via App Store
  • Last Resorts and Final Checks
    • Using Siri to Find an App
    • Resetting the Home Screen Layout
  • Signing Off…

How to Find and Unhide Apps from the Secure “Hidden” Folder (iOS 18 and Later)

Think your app’s really taking a break? Apple’s wild privacy move lets you hide apps like a magic trick, storing them in this mythical Hidden folder. It’s like the Bermuda Triangle of your app world.

Here’s how to check if your missing app is intentionally hidden:

  1. On your Home Screen, swipe left until you reach the App Library
  2. Scroll all the way to the bottom of the list of categories
  3. Tap on the locked “Hidden” folder
  4. Authenticate with Face ID, Touch ID, or your passcode
  5. You will now see a list of all apps you’ve intentionally hidden

To Unhide an App:

  1. Long-press the app icon in the Hidden folder
  2. Tap “Add to Home Screen” from the menu that appears

The app will immediately return to your Home Screen and appear in the App Library’s main categories again.

Classic Methods: Finding Apps Hidden on the Home Screen or in the App Library

If your app isn’t sitting in the Hidden folder, it’s probably just been bumped off your Home Screen or moved somewhere else. These are the spots to always check.

Find Hidden Apps Using the App Library

The App Library sorts every app you’ve got into little categories on its own, so it’s usually the smartest place to begin looking.

  1. Swipe left on your Home Screen until you reach the App Library
  2. Use the search bar at the top to type the app’s name, or
  3. Look through the automatically generated category folders (Social, Productivity, Games, etc.)
  4. Once you find the app, long-press its icon
  5. Tap “Add to Home Screen” or simply drag it out onto a Home Screen page

Unhiding Entire Home Screen Pages

Whole pages of apps can vanish if they’re hidden, which makes it feel like everything’s gone at once. It usually happens by mistake while cleaning up the Home Screen.

  1. Long-press an empty area on your Home Screen until the apps jiggle
  2. Tap the page dots indicator at the bottom of the screen
  3. You will see a view of all your Home Screen pages
  4. Pages that are hidden will have an empty circle beneath them
  5. Tap the empty circle to put a checkmark in it, making the page visible again
  6. Tap “Done”

Using Spotlight Search to Find hidden apps

Spotlight is the quickest way to dig up an app on your iPhone, no matter how far it’s been buried. It can surface apps lost in folders, tucked onto hidden Home Screen pages, or sitting quietly in the App Library. Here’s the move:

  1. Swipe down on the middle of your Home Screen to bring up Spotlight.
  2. Start typing the app’s name in the search bar.
  3. When it pops up in the results, just tap and it’ll launch straight away.

Searching Manually in Folders

Apps sometimes sneak into a crowded folder by accident, especially the ones that stretch across two or three pages. It’s way too easy to overlook them in there.

The Problem: A quick drag-and-drop can toss an app onto page 2 or 3 of a folder, where it sits buried instead of showing up front.

The Solution:

  1. Manually tap to open each folder on your Home Screen
  2. Once inside a folder, swipe left and right to make sure you’ve checked all the pages within that folder
  3. Look carefully some folders can have 3-4 pages of apps

Checking for System-Level Restrictions

Sometimes apps don’t just wander off your Home Screen — they’re actually hidden by Screen Time limits or parental controls. When that happens, the apps vanish like they were never installed.

How to Check Screen Time Restrictions

Screen Time has the power to block apps so thoroughly they won’t even appear in search. It feels less like they’re hidden and more like they’ve been erased.

  1. Open Settings and select Screen Time.
  2. Scroll down and tap on Content & Privacy Restrictions.
  3. Now, tap on Allowed Apps & Features.
  4. If the app you’re looking for is restricted, toggle on the button next to it to make it visible again.

Verifying if the App is Still Installed via App Store

The App Store can quickly reveal whether an app is just hidden somewhere or if it’s been removed from the device entirely.

  1. Open the App Store on your iPhone or iPad.
  2. Tap on the Search button in the bottom row.
  3. Type the name of the app you’re looking for in the search bar.
  4. When the app appears in the search results, tap the Open button next to it to launch it.

Last Resorts and Final Checks

When every other trick fails and the app still refuses to show up, there are two final moves that usually do the job.

Using Siri to Find an App

Siri can track down any app you’ve got installed, even the ones buried so deep in folders you’d never spot them on your own.

  1. Press and hold the Side button (or Home button on older models) to invoke Siri. Alternatively, you can just say “Hey Siri.”
  2. With Siri listening, say “Open [app name].”
  3. If not, Siri will offer to search the App Store for it

This trick works well since it skips all the hiding quirks and just opens the app straight away.

Resetting the Home Screen Layout

When to Use: Best for the moments when everything feels lost and you just need every single app to show up again.

Warning: Doing this wipes out all your custom folders and puts the Home Screen back to factory order. The upside? Every installed app reappears, listed alphabetically after the stock ones.

The Steps:

  1. Open Settings > General > Transfer or Reset [Device] > Reset
  2. Tap Reset Home Screen Layout
  3. Confirm when asked

Once it’s done, every installed app shows up on the Home Screen again, sorted alphabetically after the default apps.

Signing Off…

Hunting down hidden apps on an iPhone or iPad doesn’t have to turn into a headache. With iOS 26 juggling folders, App Library, and Screen Time limits, apps can feel missing when they’re really just tucked away somewhere. Whether they’ve been shuffled into the Hidden folder, buried in the App Library, or locked down by restrictions, these tricks will bring them back into view.

Lastly, when nothing helps, be sure to check for any third-party apps for hiding or locking apps on your iPhone, as they can sometimes have your hidden apps.

And hey, save this guide for later because let’s be real, everyone misplaces an app eventually.

mainEntity.name: Is there an app to block text messages on iPhones?

acceptedAnswer.text: Several third-party apps, such as Textkiller, Robokiller, etc., can filter and block spam text messages on your iPhone automatically. However, these apps require permission to read all your incoming texts, including OTP, bank alerts, and pretty much everything else, so we wouldn't recommend using them. A better approach is to use the built-in Messages app instead, which lets you block unwanted messages with a few simple taps.

mainEntity.name: How do you know if you're blocked on iMessage?

acceptedAnswer.text: If someone has blocked you on iMessage, you may see green bubbles instead of blue. Likewise, you'll also see the Sent as Text Message label under your messages. For more information, refer to our guide on how to know if someone has blocked you on iMessage.

acceptedAnswer.text: Turn on the Develop menu in Safari Settings → Advanced, then choose Develop → Empty Caches or press Option + Command + E on your Mac.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between clearing history and clearing website data in Safari?

acceptedAnswer.text: Clearing history removes your browsing record but leaves you signed in. Clearing website data deletes cookies, cache, and local storage, which signs you out of sites.

mainEntity.name: Why is the "Remove All" button greyed out in Safari?

acceptedAnswer.text: Open Safari → Settings... → Advanced, and enable "Show Develop menu in menu bar."

mainEntity.name: Is there a way to clear only the cache in Safari on an iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: Safari on iPhone does not include a cache only control. The closest option is Settings → Safari → Advanced → Website Data → Remove All Website Data, which clears cache and cookies while preserving browsing history. Individual site entries can also be removed from this screen.

mainEntity.name: How do I clear cookies for just one website in Safari?

acceptedAnswer.text: Go to Settings → Safari → Advanced → Website Data. Search for the site, swipe left on its entry, then tap Delete. Only that site's cookies and cache are removed without affecting others.

@graph.name: How to Find Hidden Apps in App Library on iPhone
@graph.description: Easily locate hidden apps on your iPhone by using the App Library. Learn how to search, open, and move hidden apps back to your Home Screen for quick access.

step.name: Open the App Library
step.text: Swipe left on your iPhone Home Screen until you reach the App Library.

itemListElement.text: Unlock your iPhone and go to the Home Screen.
Swipe left continuously until you see the App Library screen.

step.name: Search or Open the Hidden Folder
step.text: Scroll to the bottom of the App Library and look for the Hidden folder. Tap on it and authenticate yourself to view all hidden apps, or use the search bar at the top to type in the app’s name.

itemListElement.text: Scroll down to the bottom of the App Library.
Find the folder named Hidden and tap on it.
Authenticate if prompted to unlock the hidden apps.
Alternatively, type the app’s name in the search bar at the top.

step.name: Move the App Back to Home Screen
step.text: Once you find the hidden app, drag it back to your Home Screen so you can access it more easily in the future.

itemListElement.text: Press and hold the app icon you want to unhide.
Drag the app icon to your Home Screen and release it.

@graph.name: How to Find hidden apps on iPhone App Store
@graph.description: Use the App Store’s Search tab to quickly locate a hidden app on your iPhone or iPad, then open it right away.

step.name: Open the App Store
step.text: Launch the App Store on your iPhone or iPad.

itemListElement.text: Unlock your device and go to the Home Screen.
Tap the App Store icon to open it.

step.name: Go to Search
step.text: Use the Search tab to look up the app you want to find.

itemListElement.text: Tap the Search button in the bottom bar.
Tap the search field at the top of the screen.

step.name: Type the app name
step.text: Enter the exact name of the app in the search bar to reveal it in results.

itemListElement.text: Type the app’s name and review the suggestions.
Confirm the correct app in the results list.

step.name: Open the hidden app
step.text: Open the app directly from the App Store results once you find it.

itemListElement.text: Tap the Open button next to the app to launch it.
If you see a download icon, tap it to reinstall, then tap Open.

@graph.name: How to Use Spotlight Search to Find Hidden Apps on iPhone
@graph.description: Quickly locate hidden apps on your iPhone using Spotlight Search. Just swipe down, type the app’s name, and open it directly from the results.

step.name: Open Spotlight Search
step.text: Swipe down from the middle of your Home Screen to bring up Spotlight Search.

itemListElement.text: Unlock your iPhone and go to the Home Screen.
Swipe down from the center of the screen to open Spotlight Search.

step.name: Search for the app
step.text: Type the name of the app you’re trying to find in the Spotlight search bar.

itemListElement.text: Tap on the search bar at the top of the screen.
Enter the app’s name to check if it appears in the results.

step.name: Open the app
step.text: When the app shows up in the search results, tap on it to launch it instantly.

itemListElement.text: Look for the app in the displayed results.
Tap on the app icon or name to open it directly.

@graph.name: How to Use Siri to Find Hidden Apps on iPhone
@graph.description: Use Siri to launch a hidden app in seconds. Invoke Siri with the Side button or by saying Hey Siri, then tell it which app to open.

step.name: Invoke Siri
step.text: Press and hold the Side button on newer iPhones, or press and hold the Home button on older models, to bring up Siri. You can also say Hey Siri if hands free is enabled.

itemListElement.text: Unlock your iPhone and go to the Home Screen.
Press and hold the Side button, or use the Home button on older models, until the Siri animation appears.
If Hey Siri is enabled, say Hey Siri to activate it without pressing a button.

step.name: Ask Siri to open the app
step.text: With Siri listening, say Open followed by the app name to launch it right away.

itemListElement.text: Say Open followed by the exact app name, for example, Open Notes.
If multiple apps match, choose the correct one when Siri asks.
If the app is not installed, Siri may show the App Store so you can download it.

keyPoints.title: Locating Hidden Apps in the
keyPoints.explanation: In iOS 18 and later, hidden apps can be found in the secure 'Hidden' folder accessible through the App Library, requiring authentication to view and unhide.

keyPoints.title: Classic Methods for Finding Hidden Apps
keyPoints.explanation: Apps hidden from the Home Screen or moved across folders can be located using the App Library, Spotlight Search, or manually checking within folders.

keyPoints.title: Checking for System-Level Restrictions
keyPoints.explanation: Apps can be hidden by Screen Time or parental controls; reviewing Allowed Apps and Restrictions settings can reveal hidden or restricted apps.

keyPoints.title: Verifying App Installation Status
keyPoints.explanation: Using the App Store to search for the app can confirm whether it’s still installed or has been removed from the device.

keyPoints.title: Final Troubleshooting Steps
keyPoints.explanation: When all else fails, Siri can help find an app, or resetting the Home Screen layout restores all apps to their original positions, ensuring nothing remains hidden.

title.rendered: Best AirPods Pro 3 Cases Available Right Now in 2026

content.rendered:
Apple has finally upgraded our favourite AirPods Pro and launched the 3rd generation in the Awe dropping event. If you’re planning to grab a pair, you should buy a protective case. Why? Because these cost a fortune, and no one wants to deal with scratches, dents, or a cracked charging case.

To help save time and effort, I have listed the best AirPods Pro 3 cases you can buy right now. Some cases are slim and lightweight, others are bold and funky, and some even come with straps or cleaning tools.

Table of Contents
  • Criteria for Choosing the Best AirPods Pro 3 Cases
  • Top Picks for the AirPods Pro 3 Cases
    • 1. Best Heavy-Duty Protection: ESR Cyber Tough Magnetic Case
    • 2. Best Silicone Case: Maxjoy AirPods Pro 3 Case
    • 3. Best Funky Design: TiMOVO Hard Shell Case
    • 4. Washable AirPods Pro 3 Case: Lerobo Silicone Case
    • 5. AirPods Pro 3 Case with Hand Strap: MATEPROX Silicone Case
  • Buying Tips
  • Protect Your Shiny New AirPods Pro!

Criteria for Choosing the Best AirPods Pro 3 Cases

Before we get to the best options, here’s what we considered while choosing them:

  • Durability: Can it withstand drops, scratches, and general use?
  • Ease of use: It must be easy to use with MagSafe/wireless charging.
  • Design: Funky, sleek, or minimalistic, there’s something for each kind of user.
  • Perfect fit: Made exclusively for AirPods Pro 3.
  • Material: Daily use silicone or heavy-duty rugged protection.
  • Extras: Straps, clips, or even dust plugs for extra convenience.

Top Picks for the AirPods Pro 3 Cases

Below are some of the best AirPods Pro 3 cases right now, each with its own vibe and personality.

1. Best Heavy-Duty Protection: ESR Cyber Tough Magnetic Case

If you want maximum protection for your AirPods Pro 3, the ESR Cyber Tough Magnetic Case is the one to get. Built with military-grade durability and MagSafe compatibility, it’s perfect for commuters without losing convenience.

Pros

  • Heavy-duty build with military-grade protection.
  • Works perfectly with MagSafe chargers.
  • Textured grip to make it difficult to slip out of your hands.
  • Sleek design for a rugged case.

Cons

  • Bulkier than thin silicone cases.
  • Fewer color choices than playful designs.

2. Best Silicone Case: Maxjoy AirPods Pro 3 Case

Sometimes, simple is best. The Maxjoy silicone case is soft, lightweight, and flexible, making it perfect for everyday use. It protects your AirPods Pro 3 from scratches, dust, and small drops while keeping a minimal look.

Pros

  • Soft-touch silicone feels great in the hand
  • Slim and pocket-friendly
  • Affordable price
  • Easy to clean

Cons

  • Not as tough as rugged cases.
  • It may attract lint more than hard-shell options.

3. Best Funky Design: TiMOVO Hard Shell Case

Want your AirPods Pro 3 to stand out? I like the TiMOVO case for its bold style with a gaming console design. It’s a sturdy hard-shell case that adds personality while keeping your earbuds protected.

Pros

  • Eye-catching style
  • Hard shell design resists scratches
  • Comes with a carabiner for easy carrying
  • Secure lock design

Cons

  • Not the slimmest case

4. Washable AirPods Pro 3 Case: Lerobo Silicone Case

The Lerobo case is a great washable option for anyone who wants to keep their case looking fresh. Made from durable silicone material, it can be easily cleaned under running water. Thus, you can take your AirPods anywhere, including to the gym.

Pros

  • Washable and easy to keep clean.
  • Durable silicone absorbs shocks.
  • Available in multiple fun colors.
  • Budget-friendly option.

Cons

  • Basic design, not for those who want a premium look.
  • It can get scratches over time.

5. AirPods Pro 3 Case with Hand Strap: MATEPROX Silicone Case

If you’re always on the move, the MATEPROX Silicone Case with a keychain and hand strap is a lifesaver. No more worrying about dropping your AirPods while jogging, walking, or commuting, the strap keeps them secure and stylish at the same time.

Pros

  • Comes with a comfortable hand strap.
  • Soft silicone build for protection.
  • Easy to carry, perfect for travel or workouts.
  • Multiple color options.

Cons

  • A bit bulkier because of the strap.
  • Not as long-lasting as rugged cases.

Buying Tips

When selecting your AirPods Pro 3 case, remember the following quick tips:

  • Match protection to your lifestyle: Rugged ESR for high usage, silicone Maxjoy/Lerobo for light everyday use, TiMOVO for fashion, and MATEPROX for portability.
  • Ensure compatibility: Make sure it says it fits AirPods Pro 3, not just previous versions.
  • Consider extras: Straps, carabiners, or MagSafe support can make a big difference in daily use.
  • Pick a style you’ll actually love: You’ll be carrying these around every day!

Protect Your Shiny New AirPods Pro!

Your AirPods Pro 3 deserve the best case to match your lifestyle. Whether you’re looking for rugged protection, slim silicone, a funky statement piece or extra convenience with a strap, there’s a perfect choice for everyone in our list.

So, buy your favourite one and let me know which one it is in the comments below!

mainEntity.name: Is there an app to block text messages on iPhones?

acceptedAnswer.text: Several third-party apps, such as Textkiller, Robokiller, etc., can filter and block spam text messages on your iPhone automatically. However, these apps require permission to read all your incoming texts, including OTP, bank alerts, and pretty much everything else, so we wouldn't recommend using them. A better approach is to use the built-in Messages app instead, which lets you block unwanted messages with a few simple taps.

mainEntity.name: How do you know if you're blocked on iMessage?

acceptedAnswer.text: If someone has blocked you on iMessage, you may see green bubbles instead of blue. Likewise, you'll also see the Sent as Text Message label under your messages. For more information, refer to our guide on how to know if someone has blocked you on iMessage.

mainEntity.name: How do I clear the Safari cache without deleting my history on a Mac?

acceptedAnswer.text: Turn on the Develop menu in Safari Settings → Advanced, then choose Develop → Empty Caches or press Option + Command + E on your Mac.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between clearing history and clearing website data in Safari?

acceptedAnswer.text: Clearing history removes your browsing record but leaves you signed in. Clearing website data deletes cookies, cache, and local storage, which signs you out of sites.

mainEntity.name: Why is the "Remove All" button greyed out in Safari?

acceptedAnswer.text: Screen Time is blocking the action. Open System Settings → Screen Time → Content & Privacy, then set Web Content to Unrestricted Access.

acceptedAnswer.text: Open Safari → Settings... → Advanced, and enable "Show Develop menu in menu bar."

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Passwords stored in iCloud Keychain stay intact when you clear Safari data.

mainEntity.name: What happens to my bookmarks when I clear Safari data?

acceptedAnswer.text: Bookmarks are not affected by clearing cache, history, or website data.

title.rendered: How to close apps on iPhone and iPad for smooth performance

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Why you might close apps on iPhone or iPad: It can fix unresponsive apps, reduce background activity, and occasionally free resources for heavy tasks.
  • How app closures affect battery and performance: iOS already manages memory well, but closing apps may save battery and RAM during demanding use.
  • How to close apps on Face ID iPhones: Swipe up and hold to open App Switcher, then swipe up on app previews to close.
  • How to close apps on Home button iPhones: Double-click the Home button, find the app in App Switcher, and swipe up to quit.
  • Best practices for closing apps: You can close multiple apps at once with multi-finger swipes, but avoid overdoing it since iOS handles background apps automatically.

There are times when an app might freeze unexpectedly on your iPhone or iPad. Your only option when this happens is to close it manually. Read on as we explain when you should force close apps, how to close apps on your iPhone or iPad, and how often you should do it.

Why should you close apps on iPhone or iPad?

There are several reasons you may want to close apps on your iPhone and iPad, including performance optimization, improved battery life, reduced background activity, and dealing with frozen apps. Let’s talk about each of them in detail.

Performance optimization

This is one of the most valid reasons to close an app on your iPhone or iPad, but there’s a catch. Although iOS and iPadOS are well-optimized to free up resources on their own, it’s also true that closing unused apps can free up your device’s RAM, which helps your iPhone or iPad perform better when you want to maximize usage, like editing a video or playing AAA titles.

Battery life improvement

Another reason to manually close apps on your iPhone or iPad could come off when you’re low on battery and want to keep background apps to a minimum. For better understanding, when you leave an app open in the background, it runs up several processes behind the curtain, like using location services (GPS), media updates, or updates, which can drain your battery faster.

Tip You can always customize background apps by heading to Settings > General > Background App Refresh.

Troubleshooting unresponsive apps

Unlike the other reasons on this list, this one is perhaps the most valid for closing an app on your iPhone or iPad. While apps are designed to use the device’s resources efficiently, unexpected glitches or bugs can cause them to freeze or become unresponsive, leaving users with no choice but to close them manually. By doing so and then reopening the app, you’re likely to see improved performance.

Prevent unwanted background activity

Although even when you close an app, it continues to send you updates, i.e., notifications, closing apps on your iPhone or iPad may minimize some of the notifications, allowing you to focus on something else. It also helps you save some data if you’re out of home and running low on your cellular data plan.

Tip If you’re seeking ways to minimize notifications, you must check out our detailed guide on how to use Focus mode on an iPhone.

How to close apps on iPhone

Now that you understand why it’s sometimes necessary to close apps on your iPhone, let’s move on to how to do it. First, make sure you know whether you have a recent iPhone model with Face ID such as iPhone 17 Pro or iPhone Air or an earlier model with Touch ID or a home button, so you can easily follow the steps.

On iPhones with Face ID

If you own an iPhone X or later with Face ID, you can close apps like this:

  1. Swipe up from the bottom of the screen to access the App Switcher.
  2. Now, swipe left or right to select the app you want to close.
  3. Swipe up the app to close it.

On iPhones with Home button (or Touch ID)

If you own an earlier model like iPhone 8 or above, or iPhone SE, follow these steps:

  1. Click the Home button twice to bring up the App Switcher.
  2. Swipe to select the app you want to close.
  3. Finally, swipe up the app to close it.

Tip If you accidentally broke your Home button, you can enable Assistive Touch by heading to Settings > Accessibility > Touch > Assistive Touch.

How to close multiple apps at once on iPhone

Unlike Android phones, which have offered the option to close multiple apps at once for years, the iPhone still lacks an official method. But what’s amusing is there is a workaround. Here’s what you need to do:

  1. Access the App Switcher by swiping up from the bottom edge of the screen or double-clicking the Home button depending on your iPhone model.
  2. Swipe up on app previews using multiple fingers to close the apps. (You can easily close three or four apps at once.)

How to close apps on iPad

iOS and iPadOS are so closely tied that most features are similar on both operating systems, so you won’t have difficulty closing apps on your iPad if you read how to close apps on an iPhone. Just follow the right steps depending on your iPad model.

On iPads with Face ID (iPad Pro 3rd Gen or later)

For modern iPads with Face ID, follow these steps to close an app:

  1. Swipe up from the bottom of the screen, regardless of whether you’re using it in portrait or landscape mode, to bring up the App Switcher.
  2. Swipe to spot the app you want to close.
  3. Finally, swipe up the app to close it.

On iPads with Home button

If you’re using an iPad 9th Gen or earlier that comes with a Home button, here’s what you need to do:

  1. Press the Home button twice to bring up the App Switcher.
  2. Swipe to find the app you want to close.
  3. Swipe up the app to close it.

How often should you close apps on iPhone?

Contrary to popular belief, you needn’t always close apps on your iPhone or iPad. We have covered when it’s actually necessary, but if you’re still wondering, the short answer is: not every time necessarily!

Only when necessary

If you’ve been using an Apple device like iPhone or iPad for a while, you would already know how efficiently these devices can manage memory, so there’s no need to always close apps. In fact, you make things worse for your device when you close apps every now and then.

Excessive battery drain

While it’s still a rare phenomenon, some apps can require a lot of processing power, which translates to draining your device’s battery faster than usual. Although these are usually treated and fixed in updates soon by developers, but for the meanwhile, you can keep them closed to save your battery health.

Signing off…

As you’ve seen, closing apps on an iPhone and iPad is pretty straightforward. I hope this article helped you learn how to close apps on your iPhone or iPad when an app stops working unexpectedly. Besides, I hope it also explains in what scenarios you should close an app on your iPhone or iPad and why it’s not a good idea to keep closing apps all the time.

If you want more of these tips or know any better ways to close apps, let us know.

FAQs

What happens when I close an app on my iPhone or iPad?

When you close an app, it goes from the main screen to the background. It might still be running in a paused state, but iOS can also stop it if it needs resources. Closing an app doesn’t free up memory in most cases since iOS manages this automatically.

Will closing apps help free up RAM on my iPhone or iPad?

Yes and no. While iOS and iPadOS are built in a way to efficiently use the device’s memory, sometimes manually closing an app lets the device run a little better. If you’re struggling with low memory, you can restart your device to free up memory.

How do I know if an app is still running in the background on my iPhone or iPad?

To check if an app is running, double-click the Home button or swipe up from the bottom of the screen to access the App Switcher. You’ll see a list of open apps. If an app is there, it’s still running, or you can cross-check from the list of allowed Background Apps.

  • How to restart an iPhone or iPad (All models)
  • How to switch between apps on iPhone and iPad (7 ways)

mainEntity.name: Is there an app to block text messages on iPhones?

acceptedAnswer.text: Several third-party apps, such as Textkiller, Robokiller, etc., can filter and block spam text messages on your iPhone automatically. However, these apps require permission to read all your incoming texts, including OTP, bank alerts, and pretty much everything else, so we wouldn't recommend using them. A better approach is to use the built-in Messages app instead, which lets you block unwanted messages with a few simple taps.

mainEntity.name: How do you know if you're blocked on iMessage?

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between clearing history and clearing website data in Safari?

acceptedAnswer.text: Clearing history removes your browsing record but leaves you signed in. Clearing website data deletes cookies, cache, and local storage, which signs you out of sites.

mainEntity.name: Is there a way to clear only the cache in Safari on an iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: Safari on iPhone does not include a cache only control. The closest option is Settings → Safari → Advanced → Website Data → Remove All Website Data, which clears cache and cookies while preserving browsing history. Individual site entries can also be removed from this screen.

mainEntity.name: How do I clear cookies for just one website in Safari?

acceptedAnswer.text: Go to Settings → Safari → Advanced → Website Data. Search for the site, swipe left on its entry, then tap Delete. Only that site's cookies and cache are removed without affecting others.

mainEntity.name: Will clearing my Safari data fix website loading problems?

acceptedAnswer.text: Often, yes. Clearing data can fix slow pages, login failures, and display glitches. Stale cache and conflicting cookies cause many of these issues, and a reset forces fresh content to load.

mainEntity.name: Is private browsing safer than manually clearing my history?

acceptedAnswer.text: Private Browsing avoids saving history, cookies, and cache during the session, useful for temporary tasks or sensitive research. Manual clearing removes the buildup left from regular browsing and can improve performance.

mainEntity.name: What happens when I close an app on my iPhone or iPad?

acceptedAnswer.text: When you close an app, it goes from the main screen to the background. It might still be running in a paused state, but iOS can also stop it if it needs resources. Closing an app doesn’t free up memory in most cases since iOS manages this automatically.

mainEntity.name: Will closing apps help free up RAM on my iPhone or iPad?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes and no. While iOS and iPadOS are built in a way to efficiently use the device’s memory, sometimes manually closing an app lets the device run a little better. If you’re struggling with low memory, you can restart your device to free up memory.

mainEntity.name: How do I know if an app is still running in the background on my iPhone or iPad?

acceptedAnswer.text: To check if an app is running, double-click the Home button or swipe up from the bottom of the screen to access the App Switcher. You’ll see a list of open apps. If an app is there, it's still running, or you can cross-check from the list of allowed Background Apps.

blockGraphs.question: Will closing apps help free up RAM on my iPhone or iPad?

keyPoints.title: Reasons to close apps on iPhone or iPad
keyPoints.explanation: Closing apps can help optimize performance, improve battery life, troubleshoot unresponsive apps, and reduce background activity.

keyPoints.title: How closing apps affects performance and battery
keyPoints.explanation: While iOS manages resources efficiently, closing unused apps can free RAM for intensive tasks and reduce background processes that drain battery.

keyPoints.title: Steps to close apps on iPhones with Face ID
keyPoints.explanation: Swipe up from the bottom to access the App Switcher, then swipe left or right to find the app and swipe up to close it.

keyPoints.title: Closing apps on older iPhones with Home Button
keyPoints.explanation: Double-click the Home button, swipe to find the app, then swipe up to close it.

keyPoints.title: Handling multiple app closures and best practices
keyPoints.explanation: You can close multiple apps by swiping up on app previews with multiple fingers, but generally, you shouldn't close apps frequently as iOS manages memory well automatically.

aioseo_head_json.author_bio:
"Abhinav Anand is a freelance tech journalist, covering all things Apple at iGeeksBlog. He has reported on smartphones, laptops, and artificial intelligence and tracked tech industry layoffs during this time. His work has been published in prestigious publications such as the Financial Express, Android Headlines, SlashGear, and The Mac Observer."

About Abhinav Anand

  • Abhinav is a regular contributor to iGeeksBlog, where he writes how-to guides, explainers, and features.
  • He primarily uses a MacBook Pro and an iPhone 13 for his daily tasks. Besides, he relies on a 9th Gen iPad when he’s away from his desk and has a few Android phones.
  • Abhinav's love for technology began with reading smartphone reviews for fun. In 2021, he turned his hobby into a career in tech journalism. Now, he's the go-to person for "Which phone/laptop should I buy under X price tag?

Experience

Abhinav Anand has contributed to several major publications, including The Mac Observer, ExtremeTech, SlashGear, KnowTechie, Android Headlines, Financial Express, and Economic Times. He holds a B.A. in Journalism and Mass Communication from Guru Gobind Singh Indraprastha University. He specializes in consumer technology, covering smartphones, Apple products, and PC components.
