title.rendered: How to use the iPhone Action Button like a pro

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • What the Action Button does on iPhone: It’s a customizable button that replaces the old ring/silent switch and can launch tools, settings, or shortcuts.
  • Which iPhones include the Action Button: Available on iPhone 15 Pro series, iPhone 16 lineup (including 16e), iPhone 17 models, and iPhone Air, with workarounds for older devices.
  • How to use the Action Button: Press and hold to activate its assigned function, then press again to turn it off or exit the feature.
  • How to customize the Action Button: In Settings > Action Button, assign tasks such as Silent Mode, Camera, Flashlight, Voice Memos, Shortcuts, or accessibility tools.
  • What functions can be assigned: Options include toggling modes, launching apps, translating, recognizing music, enabling Magnifier, or even setting it to do nothing.

Do you struggle to navigate your iPhone’s menus to access different settings or functions? The Action Button can save you the trouble! This customizable button lets you access various essential functions with just one press, giving you a whole new way to use your iPhone.

In this article, I will go over everything you need to know about the Action Button on your iPhone 17 Pro, including how to set up and use it, and go over the actions you can assign to it. Let’s begin!

What is the Action Button on iPhone?

The Action Button is a physical button on the left side of your iPhone. It replaces the Ring/Silent switch we’ve seen on iPhones all these years and gives you the ability to perform several functions with just a press. For example, you can use the Action Button on your iPhone to open apps, record voice memos, turn on accessibility options, and more.

By default, pressing and holding the Action Button toggles between Silent and Ring modes. However, you can configure how you want to use the Action Button on your iPhone per your needs and preferences. Apple offers a friendly interface in the Settings app, where you can select functions you want to trigger with the Action Button or create shortcuts for advanced operations.

Which iPhones have an Action Button?

You can take advantage of the Action Button on the following iPhone models:

  • iPhone 15 Pro
  • iPhone 15 Pro Max
  • iPhone 16
  • iPhone 16 Plus
  • iPhone 16 Pro
  • iPhone 16 Pro Max
  • iPhone 16e
  • iPhone 17
  • iPhone 17 Pro
  • iPhone 17 Pro Max
  • iPhone Air

Older models don’t have the Action Button. However, you can use a workaround to get the Action Button on any iPhone model.

How to use Action Button on iPhone

With the basics out of the way, let’s see how to use the Action Button to make your everyday tasks simpler and faster!

  1. Locate the Action Button. It’s on the left side of your iPhone above the volume buttons. 
  2. Press and hold the Action Button once to trigger its current action. If it’s set to Silent Mode, you’ll feel a haptic vibration, and the phone will switch between Ring and Silent modes. 
  3. Depending on the action in use, you may press the Action Button again to toggle off the function. For example, you can turn off the Flashlight, stop recording a voice memo, turn off the active Focus mode, and stop translation. 

How to customize Action Button on iPhone

Customizing the Action Button to perform another action is easy, and you can set it to perform a variety of tasks. Here’s how:

  1. Open the Settings app on your iPhone.
  2. Scroll down and select Action Button.
  3. You’ll see a list of available actions, such as Silent Mode, Camera, Flashlight, Voice Memo, Accessibility features, and more. Swipe to any action to select it or choose Shortcut to link it to a specific app or function you’ve created.

  4. Actions such as Focus, Accessibility, etc., offer a sub-menu. Tap the menu icon below to see the available options. If you don’t assign an action here, pressing the Action Button does nothing.
  5. Once selected, press the Action Button anytime, and it will perform the assigned action instantly.
Quick tip You can also see the current state of the Action Button by glancing at Dynamic Island, which will show icons representing its current setting.

What actions can you assign Action Button?

Similar to the Apple Watch Ultra’s Action Button, your iPhone’s Action Button can perform a range of actions. Here are all the actions available for the Action Button:

  • Silent Mode: The default Action Button action that toggles between Ring and Silent modes.
  • Focus: Lets you quickly activate your preferred Focus filter.
  • Camera: Quickly launches the Camera app in your preferred mode, such as Photo, Selfie, Video, Portrait, and Portrait Selfie.
  • Torch: Lets you customize the Action Button to turn on or off the Flashlight with a press.
  • Voice Memo: Allows you to quickly capture your idea by starting a quick voice memo recording with a press of the Action Button.
  • Recognize music: Get Shazam to check what music is playing nearby or on your iPhone.
  • Translate: Get real-time translations of phrases or conversation with someone to your default language.
  • Magnifier: While going through small texts, you may launch Magnifier via the Action Button.
  • Controls: Access your favorite Control Center controls with the press of the Action Button.
  • Shortcut: The Action Button on iPhone can adapt your custom Shortcuts, such as sending a message or launching an app, among others.
  • Accessibility: You can use preferred accessibility tools, including VoiceOver, Zoom, AssistiveTouch, and others, via the Action Button.
  • No Action: It’s basically for those who wish to do nothing.

In the Action Button settings, simply swipe to the action you want to assign, select the option from the sub-menu if required, and you’re good to go. I will explain how to customize the Action button to perform specific tasks on your iPhone. 

Set a Focus 

  1. Swipe left to the Focus option. 
  1. Tap the drop-down menu and select the Focus you want to trigger with the Action Button from the available options, such as Do Not Disturb, Personal, Work, Sleep, and more.

Launch Camera using Action Button 

The iPhone 16 and iPhone 17 models feature a Camera Control button, so this action is only useful for iPhone 15 Pro and Pro Max users. 

  1. Slide to the third option, Camera. 
  1. As the Camera option appears, tap the context menu and select the mode in which you want to open the Camera app. You can choose between Photo, Selfie, Video, Portrait, and Portrait Selfie.

Assign accessibility features to Action Button

Apple has been hell-bent on making lives easier with Accessibility add-ons. And now, you can assign accessibility features to your iPhone’s Action Button.

  1. Slide left to the Accessibility option.
  2. Tap the Choose a Feature option.
  3. Select a feature according to your needs from the following menus:
    • Vision: This menu is dedicated to visually impaired users. It includes options such as Vehicle Motion Cues, Reduce White Points, etc.
    • Motor: Simplifies the in-device controls. You can access Voice Control, Apple Watch Mirroring, and similar features here.
    • Hearing: For those who find it challenging to hear, select accessibility options such as Music Haptics, Conversation Boost, etc.
    • General: Features pretty common yet useful like Guided Access and Live Speech are accessible under this menu.

Tip By assigning Live Recognition to the Action Button, you can make the most of Point and Speak feature. This uses the LiDAR sensors to detect nearby text, people, doors, and scenes and provide users with audio or haptic feedback.

Add controls to Action Button

With iOS 18, you can customize your Control Center and access controls from various apps on your iPhone. To make the upgrade more useful, you can choose a task from more than 50 controls for the Action Button.

  1. Swipe to the Controls screen.
  2. Tap on Choose a Control.
  3. It will open the list of controls under categories. Scroll and select a control.

You can open the scanner, turn on Cellular Data, launch the Calculator app, enable Dark Mode, ping your Apple Watch, and more with these controls.

Trigger shortcuts using the Action Button

The Action Button becomes even more powerful when paired with Apple’s Shortcuts app, as this allows you to create personalized automation or multi-step actions that run with just one press. So, even if the Settings app doesn’t have your preferred action built-in, you can still access it using the button.

Here’s how you can set Shortcuts on the Action Button:

  1. Swipe to the Shortcuts screen and tap on Choose a Shortcut.
  2. It will open the shortcuts gallery. Scroll down or search for the shortcut you want to assign. If you don’t find the specific one, you may need to set it up first.

For example, I wanted to launch the Calendar app quickly. So, I selected the Open App action and chose the Calendar app. Now, whenever I press the Action Button, it takes me to the Calendar app. If you take too many screenshots, you may select the Save to Photo Album shortcut.

For more complex actions, you may install shortcuts from third-party developers or create them yourself. Simply go to the Shortcuts app, tap on the plus button, and add the action.

Example of shortcuts for the Action Button:

  • Ask ChatGPT: If you have ChatGPT installed on your iPhone, you can set its shortcut to quickly ask questions and get responses on the go. Get the Start Voice Conversation with ChatGPT shortcut, and you are good to go.
  • Multi-option menu: Design a shortcut that will allow you to perform several actions when the Action Button is pressed, for instance, send a message, launch an app or check the weather. Simply create a folder in the Shortcut app and add your favorite shortcuts to that folder. Then, on the Action Button Settings, select the Show Folder shortcut and assign the folder you created.

Signing off…

The Action Button on the iPhone is a fantastic addition that brings customization and convenience to a whole new level. Be it just silencing the phone or running the shortcuts, the Action Button is bound to enhance the iPhone experience greatly.

What do you think of this new button? Let us know your thoughts in the comments below.

FAQ

Is the iPhone Action Button water-resistant?

Yes, the Action Button is designed to be water-resistant, just like the rest of the device. So, it should function without issues in wet or damp conditions.

Read more:

  • Best iOS 18 tips and tricks
  • iPhone 16 vs. iPhone 15

mainEntity.name: Is there an app to block text messages on iPhones?

acceptedAnswer.text: Several third-party apps, such as Textkiller, Robokiller, etc., can filter and block spam text messages on your iPhone automatically. However, these apps require permission to read all your incoming texts, including OTP, bank alerts, and pretty much everything else, so we wouldn't recommend using them. A better approach is to use the built-in Messages app instead, which lets you block unwanted messages with a few simple taps.

mainEntity.name: How do you know if you're blocked on iMessage?

acceptedAnswer.text: If someone has blocked you on iMessage, you may see green bubbles instead of blue. Likewise, you'll also see the Sent as Text Message label under your messages. For more information, refer to our guide on how to know if someone has blocked you on iMessage.

mainEntity.name: Is there a way to clear only the cache in Safari on an iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: Safari on iPhone does not include a cache only control. The closest option is Settings → Safari → Advanced → Website Data → Remove All Website Data, which clears cache and cookies while preserving browsing history. Individual site entries can also be removed from this screen.

blockGraphs.question: Is the iPhone Action Button water-resistant?
blockGraphs.answer: Yes, the Action Button is designed to be water-resistant, just like the rest of the device. So, it should function without issues in wet or damp conditions.

keyPoints.title: What is the Action Button on iPhone?
keyPoints.explanation: The Action Button is a customizable physical button on the left side of the iPhone, replacing the traditional ring/silent switch, enabling access to various functions with a press.

keyPoints.title: Which iPhones have an Action Button?
keyPoints.explanation: The Action Button is available on iPhone 15 Pro, 15 Pro Max, 16, 16 Plus, 16 Pro, 16 Pro Max, 16e, 17, 17 Pro, 17 Pro Max, and iPhone Air models, with workarounds possible for older models.

keyPoints.title: How to use the Action Button on iPhone
keyPoints.explanation: Locate the button, press and hold to trigger its assigned action such as toggling silent mode, and press again to toggle off the function.

keyPoints.title: How to customize the Action Button
keyPoints.explanation: Go to Settings > Action Button, select from available actions like Silent Mode, Camera, or create shortcuts, then assign them to suit your needs.

keyPoints.title: What actions can be assigned to the Action Button?
keyPoints.explanation: Actions include toggling silent mode, activating Focus, launching Camera, turning on flashlight, starting voice memos, recognizing music, translating, using Magnifier, controlling settings, shortcuts, accessibility features, or doing nothing.

title.rendered: Camera Control not working on iPhone 17? Try these fixes

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Why Camera Control may stop working on iPhone: Issues often stem from software glitches, incorrect gestures, outdated iOS, disabled settings, or even hardware interference.
  • Restarting helps clear temporary bugs: A quick restart can refresh system processes and often restores Camera Control responsiveness without further troubleshooting.
  • Gestures must be performed correctly: Using the wrong motion or missing timing can prevent Camera Control from activating, even if the feature is enabled.
  • Updating iOS resolves hidden bugs: Installing the latest update can fix software issues and restore smooth Camera Control performance.
  • Check Camera Control settings and accessibility features: Make sure the feature is turned on and not overridden by accessibility options or third-party cases.

A distinctive attribute of the iPhone 16 and iPhone 17 series is the Camera Control button, which lets you quickly open the Camera app and access its various controls. However, many iPhone 16 and 17 users have reported issues with the Camera Control not working as expected.

If it is happening with you, too, you are at the right place. This guide explains why this happens and the steps you can take to troubleshoot it when Camera Control is not working on your iPhone.

Why is Camera Control not working on my iPhone 17?

Here are some common reasons why the Camera Control button may not be working on your iPhone 17 or iPhone Air:

  • Software bugs or glitches: Temporary system issues may sometimes prevent the Camera Control from responding to your gestures.
  • Incorrect gestures: You need to use specific gestures accurately to access Camera Control’s functions. Failing to do so could cause the button to not work as expected.
  • Interference from accessories: A thick or non-compatible case on your iPhone may prevent you from accessing and performing gestures on the button properly.
  • Disabled setting: If the Camera Control feature is disabled on your iPhone, it will not respond to any gestures.
  • Outdated iOS version: A bug in an older iOS version could also break the button’s functionality.
  • Hardware damage: If the Camera Control button is physically damaged, it will simply not work. The only solution is to take it to an Apple Store or an authorized service provider for repair.

6 ways to fix iPhone 17’s Camera Control when it is not working

Here are a few proven solutions you can try to fix the Camera Control on your iPhone 17.

1. Restart your iPhone

A simple restart can often resolve minor software glitches, including when the Camera Control button becomes unresponsive. Start with a soft restart, and if it does not help, try force restarting your iPhone.

  • To soft restart your iPhone: Press and hold the Side and Volume Down buttons, then drag the Slide to Power Off button to the right. Wait a few seconds and turn the iPhone back on.
  • To force restart your iPhone: Press and release the Volume Up button, do the same with the Volume Down, and press and hold the Side button until the Apple logo appears on the screen.

2. Make sure you use the right gestures

Camera Control relies on multiple gestures. If isn’t responding when you perform one of the gestures, it could be because you are not using the correct gesture. In case you just got an iPhone 16 and are unsure about these gestures, check out our in-depth guide on how to use the Camera Control button on iPhone 16.

If you are performing the correct gestures, but the Camera Control is not responding as expected, move to the next solution.

3. Update iOS

Apple frequently releases iOS updates to fix bugs and improve system performance. If it is a widespread software issue, Apple will surely address it and fix the Camera Control button. So, check if there’s an update available and install it:

  1. Go to Settings > General > Software Update.
  2. If an update is available, tap Update Now.

  3. Now, enter your iPhone passcode and tap Agree to start the installation.
  4. Restart your iPhone after updating to see if the issue is resolved.

3. Take off the case from your iPhone

Some bulky or non-Apple-certified cases may prevent the Camera Control button from detecting gestures correctly. In addition, dirt or dust can sometimes also accumulate near the button, affecting its functionality.

Some users in the Apple Community have said that removing their iPhone 16 from the case made Camera Control responsive again. So, if your Camera Control button is not responding or misbehaving, just remove your iPhone case, and see if it helps.

If the problem is resolved, try a slimmer or Apple-certified case. Also, while you are at it, take a microfiber cloth and clean the button gently.

Tip Make sure your fingers are clean and dry for your touches to register correctly.

4. Check the Camera Control settings

If you are not able to access your iPhone camera with a single click, it could be due to some misconfigured settings. Some users in the community have also mentioned that they had to wake up their iPhone screen for the Camera Control button to work. Whatever the case, be sure to check your iPhone’s Camera Control settings:

  1. Go to Settings > Camera and tap Camera Control.
  2. Now, ensure Single Click is selected. Also, choose Camera as the app to launch.

  3. Go back and tap Display & Brightness.
  4. Go to the Camera Control section and toggle off Require Screen On.

Tip On my iPhone, Single Click was already set, and the Camera Control was inconsistent to the clicks. So, I selected Double Click, forced quit the Settings app, and set it to Single Click again.

5. Ensure Accessibility settings are enabled

The Accessibility settings on your iPhone 17 include various features that can affect how the Camera Control button functions. If the button is not responding or working properly, certain touch-related settings may be interfering with its operation.

  1. Go to Settings > Accessibility.
  2. Under Physical and Motor, select Camera Control.
  3. Ensure Camera Control option is enabled.

  4. Now, set Light-Press Force to Default, Double Light-Press Speed to Slow, and Double Click Speed to Default.

6. Reset your iPhone settings

If none of the above solutions work, resetting all settings may help. When you reset your iPhone, it will reset all your system preferences, which, in turn, will remove any misconfigured settings that could be the culprit. And don’t worry! Your data will not be deleted.

  1. Go to Settings > General > Transfer or Reset iPhone > Reset.
  2. Select Reset All Settings.

  3. Enter your passcode and tap Reset All Settings.
  4. Restart your iPhone and check if the Camera Control button is working.

Signing off

Camera Control is a useful feature, but it can be really frustrating when it stops working. But by following the troubleshooting steps above, you should be able to fix the issue and get the button working again.

If the problem persists and there are signs of physical damage, it is best to make a Genius Bar appointment and get professional assistance.

Did any of these solutions work for you? Let us know in the comments!

  • How to Use the New Center Stage Front Camera on iPhone 17
  • Is the iPhone 16e the end of the iPhone SE series?

mainEntity.name: Is there an app to block text messages on iPhones?

acceptedAnswer.text: Several third-party apps, such as Textkiller, Robokiller, etc., can filter and block spam text messages on your iPhone automatically. However, these apps require permission to read all your incoming texts, including OTP, bank alerts, and pretty much everything else, so we wouldn't recommend using them. A better approach is to use the built-in Messages app instead, which lets you block unwanted messages with a few simple taps.

mainEntity.name: How do you know if you're blocked on iMessage?

acceptedAnswer.text: If someone has blocked you on iMessage, you may see green bubbles instead of blue. Likewise, you'll also see the Sent as Text Message label under your messages. For more information, refer to our guide on how to know if someone has blocked you on iMessage.

title.rendered: Best iPhone Air Cases You Can Buy: Slim, Rugged & Clear

content.rendered:
Apple’s all-new iPhone Air has finally landed, and it’s already making waves. With its ultra-thin titanium frame, slim bezels, and lightweight design, it feels futuristic and premium. But with Ceramic Shield glass on both sides, it’s still vulnerable to drops and scratches.

That’s where a good case comes in. The right one not only protects your iPhone but also makes it more comfortable to hold. Below, I’ve rounded up the best iPhone Air cases available right now, whether you want slim and minimal, rugged and protective, MagSafe-ready, or clear to show off that gorgeous design.

Table of Contents
  • What to Look for in an iPhone Air Case
  • Top iPhone Air Cases (Editor's Picks)
  • Best MagSafe Cases for iPhone Air
  • Best Slim and Minimalist iPhone Air Cases
  • Best Rugged Cases for Maximum Protection
  • Best Clear Cases to Show Off Your iPhone Air
  • Final Thoughts: Which Case is Right for You?

What to Look for in an iPhone Air Case

Before we dive into picks, here are the essentials to keep in mind when shopping for a case:

  • Compatibility: Make sure it’s designed specifically for the iPhone Air’s dimensions and button placements.
  • Protection level: Raised bezels, shock-absorbing corners, and drop protection make a big difference.
  • Materials: Choose silicone, leather, polycarbonate, or a hybrid that balances durability and aesthetics.
  • MagSafe Compatibility: If you use wireless chargers or MagSafe accessories, make sure your case supports them. 
  • Grip & style: Matte finishes for non-slip use, glossy for sleek looks, textured for extra hold.
  • Bulk vs. Slim: Slim cases, like Spigen Liquid Air, retain iPhone Air’s lightweight feel, while bulkier ones give you maximum protection. 
  • Price Range: Premium cases (like Apple, Mous) can cost a lot more, but budget-friendly options often deliver surprisingly good protection too. 

With this in mind, you’re set to shop smart. Now, let’s dive into the goodies. 

Top iPhone Air Cases (Editor’s Picks)

These three options strike the perfect balance of design, durability, and everyday usability:

  1. Apple iPhone Air Bumper Case: The official Apple case is sleek, perfectly fitted, and provides great edge protection without hiding the back. You can also attach the new Crossbody Stap. It’s minimal but feels premium. 
  2. Spigen Thin Fit MagFit: A fan favorite for years, it provides military-grade drop protection without adding bulk thanks to the Air Cushion technology. Plus, a thin TPU layer covers the new camera plateau. 
  3. Ringke Onyx for iPhone Air: I liked this case due to its distinct matte textured surface that is easy to clean, anti-fingerprint, and smudge-resistant. It’s lightweight, flexible, and offers solid everyday protection.  

Best MagSafe Cases for iPhone Air

MagSafe is not only for charging, but it also allows you to use a number of accessories such as wallets, stands, and car mounts. If you’re completely committed to Apple’s magnetic ecosystem, these are your top picks:

  1. Smartish Gripmunk Slim case: Known for quirky designs, 6ft drop protection, and great grip with built-in finger grooves, Smartish offers MagSafe compatibility in a slim, fun package. 
  2. TORRO Leather iPhone Air Case: For a touch of class, TORRO’s genuine cowhide leather case looks amazing, ages beautifully, and works seamlessly with MagSafe. 
  3. Mous Carbon Fiber Case: This iPhone Air case is stylish yet anti-scratch, shockproof, and protective thanks to Mous’ AiroShock corners and rigid shell. With built-in magnet arrays, you can enjoy MagSafe functionality. 

Best Slim and Minimalist iPhone Air Cases

Love the featherweight feel of the Air? These keep things light while offering basic protection:

  1. TORRAS SlimFit Case: Only 0.77mm ultra-thin case with a weight of 18g provides just enough drop and scratch protection. It’s like you’re holding only your iPhone Air. Plus, its 38 built-in magnets enable fast MagSafe charging. 
  2. Pitaka Ultra-Slim Case: Made from silky-smooth, aerospace-grade aramid fiber, Pitaka’s case is only 0.99mm thin yet surprisingly strong. At just 20g, it looks great. 
  3. JETech Slim Case: Budget-friendly, 1.2mm thin, ultra-lightweight, and minimal, it’s ideal if you just want a simple shield against everyday wear. I liked its scratch and smudge-proof matte texture.  

Best Rugged Cases for Maximum Protection

Need something heavy-duty? These rugged options are built to survive tough drops and outdoor use:

  1. ESR Cyber Tough Case with Stand: Three-layer structure with Air Guard corners and 7x military-grade drop tested from 23ft, ESR’s case is insanely durable. Its Stash Stand lets you use your phone hands-free. 
  2. SUPCASE Unicorn Beetle Grip Case: Known for 20ft mil-grade drop protection, SUPCASE adds a grippy texture and even a built-in kickstand for convenience. 
  3. FNTCASE Protective Case: Get 360° protection for your iPhone Air with this case and screen protector bundle. Rugged and textured, it offers heavy-duty protection at a budget. 

Best Clear Cases to Show Off Your iPhone Air

Want protection without hiding Apple’s sleek design? Go with these transparent picks:

  1. Apple Clear Case: The official iPhone Air clear case is only 0.9mm thin, fits like a glove, supports MagSafe, and is light frosted to resist yellowing better than cheaper options. 
  2. Spigen Ultra Hybrid MagFit Case: It’s my personal favorite. A clear case with reinforced bumpers and DuraClear blue resin coating, providing transparency with extra protection. 
  3. ESR Classic Hybrid Case: With 11-ft mil-grade drop protection, slim profile, built-in magnets, and a kickstand, ESR’s hybrid case is a no-brainer for most folks.
  4. Rokform Crystal Case: If you utilize bike or car mounts, this case features a twist-lock system for convenient snapping. Along with built-in magnets and six-sided military-grade protection, it keeps your phone secure.

Final Thoughts: Which Case is Right for You? 

The right case depends on your lifestyle:

  • If you want Apple-level perfection, stick with the official cases. 
  • If you love slim and light, go for TORRAS or Spigen Thin Fit. 
  • If you’re accident-prone, rugged picks like SUPCASE or ESR will give you peace of mind. 
  • And if you just want to show off that beautiful iPhone Air design, grab a clear case. 

Whatever you choose, remember that the right case balances protection, style, and budget. Your iPhone Air’s too cool to go naked, so pop on a case today and keep adventuring worry-free.

Got a fave or question? Drop a comment, I’d love to hear!  

Don’t miss these related reads:

  • Best iPhone 17 Cases You Can Buy Right Now
  • Best Screen Protectors for iPhone Air
  • Best iPhone Air Accessories You Should Buy

mainEntity.name: Is there an app to block text messages on iPhones?

acceptedAnswer.text: Several third-party apps, such as Textkiller, Robokiller, etc., can filter and block spam text messages on your iPhone automatically. However, these apps require permission to read all your incoming texts, including OTP, bank alerts, and pretty much everything else, so we wouldn't recommend using them. A better approach is to use the built-in Messages app instead, which lets you block unwanted messages with a few simple taps.

mainEntity.name: What happens when I close an app on my iPhone or iPad?

acceptedAnswer.text: When you close an app, it goes from the main screen to the background. It might still be running in a paused state, but iOS can also stop it if it needs resources. Closing an app doesn’t free up memory in most cases since iOS manages this automatically.

@graph.name: Apple iPhone Air Bumper Case
@graph.description: The official Apple case is sleek, perfectly fitted, and provides great edge protection without hiding the back. You can also attach the new Crossbody Stap. It’s minimal but feels premium.

@graph.name: Spigen Thin Fit MagFit iPhone Air Case
@graph.description: A fan favorite for years, it provides military-grade drop protection without adding bulk thanks to the Air Cushion technology. Plus, a thin TPU layer covers the new camera plateau.

@graph.name: Ringke Onyx for iPhone Air Case
@graph.description: I liked this case due to its distinct matte textured surface that is easy to clean, anti-fingerprint, and smudge-resistant. It’s lightweight, flexible, and offers solid everyday protection.

@graph.name: Smartish® iPhone Air MagSafe Case
@graph.description: Known for quirky designs, 6ft drop protection, and great grip with built-in finger grooves, Smartish offers MagSafe compatibility in a slim, fun package.

@graph.name: TORRO Leather iPhone Air Case
@graph.description: For a touch of class, TORRO’s genuine cowhide leather case looks amazing, ages beautifully, and works seamlessly with MagSafe.

@graph.name: Mous Carbon Fiber iPhone Air Case
@graph.description: This iPhone Air case is stylish yet anti-scratch, shockproof, and protective thanks to Mous’ AiroShock corners and rigid shell. With built-in magnet arrays, you can enjoy MagSafe functionality.

@graph.name: TORRAS Magnetic Slim Fit for iPhone Air Case
@graph.description: Only 0.77mm ultra-thin case with 18g weight provides just enough drop and scratch protection. It’s like you’re holding your iPhone Air only. Plus, its 38 built-in magnets enable fast MagSafe charging.

@graph.name: JETech Slim Case for iPhone Air
@graph.description: Budget-friendly, 1.2mm thin, ultra-lightweight, and minimal, it’s ideal if you just want a simple shield against everyday wear. I liked its scratch and smudge-proof matte texture.

@graph.name: ESR Cyber Tough Case with Stand
@graph.description: Three-layer structure with Air Guard corners and 7x military-grade drop tested from 23ft, ESR’s case is insanely durable. Its Stash Stand lets you use your phone hands-free.

@graph.name: Pitaka Ultra-Slim Case
@graph.description: Made from silky-smooth aerospace-grade aramid fiber, Pitaka’s case is only 0.99mm thin but still surprisingly strong. With just 20g of weight, it looks great.

@graph.name: SUPCASE for iPhone Air Case with Kickstand
@graph.description: Known for 20ft mil-grade drop protection, SUPCASE adds a grippy texture and even a built-in kickstand for convenience.

@graph.name: FNTCASE for iPhone Air Phone Case
@graph.description: Get 360° protection for your iPhone Air with this case and screen protector bundle. Rugged and textured, it offers heavy-duty protection at a budget.

@graph.name: Apple iPhone Air Case with MagSafe
@graph.description: The official iPhone Air clear case is only 0.9mm thin, fits like a glove, supports MagSafe, and is light frosted to resist yellowing better than cheaper options.

@graph.name: Spigen Ultra Hybrid MagFit Case
@graph.description: It’s my personal favorite. A clear case with reinforced bumpers and DuraClear blue resin coating, providing transparency with extra protection.

@graph.name: ESR for iPhone Air Classic Hybrid Case
@graph.description: With 11-ft mil-grade drop protection, slim profile, built-in magnets, and a kickstand, ESR’s hybrid case is a no-brainer for most folks.

@graph.name: Rokform iPhone 17 Air Crystal Case
@graph.description: If you utilize bike or car mounts, this case features a twist-lock system for convenient snapping. Along with built-in magnets and six-sided military-grade protection, it keeps your phone secure.

title.rendered: How to Enter DFU Mode on iPhone? – Detailed Guide

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • DFU mode explained on iPhone and iPad: It bypasses iOS and connects directly with Finder or iTunes for advanced troubleshooting and firmware-related fixes.
  • When DFU mode is necessary: Use it for severe problems like boot loops, failed updates, or downgrading iOS when Recovery Mode or restarts don’t help.
  • DFU vs Recovery Mode differences: DFU keeps the screen black with deeper firmware access, while Recovery Mode shows a computer or cable icon.
  • Precautions before entering DFU mode: Back up your data, confirm iOS signing status, avoid using damaged devices, and ensure reliable cables and internet.
  • How to enter DFU mode correctly: Perform device-specific button presses, and a black screen confirms successful entry into DFU mode.

If you’ve ever felt lost or frustrated by DFU mode, I totally understand—you’re not alone, and I’m here to help. When your iPhone runs into those stubborn software issues that a simple restart or even Recovery Mode can’t fix, DFU mode (Device Firmware Update) is your ultimate solution.

In this guide, I’ll walk you through everything you need to know about DFU mode and how to enter it on any iPhone or iPad model—with expert timing tips, troubleshooting advice, and clear, friendly guidance to help you succeed, even if it’s your very first time.

What is DFU Mode on iPhone, and When Should You Use It?

DFU mode, which stands for Device Firmware Update, is like hitting the reset button on a deeper level for your iPhone or iPad. It’s the most thorough way to restore your device because it lets your iPhone connect to Finder or iTunes without loading iOS or even the bootloader.

Basically, it gives your device a clean slate.

You’d only need to use DFU mode in more serious situations, such as:

  • Your iPhone is stuck on the Apple logo or keeps restarting in a loop
  • Updates or restores keep failing, even in Recovery Mode
  • You want to downgrade to an older iOS version (as long as Apple is still signing it)
  • Your device is completely unresponsive or isn’t showing up when you connect it to your computer
Pro Tip: DFU mode is a powerful option, but it should only be used when other troubleshooting steps haven’t worked. For most users, Recovery Mode is sufficient.

DFU Mode vs. Recovery Mode: What’s the Difference?

  • How to tell which mode you’re in:
    • DFU Mode: The screen remains black, and the device seems to be “off.” However, when you connect it to your computer, the computer is still able to detect the device, allowing you to attempt a restore through recovery tools or software.
    • Recovery Mode: The screen displays an icon that looks like a cable or a computer, which typically indicates that the device is searching for a connection or input source. This may mean that the monitor is not receiving a signal from the computer or connected device.

Necessary Precautions Before Using DFU Mode

  1. Back up your data: DFU mode wipes everything from your device — your photos, apps, messages, and settings. So before you do anything, make sure to back up your iPhone or iPad. You don’t want to lose important stuff by accident.
  2. Check Firmware availability: You can only install iOS versions that Apple is still signing. If you try to install an older version that’s no longer allowed, you’ll get an error. Always check which iOS versions are currently available before you start.
  3. Be careful with Water damage: If your device has been exposed to water, don’t try DFU mode on your own. It could make things worse or even damage your phone further. It’s safer to take it to a professional repair technician first.
  4. Use the right tools: Stick to an Apple-certified cable and make sure Finder or iTunes is up to date. Cheap cables or outdated software can cause connection problems or failed restores.
  5. Have a stable internet connection: If your internet drops during the restore, your device might exit DFU mode, and you’ll have to start over. A good, steady connection helps avoid frustrating interruptions.
  6. Be patient: Getting into DFU mode isn’t always easy. It might take a few tries, even if you’ve done it before. That doesn’t mean your iPhone is broken — it’s just a tricky process. Take your time and carefully follow each step.

How to Identify Your iPhone or iPad Model

Not sure which iPhone or iPad you have? No problem. Check out our guide for detailed instructions, or look for simple clues like whether your device has a Home button. Once you know your model, follow the step-by-step instructions made for your specific device.

How to Put iPhone into DFU Mode Entry: Step-by-Step for Every Model

Learn how to enter DFU mode on iPhone Air, iPhone 17, 16e, 16, 15, 14, 13, 12, 11, XS, XR, iPhone 8, SE 2020/2022, iPhone 7 series, older iPhones like 6s, and iPads with Face ID or Home Button.

For iPhone 8 and Newer (iPhone Air)

  1. Use an Apple-certified cable to connect your iPhone to your Mac or Windows Computer.
  2. Open Finder (if you have macOS Catalina or newer) or iTunes (if you have an older Mac or Windows PC).
  3. Quickly press and let go of the Volume Up button.
  4. Quickly press and let go of the Volume Down button.
  5. Press and hold the Side (Power) button until the screen goes black.
  6. When the screen turns black, keep holding the Side button and also press and hold the Volume Down button for 5 seconds.
  7. After 5 seconds, let go of the Side button but keep holding the Volume Down button for another 10 seconds.
  8. If the screen remains black and Finder or iTunes indicates that it has found an iPhone in recovery mode, your phone is now in DFU mode.
  9. Timing Tip: If you see the Apple logo, you hold the Side button too long. Try again and release it a little sooner.

For iPhone 7 and 7 Plus

  1. Connect your iPhone to your computer.
  2. Open Finder or iTunes.
  3. Press and hold both the Side (Power) button and the Volume Down button for 8 to 10 seconds.
  4. Release the Side button, but keep holding the Volume Down button for about 5 seconds.
  5. The screen should stay black, and Finder or iTunes will detect your device.

For iPhone 6s, 6s Plus, or Earlier (and iPads with Home Button)

  1. Plug your device into your computer.
  2. Open Finder or iTunes.
  3. Hold down both the Home button and the Top (or Side) Power button for 10 seconds.
  4. Let go of the Power button, but keep holding the Home button for 5 more seconds.
  5. If the screen is still black and Finder or iTunes finds your device, you are in DFU mode.

For iPads with Face ID

  1. Connect your iPad to your computer.
  2. Open Finder or iTunes.
  3. Press and hold the Top (Power) button for three seconds.
  4. Keep holding the Top button, then press and hold the Volume Down button as well. Hold both for 10 seconds.
  5. Release the Top button, but keep holding the Volume Down button for five more seconds.
  6. If the screen stays black and Finder/iTunes detects your iPad, you’re in DFU mode.

DFU Mode Success Checklist

The screen should remain black. If you see a logo or picture, try again. Finder or iTunes may show “recovery mode” even when you are in DFU mode—this is normal as long as your screen stays black.

What to Do After Entering DFU Mode on iPhone

  1. Finder or iTunes will display a message saying your device is in “recovery mode.”
  2. Even in DFU mode, the pop-up may say “recovery mode.” As long as your device’s screen is black, you’re in DFU mode.
  3. Click OK in the pop-up, then select Restore iPhone(or Restore iPad).
  4. Your computer will download the latest available iOS version and restore your device. This may take some time.
  5. Important: Restoring in DFU mode erases all data and settings. Only backups made with the same or earlier iOS version can be restored—backups from a newer iOS version will not work.
Tip: Ensure your internet connection is stable during this process. If the download is interrupted, your device may exit DFU mode, and you’ll need to start over.

How to Exit DFU Mode

Exiting DFU mode is safe and straightforward; no special software or tools are required. Just follow the steps below for your device model to restart your iPhone or iPad and return to normal operation.

  • For iPhone 8 or newer, SE 2020/2022, and iPads with Face ID:
    • Quickly press and release the Volume Up button.
    • Quickly press and release the Volume Down button.
    • Press and hold the Side (or Top) button until you see the Apple logo.
  • For iPhone 7 and 7 Plus:
    • Press and hold both the Side (Power) button and the Volume Down button until the Apple logo appears.
  • For iPhone 6s or earlier and iPads with Home Button:
    • Press and hold both the Home button and the Side (or Top) Power button until the Apple logo appears.
What to Expect: Your device should restart and display the Apple logo if it doesn’t, check your cable and try the steps again.

When to Seek Professional Help

If DFU mode does not resolve your issue, or your phone has been water-damaged or subjected to physical harm, it’s best to contact Apple or an authorized service provider. They are trained to diagnose and fix your phone safely. Attempting to do it yourself can result in further complications or even nullify your guarantee. By seeking professional service, your phone has the optimal chance of being restored correctly.

Questions or Feedback?

Still, have questions or need help? Feel free to drop a comment below—we’re always here to help you make the most of your Apple devices! We love hearing from you and supporting your journey.

You’ve totally got this! With a bit of patience and the right steps, you’ll be a pro at using DFU mode on any iPhone or iPad. And if you ever get stuck, just reach out—we’ve all been there, and we’re more than happy to lend a hand.

FAQs

Why can’t I get my iPhone into DFU mode?

Take a moment to double-check your cable and USB port, then restart both your device and computer. Remember, timing matters here! If you spot the Apple logo, try releasing the buttons sooner next time. Don’t worry if it takes a few tries—everyone goes through this, so keep going and don’t get discouraged!

Will entering DFU mode delete my data?

Just putting your device in DFU mode will not delete your data. But if you restore your device while in DFU mode, all your data and settings will be erased.

Does DFU mode affect my eSIM?

Usually, your eSIM profile remains the same after a DFU restore; however, it’s always recommended to back up important information before restoring.

My device isn’t detected in DFU mode—what should I do?

Check that Finder or iTunes is up to date. Try using another cable, port, or computer. If the problem continues, your device might need to be repaired.

Can I downgrade my iOS version using DFU mode?

Yes, but only if Apple is still signing the version you want to install.

How do I know if I’m in DFU mode or Recovery Mode?

DFU mode: the screen is entirely black, but your computer recognizes the device.
Recovery mode: The screen shows a cable or computer icon.

Does DFU mode fix all iPhone issues?

DFU mode is helpful, but it cannot fix problems caused by broken parts or water damage. If DFU mode does not work, get help from a professional.

  • How to Check Battery Cycle Count on iPhone

acceptedAnswer.text: When you close an app, it goes from the main screen to the background. It might still be running in a paused state, but iOS can also stop it if it needs resources. Closing an app doesn’t free up memory in most cases since iOS manages this automatically.

mainEntity.name: Will closing apps help free up RAM on my iPhone or iPad?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes and no. While iOS and iPadOS are built in a way to efficiently use the device’s memory, sometimes manually closing an app lets the device run a little better. If you’re struggling with low memory, you can restart your device to free up memory.

mainEntity.name: How do I know if an app is still running in the background on my iPhone or iPad?

acceptedAnswer.text: To check if an app is running, double-click the Home button or swipe up from the bottom of the screen to access the App Switcher. You’ll see a list of open apps. If an app is there, it's still running, or you can cross-check from the list of allowed Background Apps.

mainEntity.name: Why can't I get my iPhone into DFU mode?

acceptedAnswer.text: Take a moment to double-check your cable and USB port, then restart both your device and computer. Remember, timing matters here! If you spot the Apple logo, try releasing the buttons sooner next time. Don't worry if it takes a few tries—everyone goes through this, so keep going and don't get discouraged!

mainEntity.name: Will entering DFU mode delete my data?

acceptedAnswer.text: Just putting your device in DFU mode will not delete your data. But if you restore your device while in DFU mode, all your data and settings will be erased.

mainEntity.name: Does DFU mode affect my eSIM?

acceptedAnswer.text: Usually, your eSIM profile remains the same after a DFU restore; however, it's always recommended to back up important information before restoring.

mainEntity.name: Can I downgrade my iOS version using DFU mode?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, but only if Apple is still signing the version you want to install.

mainEntity.name: How do I know if I'm in DFU mode or Recovery Mode?

mainEntity.name: Does DFU mode fix all iPhone issues?

acceptedAnswer.text: DFU mode is helpful, but it cannot fix problems caused by broken parts or water damage. If DFU mode does not work, get help from a professional.

keyPoints.title: DFU Mode Functionality
keyPoints.explanation: DFU (Device Firmware Update) mode enables your iPhone or iPad to communicate directly with Finder or iTunes without loading iOS, facilitating powerful troubleshooting.

keyPoints.title: When to Use DFU Mode
keyPoints.explanation: DFU mode is essential for addressing severe software issues like boot loops, failed updates, or iOS downgrades when basic troubleshooting hasn't worked.

keyPoints.title: DFU vs Recovery Mode
keyPoints.explanation: While DFU mode keeps the screen black for deeper firmware access, Recovery Mode displays a cable or computer icon and is less invasive.

keyPoints.title: Precautions Before Entering DFU Mode
keyPoints.explanation: Prior to using DFU mode, back up your data, verify iOS signing status, avoid water-damaged devices, use trusted cables, and ensure a stable internet connection.

keyPoints.title: Entering DFU Mode on iPhone and iPad
keyPoints.explanation: Follow device-specific steps with precise button presses, and a black screen indicates successful entry into DFU mode.

title.rendered: How to Factory Reset iPhone: Backup, Erase, and Restore

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • What a factory reset does on iPhone or iPad: It erases apps, data, and settings, restoring the device to its original software state.
  • Why factory resetting matters: It permanently removes personal information, protecting your privacy before selling, donating, or recycling your iPhone or iPad.
  • When to consider a factory reset: Do it if your device is slow, apps keep crashing, or you’re preparing to hand it over to someone else.
  • What happens during a factory reset: Your Apple ID is unlinked, all data is deleted, and saved details like Wi-Fi passwords are permanently removed.
  • How to prepare before resetting: Back up data, sign out of Apple ID, and disable Find My to avoid activation lock and ensure a clean transfer.

Thinking about giving your iPhone or iPad a fresh start? Whether your device is acting up, you’re preparing to pass it on, or you just want a clean slate, doing a factory reset can feel like a big deal. Don’t worry—I’m here to guide you through every step, so you can reset your device with confidence and peace of mind.

What is a Factory Reset on iPhone or iPad?

A factory reset wipes your device clean—returning it to its original software state, just like when you first took it out of the box. All your personal data, apps, photos, music, and files are erased, and your settings go back to default. Afterward, you can set up your device as new or restore it from a backup.

Note: Only the Erase All Content & Settings option performs a true factory reset. Other reset options (like Reset Network Settings) don’t erase your personal data.

Why Factory Resetting Matters

A factory reset isn’t just a troubleshooting tool—it’s a powerful way to protect your privacy. Erasing all content and settings ensures your photos, messages, accounts, and sensitive info are truly gone. This is especially important if you’re selling, donating, or recycling your device. Trust me, you don’t want your personal data ending up in someone else’s hands!

When Should You Factory Reset Your iPhone or iPad?

You might want to consider a factory reset if:

  • Your device is running slowly or behaving erratically.
  • Apps are crashing repeatedly.
  • You’re preparing to sell, trade-in, donate, or recycle your device.
  • You want to remove all your data for privacy reasons.

A factory reset should be your last resort after trying simpler solutions like restarting or force-restarting your device.

What Happens When You Factory Reset your iPhone or iPad?

Here’s what you can expect:

  • All user data (apps, photos, messages, music, files) is permanently deleted.
  • All settings return to default.
  • Apple Pay cards, Wi-Fi passwords, and personalized settings are removed.
  • eSIMs can be deleted if you choose that option.
  • The device is unlinked from your Apple ID if you sign out before resetting.

How to Prepare Your iPhone for a Factory Reset

  • Back up Your Data: Before you reset, make sure you back up your iPhone or iPad. This way, you won’t lose those precious photos, messages, or contacts. Whether you use iCloud, a Mac, or a Windows PC, having a backup is a lifesaver if you need to restore your info later.
  • Sign Out of Your Apple ID Before Resetting: Don’t skip this step! Before erasing your device, sign out of your Apple ID and turn off Find My iPhone/iPad. This protects your privacy, removes Activation Lock, and ensures the next owner can use the device without any hiccups.
Don’t forget: If you have an Apple Watch, unpair it from your iPhone first. This automatically backs up your watch and disconnects it, so it’s ready to pair with your new device.

How to Factory Reset Your iPhone or iPad

Here’s a quick guide to safely erase all data and reset your iPhone (even the latest iPhone Duo, iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone Air and iPhone 17 series) or iPad to factory settings.

Option 1: Reset Directly from the Device

  1. Open Settings > General.
  2. Tap Transfer or Reset iPhone (or iPad).
  3. Tap Erase All Content and Settings.

  4. Follow the on-screen instructions. You may be prompted to back up your device.
  5. Enter your device passcode if required, then confirm.

Your device will erase all data and restart as new.

Option 2: Remotely Reset Using iCloud

If your device is lost or stolen, you can erase it remotely:

  1. Visit iCloud.com and sign in with your Apple ID.
  2. Go to Find My.

  3. Click All Devices and select your iPhone or iPad.

  4. Click Erase This Device and follow the prompts.

Note: This will lock your device. You’ll need your Apple ID and password to reactivate it.

Option 3: Reset Using a Computer (Finder or iTunes)

With Finder (macOS Catalina or later):

  1. Connect your device to your Mac.
  2. Open Finder and select your device.

  3. Click Restore iPhone/iPad and follow the prompts.

With iTunes (Windows or older macOS):

  1. Connect your device to your computer.

  2. Open iTunes and select your device.
  3. Click Summary > Restore iPhone/iPad.

Option 4: Using Recovery Mode

If your device is unresponsive or not recognized by your computer:

  1. Connect your device to your computer.
  2. Put your device in Recovery Mode (the steps vary by model).
  3. On your computer, choose Restore when prompted.

This will erase your device and install the latest iOS or iPadOS.

What to Do After an iPhone Factory Reset

  • Set up your device as new or
  • Restore from your iCloud or computer backup during setup.
  • If you’re selling, donating, or recycling your device, ensure you’ve removed SIM/eSIM cards and performed a final check for personal items.

Troubleshooting and Tips

  • If your device gets stuck during the reset, try using Recovery Mode.
  • Make sure your device is charged or plugged in during the process.
  • Before handing over your device, double-check that Find My is disabled and that you’re signed out of your Apple ID.

Conclusion

Factory resetting your iPhone or iPad is straightforward when you know what to expect. By taking a few extra precautions and following these steps, you’ll protect your privacy and make the transition to a new owner seamless.

If you have any questions or tips to share, leave a comment below—I’m here to help, and your feedback helps others, too. Good luck, and enjoy your device’s fresh start!

FAQs

Does a factory reset delete everything?

Yes, if you choose “Erase All Content & Settings,” all your data and settings are removed.

Can I recover data after a factory reset?

Only if you have a backup made before the reset.

What if I forgot my Apple ID password?

You’ll need to reset your Apple ID password at appleid.apple.com before proceeding.

Does the reset remove eSIMs?

You can choose to delete all eSIMs during the reset process.

Related articles worth reading:

  • How to clear RAM on iPhone to run faster
  • How to factory reset your Apple Watch
  • How to factory reset a MacBook or any Mac

mainEntity.name: Is there an app to block text messages on iPhones?

acceptedAnswer.text: Several third-party apps, such as Textkiller, Robokiller, etc., can filter and block spam text messages on your iPhone automatically. However, these apps require permission to read all your incoming texts, including OTP, bank alerts, and pretty much everything else, so we wouldn't recommend using them. A better approach is to use the built-in Messages app instead, which lets you block unwanted messages with a few simple taps.

mainEntity.name: How do you know if you're blocked on iMessage?

acceptedAnswer.text: Take a moment to double-check your cable and USB port, then restart both your device and computer. Remember, timing matters here! keyPoints.title: What is a Factory Reset on iPhone or iPad?
keyPoints.explanation: A factory reset restores your device to its original software state, erasing personal data, apps, settings, and returning it to default, like when it was first out of the box.

keyPoints.title: Why Factory Resetting Matters
keyPoints.explanation: Factory resetting is crucial for protecting privacy when passing on or recycling your device, as it ensures all personal information is permanently removed.

keyPoints.title: When to Consider a Factory Reset
keyPoints.explanation: A reset is advisable if your device is slow, apps crash, or if you're preparing to sell, donate, or need to remove personal data for privacy reasons.

keyPoints.title: What Happens During a Factory Reset
keyPoints.explanation: All your user data and settings are permanently deleted, devices are unlinked from your Apple ID, and personalized information like Wi-Fi passwords are removed.

keyPoints.title: How to Prepare for a Factory Reset
keyPoints.explanation: Back up your data and sign out of your Apple ID and Find My to ensure privacy, prevent activation lock, and make the reset smoother, especially when passing on the device.

title.rendered: How to Force Restart Any iPhone or iPad: A Complete Guide

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Force restart is for emergencies only when an iPhone or iPad becomes frozen, unresponsive, or stuck on the Apple logo.
  • Standard vs force restart methods differ—standard uses the software menu, while force restart uses hardware buttons to override software glitches.
  • iPhone restart steps vary by model: iPhone 8 and later need three button presses; iPhone 7 uses side + volume down; older models use Home + top/side.
  • iPads with and without Home buttons differ: Face ID models need three steps, while Home button iPads use a simple two-button combo.
  • If force restart fails, try recovery or DFU—or contact Apple if you suspect a hardware issue or charging problem.

Your iPhone freezes at the worst possible time. The screen stops responding, you tap, you press the Side button, nothing. Payment queue moving, thumb getting sweaty, phone still frozen. Deep breath. The quickest fix that actually works when the screen ignores you is a force restart.  

A force restart is different from a normal shutdown from the power slider; it is a hardware level reboot that kicks in when iOS hangs. On iPhone 17 Pro the button combo uses the Side button and the volume keys, older models use different steps, and I spell out each one. Follow the guide and you can get back to your Lock Screen without erasing photos or apps. Clear steps, all models covered, no data loss. 

Force Restart vs. Standard Restart

  • Standard Restart: Use this gentle reset when your iPhone still responds but feels slow or touch lags. Power it off from the software menus, then turn it back on. On iPhone 17 Pro, open Settings, General, Shut Down to get the slider, then hold the Side button to start up. Quick refresh, no drama.  
  • Force Restart: This is for emergencies. If the iPhone is frozen, unresponsive, or stuck on a black screen, use the button combo to reboot even if the touchscreen will not respond. On iPhone 17 Pro: press Volume Up, press Volume Down, then hold the Side button until the Apple logo appears. Older models use different steps.  

Will I lose data?

No. A force restart does not delete photos, messages, or apps. It restarts the phone only. 

How to Force Restart Your iPhone (Step-by-Step)

Find your iPhone model below and follow the steps.  

(Press the buttons with a firm click, in this exact order. This helps when the iPhone is unresponsive or frozen and a normal restart will not work.)

For iPhone 8, SE (2nd gen & later), – 17 Series

iPhone Air, 17, 16e, 16, 15, 14, 13, 12, 11, XS, XR, and iPhone X have Face ID and no Home button. Whereas iPhone SE 2022, SE 2020, and 8 series have a Home button with Touch ID. But the process to force a restart of all these devices is the same.

  1. Quickly press and release the Volume Up button. Do not hold.  
  2. Quickly press and release the Volume Down button. Same deal, a quick tap. 
  3. Press and hold the Side button on the right. Keep holding even if the power off slider shows up.  
  4. Keep holding until the Apple logo appears, then release. The phone restarts, lock screen returns. 

For iPhone 7 and iPhone 7 Plus

  1. Press and hold the Volume Down button and the Sleep/Wake Side button together. Both at once.
  2. Keep holding until the Apple logo appears, then let go. The restart begins, give it a few seconds

This method is also used for the iPod Touch 7th Gen. Just use the Top button instead of the Side button.

For iPhone 6s, SE (1st gen), and Earlier

  1. Press and hold the Home button and the Sleep/Wake button at the same time. Press both together.  
  2. Keep holding until the Apple logo shows, then release. The device restarts and boots normally.

These steps are also applicable for the iPod Touch 6th Gen. Just use the Top button instead of the Side button.

How to Force Restart Your iPad (Step-by-Step)

Find your iPad model below and follow the steps. 

(Press the buttons with a firm click, exactly in this order. This sequence helps when the iPad is unresponsive or completely frozen and a normal restart will not work at all.) 

Hard Reset iPad With Face ID

These are the iPad Pro models with Face ID and no Home button. The reboot sequence matches iPhone 8 and later, so the muscle memory carries over. Follow these steps exactly.

  1. Quickly press and release the Volume Up button. 
  2. Immediately press and quickly release the Volume Down button. 
  3. Press and hold the Top button. (Power button). Keep holding even if the power off slider appears.
  4. Keep holding the Top button until the Apple logo appears, then release. The iPad restarts to the Lock Screen.

Reboot an iPad With a Home Button 

On older iPads with a Home button, use this method.

  1. Press and hold both the Home button and the Sleep/Wake (Top) button simultaneously.
  2. Keep holding both buttons until the Apple logo appears, then release. The restart begins and finishes in a few seconds.

When Should You Use a Force Restart?

  • The screen goes frozen or black and won’t respond, so you can’t use your iPhone normally.  
  • Your iPhone ignores every tap and button press, so you can’t interact with it at all.  
  • An app crashes and locks up the whole device, preventing you from closing it or getting back to the Home Screen.  
  • You get stuck on the Apple logo during startup, and the device won’t finish booting like usual.  

What to Do if a Force Restart Doesn’t Work

Still stuck? Don’t worry try these steps:

Step 1: Charge Your iPhone  

Plug the iPhone into power for at least 30 minutes. A flat battery can block a restart. Try the force restart again while it is charging. Use a known good cable or charger to rule out power issues.  

Step 2: Connect to a Computer  

If it still will not turn on, connect the iPhone to a Mac or PC. Open Finder on a Mac or iTunes on Windows, then follow the prompts to update or restore the device. Keep it plugged in until the process completes.  

Step 3: DFU Mode (Advanced)  

If Recovery Mode does not help, Device Firmware Update (DFU), is a deeper restore option. Use it only if you feel comfortable with advanced troubleshooting, since it reinstalls firmware.  

Step 4: Contact Apple Support  

If none of this works, the iPhone may have a hardware issue. Reach out to Apple Support or visit an Apple Store for professional help. Booking a Genius Bar appointment saves time.

Final Thoughts

A force restart is the quickest first aid for an unresponsive iPhone. Do it right and the frozen screen, a stubborn app, or a phone that refuses to power off or back on usually clears in seconds. Knowing the exact button combo for your model, especially the iPhone 17 Pro sequence, lets you react fast without digging through menus. The move only restarts the system, so your photos, messages, and apps stay put. Keep this guide close so the steps are ready when you need them, bookmark it in Safari or drop it in Notes for easy reach. One calm sequence, Apple logo, relief. And if you have a trick that helped you in a pinch, share it in the comments.

FAQs

Will force restarting my iPhone or iPad erase data?

No. A force restart only reboots the device; your data and settings remain completely safe on both iPhone and iPad.

What’s the difference between restarting and force restarting iPhone or iPad?

A regular restart uses the on-screen power slider in Settings or the power button menu. A force restart uses specific button combinations to reboot an unresponsive device when the touchscreen won’t respond.

How do I force restart an iPhone or iPad with Face ID?

For iPhone and iPad models with Face ID: Quickly press and release Volume Up, then Volume Down, then press and hold the Side button (iPhone) or Top button (iPad) until the Apple logo appears. This works on iPhone 12 and later, plus iPad Air (4th gen and later) and iPad Pro (3rd gen and later).

How can I force restart older iPhone or iPad models?

For iPhone 7/7 Plus: Hold the Side button and Volume Down button together until the Apple logo appears. 
For iPhone 6s, SE (1st gen), and earlier: Hold the Home button and Side/Top button together until the Apple logo appears. 
For iPad with Home button: Hold the Home button and Top button together until the Apple logo appears.

What should I do if force restart doesn’t work on my iPhone or iPad?

Try these steps in order: Charge your device for at least 30 minutes, connect to a computer and use Recovery Mode through Finder (macOS Catalina+) or iTunes (older Mac/PC), attempt DFU mode if necessary, and contact Apple Support if the device remains unresponsive.

Can I restart my iPhone or iPad without using buttons?

Yes, if your device is responsive: Go to Settings > General > Shut Down, or ask Siri “Restart my iPhone” or “Restart my iPad.” On iPad, you can also use AssistiveTouch from Settings > Accessibility > Touch > AssistiveTouch to access restart options.

mainEntity.name: Is there an app to block text messages on iPhones?

acceptedAnswer.text: Several third-party apps, such as Textkiller, Robokiller, etc., can filter and block spam text messages on your iPhone automatically. However, these apps require permission to read all your incoming texts, including OTP, bank alerts, and pretty much everything else, so we wouldn't recommend using them. A better approach is to use the built-in Messages app instead, which lets you block unwanted messages with a few simple taps.

mainEntity.name: How do you know if you're blocked on iMessage?

acceptedAnswer.text: If someone has blocked you on iMessage, you may see green bubbles instead of blue. Likewise, you'll also see the Sent as Text Message label under your messages. For more information, refer to our guide on how to know if someone has blocked you on iMessage.

mainEntity.name: How do I clear the Safari cache without deleting my history on a Mac?

acceptedAnswer.text: Turn on the Develop menu in Safari Settings → Advanced, then choose Develop → Empty Caches or press Option + Command + E on your Mac.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between clearing history and clearing website data in Safari?

acceptedAnswer.text: Clearing history removes your browsing record but leaves you signed in. Clearing website data deletes cookies, cache, and local storage, which signs you out of sites.

mainEntity.name: Why is the "Remove All" button greyed out in Safari?

acceptedAnswer.text: Screen Time is blocking the action. Open System Settings → Screen Time → Content & Privacy, then set Web Content to Unrestricted Access.

mainEntity.name: How do I enable the Develop menu in Safari to clear the cache?

acceptedAnswer.text: Open Safari → Settings... → Advanced, and enable "Show Develop menu in menu bar."

mainEntity.name: Will clearing Safari data delete my saved passwords in iCloud Keychain?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Passwords stored in iCloud Keychain stay intact when you clear Safari data.

mainEntity.name: What happens to my bookmarks when I clear Safari data?

acceptedAnswer.text: Bookmarks are not affected by clearing cache, history, or website data.

mainEntity.name: Why is Safari still slow after I cleared the cache and cookies?

acceptedAnswer.text: Quit and relaunch Safari, check for macOS and Safari updates, and disable or remove extensions that may be hurting performance completely.

mainEntity.name: What happens when I close an app on my iPhone or iPad?

acceptedAnswer.text: When you close an app, it goes from the main screen to the background. It might still be running in a paused state, but iOS can also stop it if it needs resources. Closing an app doesn’t free up memory in most cases since iOS manages this automatically.

mainEntity.name: Why can't I get my iPhone into DFU mode?

acceptedAnswer.text: Take a moment to double-check your cable and USB port, then restart both your device and computer. Remember, timing matters here! If you spot the Apple logo, try releasing the buttons sooner next time. Don't worry if it takes a few tries—everyone goes through this, so keep going and don't get discouraged!

mainEntity.name: Will entering DFU mode delete my data?

acceptedAnswer.text: Just putting your device in DFU mode will not delete your data. But if you restore your device while in DFU mode, all your data and settings will be erased.

mainEntity.name: Does DFU mode affect my eSIM?

acceptedAnswer.text: Usually, your eSIM profile remains the same after a DFU restore; however, it's always recommended to back up important information before restoring.

mainEntity.name: My device isn't detected in DFU mode—what should I do?

acceptedAnswer.text: Check that Finder or iTunes is up to date. Try using another cable, port, or computer. If the problem continues, your device might need to be repaired.

mainEntity.name: Can I downgrade my iOS version using DFU mode?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, but only if Apple is still signing the version you want to install.

mainEntity.name: How do I know if I'm in DFU mode or Recovery Mode?

acceptedAnswer.text: DFU mode: the screen is entirely black, but your computer recognizes the device.Recovery mode: The screen shows a cable or computer icon.

mainEntity.name: Does DFU mode fix all iPhone issues?

acceptedAnswer.text: DFU mode is helpful, but it cannot fix problems caused by broken parts or water damage. If DFU mode does not work, get help from a professional.

mainEntity.name: Will force restarting my iPhone or iPad erase data?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. A force restart only reboots the device; your data and settings remain completely safe on both iPhone and iPad.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between restarting and force restarting iPhone or iPad?

acceptedAnswer.text: A regular restart uses the on-screen power slider in Settings or the power button menu. A force restart uses specific button combinations to reboot an unresponsive device when the touchscreen won't respond.

mainEntity.name: How do I force restart an iPhone or iPad with Face ID?

acceptedAnswer.text: For iPhone and iPad models with Face ID: Quickly press and release Volume Up, then Volume Down, then press and hold the Side button (iPhone) or Top button (iPad) until the Apple logo appears. This works on iPhone 12 and later, plus iPad Air (4th gen and later) and iPad Pro (3rd gen and later).

mainEntity.name: How can I force restart older iPhone or iPad models?

acceptedAnswer.text: For iPhone 7/7 Plus: Hold the Side button and Volume Down button together until the Apple logo appears. For iPhone 6s, SE (1st gen), and earlier: Hold the Home button and Side/Top button together until the Apple logo appears. For iPad with Home button: Hold the Home button and Top button together until the Apple logo appears.

mainEntity.name: What should I do if force restart doesn't work on my iPhone or iPad?

acceptedAnswer.text: Try these steps in order: Charge your device for at least 30 minutes, connect to a computer and use Recovery Mode through Finder (macOS Catalina+) or iTunes (older Mac/PC), attempt DFU mode if necessary, and contact Apple Support if the device remains unresponsive.

mainEntity.name: Can I restart my iPhone or iPad without using buttons?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, if your device is responsive: Go to Settings > General > Shut Down, or ask Siri "Restart my iPhone" or "Restart my iPad." On iPad, you can also use AssistiveTouch from Settings > Accessibility > Touch > AssistiveTouch to access restart options.

keyPoints.title: Difference Between Force Restart and Standard Restart
keyPoints.explanation: A standard restart relies on the software menu, while a force restart is a hardware-level reboot used in emergencies when the device is unresponsive.

keyPoints.title: Steps to Force Restart Different iPhone Models
keyPoints.explanation: The process varies by model: iPhone 8 and later use volume buttons and side button, iPhone 7 combines volume down and side button, and older models use the Home and side/top buttons.

keyPoints.title: How to Force Restart iPad Models
keyPoints.explanation: For Face ID iPads, press volume buttons and then hold the top button; for older models with a Home button, hold the Home and top button together until the Apple logo appears.

keyPoints.title: When to Use a Force Restart
keyPoints.explanation: Use a force restart when the screen is frozen, unresponsive, or stuck on the Apple logo, indicating the device is unresponsive and needs a hard reboot.

keyPoints.title: Troubleshooting If Force Restart Fails
keyPoints.explanation: If a force restart doesn’t work, try charging the device, connect to a computer for recovery mode, use DFU mode if comfortable, or contact Apple Support for hardware issues.

title.rendered: How to restart an iPhone or iPad (All models)

content.rendered:
Restarting our iPhones is the first thought that comes to our mind whenever we encounter any issue. This is because simply restarting your iPhone can often fix issues like app crashes, sluggish performance, or connectivity problems. While restarting an iPhone is a straightforward process, it is not uncommon for new iPhone users to get confused.

Whether you just picked up the new iPhone 18 Pro or iPhone 18 Pro Max, you are waiting on the foldable iPhone Duo, you own an iPhone 17 series, iPhone Air, or an older model with a Home button, continue on this read to learn how to restart your iPhone.

How to restart iPhone 18 Pro, 18 Pro Max, Air, 17, 16e, 16, 15, 14, 13, 12, 11, X, and XR

  1. Press and hold the Side button from the right side of the device, and either Volume Up or Volume Down from the left side of the device. Leave both buttons when you see the slider.
  2. Alternatively, if your iPhone is running iOS 18 or later, you can open the Control Center and long-press the Power button in the top-right corner to bring up the Power slider.

  3. Drag the slider from left to right.
  4. Wait for at least 30 seconds.
  5. To turn ON your iPhone with Face ID, press and hold the right Side button. Leave it when you see the Apple logo on the screen.

How to restart iPhone Duo, Apple’s first foldable

iPhone Duo is the one model in the 2026 lineup that breaks the usual layout. It has no Face ID at all. Apple built Touch ID into the Side button instead, so the same button you press to sleep the phone is also the one that unlocks it, whether the device is folded shut or opened out to the 7.6-inch inner display. The volume buttons sit on the top edge rather than the left side.

The power slider still works the same way:

  1. Press and hold the Side button and either Volume button together until the power slider appears.
  2. Drag the slider from left to right.
  3. Wait for at least 30 seconds.
  4. Press and hold the Side button again until the Apple logo appears on the outer display.

Because Touch ID lives in that button, rest your finger on it lightly rather than jabbing at it, otherwise you may just trigger an unlock attempt. If you would rather not hunt for two buttons on a folded phone, the Control Center method and the Settings method further down both work on iPhone Duo as well.

How to restart iPhone and iPad with home button

The second-generation iPhone SE, iPhone 8/8 Plus, iPhone 7/7 Plus, iPhone 6s/6s Plus, iPhone SE 1st Gen, iPhone 6/6 Plus, iPhone 5s/5c/5, and all iPads with Home button have the same method of restarting.

  1. Press and hold the Side button from the right side of the device (Top button for small iPhones and iPads). Stop pressing the button when you see the slider.

  2. Drag the slider from left to right.

  3. Wait for at least 30 seconds.
  4. To turn ON your iPhone or iPad with the Home button, press and hold the right Side button (or Top button). Leave it when you see the Apple logo on the screen.

How to restart the iPad that has Face ID

If you have iPad Pro 12.9-inch 4th or 3rd generation, iPad Pro 11-inch original or 2nd generation, then the process to restart is almost the same as iPhones with Face ID. Take a look.

  1. Press and hold the Top button, and either Volume Up or Volume Down from the right side of the device. Leave both buttons when you see the slider.

  2. Drag the slider from left to right.

  3. Wait for at least 30 seconds.
  4. To turn ON your iPad with Face ID, press and hold the Top button. Leave it when you see the Apple logo on the screen.

That’s all, mate!

This is the standard way in which you can restart any iPhone or iPad. However, it is also possible to restart your device without the power or home buttons. Finally, if a simple restart or force restart is not able to resolve a problem you’re encountering, then you may have to use Recovery mode or DFU mode. Let us know in the comments below if you have any other questions.

mainEntity.name: Does DFU mode fix all iPhone issues?

acceptedAnswer.text: DFU mode is helpful, but it cannot fix problems caused by broken parts or water damage. If DFU mode does not work, get help from a professional.

mainEntity.name: Why can't I get my iPhone into DFU mode?

acceptedAnswer.text: Take a moment to double-check your cable and USB port, then restart both your device and computer. Remember, timing matters here! If you spot the Apple logo, try releasing the buttons sooner next time. Don't worry if it takes a few tries—everyone goes through this, so keep going and don't get discouraged!

mainEntity.name: Will entering DFU mode delete my data?

acceptedAnswer.text: Just putting your device in DFU mode will not delete your data. But if you restore your device while in DFU mode, all your data and settings will be erased.

mainEntity.name: Does DFU mode affect my eSIM?

acceptedAnswer.text: Usually, your eSIM profile remains the same after a DFU restore; however, it's always recommended to back up important information before restoring.

mainEntity.name: My device isn't detected in DFU mode—what should I do?

acceptedAnswer.text: Check that Finder or iTunes is up to date. Try using another cable, port, or computer. If the problem continues, your device might need to be repaired.

mainEntity.name: Can I downgrade my iOS version using DFU mode?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, but only if Apple is still signing the version you want to install.
