keyPoints.title: Apple's Hypertension Notifications Expansion
keyPoints.explanation: Apple Watch users in more than 150 countries can now receive alerts about potential signs of high blood pressure, aiding early health detection and intervention.

keyPoints.title: Regulatory Clearance and Worldwide Rollout
keyPoints.explanation: The new hypertension alert feature has gained FDA approval in the U.S. and is now being made available internationally, including in Europe and Asia, subject to local regulatory approvals.

keyPoints.title: Passive Monitoring with Heart Sensor Data
keyPoints.explanation: Utilizing the Apple Watch's optical heart sensor, the feature passively tracks blood vessel responses over 30 days to identify potential hypertension symptoms without active user input.

keyPoints.title: Compatibility with Latest Apple Watch Models
keyPoints.explanation: Hypertension Notifications are available on Apple Watch Series 9, Ultra 3, SE 3, and future models, ensuring existing users can access the new health feature without needing hardware upgrades.

keyPoints.title: Scientifically Validated Health Feature
keyPoints.explanation: Developed using health data from over 100,000 individuals and validated in clinical studies with more than 2,000 participants, the feature demonstrates medical reliability and credibility.

descriptions: Discover how Apple Watch’s new Hypertension Notifications can passively monitor your blood pressure signs and help you catch silent health issues early.
Learn about Apple’s latest health feature—passive hypertension alerts supported by robust data and FDA approval, now available in over 150 countries.
Apple Watch’s new blood pressure warning system uses advanced sensors and algorithms to notify you of potential hypertension, all without a hardware upgrade.
Find out how Apple’s validated Hypertension Notifications can be a game-changer in preventive health, detecting early signs of high blood pressure.
Stay ahead of health risks with Apple Watch’s new feature that quietly monitors your blood vessels and sends you alerts if signs of hypertension are found.

title.rendered: 8 Best MacOS Sequoia Features You Should Know About

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Apple Intelligence powers on-device AI features like ChatGPT integration, custom image creation, and smarter Siri—all using private data from your Apple ecosystem.
  • iPhone Mirroring brings seamless Mac control—you can view, navigate, and manage iPhone apps and files directly from your Mac with drag-and-drop and full security.
  • Safari adds smarter tools for web browsing including Highlights for summaries, a redesigned Reader, and an upgraded Viewer for better video and AirPlay use.
  • The new Passwords app consolidates credentials—store, autofill, and manage logins, Wi-Fi info, and Passkeys across devices in one place.
  • Window tiling in macOS boosts multitasking—snap windows into organized layouts by dragging or using keyboard shortcuts to streamline your workspace.

If you are a Mac user, you know how exciting it is when a new macOS releases. This year Apple has included many standout features in the new macOS Sequoia such as Apple Intelligence, automatic window tiling, iPhone mirroring, etc. Eager to know more? Here’s a quick overview of some of the best macOS Sequoia features that you should know about.

Table of Contents
  1. Apple Intelligence
  2. iPhone Mirroring
  3. New Safari features
  4. New Passwords app
  5. Window Tiling
  6. New video conferencing tools
  7. New features for gaming
  8. Other app-related improvements in macOS 15 Sequoia

1. Apple Intelligence

Hand down, Apple Intelligence has to be one of the most exciting features introduced in macOS Sequoia. It primarily utilizes on-device machine learning to gather data about how you use your iPhone, iPad, and Mac to offer several new AI features that can improve how you perform tasks.

Once you install the macOS Sequoia 15.2, you can access all the Apple Intelligence features to boost your productivity and creativity. You can use Siri and ChatGPT to search the web and get responses, generate or summarize text using new writing tools, and even generate images from text prompts on a Mac.

2. iPhone Mirroring

Apple already allows you to copy text between your devices or hand off calls from your iPhone to Mac using Continuity. macOS Sequoia takes this further with a new iPhone Mirroring feature. This feature lets you see what’s on your iPhone and control it right from your Mac.

With iPhone Mirroring, you can fully interact with your iPhone using the keyboard and trackpad on your Mac. Apple says that while you’re using this feature, your iPhone stays locked so nobody can access your data, and all the notifications that you receive are simply redirected to your Mac.

Last but not least, you can even drag and drop files from your Mac to your iPhone using this feature. If you are facing any issues using this feature, you can check out our detailed guide on fixing iPhone Mirroring not working issue.

3. New Safari features

Safari gets several new features in macOS Sequoia to offer a better web browsing experience. You can now use Safari Highlights to automatically detect and highlight relevant information on web pages using Machine Learning. For instance, Safari Highlights can generate a summary of content on websites with text or display directions, essential phone numbers, and quick links.

Moreover, the Safari Reader has been revamped to reduce distractions and offer a simpler way to access information with a helpful summary and an organized table of contents in longer articles. And on websites that have videos, there’s also a new Viewer feature that offers a distraction-free video experience with system playback controls and support for AirPlay and Picture-in-Picture.

4. New Passwords app

While we already had a built-in password manager in System Settings, macOS Sequoia brings a new Passwords app. With this app, you can now access your website and app passwords, Wi-Fi credentials, Passkeys, and verification codes in one place across iPhone, iPad, and Vision Pro. Plus, the new app also supports autofill, so you don’t need to enter user credentials yourself.

5. Window Tiling

Multitasking on Mac has also become easier on macOS Sequoia with Window Tiling. Now, you can simply drag an app window to the edge of the screen or use keyboard and menu shortcuts to place app windows however you want. You can quickly place app windows, or as Apple likes to call them, “tiles” side-by-side, on top of each other, or into corners if you want to use four apps at once.

6. New video conferencing tools

Apple rolled out several video conferencing tools in macOS Sonoma, including Presenter Overlay, Reactions in FaceTime, and third-party apps like Zoom and WebX. This year, with macOS Sequoia, Apple has added a new Presenter Preview feature that allows you to see what you will be sharing before you start a screen-sharing session. Additionally, there’s also a new Backgrounds feature that can be used to replace backdrops in video calls with wallpapers, color gradients, or photos.

7. New features for gaming

Apple introduced a dedicated Game Mode for Mac and Game Porting Toolkit in macOS Sonoma. This year, macOS Sequoia brings improvements to Game Mode for more FPS, and you can now experience your games with Personalized Spatial Audio on AirPods. Meanwhile, developers can access Game Porting Toolkit 2 to bring even more graphic-intensive Windows games to Mac.

The gaming announcements don’t stop here. Apple says it will be adding several new games to the App Store, including Frostpunk 2, Control, Ubisoft’s Assassins Creed: Shadows, and more.

8. Other app-related improvements in macOS 15 Sequoia

In addition to the above features, macOS Sequoia also brings some quality-of-life improvements to several built-in apps on Mac. Here’s a list of the apps that got new features:

  • Notes: Thanks to Apple Intelligence, summarize text, and automatically solve mathematical equations for you. Apart from this, the Notes app on Mac can transcribe audio and also offers a new Highlight tool to mark up text and collapsible sections to organize your notes.
  • Photos: The Photos app has been updated to automatically organize photos into Collections using themes. Plus, search has been revamped so users can find photos and videos quickly.
  • Calendar: The Calendar app in macOS 15 Sequoia can now show events and tasks from the Reminders app, making it easy to see, edit, or complete tasks throughout the day. Meanwhile, with an updated Month View, you can see events and reminders for an entire month at once.
  • Messages: Similar to iOS 18 and iPadOS 18, the Messages app on macOS Sequoia also gets several new features. You can now schedule messages to send them later, use all-new text effects to highlight any essential details, and send custom emojis and sticker Tapbacks.
  • Calculator: Similar to iOS 18 and iPadOS 18, macOS Sequoia brings an updated Calculator app with new features, including the ability to view past calculations with history and mathematical expressions as you type them.
  • Apple Maps: Apple Maps in macOS Sequoia allows you to create curated hikes and custom walking routes. With this feature, users can browse thousands of hikes across 63 national parks in the United States, filtered by length, elevation, and route type, and save them offline.

Video: Best macOS Sequoia features

Wrapping up…

macOS Sequoia is a quality-of-life update that brings many user-requested features to the Mac. Whether you’re a seasoned Mac user or a beginner, this update ensures your experience is smoother than ever. I am really enjoying the advanced Apple Intelligence features on my Mac. 

Which new macOS feature are you most excited about? Let us know in the comments section.

mainEntity.name: Is iOS 26 better than iOS 18?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. iOS 26 introduces a visually rich design, smarter system tools, and improved app interfaces—especially if you're on a newer iPhone.

mainEntity.name: Will iOS 26 slow down older iPhones?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not necessarily. While older models like the iPhone 11 may not run animations as smoothly, Apple has optimized performance across supported devices. Battery health and storage space may still affect your experience.

mainEntity.name: Can I get X Premium for free?

acceptedAnswer.text: No free trial is available. Sometimes high-follower accounts get complimentary upgrades, but generally, it's paid-only.

mainEntity.name: Do I need Premium for a blue checkmark?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. At least Premium or Premium+ (or Verified Organizations) is required.

mainEntity.name: Is X Premium ad-free?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not entirely. Basic has full ads, Premium halves them in main timelines, and Premium+ is mostly ad-free everywhere, but you might see occasional sponsored posts.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between the blue checkmarks and the gold and grey checkmarks?

acceptedAnswer.text: Blue is for individual Premium subscribers. Gold means an official business or non-profit via Verified Organizations. Grey is for governments or multilateral organizations. They come with extras like badges for affiliates and premium support for orgs.

mainEntity.name: Is the previous legacy blue checkmark and X Premium subscription checkmark same?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not really. The legacy one was for active, notable, authentic accounts verified by X's old system. The new blue is exclusive to active subscribers, with no fame check required.

keyPoints.title: Apple Intelligence Enhances Productivity and Creativity
keyPoints.explanation: This on-device machine learning feature gathers data from your Apple devices to offer new AI functionalities such as web searching with Siri and ChatGPT, text generation, and image creation from prompts.

keyPoints.title: iPhone Mirroring Improves Device Integration
keyPoints.explanation: The new iPhone Mirroring feature allows users to see and control their iPhone directly from the Mac, with secure locking, notification redirection, and the ability to drag and drop files.

keyPoints.title: Safari Gets Smarter and More User-Friendly
keyPoints.explanation: Safari now includes Highlights for automatic content summaries, a revamped Reader for distraction-free reading, and a new Viewer for an enhanced video experience with AirPlay and Picture-in-Picture support.

keyPoints.title: New Passwords App Simplifies Credential Management
keyPoints.explanation: The updated Passwords app consolidates passwords, Wi-Fi credentials, Passkeys, and verification codes across devices, offering autofill and easy access to sensitive data.

keyPoints.title: Window Tiling Makes Multitasking Easier
keyPoints.explanation: Users can now effortlessly organize app windows into tiles on the screen by dragging them to edges or using shortcuts, enabling efficient workspace management.

title.rendered: Best iOS 18 Features You Should Try Now!

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • iOS 18 is now available for supported iPhones—download it through Settings > General > Software Update following its debut at the It’s Glowtime event.
  • New features include Apple Intelligence and more control—expect smarter AI, app locking, redesigned Photos, and deeper customization options.
  • Photos app uses AI to auto-organize your gallery into smart collections like Trips or People, plus daily highlights of your top moments.
  • Home and Lock Screens get more layout freedom—rearrange icons, adjust themes, and customize Control Center shortcuts with ease.
  • Privacy gets a boost with app locks and auto-reboot—new security features protect sensitive data and reboot your iPhone after long inactivity.

Finally, the wait is over! Apple launched the official iOS 18 version at the It’s Glowtime event, which included a slew of new features and updates. From a home screen revamp to the new AI-powered Apple Intelligence, iOS 18 is going to take our iPhone experience to a whole new level.

These are the iOS 18 features you should know about and how to update your iPhone to iOS 18.

Table of Contents
  • How to Update to iOS 18?
  • Best iOS 18 Features You Should Try After You Update
    • Enhanced Photos app
    • Customizable Home Screen
    • Lock and hide apps
    • Revamped Messages app
    • Categorization in Mail app
    • Highlights in Safari
    • Tap to Cash on the iPhone
    • New Notes features
    • Updates in the Journal app
    • Game mode in iOS 18
    • Improved privacy controls and new Passwords app
    • Calculator updates
    • New Accessibility features
    • Inactivity Reboot
    • Apple Intelligence features on iOS 18.1 update
  • Video: What's new in iOS 18?

How to Update to iOS 18?

The official iOS 18 version is available to download for all supported devices. Simply go to Settings, select General and tap on Software Update. Here, you can download and install iOS 18. Users enrolled in the beta program can also remove the iOS 18 beta and upgrade to the official version. After you update successfully, you can enjoy the new features that we will discuss next.

However, note that a set of Apple Intelligence features will arrive in the iOS 18.1 update in October. More advanced AI features, such as Image Playground and Genmoji, are expected to roll out in the iOS 18.2 version later this year.

With no further ado, let’s jump into the exciting features introduced in iOS 18.

Best iOS 18 Features You Should Try After You Update

If you’re eager to learn about the new features of iOS 18, we have you covered. Below, we have highlighted the top features of iOS 18 that you should explore right now. Check it out!

1. Enhanced Photos app

The Photos app in iOS 18 is smarter and more powerful than ever. It uses AI to automatically organize your photos in Collections such as Recent Days, Trips, People & Pets, etc. You can also pin Collections to quickly access the albums that are most significant to you.

Apple suggests the Photos app shows highlights of the best pictures in the camera roll in a beautiful, poster-like view. And the best part is you will get a new highlight each day.

2. Customizable Home Screen

The Home Screen in iOS 18 has been revamped to offer more customization options. As Apple explained, you can move app icons around and apply a chosen color theme across the app grid for an extra touch of personalized flair.

The Control Center has also been updated to allow users to customize the layout and functionality of quick access controls. You can even change the shortcut controls on your Lock Screen in iOS 18!

4. Lock and hide apps

Apple has finally responded to the user’s request! iOS 18 allows you to hide and lock apps in a separate folder. To access those apps, you must authenticate yourself with your passcode, Face ID, or Touch ID.

Apple claims that information from locked apps won’t show up in searches or alerts, so no one will know you have such an app on your iPhone.

5. Revamped Messages app

Messages in iOS 18 come with new ways to express yourself. You can now add animated effects to your texts to make your conversations livelier. Using Tapback in iMessage, you can access all emojis and stickers in iOS 18. Moreover, the Send Later feature provides the convenience of scheduling messages to be sent at a selected time.

Apple also brought support for messages via Satellite so you can stay connected in every situation. With iOS 18, your Android friends will no longer feel left out, as the RCS messaging support will provide read receipts for non-iMessages.

6. Categorization in Mail app

After quite some time, the Mail app is seeing some love with new added features in the 18th iteration of the operating system. Now, the Mail app will be able to sort and organize emails in categories such as Primary, Transaction, Promotions, and Updates. So you can easily skim through and prioritize the import mail. It sounds familiar to you if you’re an avid Gmail user, right?

The Primary section will show urgent emails and messages from individuals you know. You can easily find your order confirmations and receipts in the Transactions category. Promotions are for marketing and sales communications and Updates will group newsletters and other communications.

7. Highlights in Safari

To help you find important information quickly, Apple has introduced Highlights in Safari. It will automatically identify and highlight any relevant content like directions or quick links on a web page. If you enable Reader mode, you’ll see a summary of the page and a table of contents. You may also customize a webpage view and remove unwanted objects using the Distraction Control feature.

8. Tap to Cash on the iPhone

Similar to the Tap to Pay technology, Tap to Cash makes in-person payments quick and simple. You no longer need to exchange phone numbers or email addresses to transmit Apple Cash. Just authenticate your payment with Face ID and bring your device near the recipient’s iPhone.

9. New Notes features

The Notes app also received some cool features in iOS 18. You can now record audio within a note. The best part is you will get auto transcriptions for those recordings. You can also experience the Math Note feature introduced in iPadOS on iPhone now, albeit with a few fewer features. Type in an expression to get its solution instantly. You can also see your call recording in the Notes app.

10. Updates in the Journal app

The Journal app was a great addition to iOS 17. Now, new updates let you view your writing journey on a calendar and other entertaining statistics. So you can keep track of your journaling objectives.

You can search through your journals to locate anything quickly. The Journal app now also has different widgets!

11. Game mode in iOS 18

Ready to enjoy gaming on your iPhone? The Game Mode in iOS 18 suppresses background activities so you can enjoy high frame rates for extended gameplay. Apple also claims Game Mode will significantly reduce audio latency and make wireless gaming controllers more responsive.

12. Improved privacy controls and new Passwords app

iOS 18 includes several privacy features, such as the ability to share specific contacts with apps instead of sharing all contacts.

The new Passwords app securely stores all types of information, including passwords, verifications, and security warnings. With AutoFill enabled, your passwords will immediately be uploaded to the Passwords app and sync safely between your devices.

13. Calculator updates

The native calculator app finally got its most requested feature – calculation history in iOS 18. Now, you can track your past calculations within the app. Moreover, you can access the Scientific mode in portrait mode as well. iOS 18 also brought in-app unit conversion in the calculator.

14. New Accessibility features

iOS 18 is indeed full of helpful features, and these include several Accessibility upgrades. From Eye Tracking for operating an iPhone with just your eyes to Music Haptics for people who are hard of hearing or deaf, the new Accessibility features open a new way to use the device. To learn more, refer to our guide on iOS 18 Accessibility features.

15. Inactivity Reboot

Similar to the enhanced privacy controls, there is a new subtle yet powerful security feature in iOS 18.1. This Inactivity Reboot feature tracks when you last unlocked your iPhone. If you device is not used in 72 hours, it automatically reboots. Therefore, you must unlock your iPhone using your PIN or passcode; else you can’t access your device. This protects your data from thieves and unauthorized access.

16. Apple Intelligence features on iOS 18.1 update

iOS 18 introduces Apple Intelligence, an AI-driven personal intelligence system. Apple claims that their generative AI models will be able to assess personal context to provide more helpful and relevant answers when sending texts, searching for images, and everything in between. Based on reports, the iOS 18.1 update will include AI-powered features, further enhancing these capabilities and offering even more personalized interactions across the iPhone experience.

This new feature will make Siri smarter and a pro multitasker. Apple Intelligence can create a custom Genmoji, generate images, remove unwanted objects from the background, and summarize long texts. The Apple Intelligence system will also sort and prioritize notifications.

Video: What’s new in iOS 18?

Signing off…

iOS 18 brings a wealth of new features that make your iPhone smarter, more intuitive, and more enjoyable, like an official way to mirror your iPhone screen to a Mac. Its focus on AI-powered capabilities and personalization ensures that you can boost your productivity and enhance your user experience.

If you have any questions or want to share your experiences with iOS 18, feel free to leave a comment below!

  • 21 Best iOS 18 tips and tricks you should know!
  • iOS 18.4 release date: Here’s when to expect new features

mainEntity.name: Is iOS 26 better than iOS 18?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. iOS 26 introduces a visually rich design, smarter system tools, and improved app interfaces—especially if you're on a newer iPhone.

mainEntity.name: Will iOS 26 slow down older iPhones?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not necessarily. While older models like the iPhone 11 may not run animations as smoothly, Apple has optimized performance across supported devices. Battery health and storage space may still affect your experience.

mainEntity.name: Can I get X Premium for free?

acceptedAnswer.text: No free trial is available. Sometimes high-follower accounts get complimentary upgrades, but generally, it's paid-only.

mainEntity.name: Do I need Premium for a blue checkmark?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. At least Premium or Premium+ (or Verified Organizations) is required.

mainEntity.name: Is X Premium ad-free?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not entirely. Basic has full ads, Premium halves them in main timelines, and Premium+ is mostly ad-free everywhere, but you might see occasional sponsored posts.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between the blue checkmarks and the gold and grey checkmarks?

acceptedAnswer.text: Blue is for individual Premium subscribers. Gold means an official business or non-profit via Verified Organizations. Grey is for governments or multilateral organizations. They come with extras like badges for affiliates and premium support for orgs.

mainEntity.name: Is the previous legacy blue checkmark and X Premium subscription checkmark same?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not really. The legacy one was for active, notable, authentic accounts verified by X's old system. The new blue is exclusive to active subscribers, with no fame check required.

keyPoints.title: iOS 18 Launch and Availability
keyPoints.explanation: Apple announced iOS 18 at the It's Glowtime event, featuring new updates and features, and it is available for all supported devices via Settings > General > Software Update.

keyPoints.title: Key New Features in iOS 18
keyPoints.explanation: iOS 18 introduces a revamped home screen, AI-powered Apple Intelligence, improved Photos app, customizable controls, app locking, and new privacy and security features.

keyPoints.title: Enhanced Photos App with AI Organization
keyPoints.explanation: The Photos app now uses AI to automatically organize images into collections like Recent Days, Trips, and People, with daily highlights of your best pictures.

keyPoints.title: Customization and Control Enhancements
keyPoints.explanation: iOS 18 offers more customization options for the home screen, control center, and lock screen, allowing users to personalize app layout, themes, and shortcuts.

keyPoints.title: New Privacy and Security Improvements
keyPoints.explanation: Features like app locking, increased privacy controls, and Inactivity Reboot help protect user data and enhance device security by automatically rebooting after periods of inactivity.

title.rendered: How to Use Live Voicemail on iPhone

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Live Voicemail debuted in iOS 17 and shows real-time transcriptions of incoming voicemails directly on your iPhone without using third-party apps.
  • It works locally and privately by processing the caller’s message on-device so you can read what they’re saying while they’re still speaking.
  • Enable it under Phone settings—Live Voicemail is usually on by default after updating to iOS 17, but you can toggle it manually if needed.
  • You can screen calls in real-time by tapping the Voicemail icon during an incoming call and deciding to pick up based on the transcript.
  • Voicemail transcripts are saved automatically in the Phone app, where you can listen back, read messages, or record a new greeting anytime.

Have you ever just stare at your phone screen, wondering who on earth is calling? Yeah, we’ve all been there. Well, with Live Voicemail on your iPhone, you don’t need some fancy extra apps to peek into missed calls; they get read out for you in real-time text. It’s both fun and useful.

So, here’s the deal: Live Voicemail showed up with iOS 17, giving you this nifty trick to keep better tabs on the calls coming in. The idea? You’re reading what folks are saying as they’re talking, right on your phone screen. It’s like closing the gap on missed moments without compromising your privacy. This feature runs everything directly on your device, so none of your audio touches Apple’s servers. Picture this: never again wonder if it’s that mystery number that’s important or if your meeting needs a bit of interrupting.

Wondering how you make all this magic happen? If you’re curious about setting it up and getting the most out of Live Voicemail, let’s dive right in and see how you can handle your voicemails like a pro.

Table of Contents
  • What is Live Voicemail & How Does it Work?
  • How to Turn on Live Voicemail on iPhone
  • How to Use Live Voicemail During an Incoming Call
  • How to Manage Live Voicemail Messages After the Call
  • How to Customize Your Voicemail Greeting
  • Why Isn't Live Voicemail Working?
  • Signing Off…

What is Live Voicemail & How Does it Work?

Live Voicemail feels like having a tiny superpower for handling calls to me. Instead of playing the waiting game with voicemail messages, you see what someone’s saying as it’s happening, in real-time text blinking away on your screen.

Here’s the magic: when a call hits you and you can’t or don’t pick up, Live Voicemail takes a crack at showing you a live play-by-play of their message. Words pop onto your screen in real-time, letting you choose if it’s worth picking up or if you should let the message run its course.

And the really cool part? Your caller won’t suspect a thing unless you actually answer. It’s just as though they’re leaving an ordinary voicemail. Plus, everything is done right on your iPhone using the Neural Engine, so your chats stay under lock and key, privacy-wise.

How to Turn on Live Voicemail on iPhone

Getting Live Voicemail switched on your iPhone is a breeze, and the sweet thing is, it’s usually switched on automatically once you update to iOS 17 or newer. But, if you want to make sure or toggle it off, here’s the scoop:

  1. Open the Settings app on your iPhone.
  2. Scroll down to the bottom and tap on Apps.
  3. Scroll down and tap on Phone.
  4. Tap on Live Voicemail, and toggle the switch On or Off depending on your preference.

If Live Voicemail isn’t automatically enabled on your current iOS version, you can manually enable it this way:

  1. Open the Settings and head to the Phone settings.
  2. Next, select Live Voicemail, then toggle it on if it isn’t already.
Note
    To access Live Voicemail in regions where it isn’t yet available, change the region to the U.S. on your iPhone.

How to Use Live Voicemail During an Incoming Call

Once you get the hang of it, using Live Voicemail is downright slick. Here’s the lowdown on what happens when someone calls:

When your iPhone’s buzzing, you’ve got a choice. Let it run its course naturally, or if you’re in a spot to jump straight into Live Voicemail, tap the Voicemail icon popping up on your screen.

Once that call hits voicemail, the Live Voicemail screen brightens up, and poof, you’re seeing a real-time transcription popping up as the person talks away. Kind of like watching subtitles rolling in for your voicemail.

And here’s the kicker:

  • To Answer: Spot something significant midway? Hit the green Answer button anytime to connect.
  • To Decline: If it doesn’t seem pressing, let them finish, or tap the red End button and cut things short.

The beauty here? You’re always in the pilot’s seat, rescuing key calls you might’ve missed, while letting the less pressing ones sail into voicemail oblivion.

How to Manage Live Voicemail Messages After the Call

Once someone leaves a Live Voicemail, looking after these messages isn’t rocket science; it works like your usual voicemails, but with a few extra bells and whistles.

Here’s how to access and manage your Live Voicemail messages: 

  1. Open the Phone app on your iPhone.
  2. Tap on Voicemail at the bottom right corner.
  3. Tap the Caller’s Name or Number to access their specific voicemail.
  4. Now you can read the full transcript, play the audio, share the message, or delete it.

Once a Live Voicemail message is open, you’ve several options. Scanning through the full transcript without needing to crank up the audio is super handy, especially in quiet settings or if you’re in turbo mode sifting for key deets. Still, you can also play the original audio if you want the whole voice experience, tone and all.

Those transcripts make breezing through voicemails easy-peasy, whether you’re hunting for must-know info or just wanting a quick story without sitting through the whole recording.

In case you missed: Use Apple Mail Drop to Send Large Files on Mac & iPhone

How to Customize Your Voicemail Greeting

Creating a custom voicemail greeting is a nice touch, giving callers the assurance they’ve hit the right person and setting a tone for Live Voicemail. Here’s how to spruce up your greeting:

  1. Open the Phone app and tap the Voicemail button at the bottom right corner.
  2. Here, tap on Greetings at the top right corner.
  3. Next, select Custom, then tap on the Record button.
  4. Now, record the custom outgoing greeting message and tap Save.

Remember, your greeting is their first impression. A nod to Live Voicemail in your message can be handy; consider adding a “Hey, give me your full details, and I’ll get back to you.” It encourages callers to drop something useful for Live Voicemail to work its transcription magic.

Why Isn’t Live Voicemail Working?

Occasionally, Live Voicemail might not play ball. But hang tight, most glitches are easy to sort. Let’s run through common hiccups and fixes:

  • Option is Missing: Can’t catch sight of Live Voicemail in settings? First, check that you’re rocking an iPhone XS or newer models. Double-check that you’re updated to iOS 17 or later. Peek at your region and language settings, as not all places have rolled this out yet.
  • No Transcription Appears: Live Voicemail thrives best in mellow surroundings. Unruly noise can mess up transcription accuracy. Restarting your iPhone can fix minor software gremlins causing issues, too.
  • Button is Greyed Out: Check if Screen Time restrictions or device management settings, typically set by schools or workplaces, are blocking it. These can sometimes throw a wrench in Live Voicemail’s gears.

If you’re stuck after trying these, switch Live Voicemail off and back on, or reach out to your carrier to verify if your voicemail’s set up correctly.

Signing Off…

Live Voicemail, I must say, significantly improves how we manage calls. It’s this robust, privacy-first tool that grounds you back in the driving seat for call handling, nudging you towards deciding what really needs your quick engagement and what doesn’t.

Running on-device, Apple’s crafted a spot-on feature that’s not just super useful but lets you keep a lid on security. No more trade-offs between missing important calls or having your flow broken by less essential ones.

Getting comfy with Live Voicemail can truly shift how you face calls regularly. You’ll notice a confidence boost, juggling calls more smartly while keeping your time and privacy in good standing.

FAQs

Can I answer a call while Live Voicemail is transcribing?

Yup, absolutely! That’s one of Live Voicemail’s charm points. Tap the green Answer button at any moment while reading that transcription. The caller? They won’t know you’ve had a sneak peek till you pick up.

Why don’t I see the Live Voicemail option on my iPhone? 

Live Voicemail plays with iPhone XS or newer, using iOS 17 or later. Tick those boxes and still no dice? Check if your region settings align, since it’s not rolled out globally just yet.

Does Live Voicemail work on Wi-Fi calling? 

Oh yes, it does. As long as your carrier supports it and you’re on iOS 17 or later, you’re all set.

How is Live Voicemail different from Visual Voicemail? 

Here’s the key difference: Visual Voicemail shows you a lineup of messages to play back. Live Voicemail, however, gives you live transcription as someone leaves that message, with the added ability to intervene mid-message.

Will my caller know I’m reading their voicemail live?

Not a chance. Callers won’t catch wind of you viewing their message in real-time unless you answer. From their end, it’s voicemail as usual.

Is Live Voicemail available on all carriers?

Live Voicemail works with most major carriers, but there’s some variation. If you’ve run into issues, a word with your carrier might help; they could need to tweak your voicemail settings.

How do I delete Live Voicemail transcripts?

Deleting Live Voicemail messages mirrors usual ones: swipe left on the message list and tap Delete, or dive into the message and hit the trash icon.

Why is Live Voicemail not transcribing messages?

Crummy audio quality, boisterous background antics, or unclear speech can toss the transcription off track. It performs best when callers speak clearly in peaceful zones. Restart your iPhone to resolve any temporary transcription issues.

  • How to delete voicemails on iPhone

mainEntity.name: Can I answer a call while Live Voicemail is transcribing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yup, absolutely! That’s one of Live Voicemail’s charm points. Tap the green Answer button at any moment while reading that transcription. The caller? They won’t know you’ve had a sneak peek till you pick up.

mainEntity.name: Why don't I see the Live Voicemail option on my iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: Live Voicemail plays with iPhone XS or newer, using iOS 17 or later. Tick those boxes and still no dice? Check if your region settings align, since it’s not rolled out globally just yet.

mainEntity.name: Does Live Voicemail work on Wi-Fi calling?

acceptedAnswer.text: Oh yes, it does. As long as your carrier supports it and you're on iOS 17 or later, you're all set.

mainEntity.name: How is Live Voicemail different from Visual Voicemail?

acceptedAnswer.text: Here’s the key difference: Visual Voicemail shows you a lineup of messages to play back. Live Voicemail, however, gives you live transcription as someone leaves that message, with the added ability to intervene mid-message.

mainEntity.name: Will my caller know I'm reading their voicemail live?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not a chance. Callers won’t catch wind of you viewing their message in real-time unless you answer. From their end, it’s voicemail as usual.

mainEntity.name: Is Live Voicemail available on all carriers?

acceptedAnswer.text: Live Voicemail works with most major carriers, but there’s some variation. If you've run into issues, a word with your carrier might help; they could need to tweak your voicemail settings.

mainEntity.name: How do I delete Live Voicemail transcripts?

acceptedAnswer.text: Deleting Live Voicemail messages mirrors usual ones: swipe left on the message list and tap Delete, or dive into the message and hit the trash icon.

mainEntity.name: Why is Live Voicemail not transcribing messages?

acceptedAnswer.text: Crummy audio quality, boisterous background antics, or unclear speech can toss the transcription off track. It performs best when callers speak clearly in peaceful zones. Restart your iPhone to resolve any temporary transcription issues.

@graph.name: How to turn on Live Voicemail on iPhone in iOS 18
@graph.description: Enable Live Voicemail on your iPhone running iOS 18 to see real-time voicemail transcriptions and manage calls more effectively.

step.name: Open Settings
step.text: Open the Settings app, scroll to the bottom, and tap Apps.

itemListElement.text: Unlock your iPhone and open the Settings app.
Scroll down and tap Apps.

step.name: Access Phone settings
step.text: Locate and tap Phone to open its settings options.

itemListElement.text: Scroll through the list of apps.
Tap Phone to manage call and voicemail settings.

step.name: Enable Live Voicemail
step.text: Select Live Voicemail, then toggle on Live Voicemail if it isn’t already enabled.

itemListElement.text: Tap Live Voicemail from the Phone settings menu.
Toggle on Live Voicemail to activate the feature.

@graph.name: How to turn on Live Voicemail on iPhone in iOS 17
@graph.description: Enable Live Voicemail on your iPhone running iOS 17 to view real-time voicemail transcriptions and manage calls with ease.

step.name: Open Phone settings
step.text: Open the Settings app on your iPhone and head to the Phone settings.

itemListElement.text: Unlock your iPhone and tap the Settings app.
Scroll down and select Phone.

step.name: Enable Live Voicemail
step.text: Select Live Voicemail, then toggle it on if it isn’t already enabled.

itemListElement.text: Tap Live Voicemail under the Phone settings menu.
Toggle on Live Voicemail to activate it.

@graph.name: How to set up a Voicemail greeting on your iPhone
@graph.description: Easily set up a custom voicemail greeting on your iPhone so callers hear a personalized message when you can’t answer.

step.name: Open the Phone app
step.text: Open the Phone app and tap the Voicemail button at the bottom right corner.

itemListElement.text: Unlock your iPhone and tap the Phone app.
Tap Voicemail in the bottom-right corner.

step.name: Go to Greetings
step.text: Tap on Greetings at the top right corner to open voicemail greeting options.

itemListElement.text: Locate the top-right corner of the screen.
Tap Greetings to access voicemail greeting settings.

step.name: Select Custom greeting
step.text: Select Custom, then tap the Record button to create a personalized voicemail greeting.

itemListElement.text: Tap Custom to enable recording mode.
Tap the Record button to begin recording your greeting.

step.name: Record and save greeting
step.text: Record your custom outgoing voicemail greeting message and tap Save once you are satisfied.

itemListElement.text: Record your voicemail greeting clearly.
Tap Save to confirm and set it as your outgoing greeting.

@graph.name: How to view Live Voicemail transcriptions on iPhone
@graph.description: Learn how to view and read Live Voicemail transcriptions on your iPhone so you can quickly see what a caller said without listening to the full message.

step.name: Open the Phone app
step.text: Open the Phone app on your iPhone and tap Voicemail at the bottom right corner.

itemListElement.text: Unlock your iPhone and tap the Phone app.
Tap Voicemail in the bottom-right corner of the screen.

step.name: Select the voicemail
step.text: Tap the caller’s name or number to access their voicemail message.

itemListElement.text: Browse the list of voicemails.
Tap the caller’s name or phone number.

step.name: Read or listen to the message
step.text: Read the transcript under Transcription or tap the Play button to listen to the voicemail.

itemListElement.text: Check the Transcription section to read the voicemail text.
Tap the Play button if you prefer to listen to the voicemail audio.

keyPoints.title: Introduction to Live Voicemail on iPhone
keyPoints.explanation: Live Voicemail, introduced with iOS 17, transcribes incoming calls in real-time without relying on extra apps, offering a private and handy way to see what callers are saying.

keyPoints.title: How does Live Voicemail work?
keyPoints.explanation: Live Voicemail shows real-time text of a caller’s message as they speak, allowing users to decide whether to answer or let it go to voicemail, all processed locally on the device.

keyPoints.title: Enabling Live Voicemail on iPhone
keyPoints.explanation: You can automatically enable Live Voicemail in Settings under Phone, or manually toggle it on through the Phone settings if it’s not enabled after updating to iOS 17 or later.

keyPoints.title: Using Live Voicemail during incoming calls
keyPoints.explanation: While receiving a call, you can tap the Voicemail icon to see live transcriptions of the message, giving you the option to answer immediately or decline, based on what you read.

keyPoints.title: Managing and customizing Live Voicemail messages
keyPoints.explanation: After a call, you can access transcripts in the Phone app's Voicemail section, read or listen to messages, and customize your voicemail greeting to set the right tone for callers.

title.rendered: iPhone 17 vs Pixel 10: Which Base Model Should You Buy?

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Price and Features: iPhone 17 and Pixel 10 both start at $799, but differ in hardware, display quality, camera setup, and built-in AI tools.
  • Design and Durability: iPhone 17 uses a lighter Ceramic Shield build with better water and scratch resistance, while Pixel 10 feels heavier and less resistant.
  • Display and Video: Both feature 6.3-inch OLED panels, but iPhone 17 delivers sharper resolution, adaptive refresh rates, and Dolby Vision for streaming.
  • Camera and Processing: Pixel 10 adds telephoto and ultra-wide lenses, while iPhone 17 leans on its A19 chip for steadier photos and Dolby Vision video.
  • Performance and Storage: Pixel 10 includes more RAM, but iPhone 17 runs faster overall with the A19 chip, offering comparable storage tiers at identical pricing.

Every year, Apple and Google go head-to-head with their flagship phones and 2025 is no different. The iPhone 17 and Pixel 10 are here, both starting at $799. Apple doubled down on hardware, bringing Pro-exclusive features to the base iPhone, while Google leaned heavily into AI and smart photography.

If you’re deciding which one deserves a spot in your pocket, this detailed comparison highlights where each phone shines and where it falls short.

Table of Contents
  • Quick Specs: iPhone 17 vs Pixel 10
  • Design and Build
  • Display Experience
  • Cameras
  • Performance
  • Battery and Charging
  • AI, Software, and Updates
  • Price and Availability
  • Final Verdict: iPhone 17 or Pixel 10?

Quick Specs: iPhone 17 vs Pixel 10

Design and Build

The Pixel 10 feels solid at 204g, but the iPhone 17 is noticeably lighter at 177g and a bit slimmer in hand. Both use aluminum frames with glass backs, though Apple adds its tougher Ceramic Shield 2 on the front: rated harder than the Pixel’s Gorilla Glass Victus 2.

Durability is another split. The Pixel 10 carries IP68 certification but only for 1.5m submersion. The iPhone 17 is rated for 6m, giving you more peace of mind if it takes a plunge.

In short, the Pixel 10 feels sturdy, but the iPhone 17 is lighter, more comfortable to hold, and better protected against scratches and water.

Display Experience

Both phones give you a 6.3-inch OLED that’s bright at 3000 nits and smooth at 120Hz. That’s where the similarities end.

The iPhone 17’s LTPO panel can shift refresh rates from 1Hz to 120Hz. It slows down on static screens to save battery and ramps up instantly for games or fast swipes. The Pixel 10 stays fixed at 120Hz, so while it looks smooth, it burns through more power when nothing’s moving.

  • Apple also packs in more pixels: 2622 × 1206 (~460 ppi) versus the Pixel’s 1080 × 2424 (~422 ppi). The difference shows in small text and fine details, where the iPhone looks sharper.
  • For video, the Pixel supports HDR10+, but the iPhone adds Dolby Vision, the format used by Netflix and Apple TV+. If you watch a lot of streaming content, Apple’s screen simply looks richer.

In short: the Pixel 10’s display is solid, but the iPhone 17 is sharper, smarter with refresh rates, and better for movies.

Cameras

Google arms the Pixel 10 with a triple setup: a 48MP main, 10.8MP telephoto with 5x zoom, and 13MP ultrawide. Apple keeps it simpler with dual 48MP sensors, wide and ultrawide. On paper, the Pixel clearly has more versatility, especially with the dedicated telephoto lens and features like Pixel Shift, Ultra HDR, and Best Take for fixing group shots.

Apple’s strength is in processing. The iPhone 17 leans on its larger sensors, sensor-shift OIS, and Dolby Vision HDR to deliver more consistent photos and video, even if it lacks the extra lens. It also records Dolby Vision video at up to 4K 60fps, something the Pixel can’t match.

Selfies follow the same trend. The Pixel has a 10.5MP ultrawide that fits more in the frame. The iPhone 17 uses an 18MP wide sensor paired with a 3D depth camera, which not only gives sharper selfies but also powers secure Face ID.

In short: If you want flexibility and zoom, the Pixel 10 offers more tools. If you care about video quality and consistency across shots, the iPhone 17 holds the edge.

Performance

The Pixel 10 runs on Google’s Tensor G5 chip with 12GB RAM, while the iPhone 17 uses Apple’s new A19 with 8GB RAM. On paper, the Pixel has more memory, but Apple’s silicon is faster and more efficient. The A19’s hexa-core CPU runs at higher clock speeds and pairs tightly with iOS 26, giving the iPhone smoother app launches and better sustained performance.

Graphics are another split. The Pixel relies on a PowerVR GPU, capable but tuned for efficiency. Apple’s 5-core GPU consistently delivers stronger gaming and video editing performance, and it’s backed by tighter integration with Metal-optimized apps.

Storage speeds matter too. The Pixel starts at 128GB with UFS 3.1 and 256GB with UFS 4.0. The iPhone skips 128GB and instead uses faster NVMe storage in 256GB and 512GB tiers. The best part is that the iPhone 17’s 256GB variant costs the same as the Pixel 10’s 128GB.

In short: Apple takes a massive lead in performance and also offers more storage space for the same price. 

Battery and Charging

The Pixel 10 packs a bigger 4970 mAh battery, and it shows. With 30W wired charging, you get about 55% in 30 minutes, plus 15W Qi2 wireless and even reverse wired charging. Google also adds a neat bypass charging mode to protect the battery during gaming.

The iPhone 17 runs smaller at 3692 mAh, but Apple balances it with software and the new A19 chip. Wired charging jumps to 25W, finally quicker than last year, and MagSafe/Qi2 wireless can also hit 25W, filling 50% in about 30 minutes. It also supports reverse wired charging, but no bypass mode like the Pixel.

In practice, the Pixel 10 lasts longer on a single charge and gives you more charging options. The iPhone 17 charges faster wirelessly and holds up well thanks to efficiency, but if all-day endurance is your priority, the Pixel has the edge.

In short: While the iPhone is generally more efficient with battery life, the Pixel’s larger battery alone can push it past the iPhone.

AI, Software, and Updates

This is where Pixel completely destroys iPhone. Google and therefore Pixel are software focused and it shows. The phone feels like it was built around the software and it’s new AI features. Google Gemini is more powerful than Siri and powers many features like Circle to Search, live translations as you scroll, email digests pulled straight from Gmail, photo editing with Magic Editor and Eraser, call screening, and even real-time camera smarts like Camera Coach.

Comparatively, Apple Intelligence is very basic. You get system-wide text tools, smarter photo edits, and Siri upgrades, but even now, Siri struggles with follow-up questions that Gemini breezes through. Apple Intelligence also leans on third-party help, like tapping ChatGPT for answers, which makes it feel more like a patch than a reinvention.

Both Apple and Google also went on a design overhaul this year. While the design is very subjective, we found better experience with Google’s Material 3 Expressive over the Apple’s Liquid Glass design. Everything is clearly visible and also the UI feels more fun compared to Apple’s premium glass elements.

Updates are solid on both sides. Google now promises seven years of major Android upgrades, while Apple doesn’t state numbers but has a proven track record of keeping iPhones updated for six to seven years or longer.

In short: If AI is the reason you upgrade, the Pixel 10 is the obvious pick. It feels alive with Gemini baked in everywhere, while the iPhone 17 is just getting started.

Price and Availability

The Pixel 10 was announced on August 20, 2025, and released on August 28. It starts at $799 for the 128 GB base model, with a 256 GB option priced higher.

The iPhone 17 followed on September 9, 2025, with pre-orders from September 12 and release on September 19. Apple also starts at $799, but that gets you 256 GB of storage. The 512 GB version costs $999.

In short: both flagships share the same $799 entry point in the US, but Apple offers double the storage at that price, while Google gives you the cheaper 128 GB entry tier.

Final Verdict: iPhone 17 or Pixel 10?

If you’re deep into Apple’s ecosystem and love light, sleek phones, the iPhone 17 is your best bet. It’s reliable, refined, and future-proof with iOS support. If you want hardware value and cutting-edge AI today, the Pixel 10 is the phone to beat. It’s heavier but smarter, with better cameras, bigger battery, and more daring features.

  • iPhone Air vs Samsung Galaxy S25 Edge: Which Ultra-Thin Flagship Wins
  • iPhone 17 vs iPhone 16: The Biggest Upgrade Apple Made This Year

mainEntity.name: Can I answer a call while Live Voicemail is transcribing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yup, absolutely! That’s one of Live Voicemail’s charm points. Tap the green Answer button at any moment while reading that transcription. The caller? They won’t know you’ve had a sneak peek till you pick up.

mainEntity.name: Why don't I see the Live Voicemail option on my iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: Live Voicemail plays with iPhone XS or newer, using iOS 17 or later. Tick those boxes and still no dice? Check if your region settings align, since it’s not rolled out globally just yet.

mainEntity.name: Does Live Voicemail work on Wi-Fi calling?

acceptedAnswer.text: Oh yes, it does. As long as your carrier supports it and you're on iOS 17 or later, you're all set.

mainEntity.name: How is Live Voicemail different from Visual Voicemail?

acceptedAnswer.text: Here’s the key difference: Visual Voicemail shows you a lineup of messages to play back. Live Voicemail, however, gives you live transcription as someone leaves that message, with the added ability to intervene mid-message.

mainEntity.name: Will my caller know I'm reading their voicemail live?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not a chance. Callers won’t catch wind of you viewing their message in real-time unless you answer. From their end, it’s voicemail as usual.

mainEntity.name: Is Live Voicemail available on all carriers?

acceptedAnswer.text: Live Voicemail works with most major carriers, but there’s some variation. If you've run into issues, a word with your carrier might help; they could need to tweak your voicemail settings.

mainEntity.name: How do I delete Live Voicemail transcripts?

acceptedAnswer.text: Deleting Live Voicemail messages mirrors usual ones: swipe left on the message list and tap Delete, or dive into the message and hit the trash icon.

acceptedAnswer.text: Live Voicemail plays with iPhone XS or newer, using iOS 17 or later. Tick those boxes and still no dice? Check if your region settings align, since it’s not rolled out globally just yet.

mainEntity.name: Does Live Voicemail work on Wi-Fi calling?

acceptedAnswer.text: Oh yes, it does. As long as your carrier supports it and you're on iOS 17 or later, you're all set.

mainEntity.name: How is Live Voicemail different from Visual Voicemail?

acceptedAnswer.text: Here’s the key difference: Visual Voicemail shows you a lineup of messages to play back. Live Voicemail, however, gives you live transcription as someone leaves that message, with the added ability to intervene mid-message.

mainEntity.name: Will my caller know I'm reading their voicemail live?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not a chance. Callers won’t catch wind of you viewing their message in real-time unless you answer. From their end, it’s voicemail as usual.

mainEntity.name: Is Live Voicemail available on all carriers?

acceptedAnswer.text: Live Voicemail works with most major carriers, but there’s some variation. If you've run into issues, a word with your carrier might help; they could need to tweak your voicemail settings.

mainEntity.name: How do I delete Live Voicemail transcripts?

acceptedAnswer.text: Deleting Live Voicemail messages mirrors usual ones: swipe left on the message list and tap Delete, or dive into the message and hit the trash icon.

mainEntity.name: Why is Live Voicemail not transcribing messages?

acceptedAnswer.text: Crummy audio quality, boisterous background antics, or unclear speech can toss the transcription off track. It performs best when callers speak clearly in peaceful zones. Restart your iPhone to resolve any temporary transcription issues.

keyPoints.title: Price and Core Features Comparison
keyPoints.explanation: Both the iPhone 17 and Pixel 10 are flagship smartphones starting at $799, but they differ notably in hardware, display, camera capabilities, and AI features.

keyPoints.title: Build Quality and Durability
keyPoints.explanation: The iPhone 17 boasts a lighter, more durable Ceramic Shield design with better water and scratch resistance, compared to the heavier, less water-resistant Pixel 10.

keyPoints.title: Display Quality and Video Support
keyPoints.explanation: Both phones have 6.3-inch OLED screens, but the iPhone 17 offers higher resolution, smarter refresh rate management, and Dolby Vision for enhanced streaming experience.

keyPoints.title: Camera Hardware and Processing Power
keyPoints.explanation: While the Pixel 10 has versatile camera lenses including telephoto and ultra-wide, the iPhone 17 excels in processing power, delivering consistent, high-quality photos and Dolby Vision videos.

keyPoints.title: Performance and Storage Options
keyPoints.explanation: The Pixel 10 features more RAM, but the iPhone 17's faster A19 chip outperforms in app performance, with similar storage options offered at the same price point.

title.rendered: 28 Best Apple Watch Faces to Try in 2026

content.rendered:
Your wrist lights up with your Apple Watch face, so it’s essential to pick one that truly reflects your personality and lifestyle. We’ve rounded up the best Apple Watch faces in watchOS 11 and watchOS 26 based on functionality, design, and customization.

So, whether you’re a fitness fanatic, productivity pro, or fashion enthusiast, there’s something here for you!

Table of Contents
  • 28 Best Apple Watch Faces You Should Try
    • 1. Waypoint (Apple Watch Ultra)
    • 2. Flow
    • 3. Exactograph
    • 4. Photos Face (Updated in watchOS 26)
    • 5. Flux (watchOS 11)
    • 6. Reflections (watchOS 11)
    • 7. Snoopy and Woodstock
    • 8. Palette
    • 9. Unity
    • 10. Metropolitan
    • 11. Lunar
    • 12. Playtime
    • 13. Astronomy
    • 14. Modular
    • 15. Artists
    • 16. Breathe
    • 17. California
    • 18. Contour
    • 19. Fire and Water
    • 20. GMT
    • 21. Infograph
    • 22. Memoji
    • 23. Mickey and Minnie Mouse
    • 24. Nike (Updated in watchOS 9)
    • 25. Pride
    • 26. Timelapse
    • 27. Toy Story
    • 28. Typograph
  • Make Your Apple Watch Truly Yours

28 Best Apple Watch Faces You Should Try

Apple offers a wide selection of watch faces, and each one can be personalized through the Complications section. Here’s a curated list of the top Apple Watch faces that bring both style and function to your wrist.

1. Waypoint (Apple Watch Ultra)

Waypoint is designed exclusively for the Apple Watch Ultra and is perfect for adventurers and outdoor enthusiasts. It includes a live compass built right into the watch face, letting you navigate your surroundings with ease. There’s also a dedicated complication for quick access to satellite communications, making it invaluable in remote areas.

2. Flow

Flow is one of the newest watch faces introduced in watchOS 26. It features Liquid Glass numerals that refract vibrant swirls of color, which shift dynamically as you move your wrist. This makes the face feel alive and fluid, offering a mesmerizing look while still keeping time front and center. It is best for users who love bold, artistic visuals and want a face that reacts to their movement.

3. Exactograph

This sleek and minimal design watch face is a modern reinterpretation of a regulator clock that separates the hours, minutes, and seconds into individual sub-dials, making it easy to read the time precisely. It is best suited for users who value accuracy and prefer a clean, structured aesthetic.

4. Photos Face (Updated in watchOS 26)

Want to see cherished memories every time you raise your wrist? The Photos face has received a stylish upgrade in watchOS 26 with the Liquid Glass design.

  • Translucent, morphing numerals adjust dynamically to complement your photo.
  • Option to shuffle through featured memories from your library.
  • Choose from vibrant “Glass” color overlays—Clear is best for that system-wide aesthetic.

The redesigned Watch Face Gallery also includes categorized collections like Health & Fitness, Photos, and Data Rich, making it easier to find your perfect match.

5. Flux (watchOS 11)

Apple has introduced significant display updates to the Watch Series 10, including support for a 1Hz refresh rate. To complement this feature, Apple has introduced a new watch face called Flux. It sports a minimal yet bold design, which only shows the time in large typography. Each second, you will see a bit of color fill from the bottom.

Moreover, the time numerals change shape every minute and hour. This mix-and-match of color and typography movement is fun to watch as time passes. You may customize the filling color and time font to align the watch face with your style preference.

While testing the Flux watch face, I noticed this works best on the Apple Watch Series 10 and Watch Ultra. I could only add it to my watch faces library in older models, but it didn’t appear on the display.

6. Reflections (watchOS 11)

If you want a cool yet elegant-looking watch face, consider this Reflections face. It has a unique shimmering sunburst dial that responds to your wrist motions in a subtle way. So, the nostalgic analog style looks dynamic from every angle. Moreover, the metallic finish goes well with the titanium models of Apple Watch Series 10 and Watch Ultra.

You may customize the watch face color to complement your Apple Watch band. Additionally, this offers four customizable complications to keep you productive.

7. Snoopy and Woodstock

The Snoopy and Woodstock Apple Watch face is a delightful addition for fans of the beloved Peanuts characters. This whimsical watch face brings Snoopy, the iconic beagle, and Woodstock, his loyal feathered friend, to life on your wrist.

This watch face can give you a nostalgic experience every time you check the time or interact with your Apple Watch. It adds a dash of whimsy to your daily routine and is ideal for those who value Snoopy and Wo2odstock’s classic charm. If you want to learn more, please go through our guide on how to get the Snoopy Watch face.

8. Palette

The Palette Apple Watch face is a stunning and customizable display option that transforms time into a captivating spectrum of enchanting colors that gracefully evolve throughout the day. This innovative watch face design incorporates three unique layers that elegantly overlap, offering a truly mesmerizing visual experience.

Each layer of the watch face represents a distinct element of time, which blends together to form a beautiful and dynamic display. I’d advise you to use the Palette face on the Apple Watch, as it infuses your personality and the overall wearable experience with creativity.

9. Unity

The Black Unity Apple Watch face celebrates the harmony of Black history and culture. It is genuinely unique and embraces a deep sense of unity and solidarity.

This watch face features vibrant colors inspired by the Pan-African flag and is adorned with abstract flowers in the same colors. Moreover, users can choose either a single flower or full-bloom style according to their preference. Whenever you raise your wrist, the flowers will bloom and fill in.

It’s safe to assume this watch face is for everyone who understands the importance of cultural values. This example of diversity and inclusion is definitely a must-have

10. Metropolitan

Metropolitan is the perfect choice for a traditional look. When it comes to customization, this Apple Watch face comes in four distinct designs. You may also select the backdrop colors from a range of color palettes. One of the most intriguing characteristics is that when you turn your wrist upside down, the numbers fade away, leaving pills behind. 

This watch face goes nicely with both formal and semi-formal attire. When heading to an interview, I prefer a plain watch face, making Metropolitan my personal favorite.

11. Lunar

If you want to keep track of both lunar phases and dates, Lunar is the best watch face for your Apple Watch. One of the most intriguing aspects of this watch face is that when you rotate the circular dial, the moon’s form and date change, giving you a clear image of how the moon will appear on that specific day.

You can change the color of the second hand and switch between digital and analog modes. You may also select from three calendars: Chinese, Hebrew, and Islamic. This stylish Apple Watch face will work well with casual clothing, especially when heading out at night.

12. Playtime 

Do you adore graphics as much as I do? If so, Playtime is the ideal Apple Watch face for you. Apple has teamed with Joi Fulton to provide a one-of-a-kind experience. The custom-built characters are entertaining to play with since they interact with you when you tap on them. Plus, the backdrop has a distinct movement when you rotate the Digital Crown.

When it comes to modifications, there are several background shadow adjustment possibilities. You may also choose whether or not to include background. If you’re heading to a venue where you’ll be interacting with tiny children, you should alter your watch face to Playtime.

13. Astronomy

If you enjoy talking about space, Astronomy is the best Apple Watch face for you. As you turn the Digital Crown, you may see a pictorial representation of the change between day and night. You may also access the zoom-in and zoom-out functions by tapping on the screen.

The Apple Watch face is very configurable regarding typefaces, with three options: Classic, Contemporary, and Rounded. You may view the Earth, moon, solar system, or any other random planet using full or random style choices. If you’re heading to a planetarium, you should definitely pick Astronomy as your primary watch face.

14. Modular 

Here’s an Apple Watch face for folks who enjoy statistics. Modular is available in three distinct versions: Basic, Small, and Dual. Its display screen provides a wealth of information with a glance and a tap.

The basic or dual versions also have few customization options other than changing the backdrop color and turning on or off the background. Still, the compact version has extra customization options that enable you to choose between analog and digital clocks. If you’re an athlete or prefer to spend most of your time at the gym, this is the finest Apple Watch face you can get.

15. Artists

If you prefer something minimalist yet creative, the Artist watch face is worth checking out. It includes a portrait by artist Geoff McFetridge.

You can change the design by touching the face. It also changes automatically as you lift your wrist. Moreover, it improves the appearance of the always-on display. This popular Apple Watch face can be used when visiting an art gallery.

16. Breathe

Do you need a bit of calm in your busy life? Here’s a watch face that can help. It resembles the design and animations of the Mindfulness app.

When you tap the watch face, you’ll be sent directly to the Mindfulness app for a guided meditation session. As a result, it’s a wonderful alternative for anybody looking to incorporate more mindfulness into their day. While attending a Meditation or Yoga Center, you may wear your Apple Watch with this contemplative face.

17. California

With this timeless design from California, you can give your Apple Watch a classic, formal look. It provides a variety of dial marker alternatives to get the desired design. It includes two dial options, rectangular and circular.

You may also change the symbols in seven different ways. Also, you get to select from a range of backdrop displays. I recommend wearing this watch face to an interview or any professional meeting since it will completely suit your formal attire.

18. Contour

If you want to seem stylish, you need this Contour face for your Apple Watch. The display’s appearance is influenced by time and can gradually alter to highlight the current hour. When you tap a number on the screen, the numerals execute an inward circular ripple.

You may change the watch’s style to regular or rounded to match your outfit. You may also choose whether or not to utilize the dial color feature. This unique watch face will complement your everyday outfits.

19. Fire and Water

Fire and water are two important components that Apple incorporates in its watch faces. Apple spent a lot of time creating these stunning faces for its products, which is why all its wallpapers and watch faces appear so realistic.

You may change the color of the watch face by selecting one of two options: fire or water. Additionally, you can enable the option that showcases any of the two randomly as your backdrop. The dial is available in two sizes: rectangular and circular. You can wear this as the face of your watch if you’re heading to a campfire or beach.

20. GMT

If you’re working across time zones or traveling, here’s a good watch face resembling old analog designs. It features two dials. The inner one shows your local time, while the outer one can show a second timezone.

The two-toned color scheme depicts the day and night, sunrise and sunset, in the selected city. You can customize the colors as you like and add complications to the four outer corners.

21. Infograph 

If you’re working across time zones or traveling, this GMT watch face is nice. It seems like an old-school analog design. There are two dials on it. The inside displays your current time, while the outside may display a second timezone. The time in the outside outlet may be changed by touching the display and using the Apple Watch’s Digital Crown.

The two-toned color scheme reflects the selected city’s day and night, as well as sunrise and sunset. You can change the colors and add complexity to the four outside corners as you see fit. Wear this watch face with your party clothes.

22. Memoji

Do you like Memoji? Use this watch face to add them to your wrist and enjoy watching them animate. Display your one-of-a-kind designs and personalize your watch. I liked how the Memoji interacted with you when you tapped it.

The little information panel at the bottom is fully customizable. Our comprehensive guide on utilizing Memoji on Apple Watch provides more information. You can also confidently wear this watch face when going out with your buddies.

23. Mickey and Minnie Mouse 

In honor of one of our favorite cartoons from the 90s, Apple has included a watch face featuring Mickey and Minnie Mouse. The faces are one-of-a-kind, and when you tap the display, you’ll hear the sweet voices of the characters telling you the time.

The outfits of the two characters may be changed; there are several colors for Minnie Mouse, but just two clothing color possibilities for Mickey Mouse. If you were born in the 90s, you might consider making this your primary watch face.

24. Nike (Updated in watchOS 9)

Nike’s faces for the Apple Watch are thanks to the collaboration of two of the most popular brands. There are five variations: Analog, Bounce, Compact, Digital, and Hybrid. One of the most notable features of this face is that the different variants react differently when you tap or twist the Digital Crown.

You can customize the faces to match your outfit by selecting various colors. A few versions also let you change between styles, dials, and digital or analog clocks. For example, you can use this cool Nike Apple Watch face while attending an LA game.

25. Pride 

When the surrounding colors are complementary, unique colors mix smoothly. Apple believes in equality and has created a special Pride watch face to promote the LGBTQ community. The color-mixed threads work well together to indicate time uniquely. When you tap the threads or turn the Digital Crown, vibration is sent across the treads.

The distinct face has a customization option to enable or disable the backdrop. This is a special face that demands a special occasion, so save it for Pride Month.

26. Timelapse

The Timelapse watch face showcases photographs of stunning sites worldwide for all travel enthusiasts. At your location, the landscape or cityscape changes dynamically with the passage of time.

I personally enjoy the animation of different locations, which can be accessed via a few simple taps. It’s a great way to experience views of your ideal places even if you haven’t visited them. While traveling, you may utilize this as your watch face.

27. Toy Story

Appease the child in you with this adorable watch face that features a scene from the Toy Story movie. The cute little animations of all the main Toy Story characters, such as Buzz Lightyear and Woody, are present.

You can also tap on the watch’s face to see more animations from different characters. This watch face has a playful and fun look on your watch and can be worn when attending your ward’s school.

28. Typograph

Try the typograph face, which offers three custom styles: Classic, Modern, and Rounded, for a unique look. You can choose to view just four numbers or all 12 numbers of the clock face.

You can also pick Arabic, Arabic Indic, Devanagari, and Roman symbols in addition to the default style. I’d prefer to use this watch face with formals. What do you say?

Make Your Apple Watch Truly Yours

With so many watch face options on watchOS 11 and 26, there’s no shortage of ways to personalize your Apple Watch. From health tracking to cultural celebration, there’s a face that fits every vibe and purpose.

Let us know in the comments which Apple Watch face is your favorite!

mainEntity.name: Is iOS 26 better than iOS 18?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. iOS 26 introduces a visually rich design, smarter system tools, and improved app interfaces—especially if you're on a newer iPhone.

mainEntity.name: Will iOS 26 slow down older iPhones?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not necessarily. While older models like the iPhone 11 may not run animations as smoothly, Apple has optimized performance across supported devices. Battery health and storage space may still affect your experience.

mainEntity.name: Do I need Premium for a blue checkmark?

mainEntity.name: Is X Premium ad-free?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not entirely. Basic has full ads, Premium halves them in main timelines, and Premium+ is mostly ad-free everywhere, but you might see occasional sponsored posts.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between the blue checkmarks and the gold and grey checkmarks?

acceptedAnswer.text: Blue is for individual Premium subscribers. Gold means an official business or non-profit via Verified Organizations. Grey is for governments or multilateral organizations. They come with extras like badges for affiliates and premium support for orgs.

mainEntity.name: Is the previous legacy blue checkmark and X Premium subscription checkmark same?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not really. The legacy one was for active, notable, authentic accounts verified by X's old system. The new blue is exclusive to active subscribers, with no fame check required.

mainEntity.name: Can I answer a call while Live Voicemail is transcribing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yup, absolutely! That’s one of Live Voicemail’s charm points. Tap the green Answer button at any moment while reading that transcription. The caller? They won’t know you’ve had a sneak peek till you pick up.

mainEntity.name: Why don't I see the Live Voicemail option on my iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: Live Voicemail plays with iPhone XS or newer, using iOS 17 or later. Tick those boxes and still no dice? Check if your region settings align, since it’s not rolled out globally just yet.

mainEntity.name: Does Live Voicemail work on Wi-Fi calling?

acceptedAnswer.text: Oh yes, it does. As long as your carrier supports it and you're on iOS 17 or later, you're all set.

mainEntity.name: How is Live Voicemail different from Visual Voicemail?

acceptedAnswer.text: Here’s the key difference: Visual Voicemail shows you a lineup of messages to play back. Live Voicemail, however, gives you live transcription as someone leaves that message, with the added ability to intervene mid-message.

mainEntity.name: Will my caller know I'm reading their voicemail live?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not a chance. Callers won’t catch wind of you viewing their message in real-time unless you answer. From their end, it’s voicemail as usual.

mainEntity.name: Is Live Voicemail available on all carriers?

acceptedAnswer.text: Live Voicemail works with most major carriers, but there’s some variation. If you've run into issues, a word with your carrier might help; they could need to tweak your voicemail settings.

mainEntity.name: How do I delete Live Voicemail transcripts?

acceptedAnswer.text: Deleting Live Voicemail messages mirrors usual ones: swipe left on the message list and tap Delete, or dive into the message and hit the trash icon.

mainEntity.name: Why is Live Voicemail not transcribing messages?

acceptedAnswer.text: Crummy audio quality, boisterous background antics, or unclear speech can toss the transcription off track. It performs best when callers speak clearly in peaceful zones. Restart your iPhone to resolve any temporary transcription issues.
