title.rendered: iPhone Air and iPhone 17 Pro Boxes Finally Revealed

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Apple’s Packaging Reveal Breaks Tradition: Photos of the new iPhone Air and iPhone 17 Pro packaging surfaced online, breaking Apple’s usual secrecy and generating excitement among collectors and enthusiasts.
  • Minimalist Box Design Confirmed from Retail Sources: The new iPhones feature Apple’s classic minimalist packaging, now shown directly from retail distribution centers rather than polished press images, adding to the anticipation.
  • Pre-Order Demand Indicates a Blockbuster Launch: Strong early demand, especially for the iPhone 17 Pro Max, has led to extended shipping times, highlighting the high anticipation for the upcoming release.
  • Inside the Box: New Tech and Connectivity Features: The iPhones include the latest N1 chip supporting Wi-Fi 7 (limited to 160 MHz), Bluetooth 6, and Thread, marking significant upgrades despite some technical limitations.
  • Regional Changes and Regulatory Delays for Features: The iPhone 17 series is now eSIM-only in many countries, including the US, Canada, Japan, Mexico, and Saudi Arabia, with features like Live Translation delayed in the EU due to regulations.

Apple fans finally have their first real look at the packaging for the new iPhone Air and iPhone 17 Pro. The boxes surfaced online after T-Mobile president Jon Freier shared photos of them, breaking Apple’s usual tradition of keeping packaging under wraps until launch week. This reveal is notable because Apple didn’t include box renders in its latest environmental reports, leaving collectors and enthusiasts curious.

The images show the minimalist box design Apple has stuck with for years, but this time, they come directly from retail distribution centers rather than polished Apple press materials. Apple’s iPhone Upgrade Program page also briefly displayed the new boxes, adding to the excitement ahead of launch.

Both the iPhone 17 Pro and iPhone Air officially launch worldwide on September 19, 2025, but early buyers are already facing longer waits. Pre-orders kicked off last week, and demand for the iPhone 17 Pro Max in particular was so strong that some delivery estimates slipped into October within hours. Even certain iPhone Air and standard iPhone 17 Pro models are now showing extended shipping times, signaling another blockbuster launch for Apple.

What’s New Inside the Box

Beyond the packaging, the new iPhones come with Apple’s latest N1 chip. It brings Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, and Thread connectivity, but with a catch. FCC filings confirm the chip only supports 160 MHz channel bandwidth, meaning users won’t get the full speed potential of Wi-Fi 7’s 320 MHz. For most people, this won’t be a dealbreaker, but it’s a technical limitation worth noting.

Apple is also doubling down on eSIM. The iPhone 17 series is eSIM-only in more countries now, including Canada, Japan, Mexico, and Saudi Arabia. The U.S. had already made the switch earlier, and it looks like Apple is set on phasing out physical SIM slots worldwide.

One controversial change tied to regional rules is Apple’s Live Translation feature for AirPods. It won’t be available to users in the European Union at launch due to the bloc’s strict Digital Markets Act. The feature works elsewhere, but European customers with EU-based Apple accounts will have to wait until Apple finds a regulatory workaround.

The Final Countdown

With just days left until launch, the leaked box images have added fuel to the hype around Apple’s newest lineup. Whether you’re eyeing the sleek iPhone Air or the powerhouse iPhone 17 Pro, getting your hands on one may take longer than expected if you haven’t pre-ordered already. For now, at least the mystery of what the boxes look like is solved.

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. iOS 26 introduces a visually rich design, smarter system tools, and improved app interfaces—especially if you're on a newer iPhone.

mainEntity.name: Will iOS 26 slow down older iPhones?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not necessarily. While older models like the iPhone 11 may not run animations as smoothly, Apple has optimized performance across supported devices. Battery health and storage space may still affect your experience.

mainEntity.name: Can I get X Premium for free?

acceptedAnswer.text: No free trial is available. Sometimes high-follower accounts get complimentary upgrades, but generally, it's paid-only.

mainEntity.name: Do I need Premium for a blue checkmark?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. At least Premium or Premium+ (or Verified Organizations) is required.

mainEntity.name: Is X Premium ad-free?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not entirely. Basic has full ads, Premium halves them in main timelines, and Premium+ is mostly ad-free everywhere, but you might see occasional sponsored posts.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between the blue checkmarks and the gold and grey checkmarks?

acceptedAnswer.text: Blue is for individual Premium subscribers. Gold means an official business or non-profit via Verified Organizations. Grey is for governments or multilateral organizations. They come with extras like badges for affiliates and premium support for orgs.

mainEntity.name: Is the previous legacy blue checkmark and X Premium subscription checkmark same?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not really. The legacy one was for active, notable, authentic accounts verified by X's old system. The new blue is exclusive to active subscribers, with no fame check required.

mainEntity.name: Can I answer a call while Live Voicemail is transcribing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yup, absolutely! That’s one of Live Voicemail’s charm points. Tap the green Answer button at any moment while reading that transcription. The caller? They won’t know you’ve had a sneak peek till you pick up.

mainEntity.name: Why don't I see the Live Voicemail option on my iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: Live Voicemail plays with iPhone XS or newer, using iOS 17 or later. Tick those boxes and still no dice? Check if your region settings align, since it’s not rolled out globally just yet.

mainEntity.name: Does Live Voicemail work on Wi-Fi calling?

acceptedAnswer.text: Oh yes, it does. As long as your carrier supports it and you're on iOS 17 or later, you're all set.

mainEntity.name: How is Live Voicemail different from Visual Voicemail?

acceptedAnswer.text: Here’s the key difference: Visual Voicemail shows you a lineup of messages to play back. Live Voicemail, however, gives you live transcription as someone leaves that message, with the added ability to intervene mid-message.

mainEntity.name: Will my caller know I'm reading their voicemail live?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not a chance. Callers won’t catch wind of you viewing their message in real-time unless you answer. From their end, it’s voicemail as usual.

mainEntity.name: Is Live Voicemail available on all carriers?

acceptedAnswer.text: Live Voicemail works with most major carriers, but there’s some variation. If you've run into issues, a word with your carrier might help; they could need to tweak your voicemail settings.

mainEntity.name: How do I delete Live Voicemail transcripts?

acceptedAnswer.text: Deleting Live Voicemail messages mirrors usual ones: swipe left on the message list and tap Delete, or dive into the message and hit the trash icon.

mainEntity.name: Why is Live Voicemail not transcribing messages?

acceptedAnswer.text: Crummy audio quality, boisterous background antics, or unclear speech can toss the transcription off track. It performs best when callers speak clearly in peaceful zones. Restart your iPhone to resolve any temporary transcription issues.

keyPoints.title: Apple's Packaging Reveal Breaks Tradition
keyPoints.explanation: Photos of the new iPhone Air and iPhone 17 Pro packaging surfaced online, breaking Apple's usual secrecy and generating excitement among collectors and enthusiasts.

keyPoints.title: Minimalist Box Design Confirmed from Retail Sources
keyPoints.explanation: The new iPhones feature Apple's classic minimalist packaging, now shown directly from retail distribution centers rather than polished press images, adding to the anticipation.

keyPoints.title: Pre-Order Demand Indicates a Blockbuster Launch
keyPoints.explanation: Strong early demand, especially for the iPhone 17 Pro Max, has led to extended shipping times, highlighting the high anticipation for the upcoming release.

keyPoints.title: Inside the Box: New Tech and Connectivity Features
keyPoints.explanation: The iPhones include the latest N1 chip supporting Wi-Fi 7 (limited to 160 MHz), Bluetooth 6, and Thread, marking significant upgrades despite some technical limitations.

keyPoints.title: Regional Changes and Regulatory Delays for Features**
keyPoints.explanation: The iPhone 17 series is now eSIM-only in many countries, including the US, Canada, Japan, Mexico, and Saudi Arabia, with features like Live Translation delayed in the EU due to regulations.

title.rendered: iPhone 17 Pro vs iPhone Air: Choosing Between Might and Light

content.rendered:
Apple’s iPhone 17 “Awe Dropping” event brought not one, but three brand new iPhones: the iPhone 17 and the iPhone 17 Pro/Pro Max, and the ultra-sleek iPhone Air. While the iPhone 17 indeed received many upgrades over its predecessor, the iPhone Air and iPhone 17 Pro grabbed all the spotlight. Both are stunning, both are fast, and both come with Apple’s cutting-edge A19 Pro chip, but they target very different kinds of users.

If you’re wondering which one among the two is right for you, you’re at the right place. Let’s break it down.

iPhone Air vs. iPhone 17 Pro: Quick Specs Comparison

Design and Build

Ditching the previous titanium design, the iPhone 17 Pro uses an aircraft-grade aluminum unibody with a slightly larger footprint, which looks and feels premium, sturdy, and ready for anything. For the first time, Apple has wrapped both the front and back in Ceramic Shield 2, making it far more scratch- and crack-resistant. It’s also built around a new internal “plateau” design that helps fit a bigger battery and vapor-chamber cooling system.

The iPhone Air, meanwhile, is Apple’s most radical design in years. At just 5.6 mm thin, it’s the thinnest iPhone ever. Made of polished grade 5 titanium, it looks like jewelry and feels impossibly light. Apple even used the same plateau architecture to make space for a solid battery despite the slim frame.

Display

When it comes to display quality, both phones shine equally. The only difference between the two is the display size. While the iPhone 17 Pro features a 6.3-inch display, the ultra-sleek iPhone Air offers a 6.5-inch display. Other than that, both phones have the same Super Retina XDR ProMotion display with 3000 nits of peak brightness outdoors. This makes the iPhone Air feel much closer to its Pro sibling.

Performance and Battery

Just like their identical display tech, both phones feature Apple’s blazing-fast A19 Pro chipset under the hood. Additionally, both phones include the new N1 wireless chip, offering Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, and super fast cellular performance. For casual users, the day-to-day performance feels virtually identical.

Battery life, on the other hand, tilts in favor of the iPhone 17 Pro, thanks to the newly introduced vapor chamber cooling system. Besides this, the unibody design of the iPhone 17 Pro also allowed Apple to create a larger space for the battery. While Apple has optimized the iPhone Air’s battery to last the entire day, impressive for its size, it can’t quite match the Pro’s endurance.

Camera System

This is where everything falls apart. Like its predecessor, the iPhone 17 Pro pulls out all the stops with a triple 48 MP Fusion system: Main, Ultra Wide, and a new Telephoto with a tetraprism design that delivers up to 8× optical-quality zoom and 40× digital zoom. It’s a perfect device for photography enthusiasts and professional content creators.

The iPhone Air offers a single 48 MP Fusion main camera optical-quality 2x Telephoto. While any phone featuring a single rear camera in 2025 is an instant turn-off, the iPhone Air’s camera quality is surprisingly more than enough for everyday shooters and social media creators.

Both iPhones feature the same 18 MP Center Stage front camera, which can record in landscape mode even when you’re holding the phone vertically.

Price and Value

The iPhone 17 Pro, being the flagship model, obviously comes at a higher price than the iPhone Air — $1,099. However, it has the absolute best Apple has to offer: the most advanced cameras, longest battery life, and highest performance in a durable body, so it’s worth every penny.

Despite offering nearly identical day-to-day performance, the iPhone Air comes at a friendlier price — $999.. If you value thinness, lightness, and style while still getting top-tier speed and beautiful display tech, the iPhone Air isn’t a bad choice either.

Which One Should You Buy?

The iPhone 17 Pro is built for those who push their phone to the limits: creators, power users, and anyone who needs the best cameras and battery Apple has ever made. The iPhone Air, on the other hand, is for people who want a cutting-edge iPhone that’s unbelievably thin, feather-light, and still fast enough for everything.

  • If you want a professional workhorse, go for the iPhone 17 Pro.
  • If you want a stylish everyday flagship, the iPhone Air is the one to get.

If you could upgrade today, which would you choose: Pro or Air? Share your thoughts in the comments below.

  • iPhone 17 vs iPhone 16: The Biggest Upgrade Apple Made This Year

mainEntity.name: Can I answer a call while Live Voicemail is transcribing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yup, absolutely! That’s one of Live Voicemail’s charm points. Tap the green Answer button at any moment while reading that transcription. The caller? They won’t know you’ve had a sneak peek till you pick up.

mainEntity.name: Why don't I see the Live Voicemail option on my iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: Live Voicemail plays with iPhone XS or newer, using iOS 17 or later. Tick those boxes and still no dice? Check if your region settings align, since it’s not rolled out globally just yet.

mainEntity.name: Does Live Voicemail work on Wi-Fi calling?

acceptedAnswer.text: Oh yes, it does. As long as your carrier supports it and you're on iOS 17 or later, you're all set.

mainEntity.name: How is Live Voicemail different from Visual Voicemail?

acceptedAnswer.text: Here’s the key difference: Visual Voicemail shows you a lineup of messages to play back. Live Voicemail, however, gives you live transcription as someone leaves that message, with the added ability to intervene mid-message.

mainEntity.name: Will my caller know I'm reading their voicemail live?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not a chance. Callers won’t catch wind of you viewing their message in real-time unless you answer. From their end, it’s voicemail as usual.

mainEntity.name: Is Live Voicemail available on all carriers?

acceptedAnswer.text: Live Voicemail works with most major carriers, but there’s some variation. If you've run into issues, a word with your carrier might help; they could need to tweak your voicemail settings.

mainEntity.name: How do I delete Live Voicemail transcripts?

acceptedAnswer.text: Deleting Live Voicemail messages mirrors usual ones: swipe left on the message list and tap Delete, or dive into the message and hit the trash icon.

mainEntity.name: Why is Live Voicemail not transcribing messages?

acceptedAnswer.text: Crummy audio quality, boisterous background antics, or unclear speech can toss the transcription off track. It performs best when callers speak clearly in peaceful zones. Restart your iPhone to resolve any temporary transcription issues.

title.rendered: How to Make Your iPhone Lock Screen Wallpaper Shuffle Through Photos

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Photo Shuffle changes your Lock Screen photo automatically using selected images from categories, albums, or manual picks at intervals you choose.
  • Set up Photo Shuffle from Lock Screen or Settings—pick photos manually or by theme, then choose when they should rotate.
  • You can shuffle on tap, lock, hourly, or daily—just tap the three dots during customization to change how often the photo updates.
  • Customize which images appear in Photo Shuffle by filtering for people, nature, pets, or specific albums to better reflect your favorites.
  • Photo Shuffle adds a dynamic, personal touch to your iPhone Lock Screen, keeping it fresh with meaningful memories.

What’s better than seeing one of your favorite pictures on your iPhone Lock Screen? With the Photo Shuffle feature, you can see a different picture each time you pick up your iPhone. Here’s how to use Photo Shuffle to change your iPhone wallpaper automatically.

Table of Contents
  • What is Photo Shuffle?
  • How to Create Photo Shuffle on Your iPhone
  • How to change Photo Shuffle frequency on your iPhone

What is Photo Shuffle?

Apple’s Photo Shuffle feature for iPhone lets you see multiple photos of your favorites, your friends, or your featured photos right on your iPhone Lock screen. It then displays a different photo whenever you tap or lock your device or based on a timeframe.

You can choose which pictures to use, apply a filter like other Lock screen images, and decide how often Photo Shuffle changes the pictures.

Follow along to set up Photo Shuffle on iPhone to view pictures of people, pets, nature, cities, or other subjects.

How to Create Photo Shuffle on Your iPhone

You can customize your iPhone Lock screen with Photo Shuffle in the Settings app or from the Lock screen itself. 

  1. Do one of the following to use the feature for a new Lock screen setup:
    • Open the Settings app, select Wallpaper, and tap Add New Wallpaper below.
    • Go to Lock Screen, unlock your device but remain on the Lock Screen, and then long-press an empty space. Tap the plus sign below.
  2. On the Add New Wallpaper screen, tap on Photo Shuffle. 
  3. You can then customize the photos that display on the subsequent screen as described below:
    • People, Pets, Nature, or Cities: Pick from the categories listed like People or Pets. Additionally, you can select more than one for a nice collection.
    • Album: Choose Album and then tap the album name on the right to select your preferred album from Photos.
    • Select Photos Manually: Tap this option to choose the exact pictures you want to use and move onto Step 7.
  4. Next to Shuffle Frequency, use the drop-down menu to choose how or when to change the pictures. You can pick On Tap, On Lock, Hourly, or Daily.
  5. When you finish, select Use Featured Photos or Use Album, depending on what you picked.
  6. You can then add widgets or apply a filter on the preview. If you used Select Photos Manually, tap the three dots to adjust the frequency.
  7. Tap Add when you’re done.

Finish up by setting a wallpaper pair for your Lock and Home Screen or picking a particular Home Screen background as normal.

How to change Photo Shuffle frequency on your iPhone

After you create a Photo Shuffle, you can set the frequency of the pictures. Here’s how to do it.

  1. Go to the Lock Screen, then long-press the screen and pick Customize at the bottom.
  2. Choose Lock Screen on the left.
  3. Select the category, album, or photos icon in the lower left corner, depending on what you picked for your Photo Shuffle. Then, make your changes to the pictures to display.
  4. Use the three dots in the lower right corner to change the shuffle frequency.
  5. Tap Done when you finish and tap the screen to set the updated Lock screen Photo Shuffle.

Love your Lock Screen!

The Photo Shuffle feature for your iPhone Lock Screen can not only spruce up your display but also show you your favorite pictures whenever you pick up your device. This terrific customization option can enhance your iPhone experience and make you love your Lock screen.

What do you think of the feature? Will you shuffle photos on your iPhone? Let us know!

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. iOS 26 introduces a visually rich design, smarter system tools, and improved app interfaces—especially if you're on a newer iPhone.

acceptedAnswer.text: Blue is for individual Premium subscribers. Gold means an official business or non-profit via Verified Organizations. Grey is for governments or multilateral organizations. They come with extras like badges for affiliates and premium support for orgs.

mainEntity.name: Is the previous legacy blue checkmark and X Premium subscription checkmark same?

mainEntity.name: Can I answer a call while Live Voicemail is transcribing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yup, absolutely! That’s one of Live Voicemail’s charm points. Tap the green Answer button at any moment while reading that transcription. The caller? They won’t know you’ve had a sneak peek till you pick up.

mainEntity.name: Why don't I see the Live Voicemail option on my iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: Live Voicemail plays with iPhone XS or newer, using iOS 17 or later. Tick those boxes and still no dice? Check if your region settings align, since it’s not rolled out globally just yet.

mainEntity.name: Does Live Voicemail work on Wi-Fi calling?

acceptedAnswer.text: Oh yes, it does. As long as your carrier supports it and you're on iOS 17 or later, you're all set.

mainEntity.name: How is Live Voicemail different from Visual Voicemail?

acceptedAnswer.text: Here’s the key difference: Visual Voicemail shows you a lineup of messages to play back. Live Voicemail, however, gives you live transcription as someone leaves that message, with the added ability to intervene mid-message.

mainEntity.name: Will my caller know I'm reading their voicemail live?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not a chance. Callers won’t catch wind of you viewing their message in real-time unless you answer. From their end, it’s voicemail as usual.

mainEntity.name: Is Live Voicemail available on all carriers?

acceptedAnswer.text: Live Voicemail works with most major carriers, but there’s some variation. If you've run into issues, a word with your carrier might help; they could need to tweak your voicemail settings.

mainEntity.name: How do I delete Live Voicemail transcripts?

acceptedAnswer.text: Deleting Live Voicemail messages mirrors usual ones: swipe left on the message list and tap Delete, or dive into the message and hit the trash icon.

mainEntity.name: Why is Live Voicemail not transcribing messages?

acceptedAnswer.text: Crummy audio quality, boisterous background antics, or unclear speech can toss the transcription off track. It performs best when callers speak clearly in peaceful zones. Restart your iPhone to resolve any temporary transcription issues.

@graph.name: How to create Photo Shuffle on your iPhone
@graph.description: Set up a dynamic Photo Shuffle Lock Screen on your iPhone so your favorite pictures rotate automatically on tap, on lock, hourly, or daily.

tool.name: iPhone with Face ID or Touch ID

step.name: Start a new Lock Screen
step.text: Begin by creating a fresh Lock Screen so Photo Shuffle can be applied cleanly.

itemListElement.text: Open Settings, tap Wallpaper, then tap Add New Wallpaper.
Or wake your iPhone, stay on the Lock Screen, touch and hold an empty area, then tap the plus button.

step.name: Choose Photo Shuffle
step.text: On the Add New Wallpaper screen, pick Photo Shuffle to let iOS rotate through selected images.

itemListElement.text: Tap Photo Shuffle on the wallpaper gallery.

step.name: Pick your photos by category
step.text: Let iOS surface your best shots by choosing built in categories for a quick setup.

itemListElement.text: Select People, Pets, Nature, or Cities to have iOS suggest featured photos.
Choose more than one category if you want a broader mix.

step.name: Select an album, optional
step.text: Use a specific album if you already group the photos you want to see.

itemListElement.text: Tap Album, then pick your preferred album from Photos.

step.name: Select photos manually, optional
step.text: Hand pick the exact images if you want full control over what appears.

itemListElement.text: Tap Select Photos Manually, then choose the pictures you want to include.

step.name: Set the shuffle frequency
step.text: Decide how often your Lock Screen photo should change so it matches your routine.

itemListElement.text: Open the Shuffle Frequency menu.
Choose On Tap, On Lock, Hourly, or Daily.

step.name: Confirm your source
step.text: Lock in your selection so iOS knows which photos to rotate through.

itemListElement.text: Tap Use Featured Photos if you used categories.
Tap Use Album if you selected an album.

step.name: Customize and save
step.text: Tweak the look, then add the wallpaper to finish the setup.

itemListElement.text: Add widgets or apply a filter on the preview.
If you selected photos manually, tap the three dots to adjust the frequency.
Tap Add when you are done.

@graph.name: How to change Photo Shuffle frequency on your iPhone
@graph.description: Quickly change how often your iPhone’s Photo Shuffle updates on the Lock Screen so your favorite images rotate on your schedule.

tool.name: iPhone with Face ID or Touch ID

step.name: Enter Lock Screen edit mode
step.text: Start from your Lock Screen so you can edit the Photo Shuffle settings.

itemListElement.text: Wake your iPhone and remain on the Lock Screen.
Touch and hold the screen until the wallpaper gallery appears.
Tap Customize at the bottom.

step.name: Choose the Lock Screen canvas
step.text: Make sure you are editing the Lock Screen, not the Home Screen.

itemListElement.text: Tap Lock Screen on the left.

step.name: Review your photo source
step.text: Open the photos picker for your current Photo Shuffle so you can adjust what appears.

itemListElement.text: Tap the category, album, or photos icon in the lower left.
Make any changes to the pictures you want to display.

step.name: Change the shuffle frequency
step.text: Set how often your wallpaper updates to match your preference.

itemListElement.text: Tap the three dots in the lower right corner.
Choose On Tap, On Lock, Hourly, or Daily.

step.name: Save your updated Photo Shuffle
step.text: Confirm the changes so your Lock Screen uses the new schedule.

itemListElement.text: Tap Done to finish.
Tap the screen to set the updated Lock Screen Photo Shuffle.

keyPoints.explanation: Photo Shuffle is a feature that displays different favorite photos on your iPhone Lock Screen, changing automatically based on a set timeframe or on tap.

keyPoints.title: How to Create Photo Shuffle on Your iPhone
keyPoints.explanation: You can set up Photo Shuffle via Settings or from the Lock Screen by selecting categories, albums, or manual photos, and choosing shuffle frequency.

keyPoints.title: Customizing Photo Shuffle Settings

title.rendered: How to Unlock an iPhone if You Forgot the Passcode (4 Tested Methods)

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Too many wrong passcode attempts will lock your iPhone—you’ll see increasing delays before you can try again, with only Emergency Calls available.
  • You can unlock a forgotten iPhone passcode four ways—through the lock screen, a Mac or PC, or remotely via Find My if enabled.
  • Tap ‘Forgot Passcode’ on the lock screen to erase your iPhone and start fresh after entering your Apple ID credentials.
  • Use Finder (Mac) or iTunes (Windows) with recovery mode to reset your iPhone if it’s disabled or won’t unlock from the lock screen.
  • Find My lets you erase your iPhone remotely if it’s online—visit iCloud.com, select your device, and choose Erase to remove the lock.

Getting locked out of your iPhone, perhaps because you forgot the passcode or entered the wrong one too many times, can be frustrating, especially if you rely on it for day-to-day activities. Thankfully, it’s possible to unlock a disabled iPhone. Keep reading, and we’ll show you four ways to unlock an iPhone if you forgot the passcode.

Table of Contents
  • What Happens if You Forget Your iPhone Passcode?
  • 4 Ways to Unlock Your iPhone if You Forgot Passcode
    • 1. Unlock Forgotten iPhone Passcode From Security Lockout Screen
    • 2. Reset iPhone Passcode Using Mac
    • 3. Reset Your iPhone Passcode Using Windows PC
    • 4. Reset iPhone Passcode Using Find My
  • What to Do After Resetting Your iPhone Passcode

What Happens if You Forget Your iPhone Passcode?

iPhones and iPads offer four attempts to enter a correct passcode. If you forget your passcode and can’t unlock the device in four attempts, it will disable your device for one minute. During this time, you can’t enter a passcode, open the Control Center, access your notifications, place calls, or perform any other tasks. You can, however, place Emergency Calls on your device.

Note We’re aware that Apple’s Community and most online forums suggest you have six attempts to enter the correct passcode before your iPhone gets disabled. However, our findings as of the time of writing suggest otherwise.


Once the timer ends, you get another chance to enter the passcode. However, every time you enter an incorrect passcode, the time limit increases to prevent brute-force attempts to guess the passcode. This means that if you enter the wrong passcode five times, your device will be disabled for five minutes. If you enter the wrong passcode six times, your device will be disabled for 15 minutes, and so on.

If you changed your password recently and can’t remember it, you can still use the old passcode to unlock your device for up to 72 hours. You’ll just need to tap Forgot Passcode and then tap Enter Previous Passcode. But if it has been more than 72 hours, you must erase your device to reset the passcode.

4 Ways to Unlock Your iPhone if You Forgot Passcode

There are four ways to erase your iPhone or iPad if you forget its passcode. Let’s check them out.

1. Unlock Forgotten iPhone Passcode From Security Lockout Screen

If your iPhone is disabled after you entered the wrong passcode too many times, you’ll see a Forgot Passcode option in the bottom-right corner of the screen. This option lets you erase your device and deactivate the passcode lock wirelessly without entering Recovery Mode. Here’s what you need to do:

  1. Press the Side button to wake up your iPhone or iPad.
  2. Then, tap Forgot Password in the bottom-right corner.
  3. Tap Start iPhone Reset.
  4. Enter your Apple ID password.
  5. If your device uses an eSIM, tap Keep eSIM and Erase Data.
  6. On devices without an eSIM, hit Erase Device.
Note The steps mentioned above are for iOS 18. If you want to reset your device’s passcode in iOS 16 and iPadOS 16, you’ll have to tap Erase Device instead of Forgot Passcode.

As soon as you do this, your iPhone or iPad will restart, and you’ll see an Apple logo along with a grey progress bar appear on the screen. After your iPhone or iPad boots up, you’ll be greeted with a Hello screen. From here, you can take over and set up your device.

2. Reset iPhone Passcode Using Mac

Another way to reset your iPhone or iPad passcode is to use a Mac to erase your iPhone via Recovery Mode. Here’s what you need to know:

  1. Connect your iPhone or iPad to your Mac using a compatible cable.
  2. Boot your iPhone or iPad in recovery mode using the appropriate steps.
  3. Locate your device in the Finder (or iTunes if you use an older Mac).
  4. Click Restore on the prompt asking you to restore or update your iPhone or iPad.
  5. Once your iPhone or iPad boots up, disconnect it from your Mac.

3. Reset Your iPhone Passcode Using Windows PC

Just like a Mac, you can also use a Windows PC to erase your iPhone or iPad and reset the passcode. However, in this case, you’ll have to use iTunes or the Apple Devices app instead of Finder. Here’s the step-by-step process you need to follow:

  1. Connect your iPhone or iPad to your PC using a compatible cable.
  2. Boot your iPhone or iPad in recovery mode using the appropriate steps.
  3. Now, locate your device in the Apple Devices app or iTunes for Windows.
  4. Click Restore when you see the option to restore or update on the PC.
  5. Once your iPhone or iPad boots up, disconnect it from your PC.

4. Reset iPhone Passcode Using Find My

Besides finding your lost devices and keeping track of your belongings with an AirTag, you can also use Apple’s Find My app to reset your iPhone passcode wirelessly. The prerequisites are that you need to have Find My enabled on your locked device and that it’s connected to the internet over cellular or Wi-Fi. With that out of the way, here’s the process to erase your iPhone using Find My:

  1. Go to icloud.com/find using any web browser.
  2. Click Sign In and login using your Apple ID credentials.
  3. Then, select your iPhone or iPad from the list of devices.
  4. Select Erase This Device and tap Next to reset the device.

This will remove all your data and the passcode from your iPhone or iPad. You can use the device again after entering your Apple ID password to verify your identity and disable the iCloud Activation Lock.

What to Do After Resetting Your iPhone Passcode

You can’t use your iPhone or iPad right away after resetting the passcode. As your device will be erased during the process, you’ll need to decide whether to set it up as a new device or restore the data from a backup or old device. Here’s a closer look at all the things you need to do after resetting your passcode:

  • Set up your device: After you reset the passcode, you’ll need to set up the iPhone or iPad before you can use it. This involves configuring the region, language, and privacy settings and setting up a new passcode or registering Face ID.
  • Restore your data: During the device setup process, you’ll come across a screen labeled Apps & Data. If you have an iCloud backup or a physical backup on a Mac or Windows PC, you can restore your data from here.
  • Re-download apps and other data: If you’re setting up your iPhone or iPad as a new device, you’ll need to download all the necessary apps from the App Store manually. However, if you restore your data from a backup, you don’t need to do this, as it will automatically download all your apps on the device.

Wrapping up…

As you’ve seen, there are several ways to reset your iPhone’s passcode. If you have access to a computer, you can reset the passcode by erasing your iPhone via Recovery Mode or the Erase This Device option in Find My. However, if you don’t, you can use the Forgot Passcode option on the Lock Screen. Regardless of how you do it, you’ll have an unlocked iPhone in the end, ready to use like it’s new.

FAQs

Is it possible to reset the iPhone passcode without losing data?

No. Resetting your iPhone passcode without losing your data is impossible. Regardless of which method you use, it will erase all your data. You can only get your data back by restoring your device from an existing backup.

mainEntity.name: Can I answer a call while Live Voicemail is transcribing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yup, absolutely! That’s one of Live Voicemail’s charm points. Tap the green Answer button at any moment while reading that transcription. The caller? They won’t know you’ve had a sneak peek till you pick up.

mainEntity.name: Why don't I see the Live Voicemail option on my iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: Live Voicemail plays with iPhone XS or newer, using iOS 17 or later. Tick those boxes and still no dice? Check if your region settings align, since it’s not rolled out globally just yet.

mainEntity.name: Does Live Voicemail work on Wi-Fi calling?

acceptedAnswer.text: Oh yes, it does. As long as your carrier supports it and you're on iOS 17 or later, you're all set.

mainEntity.name: How is Live Voicemail different from Visual Voicemail?

acceptedAnswer.text: Here’s the key difference: Visual Voicemail shows you a lineup of messages to play back. Live Voicemail, however, gives you live transcription as someone leaves that message, with the added ability to intervene mid-message.

mainEntity.name: Will my caller know I'm reading their voicemail live?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not a chance. Callers won’t catch wind of you viewing their message in real-time unless you answer. From their end, it’s voicemail as usual.

mainEntity.name: Is Live Voicemail available on all carriers?

acceptedAnswer.text: Live Voicemail works with most major carriers, but there’s some variation. If you've run into issues, a word with your carrier might help; they could need to tweak your voicemail settings.

mainEntity.name: How do I delete Live Voicemail transcripts?

acceptedAnswer.text: Deleting Live Voicemail messages mirrors usual ones: swipe left on the message list and tap Delete, or dive into the message and hit the trash icon.

mainEntity.name: Why is Live Voicemail not transcribing messages?

acceptedAnswer.text: Crummy audio quality, boisterous background antics, or unclear speech can toss the transcription off track. It performs best when callers speak clearly in peaceful zones. Restart your iPhone to resolve any temporary transcription issues.

title.rendered: How to Download Instagram Reels on iPhone

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Instagram now lets you download public Reels in-app if the creator enables it—downloads include a watermark and are saved directly to your Photos app.
  • Use third-party apps like InSaver for more flexibility—you can save Reels without watermarks by pasting the link into the app.
  • The ‘R↓Download’ iOS Shortcut automates saving Reels—just share the Reel to the shortcut from Instagram to download it instantly.
  • Screen recording is another option but watch privacy laws—this method works for private content but may raise copyright concerns.
  • Saved Reels appear in Photos or Files app depending on how they’re downloaded—check app-specific folders for third-party tools.

If you’ve ever come across an Instagram Reel you loved and wished you could download it to your iPhone, you’re not alone! Fortunately, Instagram has a built-in option to save public Reels for offline viewing or sharing with friends. You can also download private Reels on your iPhone if you follow that person, and they have enabled the option.

However, if you don’t find the Download button, worry not! In this guide, I’ll walk you through the easiest ways to download Instagram Reels on your iPhone—so you can watch them anytime, even offline!

3 Ways to Download Instagram Reels on iPhone

There are multiple ways to download reels on an iPhone, regardless of whether the creator allows it, from using the official Instagram app to using a third-party app or an iOS shortcut.

1. Download Reels Using the Instagram Ios App

Starting in November 2023, Instagram finally listened to the community’s feedback & demands and rolled out the option to download public reels from the official app itself. However, to keep the creators’ privacy in check, Instagram has empowered them to choose whether they want their reels to have a download option.

Also, note that the downloaded reel will have a watermark of Instagram logo and the creators name. Additionally, you can’t save reels from private accounts unless they approve you as a follower and enable the download option.

  1. Open the Instagram app.
  2. Play the reel you want to download from the app’s Feed, Discover, or Saved posts section.
  3. Tap the Share button (flying paper plane) on the right.
  4. Tap the Download button at the bottom. If the Download option isn’t available, the creator has turned off downloading in the first place.
  5. Wait for the download to complete, then head to the Photos app to view the downloaded reel.

2. Save Instagram Reels to iPhone Camera Roll With a Third-Party App

As mentioned, whether you can download an Instagram reel is in the creator’s control. So what if the creator has turned off downloading? Luckily, there are several third-party apps, such as InSaver, available on the App Store, which you can install and use to download Instagram reels on your iPhone. Here’s how:

  1. Download and install the InstDown app on your iPhone.
  2. Open the Instagram app and play the reel you want to download.
  3. Next, tap the Share button, then tap the Copy Link button.
  4. Close the Instagram app and head to the InstDown app.
  5. Now, paste the copied link in the search bar and hit Find.
  6. Wait for the app to find the reel. Once it finds it, tap the Save button to save the Instagram reel to your iPhone’s camera roll.

Now, you can view the reel from your Photos app library. The best part about this method is that it doesn’t include a watermark on the downloaded reel.

3. Download Instagram Reels Using the Shortcuts App

If using a third-party app or heading to a third-party website whenever you want to download an Instagram reel seems complex, you can use the R↓Download iOS Shortcut to do the job. Visit the link and add the shortcut to your Shortcuts app library. Then, follow these steps to download a reel using this shortcut:

  1. Open the Instagram app and play the reel you want to download.
  2. Tap the Share button on the left and select the Share to option at the bottom.
  3. Next, tap the R↓Download Shortcut tab in the Share Sheet that appears.
  4. If you are using this Shortcut for the first time, it will ask for a few permissions. Hit Allow to continue.
  5. Wait for the download process to complete, and the Instagram reel will get saved to your camera roll.

I prefer to use this method to save Instagram reels on my iPhone directly from the app without any watermarks.

Video: How to Download Instagram Reels on iPhone

Signing off…

That’s how easy it is to download reels from Instagram on an iPhone. While these methods should help you download the reels you want, if the original creator has turned off downloading and you don’t want to use a third-party app or iOS shortcut or don’t have enough data, you can use an iPhone’s screen recording tool to record them for offline viewing.

FAQs

Can I save Instagram reels to watch offline without downloading?

No, you can not save Instagram reels for offline viewing without downloading, but you can screen record the reel and watch it offline.

Is it legal to download reels from Instagram?

Yes, it is legal to download public reels if the creator has allowed it. However, using the downloaded reel for commercial purposes without the original creator’s permission is strictly prohibited.

Can I download reels from Instagram using a desktop computer?

Yes, you can copy an Instagram reel link, head over to a third-party website, and paste the reel link to download it.

Can I download Instagram Reels directly from the Instagram app on my Phone?  

Yes, but only in certain cases. The Instagram app allows you to download Reels posted by others only if the creator has enabled the download option. However, downloaded Reels will include an Instagram watermark and the creator’s name, and some may not have audio due to copyright restrictions. 

What should I do if the download option isn’t available for a particular Reel?  

If the download option is not available in the Share menu, you can use the built-in screen recorder on your iPhone to capture the Reel while playing. Alternatively, copy the Reel’s link and use an online tool to download it on your iPhone (only if the Reel is public). Both methods will not produce any watermark on the video.  

Are there any privacy concerns when downloading Reels using third-party apps?

Yes. Many third-party apps request access to your Instagram account or personal data, which could be a security risk. Additionally, downloading someone else’s content without permission might violate Instagram’s policies and copyright laws. Always use trusted sources and respect content creators’ rights. 

Can I download Reels from private accounts?  

No. If an account is private, you cannot download or access its Reels unless you follow the account, and the creator has enabled downloads. Even then, you should respect their privacy and not share their content without permission. 

Where are the downloaded Reels saved on my iPhone? 

If you saved Reels through Instagram or screen recording, they are saved in your Photos app library. However, online tools or third-party may save the Reel in the Files app or a custom folder, depending on its settings.

mainEntity.name: Can I save Instagram reels to watch offline without downloading?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, you can not save Instagram reels for offline viewing without downloading, but you can screen record the reel and watch it offline.

mainEntity.name: Is it legal to download reels from Instagram?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, it is legal to download public reels if the creator has allowed it. However, using the downloaded reel for commercial purposes without the original creator's permission is strictly prohibited.

mainEntity.name: Can I download reels from Instagram using a desktop computer?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, you can copy an Instagram reel link, head over to a third-party website, and paste the reel link to download it.

mainEntity.name: Can I download Instagram Reels directly from the Instagram app on my Phone?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, but only in certain cases. The Instagram app allows you to download Reels posted by others only if the creator has enabled the download option. However, downloaded Reels will include an Instagram watermark and the creator’s name, and some may not have audio due to copyright restrictions.

mainEntity.name: What should I do if the download option isn't available for a particular Reel?

acceptedAnswer.text: If the download option is not available in the Share menu, you can use the built-in screen recorder on your iPhone to capture the Reel while playing. Alternatively, copy the Reel’s link and use an online tool to download it on your iPhone (only if the Reel is public). Both methods will not produce any watermark on the video.

mainEntity.name: Are there any privacy concerns when downloading Reels using third-party apps?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Many third-party apps request access to your Instagram account or personal data, which could be a security risk. Additionally, downloading someone else's content without permission might violate Instagram’s policies and copyright laws. Always use trusted sources and respect content creators' rights.

mainEntity.name: Can I download Reels from private accounts?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. If an account is private, you cannot download or access its Reels unless you follow the account, and the creator has enabled downloads. Even then, you should respect their privacy and not share their content without permission.

mainEntity.name: Where are the downloaded Reels saved on my iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: If you saved Reels through Instagram or screen recording, they are saved in your Photos app library. However, online tools or third-party may save the Reel in the Files app or a custom folder, depending on its settings.

title.rendered: Apple Reportedly Planning These 10 Product Launches Soon

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Upcoming Apple Devices Later This Year: Apple is set to release several anticipated products before the end of 2025, including the M5 iPad Pro, an updated Vision Pro headset, AirTag 2, a faster Apple TV, and the HomePod mini 2.
  • Features of the M5 iPad Pro and Vision Pro: The new iPad Pro will feature Apple’s M5 chip and dual cameras, while the Vision Pro headset will get a redesign, possibly with a new color and an M4 or M5 chip.
  • Enhanced Apple Accessories and Devices: Expect improvements in the new AirTag, Apple TV with the A17 Pro chip and Wi-Fi 7, and the HomePod mini 2 with better sound quality and additional features.
  • Early 2026 Launch Plans for Macs and iPhones: Apple plans to introduce the M5 MacBook Pro and Air in 2026, along with a new external monitor and possibly an iPhone 17e, continuing its chip upgrade strategy.
  • Apple’s New Smart Home Hub and Ecosystem Expansion: Around spring 2026, Apple aims to launch a dedicated smart home hub to enhance its smart home ecosystem and compete with Amazon Alexa and Google Home, powered by revamped Siri and Apple Intelligence.

Apple may have just wrapped up its big iPhone 17 event, but the company isn’t slowing down. According to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, Apple has a packed release schedule for the coming months, with at least ten products lined up between late 2025 and early 2026. From upgraded iPads and Macs to a long-awaited smart home hub, here’s what to expect.

What’s Coming Later This Year

Apple’s fall event left some products off the stage, but they’re still on track to launch before the year ends.

  • M5 iPad Pro: Expected as soon as October, this will be the first iPad with Apple’s new M5 chip. It’s also set to feature dual front cameras for better video calls in both portrait and landscape modes.
  • Updated Vision Pro: Apple’s headset will get a refresh with an M4 or M5 chip, a redesigned strap for comfort, and possibly a new Space Black color.
  • AirTag 2: A new version of Apple’s tracker with a U2 chip for better precision finding, longer range, and more secure design.
  • Apple TV: A speed bump with the A17 Pro chip, plus Apple’s new N1 networking chip with Wi-Fi 7. It will also support Apple’s upgraded Siri and other Apple Intelligence features.
  • HomePod mini 2: A refreshed model with better sound, new chip upgrades, Ultra Wideband 2 support for proximity features, and potentially new colors.

Rolling Into Early 2026

As the new year begins, Apple will shift focus to its Mac lineup and smart home efforts.

  • M5 MacBook Pro: Scheduled for early 2026, this update will bring Apple’s most powerful laptops up to the M5 generation, though a full redesign with OLED screens is still further out.
  • M5 MacBook Air: Expected in the first quarter of 2026, this refresh will also be a simple chip bump.
  • New Mac Display: Apple is preparing a new external monitor, most likely a successor to the Studio Display with mini-LED backlighting. A Pro Display XDR successor is also in development but may come later.
  • iPhone 17e: A follow-up to the iPhone 16e, expected in spring 2026 with the same A19 chip found in the iPhone 17.
  • Smart Home Hub: Perhaps the most significant new product on the list, Apple is finally planning to launch its dedicated home hub around spring 2026. This device will work closely with the revamped Siri powered by Apple Intelligence and could help Apple compete more seriously with Amazon Alexa and Google Home.

The Bigger Picture of Apple’s Plans

This launch blitz shows Apple is preparing not just to update its core devices but also to strengthen its ecosystem in areas where it has lagged. The smart home hub, in particular, signals Apple’s intent to become a stronger player in connected homes. Meanwhile, the steady rollout of M5 chips across iPad, MacBook, and Vision Pro ensures Apple’s devices stay ahead in performance while maintaining its yearly cadence of silicon upgrades.

The next six months are shaping up to be busy for Apple fans. Whether you’re waiting for a new iPad Pro, holding out for a lighter Vision Pro, or curious about Apple’s first real smart home hub, your wallet might not be getting a break anytime soon.

mainEntity.name: Is the previous legacy blue checkmark and X Premium subscription checkmark same?

mainEntity.name: Can I answer a call while Live Voicemail is transcribing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yup, absolutely! That’s one of Live Voicemail’s charm points. Tap the green Answer button at any moment while reading that transcription. The caller? They won’t know you’ve had a sneak peek till you pick up.

mainEntity.name: Why don't I see the Live Voicemail option on my iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: Live Voicemail plays with iPhone XS or newer, using iOS 17 or later. Tick those boxes and still no dice? Check if your region settings align, since it’s not rolled out globally just yet.

mainEntity.name: Does Live Voicemail work on Wi-Fi calling?

acceptedAnswer.text: Oh yes, it does. As long as your carrier supports it and you're on iOS 17 or later, you're all set.

mainEntity.name: How is Live Voicemail different from Visual Voicemail?

acceptedAnswer.text: Here’s the key difference: Visual Voicemail shows you a lineup of messages to play back. Live Voicemail, however, gives you live transcription as someone leaves that message, with the added ability to intervene mid-message.

mainEntity.name: Will my caller know I'm reading their voicemail live?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not a chance. Callers won’t catch wind of you viewing their message in real-time unless you answer. From their end, it’s voicemail as usual.

mainEntity.name: Is Live Voicemail available on all carriers?

acceptedAnswer.text: Live Voicemail works with most major carriers, but there’s some variation. If you've run into issues, a word with your carrier might help; they could need to tweak your voicemail settings.

mainEntity.name: How do I delete Live Voicemail transcripts?

acceptedAnswer.text: Deleting Live Voicemail messages mirrors usual ones: swipe left on the message list and tap Delete, or dive into the message and hit the trash icon.

mainEntity.name: Why is Live Voicemail not transcribing messages?

acceptedAnswer.text: Crummy audio quality, boisterous background antics, or unclear speech can toss the transcription off track. It performs best when callers speak clearly in peaceful zones. Restart your iPhone to resolve any temporary transcription issues.

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Resetting your iPhone passcode without losing your data is impossible. Regardless of which method you use, it will erase all your data. You can only get your data back by restoring your device from an existing backup.

mainEntity.name: Can I save Instagram reels to watch offline without downloading?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, you can not save Instagram reels for offline viewing without downloading, but you can screen record the reel and watch it offline.

mainEntity.name: Is it legal to download reels from Instagram?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, it is legal to download public reels if the creator has allowed it. However, using the downloaded reel for commercial purposes without the original creator's permission is strictly prohibited.

mainEntity.name: Can I download reels from Instagram using a desktop computer?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, you can copy an Instagram reel link, head over to a third-party website, and paste the reel link to download it.

mainEntity.name: Can I download Instagram Reels directly from the Instagram app on my Phone?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, but only in certain cases. The Instagram app allows you to download Reels posted by others only if the creator has enabled the download option. However, downloaded Reels will include an Instagram watermark and the creator’s name, and some may not have audio due to copyright restrictions.

mainEntity.name: What should I do if the download option isn't available for a particular Reel?

acceptedAnswer.text: If the download option is not available in the Share menu, you can use the built-in screen recorder on your iPhone to capture the Reel while playing. Alternatively, copy the Reel’s link and use an online tool to download it on your iPhone (only if the Reel is public). Both methods will not produce any watermark on the video.

mainEntity.name: Are there any privacy concerns when downloading Reels using third-party apps?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Many third-party apps request access to your Instagram account or personal data, which could be a security risk. Additionally, downloading someone else's content without permission might violate Instagram’s policies and copyright laws. Always use trusted sources and respect content creators' rights.

mainEntity.name: Can I download Reels from private accounts?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. If an account is private, you cannot download or access its Reels unless you follow the account, and the creator has enabled downloads. Even then, you should respect their privacy and not share their content without permission.

mainEntity.name: Where are the downloaded Reels saved on my iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: If you saved Reels through Instagram or screen recording, they are saved in your Photos app library. However, online tools or third-party may save the Reel in the Files app or a custom folder, depending on its settings.

keyPoints.title: Upcoming Apple Devices Later This Year
keyPoints.explanation: Apple is set to release several anticipated products before the end of 2025, including the M5 iPad Pro, an updated Vision Pro headset, AirTag 2, a faster Apple TV, and the HomePod mini 2.

keyPoints.title: Features of the M5 iPad Pro and Vision Pro
keyPoints.explanation: The new iPad Pro will feature Apple’s M5 chip and dual cameras, while the Vision Pro headset will get a redesign, possibly with a new color and an M4 or M5 chip.

keyPoints.title: Enhanced Apple Accessories and Devices
keyPoints.explanation: Expect improvements in the new AirTag, Apple TV with the A17 Pro chip and Wi-Fi 7, and the HomePod mini 2 with better sound quality and additional features.

keyPoints.title: Early 2026 Launch Plans for Macs and iPhones
keyPoints.explanation: Apple plans to introduce the M5 MacBook Pro and Air in 2026, along with a new external monitor and possibly an iPhone 17e, continuing its chip upgrade strategy.

keyPoints.title: Apple’s New Smart Home Hub and Ecosystem Expansion
keyPoints.explanation: Around spring 2026, Apple aims to launch a dedicated smart home hub to enhance its smart home ecosystem and compete with Amazon Alexa and Google Home, powered by revamped Siri and Apple Intelligence.

title.rendered: Siri Executive Robby Walker To Leave Apple In October

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Key AI Executive Robby Walker Leaving Apple: Robby Walker, a senior director overseeing Siri and AI projects, is set to depart Apple in October, raising concerns about the company’s AI development efforts during a competitive era.
  • Transition of Siri and AI Projects at Apple: Following delays in Siri’s modernization and leadership changes, Walker moved to work on an AI-powered search system aimed at competing with services like ChatGPT, scheduled for release in 2026.
  • Impact of High-Profile Exits on Apple’s AI Competitiveness: Walker’s departure adds to a wave of talent leaving Apple for Meta, including top AI researchers, which sparks worries about Apple’s ability to innovate in AI amid rivals advancing rapidly.
  • Apple’s Cautious Approach to AI Development: While competitors integrate advanced models like Google’s Gemini, Apple remains cautious, relying on partnerships with companies like OpenAI and considering Google’s offerings for Siri upgrades.
  • Future Challenges and Strategy Moves for Apple AI: With Siri’s relaunch delayed and key projects ongoing, Apple faces pressure to deliver on AI promises through in-house innovation and collaborations, amid uncertainty following Walker’s exit.

Apple is about to lose another key figure in its artificial intelligence team. Robby Walker, the senior director who once oversaw Siri, is leaving the company in October, according to Bloomberg. His exit comes at a delicate moment for Apple, as the company struggles to keep pace in the rapidly evolving AI race.

From Siri To Search

Walker joined Apple back in 2013 and rose to become one of its most senior AI executives. Until earlier this year, he led Siri’s development, guiding Apple’s push to modernize its voice assistant with Apple Intelligence. But that project hit turbulence. In May 2025, Apple announced that the “new and improved Siri” would be delayed until 2026. Around that time, Walker delivered a now-famous pep talk to engineers, comparing the incomplete effort to a swimmer who nearly reached Hawaii but fell short of the destination.

Following the delay, Siri responsibilities shifted from AI chief John Giannandrea to Vision Pro leader Mike Rockwell, under Craig Federighi’s oversight. Walker himself moved to the Answers, Information, and Knowledge team, where he worked on a still-unannounced AI-powered search system. That project, internally called Answers, is designed to compete with services like Perplexity and ChatGPT and is scheduled for a 2026 release.

Why It Matters

Walker’s departure adds to a string of high-profile exits from Apple’s AI group. Meta has been the biggest beneficiary, attracting several Apple researchers with massive pay packages. Ruoming Pang, Apple’s top AI models lead, left for Meta with a reported $200 million deal. Others, like Frank Chu, Mark Lee, and Tom Gunter, also joined Meta’s growing Superintelligence Labs.

The steady talent drain has fueled concerns about Apple’s ability to execute on AI. While rivals like Google continue to roll out advanced models, most recently showcasing Gemini inside its flagship phones, Apple’s approach has been far more cautious. The company has leaned on OpenAI’s ChatGPT for Apple Intelligence’s general knowledge features and is reportedly considering integrating Google’s Gemini into the next-generation Siri.

Looking Ahead

For now, Walker’s future plans remain unclear. What is clear is that Apple faces mounting pressure to prove it can deliver on its AI promises. With Siri’s relaunch now expected in spring 2026 and the Answers search project still in development, Apple’s strategy hinges on a mix of in-house breakthroughs and partnerships with rivals. Walker’s exit in October marks yet another challenge as the company navigates what may be the biggest shift in consumer technology since the iPhone itself.

mainEntity.name: What should I do if the download option isn't available for a particular Reel?

acceptedAnswer.text: If the download option is not available in the Share menu, you can use the built-in screen recorder on your iPhone to capture the Reel while playing. Alternatively, copy the Reel’s link and use an online tool to download it on your iPhone (only if the Reel is public). Both methods will not produce any watermark on the video.

mainEntity.name: Are there any privacy concerns when downloading Reels using third-party apps?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Many third-party apps request access to your Instagram account or personal data, which could be a security risk. Additionally, downloading someone else's content without permission might violate Instagram’s policies and copyright laws. Always use trusted sources and respect content creators' rights.

mainEntity.name: Can I download Reels from private accounts?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. If an account is private, you cannot download or access its Reels unless you follow the account, and the creator has enabled downloads. Even then, you should respect their privacy and not share their content without permission.

mainEntity.name: Where are the downloaded Reels saved on my iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: If you saved Reels through Instagram or screen recording, they are saved in your Photos app library. However, online tools or third-party may save the Reel in the Files app or a custom folder, depending on its settings.

title.rendered: The Regular iPhone 17 Is Already Setting Sales Records in China

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Record-Breaking Demand in China: Pre-orders for the iPhone 17 in China shattered records, with millions rushing to reserve the model and sales surpassing last year’s iPhone 16 pre-orders within minutes on JD.com.
  • Why the Base Model Stands Out: The iPhone 17’s increased storage, larger display, and the latest A19 chip make it a compelling upgrade at the same $799 price, shifting perceptions of the standard model as a smart choice.
  • Analysts See Apple Playing It Smart: Apple’s strategic segmentation of its product lineup caters to different user needs, with the iPhone 17 offering a balanced mix of features and value, helping reverse sluggish sales earlier in the year.
  • Impact of Competitive Market Dynamics: Despite strong early sales, competitors like Huawei and Xiaomi are advancing with foldable phones and early launches, maintaining fierce competition in China’s high-end smartphone market.
  • A Strong Start for the 17 Series: The early popularity of the iPhone 17 suggests that offering meaningful features and upgrades without radical redesigns can make the base model the surprise star of the lineup.

Apple’s latest iPhone lineup is out, but it’s not the flashy new Air or the premium Pro Max making early headlines. Instead, the regular iPhone 17 is turning out to be a surprise crowd favorite. In China, pre-orders for the base model are already breaking records, with millions rushing to secure one before launch day.

Record-Breaking Demand in China

On JD.com, one of China’s biggest online retailers, the standard iPhone 17 with 256GB storage became the most pre-ordered model after sales opened on September 12. In just the first minute, JD.com reported volumes surpassing the entire first day of iPhone 16 pre-orders last year. By the next day, over 3.7 million reservations were logged for the base model alone, according to figures cited by the South China Morning Post. Apple’s own website even crashed under the traffic, and many color and storage options quickly sold out.

Some of this demand was boosted by delays to the new iPhone Air, which is waiting on regulatory approval in China. But analysts say the regular iPhone 17 likely would have been popular regardless. Pickup slots for the Pro Max sold out in minutes, and delivery dates for all iPhone 17 models in major cities have already slipped well into October.

Why the Base Model Stands Out

For years, the standard iPhone felt like the “boring” option. But the iPhone 17 changes that. It still starts at $799 (5,999 yuan in China), the same price as last year’s iPhone 16,  but Apple doubled the base storage to 256GB. It also features a larger 6.3-inch display with thinner bezels, finally catching up to Pro models with a 120Hz LTPO OLED ProMotion panel. This means smoother scrolling and the ability to drop down to 1Hz to save battery. Add in Apple’s latest A19 chip, built on TSMC’s new 3nm process, and the base iPhone suddenly feels like a serious upgrade.

These changes make the regular iPhone 17 look less like a compromise and more like a smart buy. Shoppers get a faster phone, more storage, and a Pro-level screen without crossing the $1,000 mark.

Analysts See Apple Playing It Smart

Market watchers say Apple’s decision to spread upgrades across the lineup is paying off. “Apple has astutely segmented its product line-up, ensuring each model appeals to distinct user needs,” said IDC’s Nabila Popal. In other words, the Air may woo design lovers and the Pros will keep power users, but the iPhone 17 offers the best balance of value and features.

Apple’s strategy also comes at a critical time. The company faced sluggish iPhone 16 sales earlier this year, resorting to discounts in China. Now, the iPhone 17 launch is reversing that trend, with Foxconn already asked to ramp up production. Still, rivals like Huawei and Xiaomi are moving fast with foldables and early launches, keeping the competition fierce in China’s high-end market.

A Strong Start for the 17 Series

The early success of the regular iPhone 17 shows Apple doesn’t always need a radical redesign to score big. By giving the base model features people actually want, more storage, a bigger Pro-level display, and the latest chip. Apple may have found the sweet spot. If pre-orders are any sign, this “boring” iPhone could end up being the most important model in the lineup.

excerpt.rendered: The regular iPhone 17 is off to a flying start, smashing pre-order records in China thanks to its bigger ProMotion display, doubled storage, and new A19 chip.

mainEntity.name: Is iOS 26 better than iOS 18?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. iOS 26 introduces a visually rich design, smarter system tools, and improved app interfaces—especially if you're on a newer iPhone.

mainEntity.name: Will iOS 26 slow down older iPhones?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not necessarily. While older models like the iPhone 11 may not run animations as smoothly, Apple has optimized performance across supported devices. Battery health and storage space may still affect your experience.

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, it is legal to download public reels if the creator has allowed it. However, using the downloaded reel for commercial purposes without the original creator's permission is strictly prohibited.

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, you can copy an Instagram reel link, head over to a third-party website, and paste the reel link to download it.

mainEntity.name: Can I download Instagram Reels directly from the Instagram app on my Phone?

mainEntity.name: Are there any privacy concerns when downloading Reels using third-party apps?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Many third-party apps request access to your Instagram account or personal data, which could be a security risk. keyPoints.title: Why the Base Model Stands Out
keyPoints.explanation: The iPhone 17's increased storage, larger display, and the latest A19 chip make it a compelling upgrade at the same $799 price, shifting perceptions of the standard model as a smart choice.

keyPoints.title: Analysts See Apple Playing It Smart

keyPoints.title: Impact of Competitive Market Dynamics

title.rendered: Apple Reveals iPhone 17, 17 Pro, and iPhone Air Repair and Battery Costs

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • iPhone 17 Repair Costs Overview: Apple has announced the repair prices for the iPhone 17 lineup, including new costs for screen and back glass damage across models, highlighting the increasing expenses for repairs without coverage.
  • Repair Pricing Changes Compared to Previous Models: While battery replacement prices stay consistent with last year, screen repair costs have increased, especially for the standard iPhone 17 and the iPhone 17 Pro Max, making repairs more expensive.
  • Improved Back Glass Repair Pricing: Back glass repair prices have been lowered to $159 across all iPhone 17 models, including the iPhone Air, offsetting higher screen repair costs.
  • AppleCare+ Savings and Coverage: AppleCare+ significantly reduces repair costs, offering repairs as low as $29 for screens and including benefits like unlimited accidental damage coverage, theft, and loss protection.
  • Implications for Buyers on Repair Costs and Coverage: Prospective iPhone 17 buyers should consider repair costs, which can be high without coverage, but can be mitigated by purchasing AppleCare+ to save money and gain additional protection.

Apple has revealed how much it will cost to fix the new iPhone 17 lineup, including the iPhone 17, 17 Pro, 17 Pro Max, and the all-new iPhone Air. 

While battery replacements stay flat compared to last year’s iPhone 16 series, other repairs are a mix of price hikes and surprising cuts. Here are all the repair and battery replacement costs for the entire iPhone 17 lineup. 

iPhone 17 Series Repair Pricing

Here’s how the out-of-warranty repair fees compare across the lineup:

Note: These prices are for the U.S. market only and may differ in other countries.

Apple isn’t changing much when it comes to battery replacement. The iPhone 17 Pro, Pro Max, and the new iPhone Air all cost $119 for a new battery, while the regular iPhone 17 comes in a little cheaper at $99. That’s the same pricing structure as last year, so no surprises there.

The real difference shows up in screen repairs. On the iPhone 16, the base model screen costs $279 to replace, while the Pro models cost $329. With the iPhone 17, that jumps to $329 for the base and Pro, and $379 for the Pro Max, the most expensive screen repair Apple has listed yet.

Apple did offset this by lowering the back glass repair prices. Where the iPhone 16 Pro and Pro Max were $199, the iPhone 17 lineup, including the Air, now costs $159. Even the base iPhone dropped slightly from $169 to $159, thanks to Apple’s improved repair process.

If you break both the screen and the back glass, the combined repair cost stays the same for the Pro and Pro Max as last year. But the base iPhone sees a jump, from $369 to $419. That higher price makes sense, though, since the iPhone 17 now carries the same ProMotion display and other advanced screen features once limited to the Pro line.

This breakdown highlights just how expensive repairs can get if your device is not covered by AppleCare+.

AppleCare+ Coverage Brings Big Savings

With AppleCare+, the costs drop significantly. Screen or back glass repairs can be as low as $29, while other damage ranges up to $99 per incident. AppleCare+ also adds unlimited accidental damage coverage with flat service fees, theft and loss protection for up to two claims every 12 months, free battery replacement if capacity drops below 80%, and 24/7 priority support.

  • iPhone 17: $11.99/month or $119.99/year
  • iPhone 17 Pro, Pro Max, Air: $13.99/month or $139.99/year

There’s also an AppleCare One plan that covers up to three devices for $19.99/month, with each additional device at $5.99/month.

For people prone to accidents or worried about theft, AppleCare+ can save hundreds compared to out-of-warranty fees and offers extra peace of mind. Plans must be purchased within 60 days of buying a new iPhone, and can be added online, in-store, or from iPhone settings.

What This Means For Buyers

For those planning to buy any of the iPhone 17 models, repair fees are something to keep in mind. Battery costs remain stable, but damage to the thin and fragile iPhone Air, or any iPhone 17 model, could hit your wallet hard without AppleCare+.

So, are you opting for the AppleCare+ or AppleCare One for your iPhone 17? Do let us know in the comments.

mainEntity.name: Can I answer a call while Live Voicemail is transcribing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yup, absolutely! That’s one of Live Voicemail’s charm points. Tap the green Answer button at any moment while reading that transcription. The caller? They won’t know you’ve had a sneak peek till you pick up.

mainEntity.name: Why don't I see the Live Voicemail option on my iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: Live Voicemail plays with iPhone XS or newer, using iOS 17 or later. Tick those boxes and still no dice? Check if your region settings align, since it’s not rolled out globally just yet.

mainEntity.name: Does Live Voicemail work on Wi-Fi calling?

acceptedAnswer.text: Oh yes, it does. As long as your carrier supports it and you're on iOS 17 or later, you're all set.

mainEntity.name: How is Live Voicemail different from Visual Voicemail?

acceptedAnswer.text: Here’s the key difference: Visual Voicemail shows you a lineup of messages to play back. Live Voicemail, however, gives you live transcription as someone leaves that message, with the added ability to intervene mid-message.

mainEntity.name: Will my caller know I'm reading their voicemail live?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not a chance. Callers won’t catch wind of you viewing their message in real-time unless you answer. From their end, it’s voicemail as usual.

mainEntity.name: Is Live Voicemail available on all carriers?

acceptedAnswer.text: Live Voicemail works with most major carriers, but there’s some variation. If you've run into issues, a word with your carrier might help; they could need to tweak your voicemail settings.

mainEntity.name: How do I delete Live Voicemail transcripts?

acceptedAnswer.text: Deleting Live Voicemail messages mirrors usual ones: swipe left on the message list and tap Delete, or dive into the message and hit the trash icon.

mainEntity.name: Why is Live Voicemail not transcribing messages?

acceptedAnswer.text: Crummy audio quality, boisterous background antics, or unclear speech can toss the transcription off track. It performs best when callers speak clearly in peaceful zones. Restart your iPhone to resolve any temporary transcription issues.

mainEntity.name: Can I save Instagram reels to watch offline without downloading?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, you can not save Instagram reels for offline viewing without downloading, but you can screen record the reel and watch it offline.

mainEntity.name: Is it legal to download reels from Instagram?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, it is legal to download public reels if the creator has allowed it. However, using the downloaded reel for commercial purposes without the original creator's permission is strictly prohibited.

mainEntity.name: Can I download reels from Instagram using a desktop computer?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, you can copy an Instagram reel link, head over to a third-party website, and paste the reel link to download it.

mainEntity.name: Can I download Instagram Reels directly from the Instagram app on my Phone?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, but only in certain cases. The Instagram app allows you to download Reels posted by others only if the creator has enabled the download option. However, downloaded Reels will include an Instagram watermark and the creator’s name, and some may not have audio due to copyright restrictions.

mainEntity.name: What should I do if the download option isn't available for a particular Reel?

acceptedAnswer.text: If the download option is not available in the Share menu, you can use the built-in screen recorder on your iPhone to capture the Reel while playing. Alternatively, copy the Reel’s link and use an online tool to download it on your iPhone (only if the Reel is public). Both methods will not produce any watermark on the video.

mainEntity.name: Are there any privacy concerns when downloading Reels using third-party apps?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Many third-party apps request access to your Instagram account or personal data, which could be a security risk. Additionally, downloading someone else's content without permission might violate Instagram’s policies and copyright laws. Always use trusted sources and respect content creators' rights.

mainEntity.name: Can I download Reels from private accounts?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. If an account is private, you cannot download or access its Reels unless you follow the account, and the creator has enabled downloads. Even then, you should respect their privacy and not share their content without permission.

mainEntity.name: Where are the downloaded Reels saved on my iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: If you saved Reels through Instagram or screen recording, they are saved in your Photos app library. However, online tools or third-party may save the Reel in the Files app or a custom folder, depending on its settings.
