title.rendered: iPhone 17: Everything You Need to Know

content.rendered:
Every September, Apple gives us the same question, should you upgrade or hold on for another year? This base model may not gone through the drastic design changes like the other models in the lineup, but it has got the most meaningful upgrades. Even we think, iPhone 17 base model might be the perfect iPhone to buy right now.

If you’re wondering what’s new, what’s different, and whether it’s worth your money, here’s the full story of the standard iPhone 17.

iPhone 17 Full Specifications at a Glance (Detailed Overview)

Also Read: Apple’s iPhone 17 “Awe Dropping” Event: Everything Announced

Display: Pro-display on Base Model

The base iPhone 17 finally feels premium. For the first time, the non‑Pro gets the complete Pro display experience with a 6.3‑inch Super Retina XDR OLED panel that is bigger, brighter, and smoother than before.

It supports ProMotion with an adaptive refresh rate of 1–120Hz, meaning silky scrolling, fluid gaming, and an always‑on mode that drops down to 1Hz to save power. Peak brightness reaches 3,000 nits, the highest ever on iPhone, making outdoor visibility effortless.

Protection comes from Ceramic Shield 2, which offers 3× stronger scratch resistance along with a 7‑layer anti‑reflective coating for reduced glare. Thinner bezels complete the modern look.

All together, the iPhone 17’s display marks the biggest leap ever for a base iPhone, combining Pro‑level smoothness, brightness, and durability into a single package.

Design: Same Design with New Colors

Apple says the iPhone 17 is its toughest base model yet. It uses Ceramic Shield 2, which is 3× more scratch resistant, plus a 7-layer anti-glare coating that makes it easier to see outdoors. The edges are more rounded and the bezels are slimmer, so it feels better to hold. It’s a bit taller, slightly thicker, and weighs 177g, but that extra weight helps with durability and battery life.

The iPhone 17 comes in:

  • Black
  • White
  • Lavender
  • Mist Blue
  • Sage

Performance: 20% Faster Than iPhone 16 Model

The iPhone 17 gets a clear boost in performance thanks to Apple’s new A19 chip (3nm) and 8GB RAM.

The CPU has six cores (two for heavy tasks, four for efficiency) and is paired with a five-core GPU. This makes it about 20% faster than the iPhone 16 and nearly 1.5× quicker than the iPhone 13.

Graphics are smoother, apps launch faster, and the phone handles multitasking more comfortably. A 16-core Neural Engine with extra GPU accelerators powers features like Apple Intelligence, real-time translation, and AI-based photo edits.

Storage now starts at 256GB, with a 512GB option if you need more space. All of this means the base iPhone finally delivers the kind of speed and future-readiness once reserved for the Pro models.

Camera: Two 48MP Fusion Cameras

The iPhone 17 is the first base model where every camera sensor is 48MP, giving everyday users access to Pro-level shots. The Fusion Main camera takes detailed photos and has a built-in 2× telephoto crop, so you can zoom without losing quality. The 48MP Ultra-Wide camera handles landscapes and close-up macro shots, now with 4× more detail than before.

On the front, Apple introduces an 18MP Center Stage selfie camera with a square sensor, a first for iPhone. It can automatically switch between portrait and landscape, expand for group shots: so you don’t have to turn the phone to take a landscape photo. Also this square sensor improves the 4k Video stabilization.

Key camera features include:

  • Dual Capture (front + rear recording)
  • Cinematic Mode
  • Action Mode
  • Dolby Vision HDR
  • Spatial Audio
  • Next-gen Photographic Styles (new Bright mode)
  • Wind noise reduction for clearer audio
  • Spatial video and photos for Apple Vision Pro

Battery: Improvements in Both Battery Life and Charging Speed

The iPhone 17 finally tackles battery concerns. It packs a 3692 mAh battery, giving up to 30 hours of video playback, that’s 8 hours longer than the iPhone 16. iOS 26 adds an Adaptive Power Mode that studies how you use your phone and manages power to last longer through the day. Charging is quicker as well:

  • 50% in 20 minutes with Apple’s new 40W Dynamic Power Adapter
  • 50W MagSafe wireless charging (Qi 2.2), the fastest ever on iPhone

Connectivity: eSIM Everywhere

The debut of Apple’s N1 wireless chip changes the game. Supporting:

  • Wi-Fi 7
  • Bluetooth 6
  • Thread for smart devices

This upgrade makes AirDrop, Hotspot, and other wireless features faster and more stable. Cellular connectivity still comes from a Qualcomm modem, but Apple has expanded eSIM support to 500+ carriers worldwide. That means setting up service is easier and more secure, without needing a physical SIM card. In regions like the U.S., Japan, and the UAE, the iPhone 17 will even be sold as eSIM-only, with no physical SIM slot at all.

Availability and Pricing

Apple surprised many by keeping the $799 starting price while doubling base storage to 256GB. A 512GB option is also available.

  • Pre-orders: September 12, 2025 (5 a.m. PT)
  • Launch: September 19 in 63 countries
  • Expansion: September 26 in 22 more regions
  • Trade-in: Up to $700 off with iPhone 13 or newer, higher discounts through carrier deals

Final Thoughts: The Base iPhone Finally Feels Pro

The iPhone 17 doesn’t reinvent the wheel, it refines it. By adding Pro-level features like ProMotion, an all-48MP camera system, faster charging, and smarter AI integration, Apple has made the standard iPhone far harder to ignore.

At $799, it’s not just the safe upgrade; it’s the exciting one. If you’ve been waiting for the base iPhone to finally catch up, the iPhone 17 is the one you’ve been waiting for.

mainEntity.name: Is iOS 26 better than iOS 18?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. iOS 26 introduces a visually rich design, smarter system tools, and improved app interfaces—especially if you're on a newer iPhone.

mainEntity.name: Will iOS 26 slow down older iPhones?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not necessarily. While older models like the iPhone 11 may not run animations as smoothly, Apple has optimized performance across supported devices. Battery health and storage space may still affect your experience.

mainEntity.name: Can I get X Premium for free?

acceptedAnswer.text: No free trial is available. Sometimes high-follower accounts get complimentary upgrades, but generally, it's paid-only.

mainEntity.name: Do I need Premium for a blue checkmark?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. At least Premium or Premium+ (or Verified Organizations) is required.

mainEntity.name: Is X Premium ad-free?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not entirely. Basic has full ads, Premium halves them in main timelines, and Premium+ is mostly ad-free everywhere, but you might see occasional sponsored posts.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between the blue checkmarks and the gold and grey checkmarks?

acceptedAnswer.text: Blue is for individual Premium subscribers. Gold means an official business or non-profit via Verified Organizations. Grey is for governments or multilateral organizations. They come with extras like badges for affiliates and premium support for orgs.

mainEntity.name: Is the previous legacy blue checkmark and X Premium subscription checkmark same?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not really. The legacy one was for active, notable, authentic accounts verified by X's old system. The new blue is exclusive to active subscribers, with no fame check required.

mainEntity.name: Can I answer a call while Live Voicemail is transcribing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yup, absolutely! That’s one of Live Voicemail’s charm points. Tap the green Answer button at any moment while reading that transcription. The caller? They won’t know you’ve had a sneak peek till you pick up.

mainEntity.name: Why don't I see the Live Voicemail option on my iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: Live Voicemail plays with iPhone XS or newer, using iOS 17 or later. Tick those boxes and still no dice? Check if your region settings align, since it’s not rolled out globally just yet.

mainEntity.name: Does Live Voicemail work on Wi-Fi calling?

acceptedAnswer.text: Oh yes, it does. As long as your carrier supports it and you're on iOS 17 or later, you're all set.

mainEntity.name: How is Live Voicemail different from Visual Voicemail?

acceptedAnswer.text: Here’s the key difference: Visual Voicemail shows you a lineup of messages to play back. Live Voicemail, however, gives you live transcription as someone leaves that message, with the added ability to intervene mid-message.

mainEntity.name: Will my caller know I'm reading their voicemail live?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not a chance. Callers won’t catch wind of you viewing their message in real-time unless you answer. From their end, it’s voicemail as usual.

mainEntity.name: Is Live Voicemail available on all carriers?

acceptedAnswer.text: Live Voicemail works with most major carriers, but there’s some variation. If you've run into issues, a word with your carrier might help; they could need to tweak your voicemail settings.

mainEntity.name: How do I delete Live Voicemail transcripts?

acceptedAnswer.text: Deleting Live Voicemail messages mirrors usual ones: swipe left on the message list and tap Delete, or dive into the message and hit the trash icon.

mainEntity.name: Why is Live Voicemail not transcribing messages?

acceptedAnswer.text: Crummy audio quality, boisterous background antics, or unclear speech can toss the transcription off track. It performs best when callers speak clearly in peaceful zones. Restart your iPhone to resolve any temporary transcription issues.

mainEntity.name: Is it possible to reset the iPhone passcode without losing data?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Resetting your iPhone passcode without losing your data is impossible. Regardless of which method you use, it will erase all your data. You can only get your data back by restoring your device from an existing backup.

mainEntity.name: Can I save Instagram reels to watch offline without downloading?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, you can not save Instagram reels for offline viewing without downloading, but you can screen record the reel and watch it offline.

mainEntity.name: Is it legal to download reels from Instagram?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, it is legal to download public reels if the creator has allowed it. However, using the downloaded reel for commercial purposes without the original creator's permission is strictly prohibited.

mainEntity.name: Can I download reels from Instagram using a desktop computer?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, you can copy an Instagram reel link, head over to a third-party website, and paste the reel link to download it.

mainEntity.name: Can I download Instagram Reels directly from the Instagram app on my Phone?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, but only in certain cases. The Instagram app allows you to download Reels posted by others only if the creator has enabled the download option. However, downloaded Reels will include an Instagram watermark and the creator’s name, and some may not have audio due to copyright restrictions.

mainEntity.name: What should I do if the download option isn't available for a particular Reel?

acceptedAnswer.text: If the download option is not available in the Share menu, you can use the built-in screen recorder on your iPhone to capture the Reel while playing. Alternatively, copy the Reel’s link and use an online tool to download it on your iPhone (only if the Reel is public). Both methods will not produce any watermark on the video.

mainEntity.name: Are there any privacy concerns when downloading Reels using third-party apps?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Many third-party apps request access to your Instagram account or personal data, which could be a security risk. Additionally, downloading someone else's content without permission might violate Instagram’s policies and copyright laws. Always use trusted sources and respect content creators' rights.

mainEntity.name: Can I download Reels from private accounts?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. If an account is private, you cannot download or access its Reels unless you follow the account, and the creator has enabled downloads. Even then, you should respect their privacy and not share their content without permission.

mainEntity.name: Where are the downloaded Reels saved on my iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: If you saved Reels through Instagram or screen recording, they are saved in your Photos app library. However, online tools or third-party may save the Reel in the Files app or a custom folder, depending on its settings.

mainEntity.name: Where are stickers stored on my iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: They’re part of your iCloud account, so they sync across all your Apple devices. You won’t see them in the Files app.

mainEntity.name: Does deleting a sticker remove it from previous conversations?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Stickers you’ve already sent will stay put in those chats, even if you delete the pack or remove them from your device.

mainEntity.name: Can I recover deleted stickers?

acceptedAnswer.text: If it’s from a third-party pack, just reinstall the app from the App Store. Custom stickers will need to be recreated.

mainEntity.name: Do stickers take up a lot of storage?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most sticker packs are small, typically under 5MB. Custom stickers made from Live Photos can be slightly larger, but even a large collection rarely takes up noticeable space. Check Settings > General > iPhone Storage if you want to see exact usage.

mainEntity.name: Can I hide sticker packs instead of deleting them?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Open the Stickers drawer in Messages, scroll to the end, tap Edit, then toggle off any pack you want to hide. It stays installed but won't appear while you're typing.

mainEntity.name: How do I delete Memoji stickers on iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: You can't fully delete Memoji stickers since they're tied to your Memoji character, but you can stop them from appearing. Go to Settings > General > Keyboard and toggle off Memoji Stickers. This removes them from the keyboard without deleting your Memoji.

title.rendered: iPhone 17 Pro: Everything You Need to Know

content.rendered:
After months of rumors, the iPhone 17 Pro is finally here. Announced at Apple’s big “awe dropping” September event, it comes loaded with iOS 26, a reworked design, and the most ambitious Pro upgrades we’ve seen in years. 

If you’re wondering what’s new, what’s different, and whether it’s worth the upgrade, here’s the complete breakdown of the iPhone 17 Pro.

iPhone 17 Pro Full Specifications at a Glance (Detailed Overview)

Also Read: Apple’s iPhone 17 “Awe Dropping” Event: Everything Announced

Design: A Plateau That Changes The Entire Look

This year, Apple switched from titanium to aerospace‑grade aluminum. It might look like a downgrade from titanium, but the new unibody design gives it a stronger frame. The Pro weighs 206gm, while the Pro Max goes up to 231gm.

The new “plateau” camera bump stretches across the back, making room for a larger battery and the telephoto zoom hardware. Ceramic Shield 2 now protects both front and back, with 3× better scratch resistance and 4× stronger crack resistance than last year. The bold new Cosmic Orange shade is the hero color of the lineup, standing alongside Silver and Deep Blue.

Display: Brighter Than Ever

Apple kept the same sizes: 6.3 inches for the Pro and 6.9 for the Pro Max. Both models come with the same Super Retina XDR display at 460 ppi. Peak brightness hits 3,000 nits, making it the brightest iPhone screen yet.

A new anti‑reflective coating doubles outdoor contrast. Just like before, these Pro models support ProMotion 120Hz and Always‑On display. However, this year, these features are no longer Pro‑exclusive. 

Performance: A19 Pro With Next‑Level Cooling

Under the hood, the new A19 Pro chip pushes performance up to 40% higher than last year. It comes with a 6‑core CPU (2 performance and 4 efficiency cores), a 6‑core GPU with Neural Accelerators, and a 16‑core Neural Engine, all working together to deliver hardware‑accelerated ray tracing. 

Apple also added a laser‑welded vapor chamber that uses de‑ionized water to move heat into the aluminum body, helping the phone stay cool and perform smoothly even during heavy use. The result: faster games, better AI processing, and sustained peak speeds. The new N1 chip upgrades wireless with Wi‑Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, Thread, and stronger AirDrop and Hotspot reliability.

Cameras: Eight Lenses in Your Pocket

Apple calls this its most advanced Pro camera system ever. Three 48MP sensors give you the equivalent of eight lenses:

  • Main (24mm): Larger sensor with second‑gen OIS for brighter low‑light shots.
  • Ultra‑Wide (13mm): Sharper detail, improved macro, 120° field of view.
  • Telephoto (100mm): Tetraprism lens with 4x optical zoom, plus an 8x optical‑quality zoom at 200mm, the longest ever on iPhone.

You can zoom smoothly from 0.5x to 8x with optical clarity, and push further up to 40x using digital zoom. The Photonic Engine now reduces noise and makes colors look more natural. Up front, there’s a new 18MP Center Stage camera with a square sensor that automatically rotates, expands for group selfies, and keeps 4K HDR video steady. With Dual Capture, you can even record from the front and back cameras at the same time.

Pro shooters get industry‑firsts: ProRes RAW, Apple Log 2, ACES workflows, and even genlock for syncing multiple cameras in real time. With external storage, you can record Dolby Vision HDR up to 4K120. For YouTubers, filmmakers, or content creators, this is the most complete iPhone video package yet.

Battery and Charging: Biggest Ever

Apple gave the Pro models their biggest batteries ever, and the results show. The iPhone 17 Pro lasts up to 31 hours of video playback (28 hours if streaming), while the Pro Max pushes to 37 hours, or 33 hours when streaming. In eSIM‑only versions, the batteries are larger still, with the Pro Max stretching to 39 hours.

Fast charging is supported on both: around 50% in 20 minutes with Apple’s 40W USB‑C adapter, or about 30 minutes using a 30W or higher adapter with MagSafe.

Exact battery sizes aren’t confirmed, but leaks point to the Pro just above 4,500mAh and the Pro Max at roughly 4,832mAh. eSIM‑only models are expected to be bigger still: about 4,252mAh for the Pro and 5,088mAh for the Pro Max, compared to 3,988mAh and 4,823mAh on their SIM tray versions. These differences explain the extended runtime Apple is advertising.

Connectivity and Extras

Connectivity on the Pro models is loaded. They support:

  • 5G (sub‑6) for fast cellular data
  • Wi‑Fi 7 for stronger and more stable wireless speeds
  • Bluetooth 6 for smoother connections to accessories
  • Thread support for smart home devices
  • 2nd‑gen Ultra Wideband for precise location features

The USB‑C port brings up to 10Gbps transfer speeds and DisplayPort video output, making file transfers and external display use much quicker. The Action button now includes a Camera Control mode, letting you adjust exposure, zoom, and styles instantly. And with IP68 water resistance (up to 6m for 30 minutes), durability is covered too.

Colors, Storage, and Accessories

Available in Cosmic Orange, Deep Blue, and Silver, the Pro starts at 256GB and goes up to 1TB. Pro Max introduces a massive 2TB option. Accessories include TechWoven, Silicone, and Clear Cases, a new Crossbody Strap, plus Apple’s 40W Dynamic Power Adapter and Qi2 25W MagSafe chargers.

Availability and Pricing

The iPhone 17 Pro starts at $1,099 in the U.S., and the larger Pro Max at $1,199. Both now include 256GB of storage as the base model. This makes the Pro $100 more than last year’s base model, but in reality you’re paying the same as last year’s 256GB iPhone 16 Pro. The Pro Max, on the other hand, stays at the same entry price.

On monthly plans, the Pro can be financed at $45.79 per month over 24 months, and the Pro Max at $49.95 per month. Storage upgrades, like 512GB, 1TB, and the new 2TB option on the Pro Max, raise the cost by roughly $200 per tier.

Pre‑orders open September 12 at 5 a.m. PT, with general availability beginning September 19 in over 63 countries, and rolling out to 22 more regions on September 26.

Final Thoughts: Should You Upgrade?

The iPhone 17 Pro lineup is Apple’s biggest Pro upgrade in years. From the all‑new plateau design and the brightest display yet, to the 8x telephoto zoom, ProRes RAW video, and the massive battery improvements, this is a package built for people who want more than just the basics. If you’re using a recent Pro like the iPhone 16, the jump is meaningful but not essential unless you care about cameras, battery life, or pro‑level video. But if you’re on anything older, or you’ve been waiting for Apple to push the Pro line forward in a big way, the iPhone 17 Pro is exactly that moment.

mainEntity.name: Is iOS 26 better than iOS 18?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. iOS 26 introduces a visually rich design, smarter system tools, and improved app interfaces—especially if you're on a newer iPhone.

mainEntity.name: Will iOS 26 slow down older iPhones?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not necessarily. While older models like the iPhone 11 may not run animations as smoothly, Apple has optimized performance across supported devices. Battery health and storage space may still affect your experience.

acceptedAnswer.text: No free trial is available. Sometimes high-follower accounts get complimentary upgrades, but generally, it's paid-only.

mainEntity.name: Do I need Premium for a blue checkmark?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. At least Premium or Premium+ (or Verified Organizations) is required.

mainEntity.name: Is X Premium ad-free?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not entirely. Basic has full ads, Premium halves them in main timelines, and Premium+ is mostly ad-free everywhere, but you might see occasional sponsored posts.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between the blue checkmarks and the gold and grey checkmarks?

acceptedAnswer.text: Blue is for individual Premium subscribers. Gold means an official business or non-profit via Verified Organizations. Grey is for governments or multilateral organizations. They come with extras like badges for affiliates and premium support for orgs.

mainEntity.name: Is the previous legacy blue checkmark and X Premium subscription checkmark same?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not really. The legacy one was for active, notable, authentic accounts verified by X's old system. The new blue is exclusive to active subscribers, with no fame check required.

mainEntity.name: Can I answer a call while Live Voicemail is transcribing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yup, absolutely! That’s one of Live Voicemail’s charm points. Tap the green Answer button at any moment while reading that transcription. The caller? They won’t know you’ve had a sneak peek till you pick up.

mainEntity.name: Why don't I see the Live Voicemail option on my iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: Live Voicemail plays with iPhone XS or newer, using iOS 17 or later. Tick those boxes and still no dice? Check if your region settings align, since it’s not rolled out globally just yet.

mainEntity.name: Does Live Voicemail work on Wi-Fi calling?

acceptedAnswer.text: Oh yes, it does. As long as your carrier supports it and you're on iOS 17 or later, you're all set.

mainEntity.name: How is Live Voicemail different from Visual Voicemail?

acceptedAnswer.text: Here’s the key difference: Visual Voicemail shows you a lineup of messages to play back. Live Voicemail, however, gives you live transcription as someone leaves that message, with the added ability to intervene mid-message.

mainEntity.name: Will my caller know I'm reading their voicemail live?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not a chance. Callers won’t catch wind of you viewing their message in real-time unless you answer. From their end, it’s voicemail as usual.

mainEntity.name: Is Live Voicemail available on all carriers?

acceptedAnswer.text: Live Voicemail works with most major carriers, but there’s some variation. If you've run into issues, a word with your carrier might help; they could need to tweak your voicemail settings.

mainEntity.name: How do I delete Live Voicemail transcripts?

acceptedAnswer.text: Deleting Live Voicemail messages mirrors usual ones: swipe left on the message list and tap Delete, or dive into the message and hit the trash icon.

mainEntity.name: Why is Live Voicemail not transcribing messages?

acceptedAnswer.text: Crummy audio quality, boisterous background antics, or unclear speech can toss the transcription off track. It performs best when callers speak clearly in peaceful zones. Restart your iPhone to resolve any temporary transcription issues.

mainEntity.name: Can I save Instagram reels to watch offline without downloading?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, you can not save Instagram reels for offline viewing without downloading, but you can screen record the reel and watch it offline.

mainEntity.name: Is it legal to download reels from Instagram?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, it is legal to download public reels if the creator has allowed it. However, using the downloaded reel for commercial purposes without the original creator's permission is strictly prohibited.

mainEntity.name: Can I download reels from Instagram using a desktop computer?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, you can copy an Instagram reel link, head over to a third-party website, and paste the reel link to download it.

mainEntity.name: Can I download Instagram Reels directly from the Instagram app on my Phone?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, but only in certain cases. The Instagram app allows you to download Reels posted by others only if the creator has enabled the download option. However, downloaded Reels will include an Instagram watermark and the creator’s name, and some may not have audio due to copyright restrictions.

mainEntity.name: What should I do if the download option isn't available for a particular Reel?

acceptedAnswer.text: If the download option is not available in the Share menu, you can use the built-in screen recorder on your iPhone to capture the Reel while playing. Alternatively, copy the Reel’s link and use an online tool to download it on your iPhone (only if the Reel is public). Both methods will not produce any watermark on the video.

mainEntity.name: Are there any privacy concerns when downloading Reels using third-party apps?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Many third-party apps request access to your Instagram account or personal data, which could be a security risk. Additionally, downloading someone else's content without permission might violate Instagram’s policies and copyright laws. Always use trusted sources and respect content creators' rights.

mainEntity.name: Can I download Reels from private accounts?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. If an account is private, you cannot download or access its Reels unless you follow the account, and the creator has enabled downloads. Even then, you should respect their privacy and not share their content without permission.

mainEntity.name: Where are stickers stored on my iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: They’re part of your iCloud account, so they sync across all your Apple devices. You won’t see them in the Files app.

mainEntity.name: Does deleting a sticker remove it from previous conversations?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Stickers you’ve already sent will stay put in those chats, even if you delete the pack or remove them from your device.

mainEntity.name: Can I recover deleted stickers?

acceptedAnswer.text: If it’s from a third-party pack, just reinstall the app from the App Store. Custom stickers will need to be recreated.

mainEntity.name: Do stickers take up a lot of storage?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most sticker packs are small, typically under 5MB. Custom stickers made from Live Photos can be slightly larger, but even a large collection rarely takes up noticeable space. Check Settings > General > iPhone Storage if you want to see exact usage.

mainEntity.name: Can I hide sticker packs instead of deleting them?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Open the Stickers drawer in Messages, scroll to the end, tap Edit, then toggle off any pack you want to hide. It stays installed but won't appear while you're typing.

mainEntity.name: How do I delete Memoji stickers on iPhone?

keyPoints.title: iPhone 17 Pro Design Shift
keyPoints.explanation: The iPhone 17 Pro is expected to feature a bold new rear design with a horizontal camera bar and possibly switch back to aluminum for better recyclability and alignment with Apple’s environmental goals.

keyPoints.title: Display Upgrades and Durability
keyPoints.explanation: While maintaining a 6.3-inch OLED screen with 120Hz, the iPhone 17 Pro might get a new anti-reflective, scratch-resistant coating, improving glare reduction and durability.

keyPoints.title: Performance Boost with A19 Pro and 12GB RAM
keyPoints.explanation: The phone will likely debut the new A19 Pro chip on a 3nm process, coupled with 12GB of RAM, enhancing performance, battery efficiency, and AI capabilities.

keyPoints.title: Enhanced Camera System for Creators
keyPoints.explanation: The iPhone 17 Pro could feature all three rear lenses with 48MP resolution, a new Pro Camera app, dual video recording, and a variable aperture for improved low-light and portrait shots.

keyPoints.title: Battery, Cooling, and Color Innovations
keyPoints.explanation: It may have a larger, up to 5,000mAh battery, vapor chamber cooling for thermal performance, and come in striking new colors like Copper-Orange and Sky Blue, with potential for reverse wireless charging.

title.rendered: Apple Watch Ultra 3 with Satellite Messaging, 5G Support, and Sleep Score

content.rendered:
Get ready for new adventures as Apple finally launched the Apple Watch Ultra 3 after two-year gap. Debuting at the Awe Dropping event, this beast is built tougher, smarter, and more connected than ever.

You will get sharper display, faster performance, 5G cellular, Emergency SOS via satellite, and advanced health features like hypertension alerts and Sleep Score. In this article, I will share all the specifications and features of Apple Watch Ultra 3.

Apple Watch Ultra 3 Display: Big, Bright, and Rugged

The Ultra 3 features Apple’s largest and brightest display yet, extending closer to the edges for an immersive look. It uses advanced wide-angle OLED technology and ultra-efficient LTPO3. This ensure you enjoy a faster 1Hz refresh rate in always-on mode without draining your battery.

Apple has also updated Stopwatch, Timer, and 20 watch faces to match the refresh rate so you can see the ticking seconds without raising your hand. I really liked the new Waypoint watch face. It includes a Live compass, satellite messaging complication, and Night Mode shortcut, perfect for adventures.

Built tough too with a sapphire crystal display (one of the toughest materials on earth) and a durable titanium case, it’s ready for anything you throw at it.

Hardware & Performance Upgrades

Under the hood, Apple used the same S10 chip, but the hardware boost is clear with brighter screen, better 5G, and improved GPS performance.

Battery life takes a massive leap up to 42 hours on a single charge, and up to 72 hours in Low Power Mode. When running out of juice, you can quickly plug it in for 15 minutes and get 12 hours backup. That’s serious staying power for extended adventures.

Emergency SOS via Satellite & 5G Support

The built-in two-way satellite communication is the star feature. So now, even when cell towers are unreachable, you can message emergency services, friends, and family or share your location. Moreover, if your watch detects an accident and you’re unresponsive, it will send an Emergency SOS via satellite. That’s adventure-ready peace of mind.

Plus, 5G cellular support ensures you can call, text, use apps, download media, or contact emergency services even when your iPhone is not with you. Apple has included an advanced algorithm to use two system antennas to boost the signal strength as well.

Health Features: From Sleep to Heart Alerts

The Ultra 3 now offers hypertension (high blood pressure) notifications, helping you catch early warning signs by analyzing heart-vessel responses over time. A nifty health alert on your wrist to detect serious chronic conditions.

On the other hand, the Sleep Score feature gives you an easy-to-understand breakdown of your slumber quality. It covers sleep stages like deep sleep, wake-ups, and consistency so you can actually improve how you rest.

It also keeps an eye on your breathing to track sleep apnea risk. And with the Vitals app, you get overnight stats like heart rate, blood oxygen, respiration, and wrist temperature all at a glance.

Fitness and Workout Updates in Ultra 3

The Apple Watch Ultra 3 takes workouts to a whole new level. It comes with super-accurate dual-frequency GPS, perfect for tracking runs, hikes, or rides with precision.

The new Workout Buddy acts like a personal coach, giving real-time audio feedback based on your performance. Moreover, the Workout app has been redesigned for quicker access to custom workouts, Race Route, and Pacer. Plus, Apple Music now auto-suggests playlists or podcasts to match your exercise vibes.

For sport-specific upgrades:

  • Runners get advanced stride and pace data.
  • Cyclists can track metrics and power with accessories.
  • Swimmers can measure stroke, laps, and water temp.
  • Hikers benefit from offline maps and Backtrack GPS.
  • Divers can use Oceanic+ for scuba tracking.
  • Golfers get pro-level insights with third-party apps.

watchOS 26 Features

The Apple Watch Ultra 3 runs on the brand-new watchOS 26, making it smarter and more fun to use. The interface gets a sleek new Liquid Glass design.

You’ll also see a smarter Smart Stack with context-aware tips, a handy Notes app right on your wrist, and even live translation in Messages for easier global chats. The cool wrist flick gesture lets you control alerts one-handed, and Smart Stacks hints lets you see what’s important quickly.

When Will the Apple Watch Ultra 3 Be Available?

Apple announced the Watch Ultra 3 on September 9 along with the iPhone 17 lineup and Apple Watch Series 11 and SE 3.

You can pre-order the watch on September 12. It will officially start shipping and be available in stores beginning Friday, September 19, 2025.

Enjoy Your Adventures with Ultra 3!

The Apple Watch Ultra 3 is Apple’s most rugged, advanced, and health-focused wearable yet. With its tough titanium design, bright display, and massive battery life, it’s built for explorers and athletes. Moreover, with the power of watchOS 26, and you’ve got a smartwatch that’s smarter, safer, and more personal than ever before.

What do you think of the new Apple Watch Ultra 3? Let me know in the comments below!

mainEntity.name: Can I answer a call while Live Voicemail is transcribing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yup, absolutely! That’s one of Live Voicemail’s charm points. Tap the green Answer button at any moment while reading that transcription. The caller? They won’t know you’ve had a sneak peek till you pick up.

mainEntity.name: Why don't I see the Live Voicemail option on my iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: Live Voicemail plays with iPhone XS or newer, using iOS 17 or later. Tick those boxes and still no dice? Check if your region settings align, since it’s not rolled out globally just yet.

mainEntity.name: Does Live Voicemail work on Wi-Fi calling?

acceptedAnswer.text: Oh yes, it does. As long as your carrier supports it and you're on iOS 17 or later, you're all set.

mainEntity.name: How is Live Voicemail different from Visual Voicemail?

acceptedAnswer.text: Here’s the key difference: Visual Voicemail shows you a lineup of messages to play back. Live Voicemail, however, gives you live transcription as someone leaves that message, with the added ability to intervene mid-message.

mainEntity.name: Will my caller know I'm reading their voicemail live?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not a chance. Callers won’t catch wind of you viewing their message in real-time unless you answer. From their end, it’s voicemail as usual.

mainEntity.name: Is Live Voicemail available on all carriers?

acceptedAnswer.text: Live Voicemail works with most major carriers, but there’s some variation. If you've run into issues, a word with your carrier might help; they could need to tweak your voicemail settings.

mainEntity.name: How do I delete Live Voicemail transcripts?

acceptedAnswer.text: Deleting Live Voicemail messages mirrors usual ones: swipe left on the message list and tap Delete, or dive into the message and hit the trash icon.

mainEntity.name: Why is Live Voicemail not transcribing messages?

acceptedAnswer.text: Crummy audio quality, boisterous background antics, or unclear speech can toss the transcription off track. It performs best when callers speak clearly in peaceful zones. Restart your iPhone to resolve any temporary transcription issues.

mainEntity.name: Can I save Instagram reels to watch offline without downloading?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, you can not save Instagram reels for offline viewing without downloading, but you can screen record the reel and watch it offline.

mainEntity.name: Is it legal to download reels from Instagram?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, it is legal to download public reels if the creator has allowed it. However, using the downloaded reel for commercial purposes without the original creator's permission is strictly prohibited.

mainEntity.name: Can I download reels from Instagram using a desktop computer?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, you can copy an Instagram reel link, head over to a third-party website, and paste the reel link to download it.

mainEntity.name: Can I download Instagram Reels directly from the Instagram app on my Phone?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, but only in certain cases. The Instagram app allows you to download Reels posted by others only if the creator has enabled the download option. However, downloaded Reels will include an Instagram watermark and the creator’s name, and some may not have audio due to copyright restrictions.

mainEntity.name: What should I do if the download option isn't available for a particular Reel?

acceptedAnswer.text: If the download option is not available in the Share menu, you can use the built-in screen recorder on your iPhone to capture the Reel while playing. Alternatively, copy the Reel’s link and use an online tool to download it on your iPhone (only if the Reel is public). Both methods will not produce any watermark on the video.

mainEntity.name: Are there any privacy concerns when downloading Reels using third-party apps?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Many third-party apps request access to your Instagram account or personal data, which could be a security risk. Additionally, downloading someone else's content without permission might violate Instagram’s policies and copyright laws. Always use trusted sources and respect content creators' rights.

mainEntity.name: Can I download Reels from private accounts?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. If an account is private, you cannot download or access its Reels unless you follow the account, and the creator has enabled downloads. Even then, you should respect their privacy and not share their content without permission.

mainEntity.name: Where are the downloaded Reels saved on my iPhone?

mainEntity.name: Where are stickers stored on my iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: They’re part of your iCloud account, so they sync across all your Apple devices. You won’t see them in the Files app.

mainEntity.name: Does deleting a sticker remove it from previous conversations?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Stickers you’ve already sent will stay put in those chats, even if you delete the pack or remove them from your device.

mainEntity.name: Can I recover deleted stickers?

acceptedAnswer.text: If it’s from a third-party pack, just reinstall the app from the App Store. Custom stickers will need to be recreated.

mainEntity.name: Do stickers take up a lot of storage?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most sticker packs are small, typically under 5MB. Custom stickers made from Live Photos can be slightly larger, but even a large collection rarely takes up noticeable space. Check Settings > General > iPhone Storage if you want to see exact usage.

mainEntity.name: Can I hide sticker packs instead of deleting them?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Open the Stickers drawer in Messages, scroll to the end, tap Edit, then toggle off any pack you want to hide. It stays installed but won't appear while you're typing.

mainEntity.name: How do I delete Memoji stickers on iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: You can't fully delete Memoji stickers since they're tied to your Memoji character, but you can stop them from appearing. Go to Settings > General > Keyboard and toggle off Memoji Stickers. This removes them from the keyboard without deleting your Memoji.

keyPoints.title: Apple Watch Ultra 3 Release Timeline
keyPoints.explanation: Expected to launch in the second half of 2025 after a two-year break, with September being the likely month for the release alongside other new Apple products.

keyPoints.title: Potential Display Improvements
keyPoints.explanation: Rumors suggest a switch to microLED technology and a larger 2.12-inch display for the Ultra 3, though these features may not launch until 2026 based on industry sources.

keyPoints.title: Hardware and Connectivity Upgrades
keyPoints.explanation: The Ultra 3 is expected to feature an S10 chip, 5G support via MediaTek modems with RedCap technology, and possibly faster charging speeds to enhance performance and battery life.

keyPoints.title: Enhanced Health and Safety Features
keyPoints.explanation: The upcoming model may introduce blood pressure monitoring, improved sleep tracking, and better heart rate accuracy, along with AI-driven features for smarter health insights.

keyPoints.title: Innovative Satellite Messaging Capabilities
keyPoints.explanation: Gurman hints that the Ultra 3 could be the first smartwatch to support sending messages via satellite, expanding emergency communication options without cellular networks.

title.rendered: Will the iPhone 16 Case Fit the iPhone 17? Answered!

content.rendered:
With every new iPhone release, one of the first questions Apple fans ask is: “Will my old case still fit the new model?” If you’re upgrading from an iPhone 16 to the iPhone 17, you’re probably wondering the same thing. Let’s dive into the design similarities and subtle differences to see if your iPhone 16 case will work with the iPhone 17.

Table of Contents
  • Design Similarities Between iPhone 16 and iPhone 17
  • Where the Differences Come In
  • Will Your iPhone 16 Cases Fit the iPhone 17?
  • Wrapping Up…

Design Similarities Between iPhone 16 and iPhone 17

At first glance, the iPhone 16 and iPhone 17 look almost identical. Both share Apple’s sleek design language with:

  • Similar rear camera placement
  • Matching USB-C port alignment
  • Nearly identical button positions
  • Comparable thickness

These similarities might make you think the cases are interchangeable—but the details tell a different story.

Where the Differences Come In

Apple made a few small but important tweaks with the iPhone 17 that impact case compatibility:

  • Dimensions: The iPhone 17 is about 0.08 inches taller than the iPhone 16.
  • Display Size: iPhone 17 features a 6.3-inch display, up from 6.1 inches on the iPhone 16.
  • Camera Module: The new 48MP Dual Fusion Camera system slightly changes the bump size and alignment.

Related: Apple’s iPhone 17 “Awe Dropping” Event: Everything Announced

Will Your iPhone 16 Cases Fit the iPhone 17?

Unfortunately, no. Because of the iPhone 17’s increased height and redesigned camera module, iPhone 16 cases won’t fit properly on the iPhone 17. The depth difference is minimal, but even a fraction of an inch in height can prevent cases from snapping on securely.

Wrapping Up…

The iPhone 17 takes design cues from the Pro models, most notably, both the standard and Pro now share the same 6.3-inch display size. While it’s disappointing that your iPhone 16 cases won’t carry over, this is a great chance to pick a new case that matches your upgraded device.

Are you switching to the iPhone 17 or sticking with your iPhone 16 for now? Drop your thoughts in the comments!

Don’t miss these related reads:

  • iPhone 17 Colors: Which One Should You Pick?

title.rendered: Apple Watch Series 11 with 5G and Hypertension Alerts

content.rendered:
Apple has officially unveiled the Apple Watch Series 11 at its much-hyped Awe Dropping event, and it’s already creating waves. Packed with a sleeker and durable design, 5G support, Sleep Score, and new watchOS 26 features, you can take your health and lifestyle tracking to the next level with this watch.

In this article, we will share all the Apple Watch Series 11 features you must know about.

Apple Watch Series 11: Design & Display

The Series 11 is Apple’s thinnest and most comfortable design yet. Apple has used unique Ion-X glass as covers on the aluminium Series 11 model. It’s twice as scratch-resistant so you can easily use it daily without worrying.

It’s available in new Space Gray, jet black, rose gold, silver and polished titanium options include natural, gold, and slate. A sleek, durable, and stylish upgrade!

watchOS 26 Highlights

The Series 11 debuts running watchOS 26, packed with fresh features:

  • Liquid Glass design language for a sleeker UI.
  • Workout Buddy: AI-powered fitness coaching, tailored to your regime.
  • New wrist-flick gesture: dismiss calls, silence alarms with a flick.
  • Call Screening and Hold Assist on Phone app
  • Smart Stack hints, built-in Notes app, and Live Translation.

All these smart features makes Apple Watch Series 11 a worthy upgrade.

Hypertension Notifications

Series 11 adds breakthrough a health feature, hypertension notifications.

Rather than giving actual blood pressure numbers, it monitors optical signals over 30-day period and alerts you to early signs of chronic high blood pressure. You can quickly take medical advice based on the insights, potentially saving your life.

Sleep Score

Apple now gives your sleep tracking a boost with a sleep score. It analyzes your sleep based on duration, bedtime consistency, how often you wake up, and times in sleep stages.

Each night, you will your overall sleep score and quality through easy-to-understand metrics in Sleep app. Thus you can assess your nightly rest and take steps to improve it.

Other New & Upgraded Features

  • 5G Cellular: First-ever Series model with 5G support, thanks to redesigned cellular antenna.
  • Up to 24-Hour Battery Life: A full day of use from a single charge.
  • Fast charging: You can charge your Series 11 just 15 minutes to use for eight hours.
  • New watch faces: Apple rolled out redesigned watch face gallery with two new options, Flow and Exactograph.

When Will Apple Watch Series 11 Be Available?

Apple has announced the Apple Watch Series 11 on 9th September 2025 in Awe Dropping Event, alongside the iPhone 17 lineup.

You can pre-order the watch on September 12. And starting from September 19, available to buy in stores.

Bottom Line

The Apple Watch Series 11 is a smart, stylish upgrade, especially if you’re into wellness tracking. With health-first features like hypertension alerts and Sleep Score, plus a responsive new interface powered by watchOS 26 and 5G support, I can say it’s Apple’s most well-rounded watch yet.

Which Apple Watch Series 11 feature caught your eyes? Let me know in the comments below!

keyPoints.title: Apple Watch Series 11 Launch Timeline
keyPoints.explanation: The Series 11 is expected to launch in September 2025, aligning with Apple's usual fall announcement alongside the iPhone 17, despite potential minor delays.

keyPoints.title: Design and Display Expectations for Series 11
keyPoints.explanation: The Series 11 will likely retain the sleek, squared-off design of Series 10, with thinner bezels, but MicroLED display upgrades are delayed until 2026; a new color option might be introduced.

keyPoints.title: New S11 Chipset and Connectivity Enhancements
keyPoints.explanation: The Series 11 will feature an efficient S11 chip with no noticeable speed improvements but improved battery life, and it may include a MediaTek 5G RedCap modem for faster wireless connectivity.

keyPoints.title: Health Monitoring and Features Rumors
keyPoints.explanation: Blood pressure monitoring might finally arrive, providing trend alerts rather than precise readings, along with ongoing features like ECG, fall detection, and potential sleep apnea detection.

keyPoints.title: Software and Future Directions
keyPoints.explanation: Running on watchOS 12, the Series 11 could see a UI redesign inspired by visionOS, enhanced AI features via iOS 19.4, and incremental health-focused innovations, with exciting futuristic concepts on the horizon.

title.rendered: iPhone 17 Colors: Which One Should You Pick?

content.rendered:
Apple has officially launched the iPhone 17 lineup. Every year, alongside the usual safe picks like white, black, and grey, Apple adds new shades to grab attention. That makes choosing harder than it sounds. Do you stick with a classic white or gamble on the bold new Orange? If you’re torn between safe and standout, here’s a closer look at the lineup.

Table of Contents
  • The Standard iPhone 17
  • The All-New iPhone Air
  • iPhone 17 Pro and Pro Max
  • Price And Availability
  • So, Which Color Should You Pick?

The Standard iPhone 17

The base iPhone 17 is where Apple offers the widest mix of playful and practical tones. You can go bright with Lavender, Mist Blue, or Sage if you want something fresh. Or, if you prefer a timeless look, Black and White are still here. The Mist Blue and Lavender stand out as the youthful choices, while Sage gives a more grounded, earthy vibe.

iPhone 17 Colors: 

  • Lavender
  • Mist Blue
  • Sage
  • Black
  • White

Color preference is subjective, but if you ask me, I would definitely choose Mist Blue or Sage.

The All-New iPhone Air

Replacing the Plus model, the iPhone Air is slimmer and built from titanium, which already sets it apart. Its colors feel just as refined: Space Black and Cloud White for minimalists, Sky Blue if you want something light but trendy, and Light Gold, which is almost jewelry-like. If you want a phone that looks as premium as it feels, Light Gold is the one most likely to turn heads.

iPhone Air Colors: 

  • Space Black
  • Cloud White
  • Sky Blue
  • Light Gold

After having a hands-on with the device, we prefer the Sky Blue version. However, all the colors look great in the iPhone Air lineup. 

iPhone 17 Pro and Pro Max

The 17 Pro models take on a more professional palette. They’re available in Deep Blue, Cosmic Orange, and Silver. Apple is clearly going for fewer but bolder choices here. Cosmic Orange is the statement color, loud yet elegant. Deep Blue feels classy and versatile, while Silver is the safe, sophisticated pick that never ages. Some sources also mention Black and White options, but Apple’s launch focus seems to be on these three.

iPhone 17 Pro and Pro Max Colors: 

  • Deep Blue
  • Cosmic Orange
  • Silver

With the Pro models, nothing stands out quite like the Cosmic Orange shade. However, it’s certainly a bold choice. 

Price And Availability

Here’s how the lineup looks after Apple’s September 9 launch event:

  • iPhone 17: $799
  • iPhone Air: $999
  • iPhone 17 Pro: $1,099
  • iPhone 17 Pro Max: $1,199

Pre-orders start on September 12, with availability in stores from September 19.

So, Which Color Should You Pick?

If you like phones that blend in, Black, White, and Silver are always safe. For those who want personality without being too loud, Mist Blue, Sage, and Deep Blue strike a balance. And if you want your phone to be a conversation starter, Lavender, Light Gold, or Cosmic Orange will do the job.

Don’t miss these related reads:

  • iPhone 17 vs iPhone 16: The Biggest Upgrade
  • Apple’s iPhone 17 “Awe Dropping” Event

title.rendered: Apple’s iPhone 17 “Awe Dropping” Event: Everything Announced

content.rendered:
Apple’s September 2025 keynote is, well, exactly what we had expected for months based on the many leaks and rumors. Held at Steve Jobs Theater in Cupertino, the event packed in new iPhones, refreshed Apple Watches, upgraded AirPods, and even a brand-new iPhone model that had the crowd buzzing.

The spotlight, of course, was on the iPhone 17 family. Apple unveiled three main models: the regular iPhone 17, the powerful iPhone 17 Pro, and a bold new addition of the ultra-thin iPhone Air. Let’s go through each. 

Table of Contents
  • iPhone 17: The Base Model Gets Serious Upgrades
  • iPhone Air: Thin, Light, and Bold
  • iPhone 17 Pro: Apple’s Workhorse Gets a Redesign
  • Apple Watch Lineup: Big Year for Wearables
  • AirPods Pro 3: Small Ears, Big Upgrades
  • Final Thoughts

iPhone 17: The Base Model Gets Serious Upgrades

The standard iPhone 17 is no longer the “entry-level” phone people expect. It comes with a larger 6.3-inch ProMotion display with thinner bezels, peaking at an eye-searing 3,000 nits of outdoor brightness. For the first time, even the regular iPhone gets 120Hz refresh Pro Motion displays, something only Pro models has until now. 

Under the hood is the new A19 chip, with a 6-core CPU and 5-core GPU, offering 20% better performance than last year’s A18. The cameras got a big push too: a 48MP main sensor and a 48MP ultra-wide lens. The selfie camera has a new square sensor that enables Center Stage, so whether you’re taking landscape selfies or on a Zoom call, the framing adjusts automatically.

Colors this year feel livelier: lavender, miss blue, sage, black, and white.

iPhone Air: Thin, Light, and Bold

The star of the show this year was the iPhone Air, Apple’s thinnest iPhone ever at just 5.6mm. What many expected to be called the iPhone 17 Air has instead been introduced simply as the iPhone Air. From a naming perspective, this model doesn’t quite sit within the iPhone 17 family.

For durability, Apple is using Ceramic Shield on both the front and back of the device. While the Pro models are moving back to aluminum, the Air comes with a slim titanium frame.

Despite its size, it promises “pro performance” with the A19 Pro chip. It carries a 6.5-inch ProMotion display, 120Hz refresh, and the same 3,000 nits brightness.

Apple clearly wants the Air to feel special. Accessories include a slim MagSafe battery that stretches vertically across the phone, translucent and bumper cases, and even a crossbody strap. With the MagSafe battery, Apple says you can push video playback to 40 hours. It will be available in Space Black, Cloud White, Light Gold, and Sky Blue. 

iPhone 17 Pro: Apple’s Workhorse Gets a Redesign

The iPhone 17 Pro is where Apple flexed hardest. It ditches titanium for aluminum, which some may see as a downgrade, but compensates with the biggest battery ever in an iPhone. It also introduces a new rear design Apple calls a “full-width camera plateau”, a bar stretching across the phone, similar to Google’s Pixel.

The camera system is no joke. Up front, there’s an 18MP Center Stage selfie camera. On the back, three 48MP sensors deliver what Apple calls “the equivalent of eight pro lenses.” There’s a new Fusion telephoto lens with 4x (100mm) and 8x (200mm) options, plus up to 40x digital zoom. ProRes RAW capture, Genlock support for multi-cam syncing, and updated deep-learning algorithms all point at Apple chasing serious filmmakers.

Inside is the A19 Pro chip, paired with a new vapor chamber for thermal management, promising 40% better sustained performance. The display is protected by Ceramic Shield 2 with a seven-layer anti-reflective coating. Storage goes up to 2TB on the Pro Max. Color options include silver, deep blue, and a striking cosmic orange.

Apple Watch Lineup: Big Year for Wearables

Apple didn’t just stop at phones. This year’s Watch refresh feels like a reset for the entire lineup.

  • Series 11 ($399): Slimmer design, 5G support, new Sleep Score, high blood pressure detection, and stronger glass. Battery life hits 24 hours. Comes in aluminum (jet black, silver, rose gold, space gray) and titanium (natural, gold, slate).
  • SE 3 ($249): Finally gets an always-on display, powered by the S10 chip. It adds sleep apnea detection, wrist-flick gestures, double-tap, and fast charging. Battery remains 18 hours. Colors: midnight and starlight.
  • Ultra 3 ($799): Rugged as ever but now with 42 hours of battery, 5G, and satellite connectivity. It has the biggest display ever on an Apple Watch, thanks to slimmer bezels. Comes in natural and black titanium.

AirPods Pro 3: Small Ears, Big Upgrades

After three years, Apple finally refreshed the AirPods Pro. The third-gen model adds a heart rate sensor that integrates with the Fitness app, better sweat resistance, and a smaller design with five ear tip sizes. Active Noise Cancellation has been doubled compared to AirPods Pro 2, with Apple bragging it now delivers the “world’s best ANC.” Battery life gets a bump too, 8 hours with ANC on and 10 hours in Transparency mode.

The real headline feature? Live translation powered by Apple Intelligence. Imagine traveling and hearing translations directly in your ears in real-time. At $249, they’re available for preorder now and ship September 19.

Final Thoughts

Preorders open this Friday, September 12, with all devices shipping September 19. iPhone 17, iPhone 17 Air, and iPhone 17 Pro all start at 256GB storage. The Pro Max model offers storage capacity of up to 2TB. AirPods Pro 3 are priced at $249, and the new Apple Watch lineup starts at $249 for the SE 3, $399 for Series 11, and $799 for Ultra 3. All of these devices will be available to order on Friday and reach customers a week later.

Read More:

  • iPhone 17 vs iPhone 16: The Biggest Upgrade

title.rendered: iPhone 17 vs iPhone 16: The Biggest Upgrade Apple Made This Year

content.rendered:
Apple has finally unveiled the much-anticipated iPhone 17 lineup, which succeeds last year’s iPhone 16 series. Like previous launch events, the new entry, iPhone Air, and the Pro models grabbed the spotlight, but the standard iPhone 17 isn’t playing second fiddle this year. While the design language feels familiar, several under-the-hood upgrades might tempt iPhone 16 owners to switch. However, the bigger question is whether iPhone 16 owners should give in to this temptation.

This post breaks down the key differences and helps you decide if upgrading makes sense.

Table of Contents
  • Quick Comparison: iPhone 17 vs iPhone 16
  • Design and Build
  • Display: The Game-Changer
  • Camera Upgrades
  • Performance: A19 vs A18
  • Battery and Charging
  • Price and Value
  • Verdict: Should You Upgrade?

Quick Comparison: iPhone 17 vs iPhone 16

Design and Build

The iPhone 17, in terms of design language, is entirely identical to the iPhone 16, which isn’t surprising for Apple. Both devices have the same rounded-edge aesthetic and feature the same vertically aligned rear camera module. However, iPhone 17 feels slightly lighter (however, it’s not) and comes in fresh new color options. Moreover, the materials feel more refined, though the form factor remains nearly identical.

Those craving a major design refresh will find it only in the iPhone 17 Pro models, which sport slimmer bezels and a sleeker titanium build. For standard users, however, the changes are subtle rather than revolutionary.

Display: The Game-Changer

This is the most noticeable difference between the two. With iPhone 17, Apple has finally added the ProMotion display (120Hz refresh rate) to its standard iPhones, plus it’s now 6.3 inches. On the other hand, iPhone 16 sports the same OLED display with a standard 60Hz refresh rate, which has been the norm since many previous iPhones. This much-anticipated upgrade makes scrolling, animations, and gaming buttery smooth.

Besides this, the iPhone 17 also offers higher peak brightness, 3000 nits, than the iPhone 16, which is useful for outdoor use. For many users, this single feature may be the most compelling reason to upgrade.

Camera Upgrades

At first glance, the rear camera system of the iPhone 17 and iPhone 16 appears the same. But the iPhone 17 introduces Apple’s new Dual Fusion Camera system, which fuses data from both sensors to deliver sharper details, improved dynamic range, and richer low-light shots.

Another major addition is the 12MP front-facing camera with Center Stage support. Previously limited to iPads and Macs, Center Stage uses machine learning to automatically keep you in frame during video calls, even if you move around. It’s a game-changer for FaceTime, Zoom, and other video conferencing apps, and a clear step up from the static selfie camera on the iPhone 16.

Performance: A19 vs A18

Powering the iPhone 17 is the new A19 chip, which promises better speed and efficiency compared to the iPhone 16’s A18 chip. While both processors offer snappier performance in everyday tasks, the A19 ensures longer support and better performance in demanding apps and games.

Since Apple is known for limiting features on iPhones with older chipsets, the iPhone 17 can be considered a future-proof bet.

Battery and Charging

The iPhone 17 houses a slightly larger battery and benefits from the energy efficiency of the A19 chip. This gives the iPhone 17 a slight edge in screen-on time over the iPhone 16. Moreover, Apple has also bumped up MagSafe charging speeds.

Price and Value

At launch, the iPhone 17 costs the same as the launch price of the iPhone 16, i.e, $799. But since the iPhone 16 is now discounted, it is a tempting option for those who don’t care about the new features. However, the inclusion of a ProMotion display, an upgraded set of cameras, and a more powerful processor does make the iPhone 17 feel closer to a Pro model.

Simply put, the iPhone 16 is still a strong value, but the iPhone 17 delivers Pro-like features at a lower price point.

Verdict: Should You Upgrade?

If you’re using an iPhone 16, you still have a capable device that will last for years. Apple’s software updates ensure that your phone won’t feel outdated anytime soon, and for most users, it continues to offer excellent performance, reliable cameras, and solid battery life.

But if the jump to a 120Hz ProMotion display, better low-light photography, faster performance, 256GB base storage, and longer software support matter to you, the iPhone 17 is a meaningful step forward.

In the end, the iPhone 17 is not a must-have for every iPhone 16 user. But if you want a device that feels modern, future-proof, and packed with more polished everyday features, the iPhone 17 is worth the jump.

title.rendered: X (formerly Twitter) Not Working on iPhone? 10 Easy Fixes

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Common causes for X (Twitter) issues on iPhone: Freezing, crashing, or failed loading often stem from app glitches, outdated iOS, server outages, weak internet, or low storage.
  • Quick checks before deeper fixes: Update both iOS and the X app, then verify X’s servers with tools like DownDetector to rule out broader outages.
  • Restart can clear small bugs: A quick iPhone restart often fixes temporary system glitches that stop X from opening, refreshing, or working properly.
  • Network stability is crucial: Test Safari, toggle Wi-Fi or cellular, reconnect networks, or reset iPhone network settings to stabilize X app performance.
  • Adjust iPhone settings for smoother use: Enable cellular access, correct date and time, free storage, reset keyboard, resize uploads, or reinstall X if problems persist.

If you’re reading this, chances are you’re frustrated because the X (formerly Twitter) app on your iPhone isn’t working. Maybe it’s freezing, crashing, refusing to load your feed, missing notifications, or just won’t let you sign in. Don’t worry, I’ve been there too, stuck with a spinning wheel or blank feed when I wanted to scroll.

Most of these issues have quick and easy fixes. In this guide, I’ll explain why X (Twitter) may stop working on iPhone and share 10 step-by-step solutions so you can get back to tweeting in no time.

Table of Contents
  • Why X (Twitter) May Not Work on iPhone
  • Quick Checks Before Troubleshooting
  • 10 Easy Fixes for X (Twitter) Not Working on iPhone
    • 1. Restart Your Device
    • 2. Check Your Internet Connection
    • 3. Allow Cellular Access for X
    • 4. Free Up Storage Space
    • 5. Correct Date & Time
    • 6. Switch to Default Keyboard
    • 7. Resize Media Before Uploading
    • 8. Check Notifications Settings
    • 9. Log Out and Back In
    • 10. Delete and Reinstall the App
  • Can't Log In to X (Twitter)?
  • Pro Tips to Prevent Future Issues
  • Enjoy X (Twitter) App Again!

Why X (Twitter) May Not Work on iPhone

Here are the most common reasons why the app misbehaves:

  • App glitches: Temporary bugs that cause freezing, crashing, or feeds not loading.
  • Outdated app or iOS: Older versions can lead to compatibility issues.
  • Server outages: X’s servers might be down due to updates or maintenance.
  • Network issues: Poor Wi-Fi or mobile data can block tweets from loading.
  • Low storage: A nearly full iPhone can make the app sluggish or crash.
  • Incorrect settings: Wrong date/time, denied permissions, or restricted access can cause login errors.

Quick Checks Before Troubleshooting

Do these first—they often fix the problem right away:

  1. Check your iOS version: Your iPhone must run the latest iOS. Go to Settings > General > Software Update and tap Update Now if an update is available.
  2. Update the X app: Developers often release fixes for bugs. Head to the App Store, tap your profile, and scroll to see if X needs an update.  
  3. Check X’s servers: Sometimes, the problem is on X’s side. Visit a site like DownDetector to see if servers are down. You’ll need to wait for them to fix it.  

If you’re still seeing “X Cannot be Opened” or “Cannot Receive Messages at This Time,” move on to the 10 fixes below.

10 Easy Fixes for X (Twitter) Not Working on iPhone

Here are some tried-and-true solutions to get X back in action. Work through them one by one, and you’ll likely find the fix that works for you. 

1. Restart Your Device 

A reboot clears temporary system glitches.

  1. Just hold down the Side button + Volume button 
  2. Slide to power off. 
  3. Wait for a few minutes and turn it back on.  
  4. Open the X app and see if it’s loading and working. 

2. Check Your Internet Connection

A shaky internet connection can cause X to display a blank feed, fail to load tweets or media, or prevent the app from opening. Try these: 

  • Switch between Wi-Fi and cellular: If you’re on Wi-Fi, toggle it off in Settings > Wi-Fi and use cellular data (or vice versa). 
  • Test your connection: Open Safari and load a website. If it’s slow or fails, try turning off and on your router or moving closer to it. For cellular, check your signal bars. 
  • Forget and reconnect to Wi-Fi: Go to Settings > Wi-Fi, tap (i) next to your network, hit Forget This Network, then reconnect with your password.
  • Turn off VPN: Connecting to VPN can slow down your network speed. So, disconnect from the server. 
  • Reset Your Network: If your iPhone is struggling with the internet, reset your network from Settings. 

3. Allow Cellular Access for X

If you’re using cellular data, X needs permission to access the internet. 

  1. Go to Settings and tap on Cellular. 
  2. Scroll down and tap Show All. 
  3. Find the X app and make sure the toggle is enabled.  
  4. If it’s off, flip it on and try loading the X app and posts again. 

4. Free Up Storage Space

Running low on storage can make apps like X sluggish or crash repeatedly. Check your iPhone’s storage in Settings > General > iPhone Storage.

If it’s nearly full, free up storage space:  

  • Delete unused apps, old photos, or videos you no longer need.  
  • Offload apps you rarely use. It saves their data but frees up space. 
  • Remove all content from the Recently Deleted folder. 

5. Correct Date & Time

This one’s sneaky! When your iPhone’s date and time are incorrect, X might struggle to connect to its servers or fail to open or send Direct Messages.  

If you cannot log in to the X app, this can be the cause. Typically, you will encounter alerts such as “Unauthorized or Invalid username and password” on the login page. 

  1. Open the Settings app and tap on General. 
  2. Select Date & Time  
  3. Toggle on Set Automatically.

This syncs your phone with the internet’s time, potentially fixing X iOS app issues. You can also enable Background App Refresh to ensure X is always reachable. 

6. Switch to Default Keyboard

If you’re using a third-party keyboard (like Gboard) and can’t send tweets or DMs, it’s possible they’re interfering with the X’s input fields. Switch to the default iPhone keyboard to fix it. 

  1. From the Settings app, tap General and select Keyboard. 
  2. Tap Keyboards and make sure the default one is active.

Sometimes, the built-in keyboard also acts up. In that case, tap Edit > minus sign next to the keyboard and select Delete. Hit the checkmark at the top to confirm.  

Now, tap Add New Keyboard and select your preferred iPhone keyboard. 

7. Resize Media Before Uploading

Struggling to post that perfect selfie or video clip? Large files might be the cause of media upload failure issues. Try resizing them:

  • Check your file size and ensure it’s within X’s upload limits (usually around 512 MB for videos, 15 MB for GIFs, and 5 MB for images).
  • Reduce your photo file size using built-in tools or compressor websites like iLoveIMG. Also, trim videos on the Photos app before uploading. Videos should be under 140 seconds.
  • Your video file should be in .mp4 or .mov format; otherwise, it won’t be supported. On the other hand, images and GIFs can be in JPG, PNG, GIF, and WEBP formats. So, convert your HEIC photos to JPG first.
  • If you’re on a slow connection, switch to Wi-Fi for faster uploads.

Tip: As an X Premium user, you can upload videos up to 8 GB in size.

8. Check Notifications Settings

You can miss mentions or DMs if push notifications aren’t coming through your iPhone. Let’s fix that.

  1. Go to Settings > Notifications
  2. Scroll down and select X.
  3. Ensure Allow Notifications and Time Sensitive Notifications are toggled on.
     

You can also customize which alerts you want (like mentions or DMs). While you’re at it, tap X Notifications Settings at the bottom. It will open the X app settings. Here you can enable the required ones.

Pro tip: Ensure your iPhone is not using any Focus mode like Do Not Disturb. 

9. Log Out and Back In

If the X/Twitter app is still not working on your iPhone, try logging out and back in. First, save your Post drafts, as removing your account clears them. 

  1. Open the X app and tap your profile picture in the top left corner. 
  2. Go to Settings and privacy. 
  3. Select Your account > Account information.
  4. Tap Log out and confirm. 
  5. Then, tap Sign in, enter your username and password, and select Done to log back in.

This can refresh your account’s connection to X’s servers. 

10. Delete and Reinstall the App

When all else fails, it’s time for a clean slate. Deleting the app removes its old cache files and corrupted data, which can cause glitches. 

  1. Press and hold the X app icon on your Home Screen. 
  2. Tap Remove App > Delete App. 
  3. Then head to the App Store, search for X or Twitter, and tap the cloud icon to reinstall it.

You’ll need to log in again and see if the app is opening. 

Can’t Log In to X (Twitter)?

Login issues are the worst, right? You’re itching to check your mentions, but the app’s gatekeeping. Here’s what to do: 

  • Verify your credentials: Double-check your username (or email) and password. If you’re using two-factor authentication (2FA), make sure you have the code from your authenticator app or SMS. 
  • Reset your password: Tap Forgot password? On your login screen, follow the instructions and check your email for a reset link. Don’t forget to check your spam folder! 
  • Contact X support: If you’re still locked out, reach out to X’s support team through their Help Center (accessible via a browser at help.x.com). They can help with account recovery or other login issues. 

Pro Tips to Prevent Future Issues

To keep X running smoothly on your iPhone, here are some pro tips: 

  • Keep everything updated: Regularly update your iOS and X app to avoid compatibility issues. 
  • Clear cache occasionally: In the X app, go to Settings and privacy > Accessibility, display, and languages > Data usage > Media storage > Clear media storage to free up space from cached images and videos.
  • Use a strong network: Stick to reliable Wi-Fi or a solid cellular signal for the best experience. 
  • Clear background apps: Avoid running too many apps in the background while using Twitter. 
  • Restart weekly: Make it a habit to restart your iPhone every week or so to keep things fresh. 
  • Monitor storage: Keep at least 1-2 GB of free space on your iPhone to avoid app slowdowns. 

Enjoy X (Twitter) App Again! 

Dealing with X not working on your iPhone can feel annoying, but most issues are fixable with a little patience. Begin with the basics, then proceed to more specific fixes, such as reinstalling the app or resetting your password. If you’re still stuck, X’s support team has your back. Now, go forth and tweet your heart out!  

Got any other tricks that worked for you? Drop them in the comments below, I’d love to hear them!

FAQs

Why is X (Twitter) not loading on my iPhone?

It’s usually poor internet, an outdated app/iOS, or a temporary server outage.

Why does the X app keep crashing?

Low storage, app bugs, or outdated versions. A reinstall often fixes it.

Why can’t I log in?

Check your credentials, reset your password, or contact X Support.

How do I fix X notifications not working?

Enable them in Settings > Notifications > X and check that Do Not Disturb isn’t on.

  • Threads vs. Twitter (X): Key Differences You Need to Know
  • How to Pin a Post on X (Twitter) on iPhone, iPad, or desktop
  • How to Clear X (Twitter) Cache on iPhone, Android, and Web for a Faster Experience
  • X (Twitter) Calls Enabled by Default: Here’s How to Turn Them Off

keyPoints.title: Common causes for X (Twitter) issues on iPhone
keyPoints.explanation: Problems like freezing, crashing, or load failures are often due to app glitches, outdated software, server outages, poor network, low storage, or incorrect settings.

keyPoints.title: Quick pre-troubleshooting steps
keyPoints.explanation: First, ensure your iOS and app are up to date, and check if X's servers are operational using sites like DownDetector before trying more fixes.

keyPoints.title: Restart your device to fix temporary glitches
keyPoints.explanation: A simple restart can clear minor system bugs and often resolves app loading or crashing problems.

keyPoints.title: Check your internet connection
keyPoints.explanation: Ensure a stable network by toggling Wi-Fi or cellular data, testing your connection in Safari, reconnecting Wi-Fi, and resetting network settings if necessary.

keyPoints.title: Adjust settings and updates for optimal performance
keyPoints.explanation: Allow cellular access, free up storage, correct date & time settings, switch to the default keyboard, resize media files, check notification settings, and re-login or reinstall for a smoother experience.
