title.rendered: 10 Fixes to AirDrop Not Working on iPhone, iPad or Mac

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Make sure both devices are unlocked and active—AirDrop won’t work if the screen is off or locked during the transfer attempt.
  • Set AirDrop visibility to ‘Everyone for 10 Minutes’ or ‘Contacts Only’ to ensure your device is discoverable by the sender.
  • Toggle Bluetooth and Wi-Fi on both devices to reset the AirDrop connection—both are required for transfers to work.
  • Disable Personal Hotspot and check Mac firewall settings—Hotspot interferes with AirDrop, and firewalls can block incoming file transfers.
  • Reset network settings if AirDrop still fails—this clears any persistent bugs but will erase saved Wi-Fi networks and VPN setups.

AirDrop lets you seamlessly share files, photos, contacts, and more in the original quality between Apple devices. However, like any other tech, it can also encounter minor hiccups that impact its performance.

If AirDrop isn’t working on your iPhone, iPad, or Mac, be it due to wrong AirDrop settings or compatibility issues, we’ve got you covered. Below are some effective solutions to troubleshoot AirDrop issues on your device. 

Table of Contents
  • 1. Ensure your device is powered on and unlocked
  • 2. Adjust the AirDrop settings
    • On iPhone
    • On Mac
  • 3. Toggle Bluetooth and Wi-Fi
    • On iPhone
    • On Mac
  • 4. Turn off Personal Hotspot
  • 5. Adjust your Mac's Firewall
  • 6. Check AirDrop Restrictions
    • On iPhone
    • On Mac
  • 7. Restart your iPhone, iPad, or Mac
  • 8. Turn off the VPN
  • 9. Bring the two devices closer
  • 10. Reset Network Settings

1. Ensure your device is powered on and unlocked 

Discoverability is important for AirDrop to function properly. If your device is dead or locked, it may not be visible in the list of devices available for receiving AirDrop on other devices. As a result, neither the other person will be able to send files nor will you be able to receive them. 
 
So, if you’re having trouble receiving AirDrop transfers, ensure your iPhone or Mac is powered on and unlocked. Similarly, ask the other person to ensure the same if you can’t discover their device on your AirDrop’s share list. 

2. Adjust the AirDrop settings

If your iPhone or Mac is powered on and unlocked but still can’t receive files from unsaved contacts, you should check your AirDrop settings. There are a total of three levels of controls to limit the visibility of your device for AirDrop transfers:  

  • Receiving Off: Your iPhone or Mac won’t be discoverable. Hence, no one can send you anything via AirDrop. 
  • Contacts Only: Only your saved contacts can view your device and share files. 
  • Everyone for 10 Minutes: All nearby Apple devices can view and share files with you, whether it’s a saved contact or not. 

Now that you know how each one of the three settings affects AirDrop transfers, here’s how you can adjust them on your iPhone or Mac.

On iPhone 

  1. Open Settings and go to General → AirDrop. 
  2. Here, select Everyone for 10 Minutes to receive from every nearby Apple device or Contacts Only to receive files from saved contacts.
     
  3. Alternatively, pull down the Control Center, press on the networks block in the top-left corner, long-press the AirDrop button, and select an appropriate option. 

On Mac 

  1. Open System Settings and go to General → AirDrop & Handoff.
     
  2. Click the up-down arrow keys next to AirDrop and select the appropriate option.
     
  3. Alternatively, click the Control Center button in the menu bar, click on AirDrop, and toggle on the button. Then, select a discoverability option based on your preference.

3. Toggle Bluetooth and Wi-Fi  

AirDrop relies on Wi-Fi and Bluetooth networks to share files between Apple devices. Yes, Apple did introduce the AirDrop transfer over cellular data ability with iOS 17, but Wi-Fi is still needed to initiate the transfer process. So, if AirDrop isn’t working on your iPhone or Mac, I suggest you go into the Wi-Fi and Bluetooth settings and try toggling them off and on.

On iPhone  

  1. Open Settings, go to Wi-Fi, and toggle off the Wi-Fi switch.
  2. Wait a few seconds, then turn the Wi-Fi back on.
     
  3. Similarly, head to Bluetooth and toggle it off.
  4. Wait a few seconds, then turn Bluetooth on.
     

On Mac 

  1. Open Settings, head to Wi-Fi, and toggle off Wi-Fi if it’s on.
  2. Wait a few seconds, then turn on the Wi-Fi again. 
  3. Likewise, go to Bluetooth and toggle off the switch for Bluetooth.
  4. Wait a few seconds, then turn Bluetooth back on. 

4. Turn off Personal Hotspot 

When you enable the Personal Hotspot on your iPhone, Wi-Fi automatically shuts off, and the iPhone shares your mobile internet connection with another device. If you try to use AirDrop during this time, it may not work. Turn off Personal Hotspot first, and then try sending or receiving AirDrop again.

  1. Open Settings.
  2. Go to Personal Hotspot and toggle off Allow Others to Join.
     
  3. Alternatively, head to the networks settings block in the Control Center and tap the Personal Hotspot button to turn it off. 

5. Adjust your Mac’s Firewall

The Firewall on your Mac is designed to monitor and control all outgoing and incoming network traffic. Simply put, the Firewall prevents unauthorized applications, programs, and services from accepting incoming connections. However, a too restrictive Firewall can mingle with the settings the AirDrop transfer relies on—Bluetooth and Wi-Fi—and prevent your Mac from being discoverable and receiving AirDrop requests.

So, to fix this AirDrop issue on your Mac, adjust the Firewall capabilities accordingly.

  1. Open Settings → Networks → Firewall.
  2. Click on the Options button.
  3. Here, ensure that Block All Incoming Connections is toggled off.
  4. Next, toggle on Automatically allow built-in software to receive incoming connections if not already.

6. Check AirDrop Restrictions

While the chances of this happening are slim, it’s possible that you may have disabled AirDrop using Screen Time restrictions on your iPhone for one reason or another. If this is the case, the AirDrop icon might look greyed out. You’ll need to use Screen Time on your Mac or iPhone to remove the content and privacy restrictions you previously enabled.

On iPhone

  1. Go to Settings → Screen Time → Content & Privacy Restrictions.
     
  2. Tap Allowed Apps, then toggle on AirDrop.
     

On Mac 

  1. Open Settings and go to Screen Time → Content & Privacy.
     
  2. Choose App Restrictions, then toggle on AirDrop under the Allowed in iOS section.
     

7. Restart your iPhone, iPad, or Mac

Although restarting your iPhone, iPad, or Mac can often fix minor software glitches or bugs, if it doesn’t, you can perform a hard reset.

  1. Press and release the Volume Up button.
  2. Press and release the Volume Down button.
  3. Press and hold the Side button until the Apple logo appears.

You can restart your Mac by clicking on the Apple menu > Restart.

8. Turn off the VPN 

As discussed, AirDrop relies on the local network connection to transfer files between Apple devices. An active VPN assigns a different IP address to your iPhone and can alter network configuration, making it difficult for AirDrop to establish local network connections to other devices.  
 
So, if AirDrop isn’t working on your iPhone or iPad, disconnect the VPN and try again. 

  1. Open Settings.
  2. Go to VPN or VPN and Device Management.
  3. Toggle off the Status switch.
     

The steps to disable VPN on a Mac are also pretty similar.

9. Bring the two devices closer

While AirDrop transfer over cellular data is now possible, it still relies on the Bluetooth network to initiate the process. If the two devices aren’t in the Bluetooth range (10m), the other person’s iPhone won’t be visible on yours.

To avoid this, bring the two devices closer and try the process again.

Note: When bringing the two devices closer, make sure they don’t contact one another, as this can force the NameDrop feature to activate.

10. Reset Network Settings

Tried everything, and nothing worked? Or did AirDrop start working, but the transfers are taking longer than usual? In that case, you can reset Network Settings to eliminate any glitch or bug hindering the AirDrop performance.

Wrapping up…

That’s it; these are all the tried and tested solutions that can help when AirDrop isn’t working on your iPhone, iPad, or Mac. However, if the issue persists, the Wi-Fi or Bluetooth hardware might be at fault, and seeking professional assistance is recommended in such cases.

If you have another solution that should be on this list, do share it with us in the comments.

Read more:

  • Can’t share passwords with AirDrop on iPhone? 9 Real fixes
  • How to change AirDrop name on iPhone, iPad, and Mac

mainEntity.name: Why is X (Twitter) not loading on my iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: It's usually poor internet, an outdated app/iOS, or a temporary server outage.

mainEntity.name: Why does the X app keep crashing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Low storage, app bugs, or outdated versions. A reinstall often fixes it.

mainEntity.name: Why can't I log in?

acceptedAnswer.text: Check your credentials, reset your password, or contact X Support.

mainEntity.name: How do I fix X notifications not working?

mainEntity.name: Can I record calls without the other person knowing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Nope, iOS makes the call public, letting everyone know it's being captured. You can't turn off this alert since it keeps things above board legally.

mainEntity.name: Where are my iPhone call recordings saved?

acceptedAnswer.text: You'll find all recordings in the Notes app, under the "Call Recordings" folder. They're synced through iCloud if that's running on your gears.

mainEntity.name: How do I access the transcripts of my recorded calls?

acceptedAnswer.text: Open "Call Recordings" in Notes; the transcript is cozy beneath the audio file and searchable.

mainEntity.name: Why can't I see the record button on my iPhone during a call?

acceptedAnswer.text: To get the full kit you need iOS 18 or later, the right regional settings, and Apple's Intelligence cruising cool in Settings.

mainEntity.name: Does the iPhone call recording feature work with FaceTime or WhatsApp?

acceptedAnswer.text: Nope, this little gem’s closed for just regular calls via the Phone app. Third-party recordings aren’t invited to this party.

mainEntity.name: How do I share a recorded phone call from the Notes app?

acceptedAnswer.text: In Notes, hit up the recording, slap the share button, and choose your audience. You decide if they get audio, transcript, or both.

mainEntity.name: Can I automatically record all calls on my iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: You gotta actually tap that record button for each chat there's no collective auto-record option.

mainEntity.name: How do I delete call recordings from my iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: In Notes, a left swipe on the ones to toss will reveal "Delete," or you can go batch-mode with "Edit."

mainEntity.name: Does iPhone call recording work internationally?

acceptedAnswer.text: Feature availability is gonna flex based on country and local dictates. It's wise to double-check settings and laws if you're trotting the globe with this.

aioseo_meta_data.description: If AirDrop not working on your iPhone, iPad, or Mac, be it due to wrong AirDrop settings or compatibility issues, we've got you covered.

keyPoints.title: Ensure your device is powered on and unlocked
keyPoints.explanation: Your device needs to be active and unlocked for AirDrop to discover it. Both sender and receiver should check this for smooth transfer.

keyPoints.title: Adjust AirDrop settings for discoverability
keyPoints.explanation: Set your AirDrop visibility to 'Everyone for 10 Minutes' or 'Contacts Only' on iPhone or Mac to control who can see and send files to you.

keyPoints.title: Toggle Bluetooth and Wi-Fi
keyPoints.explanation: Since AirDrop depends on Bluetooth and Wi-Fi, turning these off and on again can resolve connection issues on both iPhone and Mac.

keyPoints.title: Turn off Personal Hotspot and check firewall settings
keyPoints.explanation: Disabling Personal Hotspot and adjusting your Mac's firewall to allow incoming connections can help when AirDrop isn't working.

keyPoints.title: Reset Network Settings if needed
keyPoints.explanation: If all else fails, resetting network settings can fix lingering glitches affecting AirDrop performance.

title.rendered: How to Fix “Unable to Load Photo or Video” Error on iPhone

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • “Unable to Load” errors often relate to iCloud issues like low storage, weak internet, or media being stored in the cloud but not downloaded locally.
  • Free up iPhone storage via Settings > General > iPhone Storage to ensure there’s enough space for media files to load properly.
  • Force quit and reopen the Photos app to clear minor bugs that may prevent images or videos from loading.
  • Switch to a strong Wi-Fi connection or reset network settings—poor connectivity can block iCloud media from downloading to your device.
  • Turn off Optimize Storage and Low Power Mode to enable full-resolution downloads and background sync from iCloud.

Are you seeing the “Unable to Load Photo” or “Unable to Load Video” error when opening photos or playing videos in the Photos app on your iPhone? This issue usually appears when your device can’t access or load higher-quality versions stored in iCloud. But don’t worry—this guide explains why your iPhone shows this error and provides proven solutions to help you resolve it quickly.

Table of Contents
  • Why Does iPhone Say "Unable to Load Photo" or "Unable to Load Video"?
  • 8 Ways to Fix "Unable to Load Photo/Video" Error on iPhone
    • 1. Check iPhone Storage
    • 2. Force Quit the Photos App
    • 3. Restart Your iPhone
    • 4. Check Your Network Connection
    • 5. Turn Off "Optimize iPhone Storage"
    • 6. Disable Low Data and Low Power mode
    • 7. Update Your iPhone
    • 8. Sign Out and Back Into iCloud
  • Bonus Tip: Delete and Recover the Photo or Video

Why Does iPhone Say “Unable to Load Photo” or “Unable to Load Video”?

Several common reasons might cause this error:

  • Low iPhone storage: If your iPhone is nearly full, it may fail to load high-resolution photos and videos.
  • Poor internet connection: Weak Wi-Fi or mobile data can prevent access to iCloud content.
  • Outdated iOS or software bugs: A glitch or old iOS version may interfere with loading media.
  • iCloud Storage Optimization: If your iPhone is set to optimize storage, the full-resolution media is stored in iCloud.
  • Low Power or Low Data Mode: These features can restrict background tasks like media downloads.

Let’s explore the step-by-step solutions.

8 Ways to Fix “Unable to Load Photo/Video” Error on iPhone

Here are the most effective fixes to resolve this issue and get your photos and videos working again.

1. Check iPhone Storage

If your iPhone is running low on space, it may not download media from iCloud.

Steps:

  1. Open Settings → General → iPhone Storage.
  2. Check available storage.
  3. If it’s nearly full, delete unused apps, offload files, or clear temporary data.

2. Force Quit the Photos App

Sometimes the Photos app glitches. Force-quitting it may resolve the issue.

Steps:

  1. Swipe up from the bottom of the Home Screen and pause in the middle.
  2. Find Photos, then swipe it up to close.
  3. Relaunch the app and check if the error is gone.

3. Restart Your iPhone

Simply restarting your iPhone often resolves temporary software bugs

Steps:

  1. Press and hold the Side button + Volume Up/Down until the Slide to Power Off appears.
  2. Slide to turn off.
  3. After a few seconds, press and hold the Side button to turn it back on.

4. Check Your Network Connection

Your iPhone needs stable internet to load iCloud photos or videos.

Try This:

  • Turn on Airplane Mode, wait 10 seconds, then turn it off.
  • Go to Settings → Cellular → Toggle Photos ON if using mobile data.
  • Switch to a reliable Wi-Fi network if possible.

5. Turn Off “Optimize iPhone Storage”

When enabled, this option keeps only thumbnails on your device and stores full-resolution media in iCloud. Switch to downloading originals:

Steps:

  1. Access Settings → [your name] → iCloud.
  2. Tap Photos and select Download and Keep Originals.

This ensures that full-resolution media is stored locally.

6. Disable Low Data and Low Power mode

These modes save bandwidth and battery by restricting background tasks, including iCloud downloads.

To turn off Low Data Mode:

  • Go to Settings → Cellular → Cellular Data Options → Turn off Low Data Mode.

For Wi-Fi:

  • Go to Settings → Wi-Fi → Tap the ‘i’ next to your network → Turn off Low Data Mode.

To disable Low Power Mode:

  • Open Settings → Battery → Toggle off Low Power Mode.

7. Update Your iPhone

Running outdated iOS? Updating might patch any bugs related to the Photos app.

Steps:

  • Head to Settings → General → Software Update.
  • If available, install the latest iOS version.

8. Sign Out and Back Into iCloud

If all else fails, signing out and back into iCloud may refresh sync services.

Steps:

  1. Open Settings → Tap your name → Sign Out.
  2. Enter your Apple ID password and confirm.
  3. Wait for a few minutes, then sign in again.
Note Accept updated iCloud Terms and Conditions if prompted.

Bonus Tip: Delete and Recover the Photo or Video

Sometimes, the issue lies with one specific photo or video. Deleting and recovering it can help.

  1. Open the Photos app.
  2. Long-press the media file and tap Delete.
  3. Go to Recently Deleted → Select the file → Tap Recover.

Alternatively, duplicate the file and delete the original.

Signing off…

The “Unable to Load Photo or Video” error can be frustrating, but with these solutions, you can fix it in no time. Whether it’s adjusting storage settings, refreshing your connection, or updating iOS, these steps should get your photos and videos back on track.

If the problem persists even after trying all fixes, consider contacting Apple Support for further help.

Other useful related posts:

  • How to find Size of files and photos on iPhone and iPad
  • How to reduce photo file size on iPhone and iPad
  • How to delete duplicate photos on iPhone

acceptedAnswer.text: Nope, iOS makes the call public, letting everyone know it's being captured. You can't turn off this alert since it keeps things above board legally.

mainEntity.name: Where are my iPhone call recordings saved?

acceptedAnswer.text: You'll find all recordings in the Notes app, under the "Call Recordings" folder. They're synced through iCloud if that's running on your gears.

mainEntity.name: How do I access the transcripts of my recorded calls?

acceptedAnswer.text: Open "Call Recordings" in Notes; the transcript is cozy beneath the audio file and searchable.

acceptedAnswer.text: Nope, this little gem’s closed for just regular calls via the Phone app. Third-party recordings aren’t invited to this party.

mainEntity.name: How do I share a recorded phone call from the Notes app?

acceptedAnswer.text: In Notes, hit up the recording, slap the share button, and choose your audience. You decide if they get audio, transcript, or both.

mainEntity.name: Can I automatically record all calls on my iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: You gotta actually tap that record button for each chat there's no collective auto-record option.

mainEntity.name: How do I delete call recordings from my iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: In Notes, a left swipe on the ones to toss will reveal "Delete," or you can go batch-mode with "Edit."

mainEntity.name: Does iPhone call recording work internationally?

acceptedAnswer.text: Feature availability is gonna flex based on country and local dictates. It's wise to double-check settings and laws if you're trotting the globe with this.

keyPoints.title: Why the 'Unable to Load' Error Occurs on iPhone
keyPoints.explanation: This error typically appears when your device cannot access or load higher-quality media stored in iCloud due to issues like low storage, poor internet, outdated iOS, or storage optimization settings.

keyPoints.title: Check iPhone Storage
keyPoints.explanation: Ensure your iPhone has enough free space by navigating to Settings > General > iPhone Storage; freeing up space if needed can resolve loading issues.

keyPoints.title: Force Quit and Restart the Photos App
keyPoints.explanation: Closing the Photos app completely and restarting it can fix glitches causing the loading error, often resolving temporary software bugs.

keyPoints.title: Improve Network Connection for Better Access
keyPoints.explanation: A stable internet connection is crucial for loading photos and videos from iCloud; toggling Airplane Mode or switching to a reliable Wi-Fi network can help.

keyPoints.title: Adjust Storage and Power Settings
keyPoints.explanation: Turning off 'Optimize iPhone Storage' to store full-resolution media locally, and disabling Low Data or Low Power Mode, can facilitate proper media loading by allowing background downloads.

title.rendered: iPhone 17 Battery Capacities Allegedly Leaked

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Leaked Battery Capacities of iPhone 17 Lineup: A recent leak from a Chinese database suggests significant battery improvements across the upcoming iPhone 17 models, with notable milestones for the Pro Max.
  • Battery Sizes Vary Across Models and Regions: The leaked data shows different battery capacities for models with SIM trays and eSIM-only versions, reflecting Apple’s push toward eSIM technology to free up space for larger batteries.
  • iPhone 17 Pro Max Breaks 5,000 mAh Barrier: The Pro Max model is expected to be the first iPhone to exceed 5,000 mAh, offering possibly the longest battery life in iPhone history.
  • Battery Improvements Indicate Focus on Longevity: Apple appears to be prioritizing battery life in this release, with the Pro Max and Pro models showing substantial capacity boosts, and efficiency improvements for the Air.
  • Official Battery Data Likely Coming Soon: With EU energy labeling regulations, Apple may soon disclose official battery capacities, confirming these leaked figures after the September event.

Just days before Apple’s big September event, a new leak has surfaced that claims to reveal the battery capacities for the upcoming iPhone 17 lineup. The numbers come from a Chinese regulatory database and were first shared online by the reliable leaker ShrimpApplePro. If accurate, these listings show meaningful gains for most models and one major milestone for the Pro Max.

What The Leak Reveals

According to the filings, the standard iPhone 17 will feature a 3,692 mAh battery, a modest improvement over its predecessor. The much-rumored iPhone 17 Air, Apple’s new ultra-thin model, is said to pack a 3,036 mAh battery with a SIM tray, while the eSIM-only version climbs slightly to 3,149 mAh. This lower capacity was expected due to its slim design, but Apple is reportedly preparing a new power-efficient modem and even a battery case to balance things out.

For the higher-end models, the numbers are more exciting. The iPhone 17 Pro is listed with 3,988 mAh for SIM models and a healthier 4,252 mAh for eSIM-only units. That’s up to an 18% boost compared to the iPhone 16 Pro. The biggest upgrade is saved for the iPhone 17 Pro Max, which reportedly comes with 4,823 mAh (SIM) or 5,088 mAh (eSIM). If true, this makes it the first iPhone ever to cross the 5,000 mAh mark, an almost 8% increase over last year’s model.

Here’s a quick look at all the leaked capacities in a table:

The difference in battery sizes between models comes down to Apple’s push toward eSIM. Removing the physical SIM card tray frees up extra internal space, which Apple is finally putting to use by slightly increasing battery capacity. According to the leak, eSIM-only models could offer 3–6% more capacity than their SIM-equipped counterparts. Apple has already sold eSIM-only iPhones in the U.S. for years, and now it looks like more regions will be joining that shift.

A Step Toward Better Battery Life

If these leaks hold true, Apple is clearly prioritizing battery life in this year’s lineup. The iPhone 17 Pro Max could deliver the best endurance ever in an iPhone, while the Pro also sees a meaningful jump. The Air, despite its smaller cell, will lean on efficiency improvements to balance performance. And with Apple now required to display energy labels in the EU, we may see official capacities published soon after launch.

For now, we’ll have to wait until Apple’s September 9 event to see if these numbers are confirmed. But if accurate, iPhone users may finally get the battery gains they’ve been asking for.

mainEntity.name: Why is X (Twitter) not loading on my iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: It's usually poor internet, an outdated app/iOS, or a temporary server outage.

mainEntity.name: Why does the X app keep crashing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Low storage, app bugs, or outdated versions. A reinstall often fixes it.

mainEntity.name: Why can't I log in?

acceptedAnswer.text: Check your credentials, reset your password, or contact X Support.

mainEntity.name: How do I fix X notifications not working?

acceptedAnswer.text: Enable them in Settings > Notifications > X and check that Do Not Disturb isn't on.

mainEntity.name: Can I record calls without the other person knowing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Nope, iOS makes the call public, letting everyone know it's being captured. You can't turn off this alert since it keeps things above board legally.

mainEntity.name: Where are my iPhone call recordings saved?

acceptedAnswer.text: You'll find all recordings in the Notes app, under the "Call Recordings" folder. They're synced through iCloud if that's running on your gears.

mainEntity.name: How do I access the transcripts of my recorded calls?

acceptedAnswer.text: Open "Call Recordings" in Notes; the transcript is cozy beneath the audio file and searchable.

mainEntity.name: Why can't I see the record button on my iPhone during a call?

acceptedAnswer.text: To get the full kit you need iOS 18 or later, the right regional settings, and Apple's Intelligence cruising cool in Settings.

mainEntity.name: Does the iPhone call recording feature work with FaceTime or WhatsApp?

acceptedAnswer.text: Nope, this little gem’s closed for just regular calls via the Phone app. Third-party recordings aren’t invited to this party.

mainEntity.name: How do I share a recorded phone call from the Notes app?

acceptedAnswer.text: In Notes, hit up the recording, slap the share button, and choose your audience. You decide if they get audio, transcript, or both.

mainEntity.name: Can I automatically record all calls on my iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: You gotta actually tap that record button for each chat there's no collective auto-record option.

mainEntity.name: How do I delete call recordings from my iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: In Notes, a left swipe on the ones to toss will reveal "Delete," or you can go batch-mode with "Edit."

mainEntity.name: Does iPhone call recording work internationally?

acceptedAnswer.text: Feature availability is gonna flex based on country and local dictates. It's wise to double-check settings and laws if you're trotting the globe with this.

title.rendered: How to Watch Apple’s iPhone 17 Launch Event

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Apple’s September 2025 event set for September 9: The keynote from Apple Park will unveil the iPhone 17 lineup, new Apple Watches, AirPods, and iOS 26 updates.
  • Watch the keynote live across platforms: You can stream on Apple’s Events site, YouTube, or the Apple TV app, supported on iPhone, iPad, Mac, and smart TVs.
  • Global start times ensure accessibility: The event begins at 10 a.m. PT, with synchronized broadcast times for regions like New York, London, Tokyo, and Sydney.
  • iPhone 17 leads the hardware announcements: Apple is expected to showcase the iPhone 17 series, AirPods Pro 3, new Apple Watches, plus possible iPad Pro and AirTags refreshes.
  • iOS 26 brings notable software changes: Anticipated updates include a redesigned Camera app, advanced spam detection, and improvements to Siri AI alongside new chip-based performance boosts.

Apple is gearing up for its big “Awe Dropping” event on September 9, 2025, and all eyes are on the iPhone 17 lineup. The keynote kicks off at 10 a.m. PT / 1 p.m. ET / 6 p.m. BST / 10:30 p.m. IST, streamed live from Apple Park in Cupertino. Like past September launches, the event will also showcase new Apple Watches, AirPods, and updates to iOS 26. Here’s everything you need to know to catch it live.

Where and How to Watch

Apple is making it simple to tune in across devices:

  • Apple.com: Head to the Apple Events page to watch directly in your browser. Works on Safari, Chrome, Firefox, and more.
  • YouTube: Apple has already posted a livestream placeholder. It’s the easiest option since YouTube works on almost every device, from phones to smart TVs.
  • Apple TV App: The event will appear in a dedicated section of the app on iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple TV, and even select smart TVs and consoles.

Global Start Times

The keynote begins at 10 a.m. PT and will likely run one to two hours. Here’s what that looks like worldwide:

  • US: 10 a.m. PT / 1 p.m. ET
  • UK: 6 p.m. BST
  • Europe: 7 p.m. CEST
  • India: 10:30 p.m. IST
  • Singapore/China: 1 a.m. CST (Sept 10)
  • Japan: 2 a.m. JST (Sept 10)
  • Australia: 3 a.m. AEST (Sept 10)
  • New Zealand: 5 a.m. NZST (Sept 10)

What to Expect at the iPhone 17 Event

Apple’s invite for the event teases a glowing, color-shifting logo that hints at the new Liquid Glass UI coming with iOS 26. But the spotlight is firmly on hardware:

  • iPhone 17 lineup: Base model, iPhone 17 Pro, Pro Max, and the much-hyped iPhone 17 Air — Apple’s first ultralight phone, though analysts warn it may come with first-gen growing pains.
  • Apple Watch updates: Series 11, Ultra 3, and a new SE.
  • AirPods Pro 3: Expected to debut with improved audio and features.
  • Other rumors: A refreshed AirTag, Apple TV, and iPad Pro could make appearances, but aren’t guaranteed.

Leaks suggest big upgrades for the Pro models, including an 8x telephoto lens, scratch-resistant antireflective display, and larger batteries. Apple may also roll out its in-house C1 5G modem and custom Wi-Fi chips across the lineup.

The Bigger Picture

Beyond hardware, expect Apple to confirm more details on the iOS 26 public release. Features include a redesigned Camera app, spam text detection, and group polls in Messages. Siri’s AI overhaul, first previewed at WWDC, may be pushed to next year, though Apple Intelligence updates could still get stage time.

Whether you watch on Apple’s site, YouTube, or the TV app, the September 9 keynote promises one of the year’s biggest moments in tech. Grab your device of choice and mark the time — Apple is ready to show what’s next.

mainEntity.name: Why is X (Twitter) not loading on my iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: It's usually poor internet, an outdated app/iOS, or a temporary server outage.

mainEntity.name: Why does the X app keep crashing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Low storage, app bugs, or outdated versions. A reinstall often fixes it.

mainEntity.name: Why can't I log in?

acceptedAnswer.text: Check your credentials, reset your password, or contact X Support.

mainEntity.name: How do I fix X notifications not working?

acceptedAnswer.text: Enable them in Settings > Notifications > X and check that Do Not Disturb isn't on.

mainEntity.name: Can I record calls without the other person knowing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Nope, iOS makes the call public, letting everyone know it's being captured. You can't turn off this alert since it keeps things above board legally.

mainEntity.name: Where are my iPhone call recordings saved?

acceptedAnswer.text: You'll find all recordings in the Notes app, under the "Call Recordings" folder. They're synced through iCloud if that's running on your gears.

mainEntity.name: How do I access the transcripts of my recorded calls?

acceptedAnswer.text: Open "Call Recordings" in Notes; the transcript is cozy beneath the audio file and searchable.

mainEntity.name: Why can't I see the record button on my iPhone during a call?

acceptedAnswer.text: To get the full kit you need iOS 18 or later, the right regional settings, and Apple's Intelligence cruising cool in Settings.

mainEntity.name: Does the iPhone call recording feature work with FaceTime or WhatsApp?

acceptedAnswer.text: Nope, this little gem’s closed for just regular calls via the Phone app. Third-party recordings aren’t invited to this party.

mainEntity.name: How do I share a recorded phone call from the Notes app?

acceptedAnswer.text: In Notes, hit up the recording, slap the share button, and choose your audience. You decide if they get audio, transcript, or both.

mainEntity.name: Can I automatically record all calls on my iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: You gotta actually tap that record button for each chat there's no collective auto-record option.

mainEntity.name: How do I delete call recordings from my iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: In Notes, a left swipe on the ones to toss will reveal "Delete," or you can go batch-mode with "Edit."

mainEntity.name: Does iPhone call recording work internationally?

acceptedAnswer.text: Feature availability is gonna flex based on country and local dictates. It's wise to double-check settings and laws if you're trotting the globe with this.

title.rendered: Apple’s AI Answer Engine Could Arrive Sooner Than Expected

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Apple’s Generative AI Project Set for Early 2026: Apple is developing a new AI-powered search engine, called World Knowledge Answers (WKA), which could launch as soon as March 2026 to enhance Siri and Apple’s search capabilities.
  • World Knowledge Answers (WKA) Explained: WKA, created by Apple’s AKI team, aims to rival Perplexity and ChatGPT by providing instant, conversational answers via large language models, initially integrated into Siri.
  • Rapid Development and Ambitious Timeline: Despite being a recent project, WKA’s expected launch in March reflects Apple’s urgent push to advance in AI, with plans to extend its capabilities across Siri, Safari, and Spotlight.
  • Key Teams Behind the Innovation: Multiple teams including Siri under Craig Federighi, AI led by John Giannandrea, and Services overseen by Eddy Cue are collaborating to transform Siri into a sophisticated AI chatbot.
  • Significance of Apple’s AI Move in the Tech Race: Launching WKA and integrating advanced AI into Apple devices allows the company to catch up with rivals like ChatGPT and redefine user search experiences, strengthening its AI presence.

Apple has been quietly building a new generative AI project, and it might be ready much faster than anyone thought. Bloomberg reports that the company’s in-house “answer engine” could launch as early as March 2026, marking Apple’s boldest move yet into the world of AI-powered search.

World Knowledge Answers Explained

Internally known as World Knowledge Answers (WKA), the tool is being developed by Apple’s new Answers, Knowledge, and Information (AKI) team. The idea is simple but ambitious: create a direct rival to Perplexity and ChatGPT, delivering instant, conversational answers to user queries. Unlike traditional search, WKA will be powered by large language models (LLMs), making Siri smarter and more useful than ever before.

For now, Apple plans to roll out WKA inside the new Siri overhaul, before expanding to Safari and Spotlight in the future. That means users will first experience it through voice commands or text inside Siri, with wider integration coming later.

A Surprising Timeline

What’s surprising is the speed. Apple only recently formed the AKI team, yet WKA is already on track for a March launch. Normally, Apple takes years to bring new technologies from prototype to product, but this fast-tracked schedule shows how urgently the company wants to catch up in AI.

According to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, while WKA won’t initially be in Safari or Spotlight, it’s designed to eventually power search across Apple’s ecosystem. For a project just months in the making, that’s ambitious.

Who’s Building It

Multiple Apple teams are involved: Siri under Craig Federighi, the AI group led by John Giannandrea, and Services overseen by Eddy Cue. Together, they’re trying to reinvent Siri into something closer to today’s most advanced AI chatbots.

Apple is also hedging its bets. Internally, the company is running tests to see whether Siri should rely solely on Apple’s own models or integrate external ones from Google, OpenAI, or Anthropic. Apple has reportedly tested a Google-developed model, and the recent antitrust ruling that preserved its Google search deal gives it breathing room to keep that partnership alive.

WKA is only part of Apple’s wider AI comeback plan. Alongside it, Apple is preparing a visual redesign for Siri, considering a chatbot-like search app, and even planning a health-focused AI agent tied to a paid wellness subscription in 2026. Acquisitions are also on the table to strengthen its AI stack.

Why This Matters

Apple has been criticized for falling behind in the AI race, especially as ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Gemini push the boundaries of generative search. But the launch of World Knowledge Answers could quickly change that. By embedding it directly into Siri and later Safari and Spotlight, Apple is aiming not just to match its rivals—but to redefine how users search on its devices.

If the March timeline holds, iPhone and Mac users won’t have to wait long to see how Apple’s answer engine compares. And for the first time in years, Siri might finally feel less like an afterthought and more like the intelligent assistant Apple always promised.

mainEntity.name: Why is X (Twitter) not loading on my iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: It's usually poor internet, an outdated app/iOS, or a temporary server outage.

mainEntity.name: Why does the X app keep crashing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Low storage, app bugs, or outdated versions. A reinstall often fixes it.

mainEntity.name: Why can't I log in?

acceptedAnswer.text: Check your credentials, reset your password, or contact X Support.

mainEntity.name: How do I fix X notifications not working?

acceptedAnswer.text: Enable them in Settings > Notifications > X and check that Do Not Disturb isn't on.

mainEntity.name: Why is X (Twitter) not loading on my iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: It's usually poor internet, an outdated app/iOS, or a temporary server outage.

mainEntity.name: Why does the X app keep crashing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Low storage, app bugs, or outdated versions. A reinstall often fixes it.

mainEntity.name: Why can't I log in?

acceptedAnswer.text: Check your credentials, reset your password, or contact X Support.

mainEntity.name: How do I fix X notifications not working?

acceptedAnswer.text: Enable them in Settings > Notifications > X and check that Do Not Disturb isn't on.

mainEntity.name: Can I record calls without the other person knowing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Nope, iOS makes the call public, letting everyone know it's being captured. You can't turn off this alert since it keeps things above board legally.

mainEntity.name: Where are my iPhone call recordings saved?

acceptedAnswer.text: You'll find all recordings in the Notes app, under the "Call Recordings" folder. They're synced through iCloud if that's running on your gears.

mainEntity.name: How do I access the transcripts of my recorded calls?

acceptedAnswer.text: Open "Call Recordings" in Notes; the transcript is cozy beneath the audio file and searchable.

mainEntity.name: Why can't I see the record button on my iPhone during a call?

acceptedAnswer.text: To get the full kit you need iOS 18 or later, the right regional settings, and Apple's Intelligence cruising cool in Settings.

mainEntity.name: Does the iPhone call recording feature work with FaceTime or WhatsApp?

acceptedAnswer.text: Nope, this little gem’s closed for just regular calls via the Phone app. Third-party recordings aren’t invited to this party.

mainEntity.name: How do I share a recorded phone call from the Notes app?

acceptedAnswer.text: In Notes, hit up the recording, slap the share button, and choose your audience. You decide if they get audio, transcript, or both.

mainEntity.name: Can I automatically record all calls on my iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: You gotta actually tap that record button for each chat there's no collective auto-record option.

mainEntity.name: How do I delete call recordings from my iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: In Notes, a left swipe on the ones to toss will reveal "Delete," or you can go batch-mode with "Edit."

mainEntity.name: Does iPhone call recording work internationally?

acceptedAnswer.text: Feature availability is gonna flex based on country and local dictates. It's wise to double-check settings and laws if you're trotting the globe with this.

keyPoints.title: Apple's Generative AI Project Set for Early 2026
keyPoints.explanation: Apple is developing a new AI-powered search engine, called World Knowledge Answers (WKA), which could launch as soon as March 2026 to enhance Siri and Apple's search capabilities.

keyPoints.title: World Knowledge Answers (WKA) Explained
keyPoints.explanation: WKA, created by Apple’s AKI team, aims to rival Perplexity and ChatGPT by providing instant, conversational answers via large language models, initially integrated into Siri.

keyPoints.title: Rapid Development and Ambitious Timeline
keyPoints.explanation: Despite being a recent project, WKA's expected launch in March reflects Apple's urgent push to advance in AI, with plans to extend its capabilities across Siri, Safari, and Spotlight.

keyPoints.title: Key Teams Behind the Innovation
keyPoints.explanation: Multiple teams including Siri under Craig Federighi, AI led by John Giannandrea, and Services overseen by Eddy Cue are collaborating to transform Siri into a sophisticated AI chatbot.

keyPoints.title: Significance of Apple's AI Move in the Tech Race
keyPoints.explanation: Launching WKA and integrating advanced AI into Apple devices allows the company to catch up with rivals like ChatGPT and redefine user search experiences, strengthening its AI presence.

title.rendered: Authors Sue Apple for $2.5B Over AI Trained on Pirated Books

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Apple faces copyright lawsuit over AI training data: Two authors accuse Apple of using pirated books from shadow libraries like Bibliotik to train AI models without proper licenses.
  • Responsible AI claims challenged by allegations: Despite Apple’s public stance on ethical AI, the lawsuit says Applebot scraped unlicensed content, including books, while hiding its true data sources.
  • Anthropic’s $1.5 billion settlement sets precedent: A recent deal over pirated training data underscores the financial risks Apple could encounter if courts rule similarly in this case.
  • Tech giants under mounting copyright scrutiny: Alongside Apple, OpenAI, Microsoft, and Meta face lawsuits that could shape future AI copyright law and regulation across the industry.
  • Possible consequences for AI development costs: A ruling against Apple may redefine ownership of AI training data, raising costs and tightening controls on how AI models are developed.

Yet another class action lawsuit has been filed against Apple, and this time it’s over copyright issues.  Two authors, Grady Hendrix and Jennifer Roberson, sued Apple in California federal court, accusing Apple of using pirated books to train the AI models powering Apple Intelligence, reports Reuters.

The case centers on a controversial dataset known as Books3, which was built from so-called “shadow libraries” like Bibliotik, notorious for hosting thousands of pirated books. Plaintiffs argue that Apple relied on this dataset to train its OpenELM models and likely its larger Foundation Language Models, without ever seeking permission or paying authors. They say this conduct not only deprived them of compensation but also gave Apple a competitive edge by using their work to develop commercial products.

Apple’s Ethical AI Claims Under Scrutiny

Apple has long presented itself as a company trying to be ethical with AI. It previously signed licensing deals, including a multimillion-dollar agreement with Shutterstock for images, and even offered publishers cash for access to their archives. Apple has also stated it respects web standards like robots.txt and won’t scrape sites that block crawlers. But the lawsuit alleges a different reality, that Apple’s own web scraper, Applebot, has been collecting vast amounts of online content for nearly a decade, including unlicensed copyrighted books.

According to the complaint, Apple concealed the true sources of its training data to avoid legal challenges. The lawsuit claims Apple copied books whose outputs now compete with the originals, diluting their market value and undermining authors’ rights.

The Anthropic Precedent

The timing of this lawsuit is no accident. Just days earlier, AI startup Anthropic agreed to pay $1.5 billion to settle a class action over similar claims. Authors accused Anthropic of pulling millions of pirated books from datasets like Books3, Library Genesis, and Pirate Library Mirror to train its Claude chatbot. The settlement, hailed as the largest copyright recovery in history, could set a benchmark for what Apple might face.

That deal also required Anthropic to destroy pirated files, underscoring how seriously courts view these shadow libraries. Legal experts said Anthropic risked being financially crippled had it gone to trial. The Apple case now lands in the same federal court, drawing inevitable comparisons.

A Broader Copyright Battle

Apple is not alone. OpenAI, Microsoft, and Meta are also facing lawsuits from authors and publishers alleging their works were used without consent to train generative AI systems. With governments and courts still undecided on whether training AI on copyrighted material is fair use or infringement, these lawsuits could define the future of AI development.

For Apple, which has been pitching Apple Intelligence as a secure and privacy-focused assistant for its devices, the lawsuit strikes at its reputation as a more responsible player in AI. If successful, plaintiffs want damages, restitution, and even the destruction of Apple’s AI models trained on pirated works.

The outcome of this case could have far-reaching implications, determining not just the cost of training data but also who controls the building blocks of AI.

acceptedAnswer.text: It's usually poor internet, an outdated app/iOS, or a temporary server outage.

mainEntity.name: Why does the X app keep crashing?

mainEntity.name: Can I record calls without the other person knowing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Nope, iOS makes the call public, letting everyone know it's being captured. You can't turn off this alert since it keeps things above board legally.

mainEntity.name: Where are my iPhone call recordings saved?

acceptedAnswer.text: You'll find all recordings in the Notes app, under the "Call Recordings" folder. They're synced through iCloud if that's running on your gears.

mainEntity.name: How do I access the transcripts of my recorded calls?

acceptedAnswer.text: Open "Call Recordings" in Notes; the transcript is cozy beneath the audio file and searchable.

mainEntity.name: Why can't I see the record button on my iPhone during a call?

acceptedAnswer.text: To get the full kit you need iOS 18 or later, the right regional settings, and Apple's Intelligence cruising cool in Settings.

mainEntity.name: Does the iPhone call recording feature work with FaceTime or WhatsApp?

acceptedAnswer.text: Nope, this little gem’s closed for just regular calls via the Phone app. Third-party recordings aren’t invited to this party.

mainEntity.name: How do I share a recorded phone call from the Notes app?

acceptedAnswer.text: In Notes, hit up the recording, slap the share button, and choose your audience. You decide if they get audio, transcript, or both.

mainEntity.name: Can I automatically record all calls on my iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: You gotta actually tap that record button for each chat there's no collective auto-record option.

mainEntity.name: How do I delete call recordings from my iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: In Notes, a left swipe on the ones to toss will reveal "Delete," or you can go batch-mode with "Edit."

mainEntity.name: Does iPhone call recording work internationally?

acceptedAnswer.text: Feature availability is gonna flex based on country and local dictates. It's wise to double-check settings and laws if you're trotting the globe with this.

keyPoints.title: Apple's Copyright Lawsuit over AI Training Data
keyPoints.explanation: Two authors sued Apple, claiming it used pirated books from shadow libraries like Bibliotik to train its AI models without permission, depriving them of compensation.

keyPoints.title: Apple’s Ethical AI Promises vs. Alleged Practices
keyPoints.explanation: Despite advertising responsible AI development, the lawsuit alleges Apple collected vast online content, including unlicensed books, through its web scraper Applebot, and concealed these sources.

keyPoints.title: Legal Precedent Set by Anthropic Settlement
keyPoints.explanation: The recent $1.5 billion settlement by AI startup Anthropic for using pirated books in training sets highlights the potential scale of liability Apple could face in similar lawsuits.

keyPoints.title: Wider Industry Impact and Ongoing Litigation
keyPoints.explanation: Apple, along with OpenAI, Microsoft, and Meta, faces growing lawsuits over copyrighted works used without consent to train AI, which could shape future regulations on AI development.

keyPoints.title: Potential Consequences for AI Development and Control
keyPoints.explanation: The lawsuit's outcome may influence who owns the rights to AI models and the cost of training data, impacting how future AI systems are developed and regulated.

title.rendered: iPhone 17 Pro Leak Hints at Smaller Dynamic Island

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Possible Shrinkage of Dynamic Island on iPhone 17 Pro: A leak suggests that the Dynamic Island on the iPhone 17 Pro and Pro Max could be reduced in size by about 25%, marking the first major visual change since its debut.
  • Leak Source and Its Credibility: The leak comes from an account associated with a screen protector company, which lacks a proven track record, so the information should be viewed with caution, though it aligns with ongoing rumors.
  • Implications of a Smaller Dynamic Island: A smaller Dynamic Island would give the Pro models a more streamlined look and may be part of Apple’s strategy to differentiate the Pro lineup through both design and features.
  • Industry Predictions and Contradictions: While some analysts suggest only the Pro Max might get a smaller cutout, others believe the size will stay the same for this year, with reductions possibly coming in the iPhone 18.
  • Upcoming Apple Event and Rumors Confirmation: Apple’s September 9 event will reveal the iPhone 17 lineup and possibly confirm if the Dynamic Island shrinks, which would be its first visual update since 2022.

Apple may finally be changing the look of the Dynamic Island, at least on its higher-end iPhones. A new leak suggests the cutout at the top of the screen is shrinking on the iPhone 17 Pro and iPhone 17 Pro Max, marking the first big visual tweak to the feature since its debut in 2022.

The leak comes from an account called @that_one_g3 on X, who claims to work at a company producing iPhone screen protectors. According to images they shared, the Dynamic Island on the iPhone 17 Pro models measures about 1.5 centimeters wide. That’s roughly a 25% reduction compared to the 2cm width on current iPhone 16 models. The standard iPhone 17 and the new iPhone 17 Air, meanwhile, are said to stick with the same larger cutout.

Why This Leak Stands Out

Last-minute leaks like this aren’t unusual as accessory makers often start preparing designs just before launch. Still, the source has no proven track record, which means it should be taken with caution. Even so, this rumor aligns with months of chatter that Apple has been exploring ways to shrink the Dynamic Island.

Analyst Jeff Pu earlier suggested only the Pro Max might see a smaller cutout. Another leaker mentioned Apple’s use of “metalens” technology to reduce the size of Face ID sensors. Yet, others, including well-known analyst Ming-Chi Kuo said the Dynamic Island would remain largely unchanged this year, with any shrink coming later in the iPhone 18 lineup. This back-and-forth has left expectations uncertain.

A Push To Differentiate the Pro Models

If true, the change would give the iPhone 17 Pro and Pro Max a more streamlined look compared to the regular iPhone 17 models. It also fits Apple’s recent strategy of separating Pro models not only with better cameras and displays but also with distinct design choices. Some leakers even suggest the Dynamic Island’s software interface might get a refresh in iOS 26 to complement the new design, though no details have been shared yet.

What To Expect Next Week

Apple’s “Awe dropping” event is set for September 9, where the company will officially reveal the iPhone 17 lineup alongside iOS 26. If the Dynamic Island does shrink this year, it’ll be the first visual update since the feature’s introduction on the iPhone 14 Pro three years ago. Until then, this remains a rumor, but one that feels more plausible with each passing leak.

acceptedAnswer.text: It's usually poor internet, an outdated app/iOS, or a temporary server outage.

mainEntity.name: Why does the X app keep crashing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Low storage, app bugs, or outdated versions. A reinstall often fixes it.

mainEntity.name: Why can't I log in?

mainEntity.name: Can I record calls without the other person knowing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Nope, iOS makes the call public, letting everyone know it's being captured. You can't turn off this alert since it keeps things above board legally.

mainEntity.name: Where are my iPhone call recordings saved?

acceptedAnswer.text: You'll find all recordings in the Notes app, under the "Call Recordings" folder. They're synced through iCloud if that's running on your gears.

mainEntity.name: How do I access the transcripts of my recorded calls?

acceptedAnswer.text: Open "Call Recordings" in Notes; the transcript is cozy beneath the audio file and searchable.

mainEntity.name: Why can't I see the record button on my iPhone during a call?

acceptedAnswer.text: To get the full kit you need iOS 18 or later, the right regional settings, and Apple's Intelligence cruising cool in Settings.

mainEntity.name: Does the iPhone call recording feature work with FaceTime or WhatsApp?

acceptedAnswer.text: Nope, this little gem’s closed for just regular calls via the Phone app. Third-party recordings aren’t invited to this party.

mainEntity.name: How do I share a recorded phone call from the Notes app?

acceptedAnswer.text: In Notes, hit up the recording, slap the share button, and choose your audience. You decide if they get audio, transcript, or both.

mainEntity.name: Can I automatically record all calls on my iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: You gotta actually tap that record button for each chat there's no collective auto-record option.

mainEntity.name: How do I delete call recordings from my iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: In Notes, a left swipe on the ones to toss will reveal "Delete," or you can go batch-mode with "Edit."

mainEntity.name: Does iPhone call recording work internationally?

acceptedAnswer.text: Feature availability is gonna flex based on country and local dictates. It's wise to double-check settings and laws if you're trotting the globe with this.

keyPoints.title: Possible Shrinkage of Dynamic Island on iPhone 17 Pro
keyPoints.explanation: A leak suggests that the Dynamic Island on the iPhone 17 Pro and Pro Max could be reduced in size by about 25%, marking the first major visual change since its debut.

keyPoints.title: Leak Source and Its Credibility
keyPoints.explanation: The leak comes from an account associated with a screen protector company, which lacks a proven track record, so the information should be viewed with caution, though it aligns with ongoing rumors.

keyPoints.title: Implications of a Smaller Dynamic Island
keyPoints.explanation: A smaller Dynamic Island would give the Pro models a more streamlined look and may be part of Apple’s strategy to differentiate the Pro lineup through both design and features.

keyPoints.title: Industry Predictions and Contradictions
keyPoints.explanation: While some analysts suggest only the Pro Max might get a smaller cutout, others believe the size will stay the same for this year, with reductions possibly coming in the iPhone 18.

keyPoints.title: Upcoming Apple Event and Rumors Confirmation
keyPoints.explanation: Apple's September 9 event will reveal the iPhone 17 lineup and possibly confirm if the Dynamic Island shrinks, which would be its first visual update since 2022.

title.rendered: iPhone 17 Pro Back Design Leak Hints at Bold Redesign

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Apple’s Major Redesign for iPhone 17 Pro: The upcoming iPhone 17 Pro models are expected to feature the boldest redesign in years, with a hybrid aluminum-glass back and a large camera bump stretch across the device.
  • New Back Design Focuses on Functionality and Style: Replacing titanium with lighter aluminum, the new back will include a dedicated wireless charging cutout and a distinguished camera bar, improving durability, heat management, and aesthetics.
  • Reinforced Camera Bump: The camera bump is anticipated to extend across the full width of the back, using aluminum for added toughness and serving as a prominent design signature.
  • High Confidence in Leak Reliability: Multiple credible sources such as Sonny Dickson, Majin Bu, and Bloomberg align in their leaks, making the new back design highly probable for the iPhone 17 Pro.
  • Implications for Buyers and Future Design: If true, this redesign offers a lighter, more premium feel with seamless wireless charging and a standout camera, hinting at Apple’s focus on material refinement and a move towards a distinctive future aesthetic.

Apple’s iPhone 17 launch is just days away, and one of the biggest questions surrounding the Pro lineup seems to have been answered. For months, leaks and renders have shown conflicting designs, but new reports backed by reliable sources point to a major shake-up. If true, the iPhone 17 Pro and Pro Max will sport Apple’s boldest redesign in years.

Apple’s Bold Back Redesign Comes Into Focus

Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reports that the iPhone 17 Pro models will feature a new cutout area across the bottom two-thirds of the back, dedicated to wireless charging. This aligns with earlier leaks that suggested a hybrid aluminum-glass back instead of a full glass panel. Prototypes shared by leaker Sonny Dickson show a rounded rectangular section that clearly separates the materials, leaving the top third dominated by a full-width camera bar.

Apple’s shift away from titanium is unexpected, but it makes sense. Titanium is durable but expensive and heavy. Aluminum, on the other hand, is lighter, easier to manufacture at scale, and more cost-efficient. Pairing it with glass allows for MagSafe and Qi wireless charging, which metal alone would disrupt. This design also addresses durability concerns, heat management, and even weight, meaning the iPhone 17 Pro could feel lighter than the iPhone 15 Pro despite its larger size.

Another key change is the camera bump. Leaks suggest it will extend into a bar stretching across the full width of the phone’s back. Unlike past models, where the glass bump was prone to cracking, this new design could use aluminum for added toughness. It’s also a statement, Apple wants the camera to be a visible signature, not something you hide under a case.

How Reliable Are These Leaks?

This isn’t idle speculation. Sonny Dickson’s prototypes and Majin Bu’s CAD renders both show the same split design. Their track records are strong, and when combined with Gurman’s reporting, the evidence is hard to dismiss. Even The Information had hinted last year at a part-aluminum, part-glass back. With multiple credible voices aligning, the puzzle looks nearly solved.

What It Means For Buyers

If Apple does introduce this hybrid back, it marks the biggest iPhone Pro redesign in years. Buyers can expect a device that feels premium but lighter, with seamless wireless charging and a camera that Apple clearly wants you to notice. More importantly, it signals where Apple is headed: refining materials, balancing cost and durability, and creating a distinctive design language that could pave the way for the rumored all-glass iPhone 20.

The mystery may not be fully solved until Apple takes the stage next week, but if these leaks hold up, the iPhone 17 Pro lineup won’t just be an upgrade, it’ll be a statement piece.

title.rendered: iPhone Showing “Cannot Verify Server Identity”? Here’s How to Fix it Fast

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • This error means your iPhone can’t verify a mail server’s identity—usually due to expired SSL certificates, wrong email settings, or unstable network connections.
  • Try basic fixes first like restarting your device or Mail app—also double-check your date and time settings to rule out syncing issues.
  • Update iOS and manage certificate trust settings—an outdated system or untrusted certificate can trigger verification errors.
  • For deeper issues, remove and re-add email accounts—or reset network settings and remove third-party calendar syncs if the error keeps returning.
  • Factory reset or Apple Support are your last options—if nothing else works, these steps can help resolve persistent identity verification errors.

The Mail app on iPhone is reliable and easy to use—but sometimes, it throws up the frustrating “Cannot Verify Server Identity” error. This issue prevents you from accessing or sending emails and usually happens due to certificate issues, misconfigured settings, or network problems.

In this guide, I’ll walk you through 11 effective solutions to fix this error for good.

Why does my iPhone say “Cannot Verify Server Identity”?

This error typically occurs when your iPhone can’t validate the SSL certificate of your email server. It could be because:

  • The SSL/TLS certificate is expired or invalid.
  • You have incorrect Mail settings.
  • A temporary glitch is interfering with the connection.
  • There’s a network or profile configuration issue.

11 fixes for “Cannot Verify Server Identity” on iPhone

Here’s a list of tried and tested fixes that can help you get rid of this error in the Mail app:

1. Force quit and reopen the Mail app

A simple force quit can resolve minor bugs and refresh the app’s connection to your server.

How to do it:

  1. Open the App Switcher on your iPhone.
  2. Swipe up on the Mail app.
  3. Reopen it and try again.

2. Restart your iPhone

In most cases, force quitting and reopening the Mail app should work just fine. However, if that doesn’t work, you may want to try restarting your iPhone. Doing this will close all system processes to resolve temporary software glitches and re-establish a network connection to phase out network-related issues.

  • On iPhone X and later: Long-press the Volume Up or Volume Down and Side buttons and swipe right on the power slider to shut down the device. Wait a few seconds and press the Side button to turn it on again.
  • On iPhone 8 and earlier: Long-press the Side Button and swipe right on the power off slider to shut down the device. After some time, turn on the device by pressing and holding the Side button for around ten seconds.

3. Check your date and time settings

Incorrect date/time can disrupt secure connections.

Steps:

  1. Open the Settings app on your iPhone or iPad.
  2. Go to General and tap on Date & Time.
  3. Turn on Set Automatically.

4. Install the latest iOS update

Apple regularly fixes bugs like these through updates.

  1. Open the Settings app on your iPhone or iPad.
  2. Navigate to General and tap on Software Updates.
  3. If an iOS or iPadOS update is available, tap Update Now.
  4. Enter your passcode and wait for the update to install.

Try this: How to update your iPhone

5. Unsubscribe from third-party calendars

Third-party calendar invites without proper certificates can trigger this issue.

  1. Open the Calendar app on your iPhone or iPad.
  2. Tap Calendars to view a list of subscribed calendars.
  3. Tap the i icon next to a calendar you want to unsubscribe.
  4. Tap Delete Calendar to unsubscribe from the said calendar.

6. Delete and re-add your email account

Resetting your account can correct incorrect settings automatically.

  1. Open the Settings app on your iPhone or iPad.
  2. Scroll down, tap on Mail, and select Accounts.
  3. Select the account you want to delete and re-add.
  4. Tap Delete Account. Then, tap Delete from My iPhone.
  5. Once you remove the email account, tap Add Account.
  6. Select your account provider and enter your credentials.

7. Change SSL settings in Mail

Tweaking SSL settings might help if they’re misconfigured.

  1. Open the Settings app on your iPhone or iPad.
  2. Scroll down and tap on Mail. Then, tap on Accounts.
  3. Tap an account for which you want to check the SSL settings.
  4. Now, tap Account Settings and then tap Advanced.
  5. Turn Use SSL on or off and check if that fixes the error for you.

8. Install an MDM Profile (for Work Emails)

Workplace emails often require an MDM profile to authenticate securely.

  1. Download the MDM profile provided by your employer or email service.
  2. Open Settings and tap Profile Downloaded or Enroll In (Organization) at the top of the screen.
  3. Tap Install in the top-right corner, then follow the onscreen instructions.

9. Check certificate trust settings

If the Mail app still won’t connect securely, manually enable trust for root certificates.

  1. Open the Settings app on your iPhone or iPad.
  2. Navigate to General and tap on About.
  3. Scroll down to the bottom and tap Certificate Trust Settings.
  4. Under Enable full trust for root certificates turn on trust certificates.

10. Reset network settings

Network glitches can break the connection to mail servers.

Go to Settings → General → Transfer or Reset iPhone → Reset → Reset Network Settings.

Explore: How to reset network settings on iPhone

11. Factory reset your iPhone (Last Resort)

If all else fails, reset your device to factory settings. Backup your data first!

Then go to Settings → General → Transfer or Reset iPhone → Erase All Content and Settings.

Also read: How to factory reset your iPhone

Video: iPhone “Cannot Verify Server Identity”? 6 Quick fixes

Wrapping up…

If you’re facing the “Cannot Verify Server Identity” error on your iPhone, the fix could be as simple as restarting the device or as complex as installing a work profile. Start with the easy solutions like restarting Mail or updating iOS, then move to account or certificate fixes if needed.

Still stuck? You can always contact Apple Support or your email service provider for deeper troubleshooting.

acceptedAnswer.text: You'll find all recordings in the Notes app, under the "Call Recordings" folder. They're synced through iCloud if that's running on your gears.

acceptedAnswer.text: Open "Call Recordings" in Notes; the transcript is cozy beneath the audio file and searchable.

keyPoints.title: Causes of the 'Cannot Verify Server Identity' Error
keyPoints.explanation: This error occurs when the iPhone can't validate the SSL certificate of the mail server, often due to expired certificates, incorrect settings, or network issues.

keyPoints.title: Simple Fixes to Try First
keyPoints.explanation: Start with easy solutions like force quitting and reopening the Mail app, restarting your iPhone, or checking date and time settings.

keyPoints.title: Updating iOS and Managing Certificates
keyPoints.explanation: Installing the latest system update or manually trusting root certificates can resolve issues caused by outdated or untrusted certificates.

keyPoints.title: Advanced Troubleshooting Steps
keyPoints.explanation: Unsubscribing from third-party calendars, deleting and re-adding email accounts, or resetting network settings can help fix persistent errors.

keyPoints.title: Last Resorts and Support Options
keyPoints.explanation: If all else fails, factory resetting your iPhone or contacting Apple Support may be necessary to resolve the 'Cannot Verify Server Identity' error.

title.rendered: AirPlay 2 TVs in 2026: Top Picks for Apple Users

content.rendered:
Looking for a new TV this year? If you own an iPhone, iPad, or Mac, choosing an AirPlay 2-compatible TV is a no-brainer. With it, you can stream movies, mirror your screen, share photos, play multi-room music, and even control your TV with Siri, all without extra cables or clunky apps.

In this guide, I’ll walk you through the best AirPlay 2-compatible Smart TVs across premium, mid-range, and budget picks.

Table of Contents
  • What to Look for in an AirPlay 2 TV in 2026
  • Top Picks for Best AirPlay 2 TVs in 2026
    • Premium Picks (Over $2000)
    • Mid-Range Picks (Over $1000)
    • Budget Picks (Under $1000)
  • Supported Brands and Models with AirPlay 2
  • Buying Tips for 2026
  • How to Check if Your TV Supports AirPlay 2
  • Final Thoughts: Which TV Should You Buy?

What to Look for in an AirPlay 2 TV in 2026

Buying a TV can be overwhelming. Here’s what matters most when AirPlay support is on your checklist:

  • Picture Quality & Tech: Go for OLED or Mini-LED. In 2026, AI upscaling makes your iPhone videos look like crisp 4K movies.
  • Refresh Rate & Gaming: For sports or gaming, aim for 120Hz+ with VRR (Variable Refresh Rate).
  • Smart OS & Connectivity: webOS, Tizen, or Google TV for smoother interfaces. Look for HDMI 2.1 with eARC and Wi-Fi 6. Siri integration is a bonus.
  • Audio: Dolby Atmos + AirPlay multi-room syncing = theater vibes at home.
  • Size & Build: 65” fits most living rooms. Anti-glare screens are a must if you’ve got sunny windows.
  • Price vs Value: Don’t overspend on features you’ll never use. Mid-range TVs hit the sweet spot for most people.
  • Eco Angle: ENERGY STAR certification saves bills (and the planet).

Keep an eye on energy efficiency, too. 2025 models are getting greener with certifications like ENERGY STAR.

Top Picks for Best AirPlay 2 TVs in 2026

All these models support AirPlay 2 natively—no dongles required.

Premium Picks (Over $2000)

If budget is not an issue, this segment is perfect. These TVs offer top-tier picture quality, AI smarts, and seamless AirPlay integration. You will get 4K OLED panels for infinite contrast, high refresh rates (up to 165Hz), Dolby Vision/Atmos, and anti-glare tech to handle bright rooms.

  • Sony BRAVIA 9 Mini LED Smart TV: Sony’s XR Processor with AI is a standout for natural colors and upscaling. Its studio-calibrated sound and Acoustic Multi-Audio make AirPlay sound more immersive. Exclusive PS5 features are a bonus if you’re a gamer.
  • Samsung QD-OL2ED S95F Smart TV: The NQ4 AI Gen3 Processor upscales content beautifully, and Motion Xcelerator at 165Hz makes gaming silky smooth. With Dolby Atmos, Tizen OS, and Samsung Vision AI, AirPlay streams come alive.
  • LG Evo G5 Series 4K Smart TV: Its webOS, alpha 11 AI Processor and self-lit OLED pixels deliver perfect visuals. I love the Filmmaker Mode for true movie streaming. And the integrated sound bar perfectly synchronizes multi-room audio.

They’re ideal for film enthusiasts or Apple aficionados like me who stream from Apple TV+ to make homemade videos.

Mid-Range Picks (Over $1000)

Sweet spot for the majority of us. Anticipate ULED or QLED for HDR aplenty, 144Hz+ refresh rates, and a powerful smart OS. These offer good performance at a low cost.

  • Hisense U8 Mini-LED ULED Smart TV: With 5,000 nits brightness, a 165Hz panel, and IMAX Enhanced, it’s perfect for HDR content via AirPlay. The Hi-View AI Engine Pro auto-optimizes, and the 4.1.2 channel Dolby Atmos audio is a standout.
  • TCL QM8K Series QD-Mini LED Smart TV: TCL’s next-gen Mini-LED hits 144Hz with no-bezel design for immersive viewing. AI processing makes mirrored iPhone content sharp, and IMAX Enhanced is fun for movies.
  • Samsung OLED S90F Smart TV: If you want the same premium experience as the S95F at a lower price, go for it. AirPlay works seamlessly. The only difference is that you’ll get three built-in speakers.
  • Sony BRAVIA 5 Mini LED Smart TV: It comes equipped with the XR Processor for AI-boosted pics and 120Hz with Dolby Vision. PlayStation integration is awesome. I’ve never seen better color accuracy than Sony for photo mirroring.

Budget Picks (Under $1000)

Affordable doesn’t mean skimpy! These TVs bundle AirPlay 2 with good 4K specs for everyday users. You’ll get QLED panels, 60-120Hz speeds, and a few smart capabilities easily. Perfect for second rooms or first-time purchases.

  • Hisense U7 Mini-LED Smart TV: If you want to stream games or sports, this TV is ideal. It offers ULED, 165Hz, and Dolby Vision IQ. The anti-glare screen is handy, and the 2.1.2 multi-channel surround makes AirPlay audio dynamic. 
  • TCL QM6K QD-Mini LED Smart TV: Best affordable QD-Mini LED with 4K UHD and 288Hz gaming rate. Its enhanced QLED colors and higher contrast make AirPlay videos vivid. 
  • Westinghouse QLED Roku Smart TV: Roku OS supports AirPlay 2 effortlessly. With 4K UHD, HDR 10, and voice control, it’s simple and fun for mirroring podcasts or shows. 
  • INSIGNIA 4K UHD Fire TV: Under $300, Fire OS integrates AirPlay well. You will get a built-in Alexa for hands-free control.  

Supported Brands and Models with AirPlay 2

AirPlay 2 is widely supported in across:

  • Samsung: Most 2018+ models, like QLED/OLED series (S95F, Q80D). 
  • LG: 2019+ OLED/LED (G5, C4).
  • Sony: A-series (A9F-L, A95L), X-series (X85–X95 variants), Z-series, and all BRAVIA models from 2019 onward.   
  • Hisense: ULED/Mini-LED lines from 2020+ (U8, U7). 
  • TCL: Google TV models from 2021+ (QM8K, QM7). 
  • Roku TVs: Built-in on Westinghouse, RCA, etc., from 2019+. 
  • Amazon Fire TVs: INSIGNIA and Toshiba models with Fire OS 7+. 
  • Others: Vizio P, M, and V-series (2016+), some Philips Android TVs. 

Always confirm on the manufacturer’s site before purchase.

Buying Tips for 2026

Purchasing a good TV is indeed pricey, so you must make sure it fulfills your requirements. 

  • Think ahead: features like gaming, HDMI ports, or future smart integrations matter. 
  • Consider the OS: Tizen, webOS, Google TV, Roku, pick what you vibe with daily. 
  • Budget First: Match to your needs, like a premium for cinephiles, a budget for basics. 
  • Room Size: 55-65 inches for most; measure your space! 
  • Test in Store: If possible, try the AirPlay demo. I once avoided a glitchy model this way. 
  • Future-Proof: Go for HDMI 2.1 and Wi-Fi 6. 
  • Warranty & Returns: Amazon’s 30-day policy is a lifesaver. 
  • Eco Angle: Pick ENERGY STAR for lower bills. 

I always check recent trusted reviews before buying.

How to Check if Your TV Supports AirPlay 2

Have you decided on your TV, or have you already got it? Verify the AirPlay 2 compatibility:

  1. Look for the Works with Apple AirPlay badge on the official brand site or on the box. 
  2. Search Apple’s official list of supported models. 
  3. Go to the TV menu: Settings > AirPlay & HomeKit, and check if the AirPlay toggle appears. 
  4. If you don’t find AirPlay, check for firmware updates. Some TVs got it post-launch. 

Final Thoughts: Which TV Should You Buy? 

Wrapping up, AirPlay 2 turns your TV into an Apple-friendly powerhouse, making it smoother than ever.  

  • Want the best and don’t mind splurging? Go for the LG G5 evo or a top-tier Samsung QD-OLED. It’s my personal fave for sunny rooms. 
  • Mid-range but still want an awesome picture and smooth Apple integration? Check out the Hisense U8 with killer brightness or a solid TCL Mini-LED model. 
  • On a tight budget but need Apple connectivity? Grab a Roku-powered Westinghouse or a value Hisense/TCL with AirPlay. 

Ultimately, pick based on your setup. In my experience, the right TV makes everyday streaming feel like the next level.  

What’s your must-have feature in a TV? Drop a comment below!

mainEntity.name: Why is X (Twitter) not loading on my iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: It's usually poor internet, an outdated app/iOS, or a temporary server outage.

mainEntity.name: Why does the X app keep crashing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Low storage, app bugs, or outdated versions. A reinstall often fixes it.

mainEntity.name: Why can't I log in?

acceptedAnswer.text: Check your credentials, reset your password, or contact X Support.

mainEntity.name: How do I fix X notifications not working?

acceptedAnswer.text: Enable them in Settings > Notifications > X and check that Do Not Disturb isn't on.

mainEntity.name: Can I record calls without the other person knowing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Nope, iOS makes the call public, letting everyone know it's being captured. You can't turn off this alert since it keeps things above board legally.

mainEntity.name: Where are my iPhone call recordings saved?

acceptedAnswer.text: You'll find all recordings in the Notes app, under the "Call Recordings" folder. They're synced through iCloud if that's running on your gears.

mainEntity.name: How do I access the transcripts of my recorded calls?

acceptedAnswer.text: Open "Call Recordings" in Notes; the transcript is cozy beneath the audio file and searchable.

mainEntity.name: Why can't I see the record button on my iPhone during a call?

acceptedAnswer.text: To get the full kit you need iOS 18 or later, the right regional settings, and Apple's Intelligence cruising cool in Settings.

mainEntity.name: Does the iPhone call recording feature work with FaceTime or WhatsApp?

acceptedAnswer.text: Nope, this little gem’s closed for just regular calls via the Phone app. Third-party recordings aren’t invited to this party.

mainEntity.name: How do I share a recorded phone call from the Notes app?

acceptedAnswer.text: In Notes, hit up the recording, slap the share button, and choose your audience. You decide if they get audio, transcript, or both.

mainEntity.name: Can I automatically record all calls on my iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: You gotta actually tap that record button for each chat there's no collective auto-record option.

mainEntity.name: How do I delete call recordings from my iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: In Notes, a left swipe on the ones to toss will reveal "Delete," or you can go batch-mode with "Edit."

mainEntity.name: Does iPhone call recording work internationally?

acceptedAnswer.text: Feature availability is gonna flex based on country and local dictates. It's wise to double-check settings and laws if you're trotting the globe with this.
