@graph.name: Sony BRAVIA 9 Mini LED Smart TV
@graph.description: Sony’s XR Processor with AI is a standout for natural colors and upscaling. Its studio calibration and Acoustic Multi-Audio make AirPlay more immersive. Exclusive PS5 features are a bonus if you’re a gamer

@graph.name: SAMSUNG 65-Inch Class OLED S95F 4K Smart TV
@graph.description: The NQ4 AI Gen3 Processor upscales content beautifully, and Motion Xcelerator at 165Hz makes gaming silky smooth. With Dolby Atmos, Tizen OS, and Samsung Vision AI, AirPlay streams come alive.

@graph.name: LG Evo G5 Series 4K Smart TV
@graph.description: Its webOS, alpha 11 AI Processor and self-lit OLED pixels deliver perfect visuals. I love the Filmmaker Mode for true movie streaming. And the integrated sound bar perfectly synchronizes multi-room audio.

@graph.name: Hisense U8 Mini-LED ULED Smart TV
@graph.description: With 5,000 nits brightness, a 165Hz panel, and IMAX Enhanced, it’s perfect for HDR content via AirPlay. The Hi-View AI Engine Pro auto-optimizes, and the 4.1.2 channel Dolby Atmos audio is a standout.

@graph.name: TCL QM8K Series Mini LED QLED 4K Smart TV
@graph.description: TCL’s next-gen Mini-LED hits 144Hz with no-bezel design for immersive viewing. AI processing makes mirrored iPhone content sharp, and IMAX Enhanced is fun for movies.

@graph.name: Samsung OLED S90F Smart TV
@graph.description: If you want the same experience of the premium S95F at a lesser price, go for it. AirPlay works seamlessly. The only difference is that you’ll get three built-in speakers.

@graph.name: Sony BRAVIA 5 Mini LED Smart TV
@graph.description: It comes equipped with the XR Processor for AI-boosted pics and 120Hz with Dolby Vision. PlayStation integration is awesome. I’ve never seen better color accuracy than Sony for photo mirroring.

@graph.name: Hisense U7 Mini-LED Smart TV
@graph.description: If you want to stream games or sports, this TV is ideal. It offers ULED, 165Hz, and Dolby Vision IQ. The anti-glare screen is handy, and the 2.1.2 multi-channel surround makes AirPlay audio dynamic.

@graph.name: TCL QM6K QD-Mini LED Smart TV
@graph.description: Best affordable QD-Mini LED with 4K UHD and 288Hz gaming rate. Its enhanced QLED colors and higher contrast make AirPlay videos vivid.

@graph.name: Westinghouse QLED Roku Smart TV
@graph.description: Roku OS supports AirPlay 2 effortlessly. With 4K UHD, HDR 10, and voice control, it’s simple and fun for mirroring podcasts or shows.

@graph.name: INSIGNIA 4K UHD Fire TV
@graph.description: Under $300, Fire OS integrates AirPlay well. You will get a built-in Alexa for hands-free control.

title.rendered: 11 Ways to Fix WhatsApp Calls Not Working on iPhone and Android

content.rendered:
Ever been in the middle of an important WhatsApp call and suddenly the audio cuts out or the video freezes? Or worse, you’re unable to initiate a WhatsApp call at all? Yep, we’ve all been there.

WhatsApp calls are super handy, but when they stop working, it can be beyond frustrating. The good news? Fixing it is usually easier than you think. In this guide, I’ll show you how to fix WhatsApp call not working on iPhone and Android so you can quickly hop back onto your next voice or video call.

Table of Contents
  • Why WhatsApp Calls Fail on iPhone or Android
  • 11 Ways to Fix WhatsApp Calls Not Working
    • 1. Check Internet Connection
    • 2. Restart Your Device
    • 3. Update WhatsApp and Your System
    • 4. Check WhatsApp Outage
    • 5. Grant Camera & Microphone Permissions
    • 6. Enable Notifications
    • 7. Turn Off Low Data Mode
    • 8. Disable Silent/Do Not Disturb
    • 9. Delete & Reinstall WhatsApp
    • 10. Enable Background App Refresh
    • 11. Contact WhatsApp Support
  • Final Thoughts

Why WhatsApp Calls Fail on iPhone or Android

You may be wondering: “Why can’t I video call on my iPhone?” or “Why isn’t WhatsApp ringing on my Android?” The causes aren’t always obvious, but the symptoms usually are.

Common signs WhatsApp calls aren’t working:

  • Tapping the call button does nothing.
  • Calls try to connect but never do.
  • Incoming calls don’t ring.
  • Audio drops, you can’t hear the other person, or they can’t hear you.
  • Video freezes, turns black, or looks glitchy.

The main culprits:

  • Shaky internet: Weak Wi-Fi, spotty mobile data, or VPN interference.
  • Outdated software: Old versions of WhatsApp or your phone’s OS.
  • Permissions denied: No mic, camera, or notification access.
  • Phone settings: Do Not Disturb, Silent Mode, or Low Data Mode.
  • Server outages: WhatsApp might be down globally.
  • Device limitations: Older phones may not support the latest app updates.
  • Bugs & storage issues: Cache buildup or corrupted files.

11 Ways to Fix WhatsApp Calls Not Working

These fixes apply to both iPhone and Android (with slight variations). Follow them step by step, and you’ll be back to calling in no time.

1. Check Internet Connection

First things first: Is your internet playing nice? WhatsApp calls require a stable connection, so a weak signal may prevent calls from working. 

  • Try switching from Wi-Fi to mobile data (or vice versa) to see if that helps.  
  • If you’re using a VPN, turn it off. It can slow things down or block calls entirely. 
  • Also, cycle your router if the internet speed is slow. Unplug it for 30 seconds, plug it back in, and reconnect.  
  • On your phone, toggle Airplane mode on/off for a quick reset.  
  • If you’re in a spotty area, move closer to your router or try a different network.  
  • Network issues persisting? As a last resort, reset your network settings.
Pro tip Run a speed test on your browser to confirm your connection is strong enough (aim for at least 1 Mbps for voice, more for video).

2. Restart Your Device 

A simple reboot clears temporary glitches.

  • For iPhone: Hold the Side button and Volume down until the slider appears, slide to power off, wait 30 seconds, then turn back on.
  • For Android: Hold the power button, select Restart.

After restarting, open WhatsApp and test a call. This has fixed WhatsApp call not ringing and call failed problems for tons of folks. 

3. Update WhatsApp and Your System

Outdated software is a sneaky troublemaker.  

  1. Head to the App Store (iPhone) or Google Play Store (Android). 
  2. Search for WhatsApp. 
  3. Hit Update if available.  

WhatsApp’s latest versions often patch call bugs, such as the recent security fix for iOS exploits.  

Also, check your phone’s OS and ensure it’s up-to-date. 

  • iPhone users, go to Settings > General > Software Update. If an update is available, download and install it. 
  • Android: Settings > System > System Update.  

Once your phone restarts, try initiating a WhatsApp call. Updates can resolve audio drops or connection failures. 

4. Check WhatsApp Outage 

Sometimes it’s not your fault! WhatsApp might be having a bad day.

  • Visit DownDetector or search “WhatsApp down” on X (Twitter).
  • If it’s global, wait it out.

5. Grant Camera & Microphone Permissions

WhatsApp needs permission to use your mic and camera. Without it, calls won’t initiate and have audio/video issues.

  • On iPhone: Access Settings > Apps > WhatsApp and toggle on Microphone and Camera.
  • Android: Go to Settings > Apps > App Management > WhatsApp > Permissions. Here, ensure Camera and Microphone is allowed.
  • Try stating a call: Start a WhatsApp call and see if it prompts you. Tap Allow to grant access. If not, toggle permissions off/on.
  • Test during a call: If you encounter audio or video glitches, tap the mic and camera icon to disable them, then re-enable.

This fixes “can’t hear audio” or “no video” issues in WhatsApp calls every time.

6. Enable Notifications

If specifically WhatsApp calls aren’t ringing on your iPhone or Android, notifications might be the villain.

  • Check phone settings: Go to iPhone Settings app > Notifications > WhatsApp > Allow Notifications and toggle on Sounds.
  • In WhatsApp: Settings > Notifications > Turn on all the options.

On Android, steps are similar in the app and system settings. You can also set a different ringtone for calls in WhatsApp settings. Thus, you will never miss incoming calls. 

Tip If calls are not ringing only for unsaved contacts, go to WhatsApp Settings > Privacy > Calls > Toggle off Silence unknown numbers.

7. Turn Off Low Data Mode 

Low Data Mode saves your data consumption. It’s helpful if you’re on a limited data plan, but it causes WhatsApp calls to lag or fail.

On iPhone, you need to disable the feature on Wi-Fi or cellular, depending on what you use.

  • For mobile data: Navigate to Settings > Cellular > Cellular Data Options and toggle off Low Data Mode.
  • For Wi-Fi: Settings > Wi-Fi > Tap (i) button next to your network > Turn off Low Data Mode.
      

If you’re an Android user, go to Settings > Network & Internet > Data Saver off. This is a game-changer for video calls that won’t load. 

Tip Still experiencing poor call quality? Access WhatsApp Settings > Privacy > Advanced and toggle off Protect IP address in calls. This ensures your calls are not routed through WhatsApp servers. However, hackers can infer your location.

8. Disable Silent/Do Not Disturb

Your phone might be on mute without you realizing, silencing incoming call rings.  

  • iPhone: Swipe down Control Center, tap the moon icon to turn off Do Not Disturb or Focus modes. From Settings, select Sounds & Haptics and drag the Ringtone slider to the right.
  • Android: Head to Settings > Sound & Vibration > ensure Do Not Disturb is off. Also, set Ring mode and increase Ringtone volume to ensure calls ring loud. 

9. Delete & Reinstall WhatsApp

If nothing’s working, a fresh start helps.

  1. Long-press the WhatsApp icon from your home screen.  
  2.  Select Remove App (iOS) or Uninstall (Android).  
  3. Confirm your choice to delete WhatsApp. 
  4. Then search WhatsApp on the App Store or Google Play Store and reinstall it.

This clears the cache and corrupted files that might be causing audio/video glitches during calls. However, back up your chats first: WhatsApp Settings > Chats > Chat backup. So, when you reinstall it, all your messages are back.

10. Enable Background App Refresh

Calls need WhatsApp to run in the background for constant reachability.

  • iPhone: Open Settings and go to General > Background App Refresh and select Wi-Fi & Cellular Data and ensure WhatsApp is allowed.
  • Android: Settings > Apps > WhatsApp > Battery usage > Allow background activity. This keeps the app alert for incoming calls, fixing those silent misses.

11. Contact WhatsApp Support 

If all else fails, reach out to the pros.

  1. In WhatsApp, navigate to Settings > Help > Help Center.
  2. Scroll down and tap Contact Us.
  3. Explain your problem with symptoms, device, OS version and send logs if requested.

They’re quite prompt and can identify server-side issues or point you in the right direction.

Final Thoughts

That’s it! One of these fixes should solve your WhatsApp call not working problem. In most cases, the issue is due to network hiccups, outdated apps, or permission settings.

Pro tip: If you’re still using an older phone (like iPhone 6 or older Androids), consider upgrading. WhatsApp gradually drops support for outdated devices. Staying updated with the latest app and OS ensures smoother calls.

Now go ahead and enjoy those family video calls and work chats without interruption.

Related articles worth reading:

  • How to Block and Unblock Someone in WhatsApp on iPhone
  • WhatsApp Storage in Full? How to Clear It on iPhone
  • How to turn off backup for individual apps on Android
  • How to Back Up WhatsApp Messages on iPhone and Android

mainEntity.name: Why is X (Twitter) not loading on my iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: It's usually poor internet, an outdated app/iOS, or a temporary server outage.

mainEntity.name: Why does the X app keep crashing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Low storage, app bugs, or outdated versions. A reinstall often fixes it.

mainEntity.name: Why can't I log in?

acceptedAnswer.text: Check your credentials, reset your password, or contact X Support.

mainEntity.name: How do I fix X notifications not working?

acceptedAnswer.text: Enable them in Settings > Notifications > X and check that Do Not Disturb isn't on.

mainEntity.name: Can I record calls without the other person knowing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Nope, iOS makes the call public, letting everyone know it's being captured. You can't turn off this alert since it keeps things above board legally.

mainEntity.name: Where are my iPhone call recordings saved?

acceptedAnswer.text: You'll find all recordings in the Notes app, under the "Call Recordings" folder. They're synced through iCloud if that's running on your gears.

mainEntity.name: How do I access the transcripts of my recorded calls?

acceptedAnswer.text: Open "Call Recordings" in Notes; the transcript is cozy beneath the audio file and searchable.

mainEntity.name: Why can't I see the record button on my iPhone during a call?

acceptedAnswer.text: To get the full kit you need iOS 18 or later, the right regional settings, and Apple's Intelligence cruising cool in Settings.

mainEntity.name: Does the iPhone call recording feature work with FaceTime or WhatsApp?

acceptedAnswer.text: Nope, this little gem’s closed for just regular calls via the Phone app. Third-party recordings aren’t invited to this party.

mainEntity.name: How do I share a recorded phone call from the Notes app?

acceptedAnswer.text: In Notes, hit up the recording, slap the share button, and choose your audience. You decide if they get audio, transcript, or both.

mainEntity.name: Can I automatically record all calls on my iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: You gotta actually tap that record button for each chat there's no collective auto-record option.

mainEntity.name: How do I delete call recordings from my iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: In Notes, a left swipe on the ones to toss will reveal "Delete," or you can go batch-mode with "Edit."

mainEntity.name: Does iPhone call recording work internationally?

acceptedAnswer.text: Feature availability is gonna flex based on country and local dictates. It's wise to double-check settings and laws if you're trotting the globe with this.

title.rendered: How to Crop Photos on iPhone or iPad

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Crop photos using Quick Crop or manual tools in the Photos app to trim or reframe images directly on your iPhone.
  • Quick Crop offers fast resizing options like Square or Widescreen, ideal for social sharing or quick visual fixes.
  • Use manual crop for more control—drag corners in Edit mode to crop with precision and match custom layouts.
  • iOS 18 adds batch cropping support—copy crop settings from one photo and apply them to others for faster editing.
  • You can always revert edits back to original—Photos app stores the original image, letting you undo cropping anytime.

Cropping photos on an iPhone is easy, thanks to the built-in editing tools in the Photos app. Not only can you easily crop photos on your iPhone with these tools, but you can also undo the changes and revert the photos to their original state if you cropped them incorrectly.

This guide details how to use the Photos app to crop photos on your iPhone.

Table of Contents
  • How to crop a photo on your iPhone or iPad
    • Automatically crop a photo in the Photos app
    • Manually crop a photo in the Photos app
    • Resize photos on your iPhone or iPad
  • How to crop multiple photos at once on your iPhone
  • How to revert a cropped photo to the original

How to crop a photo on your iPhone or iPad

The Photos app offers two ways to crop images on an iPhone or iPad. You can use the app’s built-in editing tools or the Quick Edit feature. Here’s how to do it!

Automatically crop a photo in the Photos app

  1. Open the Photos app and head to the image you want to crop.
  2. With the image opened, pinch out to zoom in to a desired level.
  3. Tap the Crop button in the top-right corner of the screen.
  4. Hit Done to save the image.

By default, the Quick Crop feature crops the image using the same aspect ratio shown on the screen. However, you can change the default setting if you want to maintain the image’s original aspect ratio or crop it in a different aspect ratio.

  1. With the image zoomed in, long press the Crop button.
  2. Choose among the four available aspect ratio options: Full Screen, Original, Widescreen, and Square.
  3. Hit Crop to crop the image and save it by tapping Done.

Your iPhone will remember your choice and crop your images in that aspect.

Manually crop a photo in the Photos app

If you’re using an older version of iOS on your iPhone or want more precision, you can use the built-in Crop tool in the Photos app to crop your photos. Here’s how:

  1. Open the image you want to crop in the Photos app.
  2. Tap the Edit icon next to the “i” button at the bottom.
  3. Select Crop in the bottom toolbar, and a rectangular box will appear around the image.
  4. Drag the rectangle corners to enclose the area you want to keep in the photo.
  5. Tap Done in the top right corner to crop and save the image.

Resize photos on your iPhone or iPad

For times when you want to resize an image to specific dimensions after cropping it, you can select a preset aspect ratio accordingly in the Photos app like this:

  1. Repeat the first two steps of the previous section.
  2. Tap the Crop tool and choose an Aspect Ratio from the options that appear: Original, Freeform, Square, or Wallpaper.
  3. For more aspect ratio, tap Original and select Landscape or Portrait view. Then swipe to the right and choose a ration.
    • Landscape: 16:9, 5:4, 7:5, 4:3, 5:3, or 3:2
    • Portrait: 9:16, 4:5, 5:7, 3:4, 3:5, or 2:3
  4. Once done, use the rectangular corners to enclose the desired area in the image.
  5. Tap the Done button.

The built-in editing tools in the Photos app allow you to crop photos and rotate or flip them to your desired orientation on the iPhone.

How to crop multiple photos at once on your iPhone

The Photos app lets you copy edits and apply them to multiple images in iOS 18. All of the chosen images will be cropped like the first one.

  1. Open the cropped image in the Photos app.
  2. Tap on the three-dot icon in the top right corner and select Copy Edits.
  3. Toggle on Crop and tap on Copy.
  4. Now, go back to your library and tap Select.
  5. Choose the photos and tap on the three-dot icon at the bottom.
  6. Now, select Paste Edits.

How to revert a cropped photo to the original

At any point, if you want to revert a cropped photo to its original state, you can undo the crop using these steps:

  1. Open the cropped image.
  2. Hit the Edit icon at the bottom of the screen.
  3. Tap on Revert and hit Revert to Original when the confirmation prompt appears.

Note that this action will also remove any additional edits you have made to the photo.

Signing off

With just a few taps, you can crop photos on your iPhone to remove unwanted elements or empty spaces and draw attention to the main subject. While the built-in Crop tool in the Photos app can do the job just fine, if you want additional cropping or editing features, you can check out third-party photo editing apps.

Read more:

  • How to rotate multiple iPhone images at once
  • How to edit photos on iPhone
  • How to use People Album in Photos App on iPhone or iPad
  • How to reduce photo file size on iPhone and iPad

mainEntity.name: Can I record calls without the other person knowing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Nope, iOS makes the call public, letting everyone know it's being captured. You can't turn off this alert since it keeps things above board legally.

mainEntity.name: Where are my iPhone call recordings saved?

acceptedAnswer.text: You'll find all recordings in the Notes app, under the "Call Recordings" folder. They're synced through iCloud if that's running on your gears.

mainEntity.name: How do I access the transcripts of my recorded calls?

acceptedAnswer.text: Open "Call Recordings" in Notes; the transcript is cozy beneath the audio file and searchable.

mainEntity.name: Why can't I see the record button on my iPhone during a call?

acceptedAnswer.text: To get the full kit you need iOS 18 or later, the right regional settings, and Apple's Intelligence cruising cool in Settings.

mainEntity.name: Does the iPhone call recording feature work with FaceTime or WhatsApp?

acceptedAnswer.text: Nope, this little gem’s closed for just regular calls via the Phone app. Third-party recordings aren’t invited to this party.

mainEntity.name: How do I share a recorded phone call from the Notes app?

acceptedAnswer.text: In Notes, hit up the recording, slap the share button, and choose your audience. You decide if they get audio, transcript, or both.

mainEntity.name: Can I automatically record all calls on my iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: You gotta actually tap that record button for each chat there's no collective auto-record option.

mainEntity.name: How do I delete call recordings from my iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: In Notes, a left swipe on the ones to toss will reveal "Delete," or you can go batch-mode with "Edit."

mainEntity.name: Does iPhone call recording work internationally?

acceptedAnswer.text: Feature availability is gonna flex based on country and local dictates. It's wise to double-check settings and laws if you're trotting the globe with this.

@graph.name: How to Automatically crop a photo in the Photos app on iPhone
@graph.description: Quickly crop photos on your iPhone using the Photos app’s automatic quick crop feature. Zoom in, crop, and save in just a few taps.

step.name: Open the photo
step.text: Launch the Photos app and open the image you want to crop.

itemListElement.text: Open the Photos app.
Tap on the image you want to crop.

step.name: Zoom in
step.text: With the photo open, pinch out to zoom in until the framing looks right.

itemListElement.text: Place two fingers on the screen.
Pinch outward to zoom in on the subject.

step.name: Apply the crop
step.text: Tap the Crop button in the top-right corner to apply the quick crop.

itemListElement.text: Tap the Crop button once you’re satisfied with the zoom level.

step.name: Save the cropped photo
step.text: Hit Done to confirm and save the cropped version of your photo.

itemListElement.text: Tap Done in the bottom-right corner.
Your cropped photo is now saved in Photos.

@graph.name: How to Manually crop a photo in the Photos app
@graph.description: Manually crop photos on your iPhone for precise framing. This quick guide shows how to open the editor, adjust the crop box with corner handles, and save the result.

step.name: Open the photo in Photos
step.text: Open the image you want to crop in the Photos app so you can start editing.

itemListElement.text: Launch the Photos app on your iPhone.
Select the image you want to crop.

step.name: Enter Edit mode
step.text: Tap the Edit icon next to the information button at the bottom to open the editing tools.

itemListElement.text: Tap Edit to bring up the editing toolbar.

step.name: Choose Crop
step.text: Select Crop in the bottom toolbar. A rectangular box appears around your photo that you can adjust.

itemListElement.text: Tap Crop in the toolbar to show the adjustable frame.

step.name: Adjust the crop box
step.text: Drag the rectangle corners or edges to enclose exactly what you want to keep in the image.

itemListElement.text: Press and hold a corner handle to start adjusting.
Drag inward or outward until the framing looks right.

step.name: Save your crop
step.text: Tap Done in the top right corner to apply the crop and save the edited image.

itemListElement.text: Review the preview to confirm the composition.
Tap Done to save the cropped photo.

@graph.name: How to Resize photos on your iPhone or iPad
@graph.description: Easily resize photos on your iPhone or iPad using the Photos app’s crop tool with preset aspect ratios like Square, Wallpaper, Landscape, or Portrait.

tool.name: iPhone or iPad with Photos app

step.name: Open the photo and enter Edit mode
step.text: Open the photo in the Photos app, tap Edit, and select Crop from the toolbar.

itemListElement.text: Launch the Photos app and open your image.
Tap Edit, then tap Crop to bring up editing options.

step.name: Choose an aspect ratio
step.text: Tap Aspect Ratio and pick from options like Original, Freeform, Square, or Wallpaper. For more ratios, tap Original and switch to Landscape or Portrait view, then swipe to see ratios.

itemListElement.text: Tap Aspect Ratio from the crop options.
Choose from Original, Freeform, Square, or Wallpaper.
For additional options, tap Original, then select Landscape or Portrait.
In Landscape, you can choose 16:9, 5:4, 7:5, 4:3, 5:3, or 3:2.
In Portrait, you can choose 9:16, 4:5, 5:7, 3:4, 3:5, or 2:3.

step.name: Adjust the crop box
step.text: Drag the rectangle’s corners or edges to enclose the area of the photo you want to keep with the chosen ratio.

itemListElement.text: Use the crop handles to adjust the framing.
Make sure the subject fits well inside the aspect ratio box.

step.name: Save the resized photo
step.text: Once satisfied, tap Done in the top right corner to apply the resize and save your photo.

itemListElement.text: Tap Done to save your resized image.

@graph.name: How to crop multiple photos at once on your iPhone
@graph.description: Batch-apply the same crop to many photos on your iPhone using Copy Edits and Paste Edits, so you can save time and keep a consistent look across your images.

step.name: Open a photo that already has the crop you want
step.text: Open the cropped image in the Photos app, which will act as the source for your batch crop.

itemListElement.text: Launch the Photos app on your iPhone.
Open the photo that has the crop you want to reuse.

step.name: Copy the crop edits
step.text: Tap the three-dot icon in the top right and choose Copy Edits. Turn on Crop, then tap Copy to copy just the crop settings.

itemListElement.text: Tap the three-dot icon at the top right.
Select Copy Edits from the menu.
Toggle on Crop so only the crop is copied.
Tap Copy to confirm.

step.name: Select your target photos
step.text: Return to your library, tap Select, and choose all the photos you want to crop the same way.

itemListElement.text: Go back to the Photos library view.
Tap Select and choose the photos you want to update.

step.name: Paste the crop onto all selected photos
step.text: Tap the three-dot icon at the bottom and choose Paste Edits to apply the copied crop to every selected photo.

itemListElement.text: Tap the three-dot icon at the bottom of the screen.
Select Paste Edits to apply the crop to all selected photos.

@graph.name: How to revert a cropped photo to the original on iPhone
@graph.description: Easily restore a cropped photo to its original version in the iPhone Photos app. This step-by-step guide shows you how to undo edits and bring back the full image.

supply.name: Cropped photo you want to restore

step.name: Open the cropped image
step.text: Launch the Photos app and open the photo you previously cropped that you want to restore.

itemListElement.text: Open the Photos app.
Tap the cropped photo to view it.

step.name: Enter Edit mode
step.text: Tap the Edit icon at the bottom of the screen to access editing tools.

itemListElement.text: Tap the Edit button at the bottom.

step.name: Revert to original
step.text: Tap Revert, then confirm by selecting Revert to Original to restore the uncropped version of the photo.

itemListElement.text: Tap Revert in the lower-right corner.
Tap Revert to Original when the confirmation prompt appears.

keyPoints.title: Photos App Cropping Methods
keyPoints.explanation: You can crop images on your iPhone using the built-in editing tools or the Quick Crop feature, with options to undo and revert changes.

keyPoints.title: Using Quick Crop for Fast Editing
keyPoints.explanation: Quick Crop allows quick adjustments by zooming in, selecting aspect ratios like Square or Widescreen, and saving your edits efficiently.

keyPoints.title: Manual Cropping for Precision
keyPoints.explanation: For detailed editing, use the manual crop tool by dragging corner handles in the Photos app's Edit mode to precisely select the cropped area.

keyPoints.title: Batch Cropping with iOS 18
keyPoints.explanation: The latest iOS update introduces batch cropping, letting you copy edits from one photo and apply them to multiple images at once, saving time.

keyPoints.title: Reverting to Original Image
keyPoints.explanation: If you need to undo cropping or other edits, you can revert a photo back to its original state in the Photos app without hassle.

Vikhyat has a bachelor’s degree in Electronic and Communication Engineering and over five years of writing experience. His passion for technology and Apple products led him to the tech writing space, where he specializes in writing App features, How-to guides, and troubleshooting guides for fellow Apple users. 

 

About Vikhyat Rishi

  • Vikhyat has over five years of experience writing consumer tech content.
  • During his association with Smartprix and Beebom, Vikhyat has tested, tested, and reviewed numerous gadgets, including but not limited to smartphones, TVs, and more.
  • His passion for technology and Apple products led him to iGeeksBlog, where he specializes in writing How-to and troubleshooting guides for fellow Apple enthusiasts.

Experience

Vikhyat embarked on his journey in consumer technology writing in 2019, driven by his passion for technology. He has sharpened his skills through associations with Smartprix and Beebom, where he extensively tested and reviewed various gadgets, focusing mainly on smartphones. Currently, Vikhyat specializes in crafting How-to and troubleshooting guides for the Apple ecosystem at iGeeksBlog. When not typing away on his MacBook Air, he loves exploring the real world.

title.rendered: 9 Compelling Reasons to Buy an Apple Watch

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Seamless iPhone pairing: Apple Watch syncs instantly with iPhone for calls, texts, music control, and even unlocking your iPhone straight from the wrist.
  • Health tracking built in: It monitors heart rate, ECG, sleep, blood oxygen, and wrist temperature, sharing detailed insights directly into the iPhone Health app.
  • Motivation that sticks: Activity Rings and social fitness sharing encourage daily movement while Workout Buddy helps you stay consistent with goals and accountability.
  • Emergency help on wrist: Apple Watch detects crashes, hard falls, or abnormal heart rates and can alert emergency services or contacts automatically.
  • Style meets function: Multiple sizes, colors, and strap options plus custom watch faces let you make Apple Watch feel personal while staying practical.

It’s an understatement to call the Apple Watch just a companion device for an iPhone. Ever since its launch, the Apple Watch has made its own name by offering a powerful blend of style, technology, health monitoring, and everyday convenience. With the Apple Watch vs. Whoop band debate going strong, wondering whether it’s worth investing in an Apple Watch isn’t uncommon.

Here are nine compelling reasons why the Apple Watch stands out and is worth investing in.

Table of Contents
  • 1. Flawless Integration with iPhone
  • 2. Advanced Health Monitoring
  • 3. Fitness & Motivation Made Simple
  • 4. Safety Features That Actually Save Lives
  • 5. Stylish and Customizable
  • 6. Everyday Convenience
  • 7. Helps Reduce Screen Time
  • 8. watchOS Beats Every Other Smartwatch Platform
  • 9. Long-Term Value with Updates
  • Who Should Get an Apple Watch?
  • Should You Buy an Apple Watch?

1. Flawless Integration with iPhone

Apple has designed the Apple Watch to work hand in hand with the iPhone. With an Apple Watch on your wrist, you can perform almost all the activities without needing to pull out your iPhone from your pocket. You can make and receive calls, send and reply to messages, check notifications, control music playback, and even use it as a remote camera shutter for the iPhone.

Additionally, you can even unlock your iPhone with your Apple Watch on your wrist if the Face ID fails or you forget the passcode.

2. Advanced Health Monitoring

While the Apple Watch is still not an official medical device, the newer models can track and monitor your blood oxygen levels, heart rate, ECG, and sleep. It’s like a mini health hub tied to your wrist. It can even alert you to irregular heart rhythms and remind you to take your medication.

Female users can also benefit from the Cycle Tracking app to stay notified when their next period or fertile window is approaching. Besides this, the latest models can even use the built-in temperature sensors to estimate your ovulation date and enhance the accuracy of your period predictions based on your wrist temperature data.

All the tracked data is shared with the Health app on your iPhone, where you can view the detailed dashboards for all your health categories.

While most of these health tracking features are available on other smartwatches as well, none of the available options are as accurate as the Apple Watch.

3. Fitness & Motivation Made Simple

Staying consistent with fitness can be tough, especially when life gets busy. This is where the Apple Watch shines: it tracks your workouts and nudges you toward building healthier habits in small but meaningful ways.

At the heart of the Apple Watch’s fitness tracking ability are the Activity Rings. Closing your Move, Exercise, and Stand rings feels surprisingly satisfying, almost like checking off a to-do list. And when you don’t meet your daily goals, the Watch gently reminds you instead of making you feel guilty. That little tap on your wrist can be the push you need to take the stairs, go for a short walk, or finish that quick workout session.

Besides this, watchOS 26 introduces Apple’s intelligence-powered fitness coach feature named Workout Buddy. The new feature analyzes a combination of real-time workout data, your workout history, Activity Ring progress, pace, training load, and more to deliver motivational voice feedback during your session to help you stay motivated.

The Watch also makes fitness social by allowing you to share your fitness stats and progress with your friends, and getting a notification that someone just completed their workout creates a sense of accountability.

4. Safety Features That Actually Save Lives

Only a handful of devices claim they’ve saved lives, and the Apple Watch is one of them, with many media reports and user experiences backing the claim.

The Apple Watch can detect if you are involved in a severe fall or a vehicle crash and call the emergency services and contacts on your behalf. This way, help can reach you even if you’re unconscious.

Besides, it also warns you of potentially harmful sound levels when you’re in a surrounding where decibel levels can adversely affect your hearing. Additionally, you’re notified if the Apple Watch detects an elevated heart rate for more than ten minutes while you’re inactive.

All these safety features make the Apple Watch reassuring for older users or anyone who values peace of mind.

5. Stylish and Customizable

The Apple Watch is a perfect example of when tech meets fashion. It comes in a variety of sizes and color options that suit your wrist size and style. Additionally, there are literally hundreds of watch band options available from Apple, as well as third-party brands. This way, you can buy a watch band that adapts to every outfit you wear with your Apple Watch, whether for the gym, office, or a night out.

Besides the outer aesthetics, you can customize the Apple Watch with the watch face that suits your fancy. You can even use your own photos as the watch face.

6. Everyday Convenience

From tapping your wrist to pay with Apple Pay to unlocking your Mac, navigating with Maps, or summoning Siri, the Apple Watch makes everyday tasks easier. It removes small frictions from your day and replaces them with quick, seamless actions.

7. Helps Reduce Screen Time

One of the underrated benefits of owning an Apple Watch is reduced screen time. Having an Apple Watch, especially a cellular model, limits looking at your iPhone screen dozens of times a day just to check notifications by offering a quick glance right at your wrist.

If I talk about my personal experience, I often head out of my home, leaving my iPhone behind with just my Apple Watch on my wrist. The reason is that having an Apple Watch at my disposal doesn’t make me miss my iPhone at all. This way, I can focus on the task at hand without being unnecessarily distracted by my iPhone, while still ensuring I don’t miss anything important.

This simple shift helps cut down on unnecessary scrolling and keeps you more present in the moment.

8. watchOS Beats Every Other Smartwatch Platform

WatchOS is the reason the Apple Watch excels in every aspect. While many brands, including Samsung, Google, and Garmin, offer smartwatches with similar functionality, none can match the offerings of watchOS.

Over the years, Apple has redefined the watchOS with regular updates, a massive app ecosystem, smooth performance, and deep integration with iOS. Even though watchOS is currently in its twelfth iteration (watchOS 26), no other smartwatch platform offers even a close balance of usability, reliability, and innovation.

9. Long-Term Value with Updates

When it comes to fitness tracking, Whoop is undoubtedly ahead of the Apple Watch. However, Whoop isn’t a one-time investment; you need to keep renewing the subscription. On the other hand, the Apple Watch is a one-time investment.

Once you buy an Apple Watch, Apple consistently adds new features to your Apple Watch with each new watchOS update, watchOS 26 being the latest one. The new feature additions ensure your Apple Watch continues to feel fresh and relevant, even if you don’t own the newest model. Plus, you can replace the watch band anytime and make your older Apple Watch appear like a new one.

Who Should Get an Apple Watch?

Like every other tech device, the Apple Watch isn’t for everyone. However, for someone who wants to take better control of their health, the watch’s fitness, heart, sleep, and activity tracking will give you insights you didn’t know you needed.

Moreover, the cellular model is perfect for those who like to stay connected without being glued to their phone. You can glance at your wrist for notifications, respond to quick texts, or even make and answer calls without your iPhone.

Should You Buy an Apple Watch?

And that’s it; now you know that an Apple Watch is worth investing in if you want a device that helps you stay healthier, safer, and more productive. The device has all the qualities to fit quietly into your routine, offering just the right nudge when you need it, and staying out of the way when you don’t.

If you’re still wondering which model best fits your lifestyle, check out our guide on how to choose which Apple Watch to buy for a detailed breakdown.

Got questions about a specific Apple Watch model? Share them in the comments, and we’ll respond quickly.

  • How to Reset Your Apple Watch to Factory Settings
  • All Apple Watch Icons and Symbols Meanings Explained

mainEntity.name: Why is X (Twitter) not loading on my iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: It's usually poor internet, an outdated app/iOS, or a temporary server outage.

mainEntity.name: Why does the X app keep crashing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Low storage, app bugs, or outdated versions. A reinstall often fixes it.

mainEntity.name: Why can't I log in?

acceptedAnswer.text: Check your credentials, reset your password, or contact X Support.

mainEntity.name: How do I fix X notifications not working?

acceptedAnswer.text: Enable them in Settings > Notifications > X and check that Do Not Disturb isn't on.

mainEntity.name: Can I record calls without the other person knowing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Nope, iOS makes the call public, letting everyone know it's being captured. You can't turn off this alert since it keeps things above board legally.

mainEntity.name: Where are my iPhone call recordings saved?

acceptedAnswer.text: You'll find all recordings in the Notes app, under the "Call Recordings" folder. They're synced through iCloud if that's running on your gears.

mainEntity.name: How do I access the transcripts of my recorded calls?

acceptedAnswer.text: Open "Call Recordings" in Notes; the transcript is cozy beneath the audio file and searchable.

mainEntity.name: Why can't I see the record button on my iPhone during a call?

acceptedAnswer.text: To get the full kit you need iOS 18 or later, the right regional settings, and Apple's Intelligence cruising cool in Settings.

mainEntity.name: Does the iPhone call recording feature work with FaceTime or WhatsApp?

acceptedAnswer.text: Nope, this little gem’s closed for just regular calls via the Phone app. Third-party recordings aren’t invited to this party.

mainEntity.name: How do I share a recorded phone call from the Notes app?

acceptedAnswer.text: In Notes, hit up the recording, slap the share button, and choose your audience. You decide if they get audio, transcript, or both.

mainEntity.name: Can I automatically record all calls on my iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: You gotta actually tap that record button for each chat there's no collective auto-record option.

mainEntity.name: How do I delete call recordings from my iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: In Notes, a left swipe on the ones to toss will reveal "Delete," or you can go batch-mode with "Edit."

mainEntity.name: Does iPhone call recording work internationally?

acceptedAnswer.text: Feature availability is gonna flex based on country and local dictates. It's wise to double-check settings and laws if you're trotting the globe with this.

keyPoints.title: Flawless Integration with iPhone
keyPoints.explanation: The Apple Watch seamlessly syncs with the iPhone, allowing users to perform most tasks such as making calls, sending messages, and controlling music directly from their wrist, even unlocking the iPhone with the watch.

keyPoints.title: Advanced Health Monitoring
keyPoints.explanation: The latest Apple Watch models can track blood oxygen, heart rate, ECG, sleep, and even monitor wrist temperature, sharing data with the Health app and offering high accuracy for health insights.

keyPoints.title: Fitness & Motivation Made Simple
keyPoints.explanation: With features like Activity Rings and the Workout Buddy, the Apple Watch motivates users to stay active, build healthier habits, and enjoy social fitness sharing for accountability.

keyPoints.title: Safety Features That Actually Save Lives
keyPoints.explanation: The Apple Watch can detect severe falls, vehicle crashes, and high heart rates, automatically contacting emergency services and health contacts, which has been reported to save lives.

keyPoints.title: Stylish and Customizable
keyPoints.explanation: Available in various sizes, colors, and with a wide array of watch bands, the Apple Watch combines fashion with personalization, including customizable watch faces and photo options.

aioseo_head_json.author_bio:
Vikhyat has a bachelor’s degree in Electronic and Communication Engineering and over five years of writing experience. His passion for technology and Apple products led him to the tech writing space, where he specializes in writing App features, How-to guides, and troubleshooting guides for fellow Apple users. 

 

About Vikhyat Rishi

  • Vikhyat has over five years of experience writing consumer tech content.
  • During his association with Smartprix and Beebom, Vikhyat has tested, tested, and reviewed numerous gadgets, including but not limited to smartphones, TVs, and more.
  • His passion for technology and Apple products led him to iGeeksBlog, where he specializes in writing How-to and troubleshooting guides for fellow Apple enthusiasts.

Experience

Vikhyat embarked on his journey in consumer technology writing in 2019, driven by his passion for technology. He has sharpened his skills through associations with Smartprix and Beebom, where he extensively tested and reviewed various gadgets, focusing mainly on smartphones. Currently, Vikhyat specializes in crafting How-to and troubleshooting guides for the Apple ecosystem at iGeeksBlog. When not typing away on his MacBook Air, he loves exploring the real world.

title.rendered: How to Use the Measure App on Your iPhone

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • The Measure app is built-in on iPhones from SE (1st gen) and newer—no download needed, but features may vary by model.
  • To measure a single object, set two points in the app—the result appears instantly and can be copied or saved via screenshot.
  • Measure multiple sides by repeating the process—all lines stay visible so you can capture multiple dimensions in one session.
  • You can also measure surface area of rectangles—just hover your iPhone over the object and tap + when it auto-detects.
  • The Level tool helps check flatness and tilt—use it to find 0° on tables, walls, or other surfaces when alignment matters.

Gone are the days when you had to hunt for the measuring tape every time you needed to measure something. With your iPhone at your disposal, you can use the Measure app to measure multiple dimensions of an object. Whether you’re measuring furniture, checking the level of hanging pictures, or just curious about an object’s dimensions, the Measure app can do it all.

Keep reading to learn how to use the Apple’s Measure app on your iPhone or iPad.

Table of Contents
  • How to measure on your iPhone with the Measure app
    • Measure a single dimension of an object
    • Measure multiple dimensions of an object
    • Measure the surface area of a rectangular object
  • How to measure the level of an object on iPhone
  • How to measure a person's height with iPhone
    • Ruler View
    • Guides
    • Measurement History
  • How to clear measurement in the Measure app on iPhone

How to measure on your iPhone with the Measure app

The Measure app comes pre-installed on your iPhone and iPad, but if you have uninstalled it for any reason, you can go to the App Store and install it from there.

However, not all iPhone and iPad models are compatible with the Measure app. Here’s the list of devices you can use the Measure app on:

  • iPhone SE 1st all generations
  • iPhone 6s or later models
  • iPad 5th generation or later models
  • All iPad Pro models
  • 7th Gen iPod Touch

Measure a single dimension of an object

  1. Open the Measure app and follow the on-screen instructions to move your iPhone around.
  2. Continue slowly moving your iPhone until the AR tech comes into action.
  3. Once it does, you’ll see a Circle with a Dot in the center on top of the spot you want to start measuring from.
  4. Next, tap the + button and slowly move your iPhone until the same circle appears on the object’s endpoint.
  5. A dotted line appears while you move your iPhone to keep the measurement track in check.
  6. Once the circle appears on the endpoint, tap the + button again.
  7. The measurement of the distance between the two points will appear above a straight line.
  8. If you discover that the start and the end point are not in a straight line, you can touch & hold on to any of the points and drag it to reposition it.
  9. Once satisfied with the measurement, tap the Capture button at the bottom right to save the screenshot to the Photos app.

Measure multiple dimensions of an object

If you are confused about whether a particular object will fit in the space you have created for it in your house, you will need to measure more than a single dimension. Fortunately, the Measure app lets you measure multiple dimensions of an object in a single session.

  1. Repeat all the steps from the previous section except the last one.
  2. Position the Dot at the desired point of the currently available line and tap the + button.
  3. Move your iPhone to the endpoint to create a straight dotted line between the start and end point of your second measurement.
  4. Next, tap the + button again to confirm the selection.
  5. You can also use your finger to fiddle with the straight line if you are unsatisfied with the result.
  6. Once done, you can view both the measurements simultaneously on your screen.
  7. Repeat the process to add as many measurements as you want.
  8. Finally, tap the Capture button to save the measurement screenshot to the Photos app.

Measure the surface area of a rectangular object

  1. Position the viewfinder over a rectangular object with the Measurement app opened on your iPhone.
  2. The Measure app will automatically detect the rectangular object, and dotted lines will appear around it.
  3. Next, tap the + button, and the measurement of the entire object will appear around it with its surface area at its center.
  4. Tap the Capture button to save the measurement.
  5. You can also tap on the surface area measurement how to view the Measure app measured it and copy it as well.

How to measure the level of an object on iPhone

Along with the ability to mention the dimensions, the Measure app also allows you to check if a surface is level. Here’s how:

  1. With the Measure app opened, tap the Level icon at the bottom right to switch to Level mode.
  2. Place the iPhone on the surface you want to check.
  3. The app will show 0 degrees if the surface is flat.
  4. If not, the angle of deviation will appear on the screen.

How to measure a person’s height with iPhone

Starting with the iPhone 11 Pro, Apple added a new LiDAR sensor within the camera module of its Pro iPhones. The Measure app uses the LiDAR sensor to measure a person’s height.

  1. Open the Measure app.
  2. Now, ask the person whose height you want to measure the height if to stand opposite to the rear camera and ensure that they appear from head to toe on your iPhone’s screen.
  3. Once done, a white line with the person’s height will appear above the person’s head.
  4. Note down the measured height or tap the Capture button to save the screenshot in the Photos app.

Ruler View

This is another feature only available to iPhones with LiDAR sensors. It works similarly to how a measuring tape works. Basically, the Ruler View lets you see the incremental length of the object in the direction you move your iPhone.

Move your iPhone closer to the object you are measuring, and the Ruler View will appear automatically.

Guides

Similar to how the grid line works in the Camera app, the Guides feature in the Measure app shows the horizontal and vertical lines guides when measuring an object. The feature automatically detects the object’s edges to help you measure it correctly.

To access the guidelines in the Measure app on Pro iPhones, simply tap the + button on the guide and start measuring.

Measurement History

Measurement History is activated when measuring multiple objects one by one in a single session. To access your measurement history, tap the List button at the top left corner, and all the screenshots you took while measuring will appear.

How to clear measurement in the Measure app on iPhone

The resulting measurement may often not be as accurate as you want it to be. In that case, you can clear the measurement and start all over again.

To do so, simply tap the Clear button at the top right corner.

Happy measuring…

That’s all you need to learn about the Measure app on your iPhone or iPad. With just a bit of practice, you’ll be a pro at measuring objects in no time and ditch the traditional measuring tape for good.

If you are still left with doubts and queries, comment them below, and I’ll happily help.

FAQs

How accurate is the measure app on iPhone?

I used the Measure app and measuring tape to measure various objects, and the Measure app’s accuracy came as close as 95%.

How to measure degrees on iPhone?

You can use the Level feature in the Measure app to measure degrees on your iPhone.

You would like to explore:

  • Measure distance between two points in Google Maps on iPhone
  • How to clear RAM on iPhone
  • Best LiDAR apps for iPhone and iPad

mainEntity.name: Can I record calls without the other person knowing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Nope, iOS makes the call public, letting everyone know it's being captured. You can't turn off this alert since it keeps things above board legally.

mainEntity.name: Where are my iPhone call recordings saved?

acceptedAnswer.text: You'll find all recordings in the Notes app, under the "Call Recordings" folder. They're synced through iCloud if that's running on your gears.

mainEntity.name: How do I access the transcripts of my recorded calls?

acceptedAnswer.text: Open "Call Recordings" in Notes; the transcript is cozy beneath the audio file and searchable.

mainEntity.name: Why can't I see the record button on my iPhone during a call?

acceptedAnswer.text: To get the full kit you need iOS 18 or later, the right regional settings, and Apple's Intelligence cruising cool in Settings.

mainEntity.name: Does the iPhone call recording feature work with FaceTime or WhatsApp?

acceptedAnswer.text: Nope, this little gem’s closed for just regular calls via the Phone app. Third-party recordings aren’t invited to this party.

mainEntity.name: How do I share a recorded phone call from the Notes app?

acceptedAnswer.text: In Notes, hit up the recording, slap the share button, and choose your audience. You decide if they get audio, transcript, or both.

mainEntity.name: Can I automatically record all calls on my iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: You gotta actually tap that record button for each chat there's no collective auto-record option.

mainEntity.name: How do I delete call recordings from my iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: In Notes, a left swipe on the ones to toss will reveal "Delete," or you can go batch-mode with "Edit."

mainEntity.name: Does iPhone call recording work internationally?

acceptedAnswer.text: Feature availability is gonna flex based on country and local dictates. It's wise to double-check settings and laws if you're trotting the globe with this.

@graph.name: How to Measure a Single Dimension of an Object on iPhone
@graph.description: Learn how to quickly measure the length or width of an object using the Measure app on your iPhone. This step-by-step guide shows you how to start, adjust, and capture accurate measurements with ease.

step.name: Open the Measure app
step.text: Open the Measure app on your iPhone and follow the on-screen instructions to move your device around until the AR technology activates.

itemListElement.text: Launch the Measure app on your iPhone.
Slowly move your iPhone around until the AR technology recognizes your surroundings.

step.name: Set the starting point
step.text: Place the circle with a dot over the point where you want to begin measuring and tap the plus button to mark it.

itemListElement.text: Align the circle with a dot over the desired starting point.
Tap the plus button to mark the beginning of your measurement.

step.name: Mark the endpoint
step.text: Move your iPhone slowly toward the endpoint of the object. Once the circle aligns with the end, tap the plus button again to complete the line.

itemListElement.text: Move your iPhone steadily until the circle appears at the object’s endpoint.
Tap the plus button again to finish the measurement line.

step.name: Adjust the line if needed
step.text: If the line is not perfectly straight, touch and hold either endpoint, then drag it into the correct position.

itemListElement.text: Touch and hold any endpoint of the line.
Drag the point until the line is straight and accurate.

step.name: Save the measurement
step.text: Once you are satisfied with the measurement, tap the Capture button at the bottom right to save a screenshot in your Photos app.

itemListElement.text: Review the measurement displayed above the line.
Tap the Capture button to save the measurement screenshot in Photos.

@graph.name: How to Measure multiple dimensions of an object on iPhone
@graph.description: Measure several sides of an object with the iPhone’s Measure app. This friendly walkthrough shows how to add, adjust, and save multiple measurements on one screen.

step.name: Set up the Measure app
step.text: Open the Measure app and move your iPhone around until the AR view locks onto the scene. Make sure you can see the object clearly on the screen.

itemListElement.text: Launch the Measure app on your iPhone.
Slowly move your iPhone so the AR view initializes.

step.name: Start your next measurement
step.text: Place the on-screen dot on a point of the existing line, then tap the plus button to mark the new starting point.

itemListElement.text: Align the dot with the point on the current line where you want to begin.
Tap the plus button to set the starting point.

step.name: Mark the new endpoint
step.text: Move your iPhone toward the other end of the side you want to measure. When the dot aligns with the endpoint, tap the plus button again.

itemListElement.text: Pan your iPhone until the dot reaches the endpoint of the second side.
Tap the plus button to complete the second measurement.

step.name: Fine tune the line
step.text: If the line is slightly off, touch and hold either point and drag it until the line looks straight and accurate.

itemListElement.text: Touch and hold a point to pick it up.
Drag the point to refine the alignment.

step.name: Review multiple measurements
step.text: Check that both measurements appear on screen and read clearly above their lines.

itemListElement.text: Confirm that the app shows the lengths above each line.
Make adjustments if any value looks off.

step.name: Add more sides as needed
step.text: Repeat the same process to capture additional sides or edges until you have all the dimensions you need.

itemListElement.text: Set a new start point on an existing line or a new edge.
Move to the endpoint and tap the plus button again.

step.name: Save your measurements
step.text: When everything looks right, tap the Capture button to save a screenshot of all measurements to the Photos app.

itemListElement.text: Review the on-screen measurements one last time.
Tap the Capture button to store the screenshot in Photos.

@graph.name: How to Measure the Surface Area of a Rectangular Object on iPhone
@graph.description: Quickly calculate the surface area of a rectangular object using your iPhone’s Measure app. This step-by-step guide shows you how to detect, measure, and save results with ease.

step.name: Set up the object
step.text: Place your iPhone so the viewfinder is directly over the rectangular object you want to measure. The app will highlight the shape with dotted lines.

itemListElement.text: Open the Measure app on your iPhone.
Hold your iPhone over the rectangular object until dotted lines outline it.

step.name: Capture the measurement
step.text: Once the app outlines the rectangle, tap the plus button to confirm. The dimensions and surface area will appear with the value shown in the center.

itemListElement.text: Wait for the app to detect the rectangular shape automatically.
Tap the plus button to display the surface area measurement.

step.name: Save the measurement
step.text: Tap the Capture button at the bottom right corner to take a screenshot and store it in the Photos app.

itemListElement.text: Review the displayed surface area on the screen.
Tap the Capture button to save a screenshot in Photos.

step.name: Copy the measurement
step.text: If you want to use the exact values elsewhere, tap the surface area label and copy the measurement.

itemListElement.text: Tap the surface area result shown in the center of the rectangle.
Select Copy to save the value for later use.

@graph.name: How to measure the level of an object on iPhone
@graph.description: Use your iPhone’s Measure app to check if a surface is perfectly level. This short guide shows how to switch to Level mode, place your phone correctly, and read the angle.

step.name: Open Level mode
step.text: Open the Measure app, then tap the Level icon at the bottom right to switch to Level mode.

itemListElement.text: Launch the Measure app on your iPhone.
Tap the Level icon at the bottom right.

step.name: Place the iPhone on the surface
step.text: Gently place your iPhone on the surface you want to check without pressing down or tilting it.

itemListElement.text: Lay the iPhone flat on the surface or edge you want to test.
Hold the phone steady so the reading can settle.

step.name: Read the level
step.text: Check the on-screen value. The app shows 0 degrees if the surface is level, otherwise it displays the angle of deviation.

itemListElement.text: Look for 0 degrees to confirm the surface is level.
If you see a number, that is the angle of deviation from level.

@graph.name: How to measure a person’s height with iPhone
@graph.description: Use your iPhone’s Measure app to quickly check someone’s height. This guide walks you through positioning, measuring, and saving the result as a screenshot.

step.name: Open the Measure app
step.text: Launch the Measure app on your iPhone to begin the process.

itemListElement.text: Find the Measure app on your iPhone and open it.

step.name: Position the person
step.text: Ask the person to stand in front of the rear camera so their full body, from head to toe, is visible on your screen.

itemListElement.text: Make sure the person stands on a flat surface.
Adjust your iPhone so their entire body fits within the viewfinder.

step.name: Read the height measurement
step.text: A white line with the person’s height will automatically appear above their head on the screen.

itemListElement.text: Look at the top of the person’s head on your iPhone screen.
Read the height displayed in the white line above their head.

step.name: Save or record the result
step.text: Either note down the displayed height manually or tap the Capture button to save a screenshot in the Photos app.

itemListElement.text: Write down the height if you just need the value.
Tap the Capture button to save the measurement screenshot in Photos.

keyPoints.title: Pre-installed Measure App and Compatibility
keyPoints.explanation: The Measure app is pre-installed on iPhone and iPad models from iPhone SE 1st generation onwards, with compatibility depending on the device model.

keyPoints.title: Measuring a Single Object Dimension
keyPoints.explanation: Open the Measure app, follow on-screen instructions to move your iPhone around, set start and end points with circles, and capture the measurement, which appears on the screen.

keyPoints.title: Measuring Multiple Dimensions of an Object
keyPoints.explanation: Repeat the process for different start and end points to measure multiple dimensions, viewing all measurements simultaneously and saving screenshots.

keyPoints.title: Measuring Surface Area of a Rectangular Object
keyPoints.explanation: Position the iPhone over a rectangular object, let the app detect it, then tap '+' to see and save the surface area measurement.

keyPoints.title: Using the Level Feature to Measure Angles
keyPoints.explanation: Tap the Level icon in the Measure app to check if a surface is level, with 0 degrees indicating a flat surface or showing the deviation angle.

title.rendered: iPhone Battery Stats Explained: Check What’s Draining Power

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Understanding iPhone Battery Tracking: iPhone logs app activity, screen time, and processes, then displays graphs and app usage data to reveal battery drain patterns.
  • How to Access Battery Usage Stats: Open Settings > Battery to view detailed charge graphs, activity history, and app-specific consumption across the past 24 hours or 10 days.
  • Deciphering Battery Graphs: Green indicates normal use, yellow shows Low Power Mode, and red marks critical levels, with charging times highlighted for clarity.
  • Using Long-term Battery Health Tools: Battery Health & Charging displays maximum capacity, cycle count, and charging patterns so you can manage overall lifespan and performance.
  • Tips for Better Battery Management: Review battery reports, limit background refresh, enable Low Power Mode, and watch app usage closely to keep your iPhone lasting longer.

For years, the biggest worry for iPhone users has been battery life. While Apple hasn’t drastically increased physical battery sizes, it has continuously optimized iOS to squeeze out more usage. Today, your iPhone has a dedicated Battery section that reveals detailed insights into power consumption, helping you see exactly what’s draining your phone and how to manage it better.

This guide walks you through how iPhone battery tracking works, where to find these stats, and how to use them to extend your iPhone’s battery life.

Table of Contents
  • How iPhone Battery Tracking Works
  • How to View Your iPhone's Battery Usage
  • Understanding iPhone Battery Graphs
    • Daily vs. 10-Day Battery Views
    • Breaking Down Battery Usage by App
  • Checking Battery Health and Charging Options
  • Smart Tips to Make the Most of Battery Stats
  • Stay in Control of Your iPhone's Battery Life

How iPhone Battery Tracking Works

Your iPhone’s built-in power management system monitors every detail of your usage, screen time, background processes, charging behavior, and even low-power sessions. iOS then organizes this data into two clear views:

  • Graphs: Showing your battery level over time and screen-on vs. screen-off activity.
  • App Data: Breaking down which apps or processes consumed the most power.

This combination helps you identify not just when your iPhone is draining power, but why.

How to View Your iPhone’s Battery Usage

To check your iPhone’s battery insights:

  1. Open the Settings app on your iPhone. 
  2. Locate and tap Battery to access battery settings. 
  3. Now, wait for iOS to load your iPhone’s detailed battery usage stats. 
  4. Once it does, iOS presents you with two graphs representing different key stats.

Here, you’ll find two main graphs:

  • Battery Level Graph: Tracks charge percentage throughout the day.
  • Activity Graph: Shows how long your iPhone was in use—both with the screen on and off.

Understanding iPhone Battery Graphs

Apple has designed the battery level graph to give you deep insight into a high-level overview and detailed breakdown of your iPhone’s power consumption over the last 24 hours and 10 days.

If you look closely at the Battery Level graph, you’ll notice different colored lines based on the time frame against the battery charging level. Here’s what each color represents.

  • Green: Normal battery usage while running on battery power. 
  • Yellow: Indicates your iPhone was in Low Power Mode, helping extend usage by reducing background activity and visual effects.
  • Red: Represents the hours when the battery percentage was critically low, i.e., below 20%.

Plus, a lightning sign appears below the lines representing the periods when your iPhone was charging.

Just below the Battery Level graph, you’ll find the Activity graph, which shows how long your iPhone was actively in use. Like the Battery Level graph, Apple has broken down the Activity graph into two colors:

  • Screen On (blue): The time your display was lit up, usually reflecting direct usage like browsing, streaming, or gaming. 
  • Screen Off (turquoise): Time when apps were still running in the background even though the screen wasn’t on, such as music playback, downloads, or background refresh.

When combined, these graphs help you determine if a significant drain was caused by direct usage (such as video playback) or by hidden background processes.

Daily vs. 10-Day Battery Views

At the top, switch between:

  • 24-Hour View: Hour-by-hour breakdown of charging and usage.
  • 10-Day View: Long-term trends and recurring app drain patterns.

This is especially helpful after iOS updates; you’ll quickly notice if an app suddenly starts misbehaving.

Breaking Down Battery Usage by App

Below the Battery Level and Activity graph, there’s another section named “Battery Usage By App.” Under this section, you’ll find a list of all installed apps and how much battery each app has consumed within the last 24 hours or 10 days.  
 
By default, the “Battery Usage By App” section is set to show the battery usage per app. You can tap the “Show Activity” tab next to “Battery Usage By App” to view how long each app was used on-screen or in the background.

 
This way, you can easily identify apps that are draining power disproportionately, whether through heavy screen use or background tasks.

Checking Battery Health and Charging Options

Beyond daily stats, iOS also provides long-term battery health tools under Battery Health & Charging:

  • Maximum Capacity: Shows your battery’s health compared to when it was new.
  • Cycle Count: Displays the total number of complete charge cycles your iPhone battery has gone through.
  • Optimized Battery Charging: Slows charging above 80% until you need the phone, reducing battery aging.
  • Charging Limits (iOS 18+): Lets you cap charging at 80% to extend lifespan.

Smart Tips to Make the Most of Battery Stats

Use these insights to optimize your iPhone’s battery life:

  • Turn off Background App Refresh for apps that consume too much power. 
  • Keep an eye out for apps that drain energy despite minimal use. These may need updating or replacing. 
  • Use Low Power Mode during long days to reduce background activity and extend battery life. 
  • Check trends weekly to catch any abnormal drain early, especially after a software update.

Stay in Control of Your iPhone’s Battery Life

With Apple’s built-in battery insights, you no longer have to guess what’s eating your charge. The graphs, app-level breakdowns, and charging tools give you the power to monitor and manage your iPhone’s energy consumption like a pro.

Make it a habit to review your stats regularly, and you’ll keep your iPhone running smoothly all day.

Don’t miss these related reads:

  • 10 Tips to Maintain Your iPhone’s Battery Health
  • How to Fix Overnight Battery Drain Issue on iPhone
  • How to Check Battery Cycle Count on Any iPhone in Seconds

acceptedAnswer.text: Nope, iOS makes the call public, letting everyone know it's being captured. You can't turn off this alert since it keeps things above board legally.

mainEntity.name: Where are my iPhone call recordings saved?

acceptedAnswer.text: You'll find all recordings in the Notes app, under the "Call Recordings" folder. They're synced through iCloud if that's running on your gears.

mainEntity.name: How do I access the transcripts of my recorded calls?

acceptedAnswer.text: Open "Call Recordings" in Notes; the transcript is cozy beneath the audio file and searchable.

mainEntity.name: Why can't I see the record button on my iPhone during a call?

acceptedAnswer.text: To get the full kit you need iOS 18 or later, the right regional settings, and Apple's Intelligence cruising cool in Settings.

mainEntity.name: Does the iPhone call recording feature work with FaceTime or WhatsApp?

acceptedAnswer.text: Nope, this little gem’s closed for just regular calls via the Phone app. Third-party recordings aren’t invited to this party.

mainEntity.name: How do I share a recorded phone call from the Notes app?

acceptedAnswer.text: In Notes, hit up the recording, slap the share button, and choose your audience. You decide if they get audio, transcript, or both.

mainEntity.name: Can I automatically record all calls on my iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: You gotta actually tap that record button for each chat there's no collective auto-record option.

mainEntity.name: How do I delete call recordings from my iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: In Notes, a left swipe on the ones to toss will reveal "Delete," or you can go batch-mode with "Edit."

mainEntity.name: Does iPhone call recording work internationally?

acceptedAnswer.text: Feature availability is gonna flex based on country and local dictates. It's wise to double-check settings and laws if you're trotting the globe with this.

keyPoints.title: Understanding iPhone Battery Tracking
keyPoints.explanation: Your iPhone monitors usage, screen time, and background processes, presenting data through graphs and app consumption details to help you identify power drain sources.

keyPoints.title: How to Access Battery Usage Stats
keyPoints.explanation: Go to Settings > Battery to view detailed battery graphs and stats, including charge level and activity over time, to monitor your power consumption.

keyPoints.title: Deciphering Battery Graphs
keyPoints.explanation: Battery graphs display levels and activity with color codes: green for normal, yellow for low power mode, and red for critically low battery times; also showing charging periods.

keyPoints.title: Using Long-term Battery Health Tools
keyPoints.explanation: Check your battery's maximum capacity, cycle count, and charging habits via Battery Health & Charging to maintain optimal battery health and lifespan.

keyPoints.title: Tips for Better Battery Management
keyPoints.explanation: Regularly review your device's stats, turn off background app refresh, enable low power mode, and monitor app usage to extend your iPhone's battery life.

title.rendered: How to Close All Tabs in Safari on iPhone and iPad at Once

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Close all Safari tabs instantly by long-pressing the tab switcher and selecting “Close All Tabs” for a fast browser reset.
  • From the tab overview, long-press ‘Done’ to close all tabs—a quick method if you’re already viewing open pages.
  • Set tabs to auto-close after 1 day, week, or month in Settings > Safari > Close Tabs to keep your browser clutter-free.
  • Use tab search to close similar pages together—search by keyword, then close all matching tabs in one go.
  • Deleting a Tab Group clears all its tabs—a useful way to bulk-close themed sessions or research topics.

Having too many tabs open in Safari can affect its performance and lead to an inefficient browsing experience. While you can close tabs individually in Safari, depending on the number of open tabs, it can become quite tedious and time-consuming.

Fortunately, you can close all your Safari tabs on your iPhone or iPad in one go. In this article, I will show you all the possible ways to do it.

Table of Contents
  • How to close all Safari tabs on iPhone and iPad at once
  • How to close all Safari tabs on iPhone from the tab switcher screen
  • How to close Safari tabs automatically on iPhone and iPad
  • How to close similar Safari tabs at once on an iPhone
  • How to close all Safari tabs on iPhone with Tab Groups

How to close all Safari tabs on iPhone and iPad at once

It’s pretty easy to close all your Safari tabs on iPhone and iPad running iOS 18 or iPadOS 18. Here are the steps you need to follow:

  1. Launch Safari on your iPhone and long-press the tab switcher icon in the bottom-right corner of the screen. On an iPad, this icon will be in the top-right corner.
  2. Select Close All [number] Tabs.
  3. Confirm by tapping Close All Tabs.

How to close all Safari tabs on iPhone from the tab switcher screen

Another way to close all your Safari tabs at once is to use the Tab Switcher screen. This view shows you all your open tabs in a grid, making it easy to take a quick look and close them all at once.

  1. Inside Safari, tap the tab switcher icon.
  2. Take a look at the tabs if needed.
  3. Long-press the word Done.
  4. Tap Close All [number] Tabs.
  5. Select Close All Tabs from the pop-up menu.

How to close Safari tabs automatically on iPhone and iPad

If you have the habit of leaving a lot of Safari tabs open, you can set your iPhone or iPad to automatically close tabs after a certain amount of time. This way, you won’t have to worry about too many tabs slowing down your browser.

  1. Open the Settings app.
  2. Scroll down and select Safari.
  3. Tap Close Tabs.
  4. You can choose the time frame for closing tabs automatically: After One Day, After One Week, or After One Month.

Safari will now automatically close your tabs based on your chosen time frame.

How to close similar Safari tabs at once on an iPhone

When you’re researching something, you may end up opening a bunch of tabs related to the same topic. In such a situation, you can close them all at once using a handy feature in Safari. This ensures your other important tabs remain intact.

  1. Open the tab switcher screen in Safari.
  2. Tap the top of the screen to reveal the search bar.
  3. Type a word you think would be common on all the tabs you want to close, and you’ll see all the open tabs that match this word.
  4. Long-press the word Cancel and tap Close [number] Tabs Matching “search-word”.

How to close all Safari tabs on iPhone with Tab Groups

Tab Groups is a Safari feature that lets you keep your tabs organized using folders. If you’ve used it to keep all similar tabs organized in one Tab Group, deleting that Tab Group will close all open tabs inside it. Here’s how:

  1. Go to the tab switcher screen in Safari.
  2. Long-press one of the tab thumbnails.
  3. Tap Close Other Tabs. Except for this tab, all others will close.

Signing off…

That’s it. The above methods should help you declutter Safari on your iPhone or iPad and give you a clean slate to start fresh.

Moving forward, be sure to use Tab Groups or profiles in Safari to keep your tabs organized and avoid having an overcrowded stack of tabs again.

Read more:

  • Safari extensions for iPhone and iPad
  • How to hide IP address in Safari
  • How to clear Safari cache on iPhone or iPad
